There are two great elements about this particular shaver. The first is that it is quiet. After using a Panasonic wet/dry, that sounded like an outboard motor, this Norelco can be used in a library. Very nice. The other great element is the closeness of the shave, which is excellent.

I've always liked the "triple head" configuration of the Norelco shavers and this one is the best yet, with the settings for more sensitivity, and the heads that flex with your face so you don't miss anything. For me, the "normal" setting is sensitive enough to use, but it's nice to know you can make adjustments if needed.

The battery life is quite good; I took it on a recent three week business trip and only needed to charge it once!

My only criticism of the product is about the trimmer attached. It really doesn't do a wonderful job. It's not horrible, but it's just not as good as the rest of the shaver. The trimmer is a bit small and awkward to handle. I still keep my old Panasonic around when I want to do trimming! Otherwise, it was well worth the investment!

Recommended.

title: Must-have product
text:
I have dark, thick hair on my head but for whatever unfortunate genetic reason, I have very light and thin eyebrows, and fill them in with makeup every single day. I have never dyed them before. This dye darkened them to match my hair perfectly, and my method of application gave me the perfect shape with no skin staining or irritation.

First of all, I only used about 1/4 of the powder in the capsule because I could tell that would probably be more than enough (and it was), so this stuff is going to last forever.

Instead of washing my face beforehand, I used a dry microfiber cloth to wipe off my eyebrow area as clean as I could. I think the fact that I didn't wash my face meant that my skin had a small layer of oil on it for protection against staining and irritation. A little oil also will not hinder the hair coloring process.

I used the included application brush, putting very small amounts of the dye on the brush and applying it in light, careful strokes. The movement is like sketching in a sketchbook instead of drawing solid lines all at once, and I did not have a pile of dye on my brows at the end.

I know that with my hair, I need to leave dye on it for a long time, so I left this on for 10 minutes. I rinsed the dye off with cool water to avoid opening up my pores. I checked my brows and thought they could be a little darker, so I re-applied and left on for another 5-10 mins. Total of 15-20 mins.

Finally, I washed it off for good with a gentle unscented soap, using my fingernails to help get all the dye off and exfoliate the skin underneath and around my brows, so I was left with no stains.

And that was that. I have eyebrows now! I can even TOUCH them! I can't believe I never tried this before, this will be a staple in my life now.

title: Comparable to the basic Waterpik portable with a few improvements and extras
text:
This unit is comparable to my very basic travel Waterpik flosser. In fact it has several features that the basic model lacks for around the same price. This unit has three speeds, whereas the entry level Waterpik only has one. The fastest speed is comparable with the one speed on my Waterpik, and it’s the only speed I need. This unit has a charge light (blinks until charged) while there is no such light on the comparably priced Waterpik. This device has about the same sized reservoir as the Waterpik, but because of the design, it’s on the bottom as opposed to along the sides of the unit, the result being that it makes it a lot bulkier, which is unfortunate in a travel water flosser. Unfortunately, there is no advantage to this design as like the Waterpik, it begins to stop pumping water as the tank gets lower, forcing the user to keep the unit vertical in order to get to the water at the very bottom of the reservoir, which can become quite awkward while trying to get around the teeth and gums. I’ve owned several of these, and to be fair, they all suffer from this same problem.

One more thing: this unit comes with a nice case and a stash of attachments (which are usually found in home units and don’t generally come with portable units ,) none of which I have much use for, but I guess it’s good to know they’re there. It does include two of the standard water flosser adaptors, so two people can use it.

The only thing that remains to be seen is how long this puppy will last. This is my 3rd travel water flosser. I’ll report back should something ontoward occur, or if it continues to work well.

title: 100% worth the money
text:
I was looking for a badger shaving brush since the boar brush I have had became completely unusable after just 2 years of use. It was losing hairs almost every day. Need to note that was a cheap one which came in a set with a soap and a bowl for $12 altogether. After eliminating expensive badger brushes from my search I narrowed the options to this one, Colonel Conk's brush and Kingsley's each costs around 22-25$. After long comparison when each of the brushes made it in and out of my cart at least one time I picked the SimplyBeautiful one mostly because of the chrome handle. Although, I was afraid it would be too heavy for me. Indeed, when it came the handle seemed somewhat heavy for the first time. I think it is heavy enough, to kill a person if you throw it at his head. But I got used to the weight incredibly fast maybe at the second shaving. It gives good lather which covers the places on face which need to be covered. With my old shaving brush I had not only my face covered but lather would be at some unexpected places of the bathroom so it was not very soap efficient. I have seen only 1 fallen bristle from the new brush and this happened on the second week of use. I think this is normal for a new shaving brush. Now it is 3 weeks went by since I started using it and I have no complains at all. Moreover, my bathroom looks more sophisticated with it. I store this item as they recommend upside down in a stand. I like starting mornings with shaving now and recommend it to all.
Now it is December 2012 and a year went on. Still cannot complain. I have seen 2-3 fallen bristles for the entire period and consider this as acceptable.

title: Looks nice and easy to use...jury’s still out on results.
text:
This thing looks very nice, and feels even nicer! It’s beautiful, and very easy to use. However, it is difficult to grip at times, especially if your hands are wet or moisturized. There are two clipped corners to allow for optimal grip location, so that is a much-appreciated design feature. Nevertheless, the smooth glass edges can make it tricky to get a consistent, sturdy grip. I wear nitrile gloves while using it, so that I feel more confident in the hold I’ve got on it, especially over a hard surface. So, keep that in mind. That being said, though, it is far more aesthetically appealing, user-friendly, and gentler than the traditional pumice stones or foot graters.

A protective storage case would be a great addition to this item. I saved all the packaging and have been placing the file back into the plastic packaging tray and then placing that tray back into the outer plastic packaging box. Something similar to a travel bar soap container or a retainer case would be perfect (slimmer, of course, to fit the file)! The storage case with drainage holes for drying would minimize the risk of breaking the file during cleaning, drying, and storing it. For the current price point, I personally think a reusable storage case should be included.

All that aside, my only real concern, and the reason for the current rating, is that my feet actually felt and looked dryer and rougher several days to a week after the first use. I realize this may be due to my own user error, as I followed the exfoliation with my usual moisturization regimen. It is reasonable to assume I should have taken extra steps to protect and care for me feet immediately following the exfoliation, as the delicate, softer skin was exposed. So, I am going to try it again, this is over-moisturizing and wearing plush socks for the few days afterward. I will update my review with my new results!

Overall, I currently recommend this foot file. I find it to be worth trying out, and is a better alternative to the more abrasive methods. I have included photos showing the packaging and tray in which I keep it stored, as well as close-ups of the smooth top size and gritty underside. Hope they help!

text: Those who are concerned with the latest and most effective electric toothbrush would do well to consider the ORAL-B VITALITY model.  When an electric toothbrush performs on a high level as this one, then performance trumps price, which in any case is quite reasonable. What I found useful was the dual revolving bristle head.  This twin set of bristles is a double edged sword.  True, it cleans and massages well, thus insuring the fast removal of plaque, but on the down side, the user must remember to take care not to exert too much pressure since it is easy to forget that gum tissue is far more fragile than tooth enamel.  There are several other plusses, the most notable being its portable recharger that allows one to use it in a normal manner for several days. Finally, it has the added advantage common to all electric brushes; one can easily swoop away plaque from hard to reach areas such as behind the front teeth.  When one considers the opposition, the primary reason to buy one over the other is how well the brush does its job in a safe, efficient, and reliable manner.  The ORAL-B VITALITY brush stands out.

title: Warning - product is not as portrayed on site
text:
I purchased 4 of these as a gift to my mother and grandmother. I turned them onto Ruby Stone years ago, but they are not able to find them locally anymore. This set had the buffer added which they didn't need, but wouldn't mind if it was in the package; the real purchase here was the Ruby Stone file itself.

The picture shows the Ruby Stone like I expected to receive it - a pullout version like I have used in the past. It's always been very easy to use and, most importantly easy to handle and gentle. There are arthritic hands in play here. Instead the file is some sort of flip out side-sheath with a very point top. I guess you are supposed to be able to flip it out or pull it out completely (since whenever I flip it it just end up coming out all the way) and then put it back. I found it hard to get out (the plastic is cheap and curves in to grab the file) and almost impossible to get back in. There is no way that arthritic hands could handle. I think the pointy end, combined with the difficulty to manage, only makes this a dangerous combo. Sure, if someone removes the file for them the first time they can ditch the case but I hate that then there is nothing protecting the stone file from breaking (this version is much thinner than past versions as well, by about half the thickness. And, not that this makes any difference but is nice to know, it is white vs the original pink).

Overall, I am very disappointed. I tried to return the files but will have to pay shipping even though I was misled. So now I am stuck with them. I will scour local stores to find something different for my mother and grandmother.

I do not recommend this product unless you cannot find any other ruby stone alternative. And I hope the image gets updated so others are not misled and left to hold the expense for a product they don't want like I was.

title: Worked well for curly hair.
text:
I own several straightening products but never owned a ceramic straightener comb brush. Some of the previous straightening products I have used have included a blow dryer and straightening iron. The blow dryer takes the most amount of time and the straightener reacquired me to constantly brush my hair before trying to straighten (I have really curly/wavy hair). I found that this Hairika Ceramic Straightener brush cut down my straightening time. I used it on dry hair with a bit of product. First I brushed my hair out and then took small sections and brushed the straightener comb through my hair. It was pretty simple and worked well. I found that it took away the frizzy look and still left a little volume (I don't normally aim for stick straight hair). I was pleased with the results. Also it was simple to turn on (just hold the on button for 3 seconds). The + and - are used to increase and decrease the temperature. The one downside I found was while using the brush I would accidentally press the + and - and change the temperature. The screen was easy to use to see what the temperature was. It would be beneficial to be able to have a hold button to lock a temperature. Overall I am pleased with this purchase and will be using it to cut my straightening time when I choose to straighten my hair. I also appreciated the nice packaging (see pictures). The brush came in a nice box with lid, some pins to help hold the hair that is not being straightened, a bag for storage and clear instructions. I will caution that using any straightening products too often can damage hair. I straighten hair only once a week and make sure to use appropriate hair products to reduce the heat damage. This brush would make a great gift.

* I received this brush at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest and unbiased feedback.

title: Palm oil - pore clogging - failed applicator
text:
Not so good: Tube design failed, pore clogging, not 2-in-1
Good: color
Unknown: lasting?

I was glad I read a few reviews before I opened it, then I opened it carefully, pushed gently, and it burst out the sides all the same. I wasn't sure if it was because the on/off was marked on the lid but not the tube, maybe I just turned it the wrong amount? ½ turn seemed reasonable, so I turned it tighter and more came out the sides. For what it's worth, the instructions just have us dabbing a couple dots on with the sponge and blending with the fingers or brush. The sponge is an entirely unnecessary addition.

As you can see from the photo, this did allow me to put a nice and thick layer on my arm just in case anyone is looking to see how dramatic it can be. I do like the color, it's a good match, but I wouldn't use it on my eyes or my lips because the product says 'liquid blush.' There is a graphic on this page that says 2-in-1, despite showing eyes/blush/lips on the very same graphic, which I am pretty sure would be 3-in-1.

The last issue is the ingredients. The top ingredient is Ethylhexyl Palmitate, which is a pretty well known comedogenic (pore clogging) problem, so it's not great if you have breakouts. That's why I don't know how long it lasts or well it holds up over time, it's not worth the high risk of breakouts so I didn't wear it long. You might have guessed that 'palmitate' is also a derivative of Palm Oil, which is an industry that is destroying many biodiverse forests.

Two stars for color, texture feels nice, but I would only recommend this to people with clear skin that don't really have any desire to use the applicator sponge.

Then use the thinnest layer possible of the Murron gel peel off base coat. Cure for 30 seconds or more. Apply your gel color and top coat as normal.

title: Curls Lashes, No Pinching
text:
I am a makeup junkie, so naturally I have used many eye lash curlers in my time. I am rating this one by Bella and Bear 3 stars, simply because in my use it didn't perform better, or worse than my current drug store bought eye lash curler. So let me break down my review.

The packaging of this is gorgeous. Very feminine and girly. I fell for it! The curler inside came with 1 pad that was attached to it. The claim for that being unlike most curlers, this one works so well that you don't need replacements. Obviously I cannot give my claim to that one as I have only had this curler for a couple of weeks. So far the pad has held up wonderfully as you would hope it would. The pad is black in color, and the handles of the curler are a dark pink. Feels durable, and not flimsy.

Using this is pretty basic. If you know how to curl your lashes, then you know what to do. I tested this curler against my current drug store curler. On my left eye I did this one by Bella and Bear, on the right, my old curler. I didn't experience any pinching, or discomfort while using this one. My end results after putting on 1 coat of mascara were pretty much identical. I honestly couldn't tell much of a difference. The curl also stayed for the same amount of time as my drug store curler.

The final thing that made me give this 3 stars is the price. My drug store curler cost me about $10. If the price was a bit more competitive with other curlers that provide the same results, then I would definitely up this rating to 4 stars.

*Please note that I was sent this product complimentary to try out in my home in order to share my honest experience, thoughts and review.

title: Itchy scalp & covered in hives ... again :(
text:
I wanted to like this shampoo. With the reviews, how couldn't I? I came to Amazon several months ago looking for the right shampoo that was paraben & sulfate free. I am trying to be more conscientious about the chemicals and scents that I use on my body and this over-delivered. I purchased it in the vanilla scent and anxiously awaited for my hair transformation.

After two shampoos, my scalp started itching constantly. My scalp, back of my neck, and the top of my back (all areas where the shampoo had come into contact with my hair and skin) were covered in itchy, irritated bumps. I stopped using the shampoo immediately. It took me two weeks for my skin and the itch to clear up and go away. I passed the bottle on to a friend with the disclaimer "People love it, but it covered my skin in hives ..." I was later told it worked just fine for them. Go figure.

A few weeks ago it was time to hunt for a new shampoo. Again, I found Sweet Baby Shampoo. More stellar reviews, one of which specifically called out the hives. That reviewer stated that after switching to the unscented, the hives never re-appeared. Perfect! One-click purchase. I was down to give it another go. Again, stellar reviews.

Three shampoos and the scalp itching is back. The hives are smaller this time, but they're still there. I do not get it. What is in this stuff?! In a pinch, I have washed my hair with all sorts of crummy products. I spent a week in the desert with high alkaline dust matting down my hair and washed my hair with bar soap. No problem (other than dried out hair). I've used $1 drug store brands, the crap they stock in hotels, even the all purpose shampoo / conditioner / soap concoction they supply for free in the gym. Never had a single reaction to any of it. Think about it. Something isn't adding up. Sadly.

I decided to order a 2nd one so that I could wear the pair together and get the fullness I wanted. Meanwhile, I decided to do a full co-wash and this thing became a tangled unmanageable mess! I spent about 2 hours un-matting it and trying to recover it. After it dried it was stretched out, very little curl definition and kind of a mess. So once again I sectioned it, deep conditioned it, and put my normal defining products in it and then that was all she wrote. Completely unsalvageable. I am so disappointed. Now I do have the 2nd one but can only wear the one so I still don't have the fullness I wanted and I pretty much know that once I wash this one that'll probably be the end of it's days. So my suggestion is to use minimal product. Try to do more of a spray wash vs a full-on wash and get as much use out of it as you can.

I will mention however that when the 2nd one came it was more of a 3c texture and when I contacted the seller to let them know I needed the tighter curl they sent one out to me super fast and with no hassle so the customer service is good. I do still have the looser curl but I am not currently wearing it so I don't know how that one will wear. From what I understand the 3c version is the one they now send with this listing.

I have purchased this now three times, and I can say that I am super pleased with this conditioner. I get compliments on how healthy my hair looks, and it overall leaves my hair with a nice volume (not too much) and a great smell.

A note about making the conditioner:
After trial and error, I discovered the best way to make this and not end up with any lumps (which eventually dissolve) is to break the bar up into a glass or metal bowl, and then once you pour in the boiling water, use a metal whisk to stir it until you don’t see any more lumps. It’ll initially be very watery, and you’ll think “oh no, is this not going to work?” Let it sit and cool, and you’ll come back to some fabulous conditioner (as long as you only used 12 ounces of water).

Enjoy having lovely hair and helping the planet!

title: Pain Relief in a Roller!
text:
I got the hot pink Derma Roller yesterday and immediately put it in the freezer. This morning I got it out to give it a try, and I'm already addicted! I was actually a bit dubious about this product, truth be told, but it's fantastic!

It feels wonderful to roll it across my forehead, throat, and eyes. The first touch made me jump a little bit because it's REALLY cold, but after the initial contact, it feels good. I'm probably too old to anti-age, but I'm going to use it just because it makes me feel so good, and I plan to give one to each of my daughters.

I get migraines, as does my youngest daughter, so we spend a lot of time in the dark, with ice packs on our necks and foreheads. The next time I'm struck, I'm going to roll this magic device on the back of my neck, and I fully expect it to work better than just an ice pack or bag of frozen peas. Hopefully I won't have to test this anytime soon, but after I do, I'll update this post to let you know how/if it worked.

Last year I broke my wrist and even after weeks of physical therapy, I was still in a lot of pain and, again, spent a lot of time on ice and heat. I wish I had this then because as I roll it over my wrist right now, I can tell that it would have felt SO good when I was still recovering.

The bright colors are cheerful, and make me smile, and anything that makes me smile, is worth having.

title: Like Other's State this Doesn't Stay Put
text:
I bought this for my wife to help her keep her flat iron safe from damaging with heat and to tidy up the counter space. I should also note that I use this stand with her flat iron for safety when coupled with a smart plug to turn her iron on and off at specific times before she goes to work. I wanted to have her flat iron preheated for her when she was dressed for work and also to ensure she turned it off after she was done using it, as she is notorious for leaving it plugged in and worrying me about setting the house on fire.

Her flat iron is a Paul Mitchell something or other (about 1.25") and fits perfectly. The opening appears that it would hold up to a 1.5" flat iron depending on the exact dimensions. The plastic gets hot while her iron is in it, but I see no reason why it would melt or catch fire. I purposely tested it with her flat iron just sitting in the holder for 30 minutes, and while the plastic was hot to the touch (go figure her flat iron is set at 410 degrees ), it does not appear to be a safety or fire hazard.

My only complaint is that I cannot get the suction cups to stick to any smooth surface for more than 24 hours. I've tried smooth tile, the smooth granite counter, and the glass mirror for mounting surfaces. The suctions cups always fail within about a day no matter what I do to prepare the surface or the suction cups (i.e. rubbing alcohol, glass cleaner, soapy water, plain water). Once she figures out exactly how she likes it positioned and uses it that way for a while, I'll probably end up using the included anchor and screw to mount it to the wall for her.

Give this product about four weeks to see any real results. Retinol products take months of use to see any impact on deeper issue like lines and wrinkles. text:
I bought the 8040x a couple of days ago and even I am surprised at how impressed I am with the shaver. I have always been a reader of reviews on Amazon and this is but my second review. This product makes me want to recommend it to everyone I see. Wow!! First, let me tell you about the shavers I have had.

My past shavers: I have had a Braun Synchro (lost with luggage on an international trip), a Norelco Reflex that I absolutely hated (but still hung on to for emergencies) and a Braun Activator 8595 (with Clean N Charge station) that I had till recently and absolutely loved. My Braun Activator (which I had for the past 3 years) broke when it slipped from my hand last week. Hence, I was in the market for a new shaver and thought I will research the shavers available since I was going to spend some money.

My new 8040X: I used my old Norelco Reflex for a week on a temporary basis till I bought a better model and absolutely hated it. It made my skin all red. As I was researching I came across the 8040X on Amazon and was intrigued by the idea of a wet shaver (having used only foil dry ones thus far). I tried it out in the shower for the past couple of days and I must say it has absolutely blown me away. It is so convenient, and the smoothest shave I have had in several years (as good as a Mach 3 shave that I stopped years ago). My wife was super impressed and to quote another review on this site....my cheeks AND I MUST EMPHASIZE even my neck, chin feel like "Baby's bottoms". The lotion that comes along with the shaver is awesome and goes along really well with the Nivea after shave lotion that I was already used to. Cleaning is a breeze...just hold it under water and run the motor for 30 secs. No more Clean and Charge Refills (boy are they expensive)

For the past several years I have been held hostage by the Braun company consumables (Clean and Charge solutions). It is a great relief that I found a shaver that wont hold me hostage like that, save for a little bit of moisturizing lotion that goes in the shaver (you dont really need a lot if you shave in the shower or by the sink). I am planning on buying one each for both my brothers as well as my father in law. Wonderful shaver and very well worth the money.

I have no intention of returning this shaver (I bought it thinking that I will try it for 3 weeks). Go out and buy this model, save your money and do not buy the 8060...dispensing the lotion into the shaver is really easy.

I will try and refresh this review in the next few weeks.

AS PROMISED ---- UPDATED APRIL 2008 --- AFTER 6 WEEKS OF USE

It has been at least 5-6 weeks since I bought the shaver and not surprisingly, I have not returned it to Philips. This is a great shaver. I have tried using it in the shower as well at the sink.

After having read complaints about the cost of consumables that come with this shaver, I decided to put it to the test. I began by trying Edge shaving gel prior to shaving with terrible results. It resulted in a very sticky shave....not good at all. I then decided to try a small travel pack of Nivea shaving gel.... and believe it or not....it worked like a charm....as good as the shaving conditioner. Apply a very small amount and do not lather it up vigorously...just a thin film.

Here is what I do nowadays..... I apply very little of the Nivea shaving GEL (not conditioner) and apply gently, do not lather up heavily. I use the shaver with little or no conditioner and it works just as well either in the shower or at the sink. Very little irritation and smooth effective shave. Also, applying the gel on your face prior to shaving prevents spraying of debris on and around your basin.

If there is anything I do not like about this shaver, it is the power and speed of the motor. While I cannot attest or comment on previous Coolskin models, that I have never owned, I can say that I can live with the power and speed of this shaver for several reasons. It is smooth, does not irritate your skin (which is extremely important for me after having experienced other shavers and razors) and easy to use. Go get one and if possible try getting it at one of your local stores like Bed Bath Beyond or Linens n things with a 20% off coupon.

title: Read before you buy...
text:
-I’ve used lots of their products…and I always got compliments, but the final straw was their deplorable customer service. I figure if this is how I’m treated, then they most-assuredly treat all the other paying customers in the same exact manner. They wanted my opinion (not kidding – they really asked) so not only did I respond honestly, but I asked a question. Asked repeatedly. Rather than professionally answer my question, effectively teaching one customer at a time - waiting and waiting and waiting and waiting, continuing to ask. Ha, they tried to give me free products, and I refused them. I Just. Wanted. An. Answer - and not to be ‘bought off’, thinking that they were hiding behind emails, with no individual names, but ‘Team’ this and Team that. This may be a plausible solution for some, but not me. What an unequivocally repulsive way to treat a faithful and paying customer.

-I’m not sure what changed, but Lisa Crary (CEO and owner) used to care. Used to have great staff. Used to respond to questions. But certainly not now. The products are acceptable enough, but expensive, purchasing from retailers (I grew sick of the ridiculous price mark-up) as well as directly from Sanitas. Even directly from the manufacturer, still pricy, but shipping was too inconsistent.

-I’ve used FIVE cleansers (Glycolic Citrus, Enzyme Foaming, Milk & Honey, Lemon Crème Scrub, Lemon Crème Cleanser) seven types of treatment products (Brightening Peel Pads, Glyco Solution, PeptiDerm Eye, Essential Eye Essence, Hyaluronic Concentrate and the Serum, AHA kit, Retinol Peeling Crème, RejuvenA) three moisturizers (Topical C, Antioxident moisturizer, Vitamin C moisturizer) and three types of masks (Cranberry Lactic, Papaya Pineapple, Pumpkin Enzyme). Also, a few of the body products (Redensifying Lip Complex, Hydrating Sugar scrub, Brightening Hand cream, Foot Repair) and serums (Vita Rich, Vita C) just to try. The body stuff I positively hated, but I tried them none-the-less, since I *was a loyal customer. That’s just from memory, and there’s likely more. Oh, and their sunscreen. No one could tell me when it would be available again. The Moisture Mist too.

-Pppfffttt, the money I have spent with that line of skin care. The super weird expiration code nearly drove me nuts, but I finally deciphered it with lots of research and phone calls over time. Some of the numbers don’t mean anything, but the letters are the most crucial – indicating the year produced.
-To refrain from giving Sanitas any more of my money, I purchased online from that *huge retailer that starts with an a, that always ships so quickly – and got a few expired products. Good thing the return policy is incredibly stellar, however my time was still wasted. Well, I admit that’s on me.

-The packaging is nothing short of a nightmare, trying to get all the product out of the container being impossible, equaling a waste of money. Some of these products are in a pump style, in which case not all of the pumps even function. Of course, I called… they just didn’t care. I wish I’d save pictures, but anger forced me to toss it.

-Get this! Some of the spas, dermatologists, and estheticians that carry the Sanitas line will *sell to customers the free products given to them by the manufacturer to further promote their line. The audacity of such is so incredibly offensive, and Sanitas should have removed their products from those retailers – but they didn’t do anything of the kind, because they didn’t care. I can easily say I’m over them, and others should be very cautious.

-*Maybe what I have read on ‘job sites’ (where employees give their personal opinions about their employers, working conditions, work to life balance, management, wages, etc.) is unquestionably true, but it definitely can’t be good for the quality of products. *Maybe that’s the reason for the change. Whatever is the reason, I’ll never *ever use that skincare line again…

…and instead switched to a skin care line from the Far East. Don’t waste your time and money. Know this - there’s better products out there.

text:

I check to make sure that there is no separation and that the blending still holds. It is still the way it should be. I then rubbed it into my feet, and put on my shoes and socks. I have had it on for about 4 hours now. I took off my shoes and socks and checked my feet. They are much softer then this morning.
This means that this is a good product, and does just what it should.
I am disabled and I always leave a review on products I purchase/receive. Whether good or bad, I am always honest. It makes me feel like I am productive again. And I would hate for someone to purchase something bad and waste money if I didn't say something.
But I can assure you that this is a good coconut oil.

title: Patience wins and you will get nice nails
text: i rarely write reviews. but felt the need to write one for this producd. I have tried a few different products for my nails, dipping powder, pink and white powder like they do in the salons, and now this product. this one was by far the easiest and my nails came out great. as long as you follow the instructions you will be fine. It comes with 3 builders, clear, white and pink. I used the clear then one coat of pink and it was close to looking like a natural nail. you can clean the builder brush with rubbing alcohol and it comes clean very easily. the fibers are a little finicky and will lean forward off your finger sometimes because of the weight of the purple end. I just added a little more builder, pressed with the bent tweezers and propped the purple end up a little. everything dries very quickly under the lamp although the legs for the lamp don't want to stay up and it falls down a lot. the fibers are difficult to cut, when you cut them they spread out so they cut at weird angels. I would recommend having some sort of vacuum running as this IS fiberglass, so fibers made from glass and they will get stuck in your clothes and in your fingers and it is uncomfortable. overall the process was a little slow but the result is amazing. I have issues with my hands shaving when using fine motor skills, think Parkinson's type shaking, I have learned to use the shaking to my advantage but even with the shaking I got beautiful nails. I also ordered the silk fiberglass sheets and am going to try them next time.

This is the only polish I will use from now on.

title: The better ones, Soapwalla (my previous favorite)
text:
Over the past year and a half, I've been searching for a non-commercial deodorant that would work for me. Due to formulation changes over the past 10-15 years, it has gotten to a point where I can only use around 3 different commercial deodorants that do not cause chemical burns to my pits with long use. I've used many other popular and not so popular alternatives and haven't found that "perfect" product yet. The better ones, Soapwalla (my previous favorite), Piper Kai, and Primal Pit Paste, all cause serious irritation after 2-4 weeks and I discovered that baking soda and some essential oils cause serious irritation and eventually makes my pits raw which causes my skin to peel away. I've recently retried some Soapwalla I had for a pinch and it actually caused my pits to severely break out only one day (which surprised me). Evidently, my sensitivity to baking soda has increased over the past year.
I've used this Fat and The Moon deodorant for 2.5 weeks now and am very pleased with it. It only causes some minor bumps under my pits which is really good for me since these aren't getting worse. This is a deodorant, not an antiperspirant, so I do sweat a lot. However, I've noticed that even after exercise I'm not very stinky. With most of the other deodorants I've used, workout stank is always a problem. A couple have actually intensified the stank by adding their own. Not so here.
The only cons I have with this product so far are that I do notice it can stain some shirts with oil discoloration, but so far have been treatable. (I've used products that have stained shirts MUCH worse to where it wasn't treatable.) The other con I have about this is the smell. I'm a guy and I'm okay with this scent, but sometimes it's a bit too "earthy" smelling for me. I might even go for an unscented version of this if that is possible.

But even with the cons, I do like this product and I'm going to reorder this deodorant in the full 2 ounce size.

text:
This is my second scrub with this company. The first was great, but I find that the fragrance is too much for me with this Honey one. These products do contain "parfum" as an added ingredient, but it is last on the list. I have included a picture of the ingredients as I do not see the list anywhere else. My other salt scrub by this company-bloodorange, and that scent is wonderful and fresh, in bottle, in shower, and on skin after (very light). This one is just heavy, rather perfume like. I have noticed some shea containing products have that, but the other one that I do like has shea as well but isn't cloying. So I don't know. I'm afraid it might trigger a headache for me. I may have to have someone else in the household finish it off. Love the other one I mentioned, though!

As for how it works- no problem. A thick frosting like creamy texture with a hint of grit. It does a nice job cleaning, polishing, and leaving the skin feel smooth and moisturized. It is a gentle scrub- very gentle. Definitely softens skin. I scoop out a generous 1/8-1/4 cup amount to use on my body. With that amount, I expect several uses from this squat container. I particularly like this one for my legs and feet as they are the most neglected in terms of skin care.

I really do like Natural Soultion salt scrubs, and it appears that there are 4 kinds. This one based solely on the fragrance is a miss for me, but another one happened to be a hit for me, which I will continue to use as needed.

EDIT: While a whiff from the container is too strong for me, the actual aroma in the shower continues to be pretty tame. It dawned on me to smell my skin after showering (something I didn't do with prior showers prior to initial review), and my skin doesn't have that strong smell that I note from the container. It smells pleasant and light, and I wanted to come back to say so.SO I just wanted to say that I haven't had a headache, and I don't actually smell like the scent from the container- I was concerned I would have that perfume smell. It isn't there, thankfully.

I'd boost it to a 5 rating, but the product descriptions says, "No Artificial Fragrances Or Perfumes", and "parfum" is on ingredient list- and doesn't say where that is derived from.

title: Really Excellent for Waves & Curls
text:
I have long hair that's wavy to curly, in layers. It's not kinky, is very thick, and is about average in terms of coarseness-- neither course nor fine. It is prone to frizz, and I live in the South where it is very humid.

Finding a product I like is a challenge, but I really do love this one. In the shower, I wring my hair out, then apply the product--a quarter-sized dollop, then comb it through with a wet shower comb to re-wet as directed. After applying, I often end up wrapping my hair in a towel after I get out so my hair isn't soaking, and I have not noticed this affecting my outcome. In an hour, I've got a head full of soft, shiny curls. There's no frizz, no tangles, no flaking, and no stickiness. And you've got volume at the roots-- no slicked down, weighed down, crunchy roots!

The best part is the next day or two. If I twist my hair up in a bun and go to sleep, I will get a different look in the morning-- looser waves, still soft and touchable without the greasy roots or weird stiff hair that other products give you. I love a product that doesn't require a daily do-over.

I started out with the 2 oz size to try out (I'm jaded when it comes to hair products), but I will be moving up to the 32 oz now-- that's how much I like it!

text: I was concerned this builder gel would be difficult to work with based only on how runny it looks in the product pix.  In real life it looks runny and sticky, but is surprisingly easy to work with.  After applying a long bead of the gel with the included brush, I pushed the gel to my desired shape, and then let it self level to smooth itself out. In fact, if I tried to get the shape perfect with the brush, the gel got stickier and messier, so I quickly learned to let the gel smooth itself out.  Tip: once you get your shape all smoothed out, turn your nail upside down and let gravity create a natural apex before popping it under the lamp. So far I’ve only used the clear gel.  I created on extension (not shown), attached rhinestones to several pride nails, and fully encapsulated a fully covered rhinestone nail.  1 thick layer of this hard gel and a have encased rhinestones that fully cured in just over 2 minutes!  I also plan to use this for simple overlays when my nail need additional support.  The sticker nail forms work well, the slip solution is good for clean up work (not shaping the gel), and the brush/spatula tool work as expected. After a few trial and error rounds of doing glue-on nails, I learned to choose the nail that is the size smaller than the size you think is right (it spreads flat after it’s glued and then this also saves your cuticles). Also use a very small amount of glue. Even if you think it’s too little, it’s probably too much. It’s much easier to glue a nail back on than to deal with dried glue all over your cuticles and between your nail and finger skin. Also rubbing alcohol takes the excess glue off if you do have issues.

Also! Big tip - start with your pinky nails first. Do both pinkies, both rings, both middles, etc. Your thumbs are very useful in the application process so it’s best to do them last.

2. Make up enhancer -- If you want that dewy look and don't want to spend a fortune at sephora, ulta or department store make-up counters...add this to your arsenal. On the first night I had 56 extensions loose and sliding out. I then had to go pay to have another box installed. FIFTY SIX.

Problem #3- the ends of the extension (closest to your scalp) are frayed edges. Instead of being keratin bonded and smooth, they are like little brooms of sharp hairs that constantly itch your scalp. I mean, insanely uncomfortable.

I attempted to contact the seller. She stated she would send me a new pack of beads to try. She never sent them. It wouldn't have mattered anyway because she has clearly never seen the product or she would realize that you can't use a new microbead with these as here is literally no way to get the old, broken bead off.

These were purchased for approximately $325. I spent another $300 to have them installed. $625 to have them in for less than a week. If you want to spend over $600 for a week of slipping extensions, then these are for you.

title: My skin went from dry/dehydrated to oily after using this toner 😔
text:
The sedum extract in this essence was quite intriguing to me. As someone with chronically dry, sometimes dehydrated skin I thought this toner could help me. "Sedum is a succulent leaf known for its intense hydration, vitamins & mineral level. It holds more hydration than watermelon and is rich in phytoestrogen that further boosts hydration and improves the skin condition." When I read that, I thought this sounded like the recipe for perfect skin, but every time I use this essence my face turns super oily. I have never experienced this kind of change from any of the hydrating essences I own.

The scent on this is light, clean, and fresh, very herbal. You should be aware that this product is fragranced with natural fruit oils & extracts. A few minutes after application though, the scent dissipates quickly. My skin is crazy reactive & very sensitive, but I did not experience any adverse reactions to the ingredients used in this essence.

There was also a generous amount of samples from Celimax included with this toner. 😀 They sent 2 Noni ampoules, 3 serum packettes, and 2 AHA/BHA exfoliating/brightening pads (labeled for underarms, but can be used elsewhere). Korean brands are so very gracious with samples! Thank you, Celimax! ❤

Both the package & bottle both come safety sealed. The bottle is of nice size (150ml) and features a shaker style spout for easy dispensing. I pour a small amount of the essence into my hands, then pat into the skin after cleansing. Then I apply my serums & moisturizer.

Though I don't find this product to be a particularly good fit for my skin right now (during the hot & humid Florida summer heat, when my oil production is already at it's peak), I think this essence may work better for me in the winter. I do think it's a nice product, so it still gets a 4 star rating from me.

title: Nice but could be made better
text:
This roller does indeed turn applying skin care products into a spa experience. Pop this baby in the fridge on hot summer days as a way to take your skin from tired to taut. Warm it up to help your skin absorb products more easily. It washes clean and doesn't absorb any of the products. The trouble comes from how it's put together. The metal caps that hold the rollers on each end of the wand/handle come off too easily. They aren't glued or crimped on, nor are the little metal caps snug fitting. Both ends where off when my roller arrived so I actually thought I had to assemble everything prior to each use. If I hold the roller up to where it's straight up and down, the roller that is facing the floor slides right off the handle. In a way this isn't a completely horrible thing since being able to disassemble the roller works better for travel. Just please be careful when opening your storage bag and pulling out the roller in case yours is the same way. If it were to fall onto a hard enough surface from a high enough height, the rollers could crack or shatter.

Aside from the poor craftsmanship, I do enjoy using this roller and not only for applying skincare products. Sticking the roller in the freezer for 20 minutes then using it on my face and neck when I am suffering from a migraine is a godsend. I recommend having two so that you can use one to battle your headache while the other one cools down. The rollers hold cold (or heat) for several minutes, and can be wonderful tools to help relieve pain from stuffed up sinuses as well as headaches. The little gua sha tool that is included is also wonderful for more than applying skin care products. Chilling the gua sha before use can help treat puffy eyes, headaches, small bruises, mosquito bites, foot massages, and so on. Both this and the roller are completely smooth - no rough edges or bumps.

Also included are a black velvet bag for storage, a handy booklet showing how to use both the roller and gua sha, and a hand written note thanking me for my purchase which is a really sweet gesture. All-in-all the tools are nice products, but for the price you'd think the manufacturers could afford glue to keep the rollers on the handle.

title: A Must Have, REALLY!  Buy It!!!
text:
Just so you know, I have seen the original version of this glove for awhile & have been extremely skeptical about how useful it could be. It looked silly to me even with one thumb, LOL! However, I am coming off of two arm and hand surgeries back to back (right & left ) & all my brushes were extremely dirty and I was dreading washing them like the plague. (I'm still recovering so my hands & arms are only at 80% strength) I ran across this new version & watched the video on Sigma's site and thought I would try it out because I really needed something to make this easier right now.

I have many brushes including a bunch of big dense ones like the SigMax brushes. I loath the chore of washing my brushes. I do it less often than I should. My hands become prunes, I wreck my nails and it takes for-like-ever! Plus, I can never seem to get the big dense ones clean enough deep in the center no matter how long I stand there and try to wash them.

Today I used this brush cleaning glove and HOLY FRIGGIN' MOLY!!! It's next level stuff!

It was so EASY to DEEPLY clean all my brushes in a FRACTION of my normal time. My dense brushes have never been this clean. It was an actual pleasure to wash them! Never thought I would ever say that.

Do not get an imitation. I saw those & thought about saving some money but in the end bought this glove. They really designed this to actually do all the work for you AND save your hands & nails. It is well thought out.

All the different areas have a very useful purpose that do all the work. You need all the different areas. The area where you shape your brush at the end actually also squeezes out all the excess water from even those dense SigMax brushes. They felt 50% dry right after washing! I'm sure they will dry faster than ever. The terry inner glove made the whole silicone glove experience really nice and cozy. Your hand is comfortable all during the washing & after. None of that sweaty, sticky feeling you can get with rubber gloves. My hand was completely dry even after about 30 brushes!

I like this new design, with the 2 thumbs, because you can always use your dominant hand to hold the brush. With one thumb you would have to switch hands to use the other side of the glove. One side is for face/larger brushes & the other is for eye/smaller brushes.

I use Dr. Bronner's Castile Liquid Soap in the Baby Mild formula. Get yourself a pump dispenser & mix half soap and half water in the dispenser. Having the pump helps speed along the washing process as you just pump the soap onto the center cleaning area of the glove. You never have to put down the brush you are cleaning. This also helps keep the brush aimed down helping you not get water running up into the ferrule by accident as you work.

This glove also makes it easy to know, just by sight, when your brush is completely clean, soap foam is white, and completely rinsed, no foam comes out of your brush when swirled after rinsing.

My brushes are thoroughly deep cleaned for the first time in ages. They look brand new!

If you have a bunch of brushes or even if you don't have that many but have some of the big dense ones, think of this glove as an investment. It will help you preserve the life of your brushes and keep bacteria off your face, yuck.

It is really well made and should last a really long time. They only thing I could see happening is replacing the inner glove as it is terry cloth.

I LOVE this and will happily be washing my brushes all the time now. My face, hands & nails are all going to benefit.

title: Excellent hand cream
text:
UPDATE - 09/30/16 ========================================
Still loving this moisturizer and just ordered another package. This stuff goes on well, absorbs quickly into the skin and doesn't leave a greasy feeling! My skin feels truly moisturized. I love using it on my hands and feet before bedtime, this way it really absorbs into my skin overnight.
Love it, love it, love it!

========================================================
Not many people know this, or give it another thought sometimes - anything you put on your skin gets absorbed through the skin and ends up in the blood stream. This is why I am rather careful when picking my skin care products. I have been staying away from most hand creams for a while now just because for the most part there's at least a few potential carcinogens lurking among the ingredients. Even though the big famous brand creams make your skin feel wonderful the question is if the trade off is worth it.

Unfortunately, even so called organic products aren't always that safe. Provided, manufacturers of this goodness are disclosing all the ingredients on the label (and not hiding anything) this cream looks safe enough to eat. Therefore, I have been happily slathering it all over my hands (and any other body parts needing additional moisture) in the past few weeks and I am quite pleased with the results.

This white fluffy goodness feels surprisingly light and absorbs quickly into the skin. I must admit, it is a tad thinner in texture than I had expected but on the other hand this lightness ensures there's no oily residue left on your hands. The cream has no scent whatsoever which is a definite positive for those who are sensitive or don't particularly appreciate scented products. I'm adding a drop of essential oil of my choice (whatever I feel like that day) when I apply the cream if I feel like smelling something nice. Basically this cream is your blank canvas and leaves much room for creativity.

One thing I would probably change about this product is the packaging. (At least maybe as an option for buyers to choose from) I really think that tubes are better for hand creams - way easier to dispense and so much more hygienic (sticking your fingers into the container doesn't really help keep it germ free). Other than that I am happy to give this product my approval.

I purchased this product at a discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased review, all opinions are based on my own personal experience with the product.

I needed to try something. Arrived in a timely manner; 2 days sooner than initially quoted. Instructions are easy enough. I washed and dried my feet, then put these bad boys on. Recommended time is for 50-90 minutes; longer for feet more in need (my heels are so cracked and flakey I wasn’t about to have photographic evidence). I was aiming for 90 minutes. I massaged them around in my feet to ensure that the product was all over. At about 80 minutes I started noticing a tingling and so rinsed the product, as described, to avoid any sensitivity or rashes. And that was that. Day 1: no noticeable difference. Day 2: The skin on my feet is noticeably tight. The left foot has very slight flaking around the toes and the right foot has a spot starting to obviously peel. Took a shower, no extra attention to the feet other than regular wash and now there is obvious peeling on both feet. Day 3: noticeable itchiness and more peeling to be had on the soles of my feet. Day 4: Ok, this peeling is gross! Holy smokes, everything is peeling it even feels like the tops of my feet may start peeling. Day 5: OMG all the peeling. Day 6: Peeling has calmed down on the bottom of the foot and around the toes but the tops of the feet haven’t started at all but it looks and feels like it is going to. Day 7: I cheated. I soaked my feet and gave them a very light pumice scrub to get the skin from the tops of my feet off and to touch up a dry patch on one heel. Final verdict: totally worth it. Recommendations: After reading through use and reviews of other similar products, I would recommend soaking your feet every day. It may help avoid the issue I had with the skin on the tops of my feet.

title: Not ideal for very pale skin, but usable
text:
For the record, I am a longtime Physicians Formula wearer, and their products can be hit or miss. I am not being paid to leave a review, or representing anyone but myself here. This is the first time I tried PF's countouring powder, and I've used it for about three seasons. I like it. I don't love it.

I have very pale skin with pink undertones that is uber-sensitive and I have to be very careful about sun exposure. Anything can make me break out in hives or eczema, at any time, even if I used it daily for years. Thankfully, PF products have never done that to me, in almost a decade.

As for this product, the shades are where I take some issue. They worked best for my tone in summer, but now, in winter -- I'm shopping for a different product.

* The dark shade is really mahogany-like, so I have to blend, blend, blend in daylight or risk looking like I smeared mud on my face. It's good for shading jawline and cheekbones with a light touch at temples if you need it. Beware, though. If you are very pale, you want a very light touch with this one.

*The medium shade is very subtle and helps blend and soften the dark. It also works well as a matte bronzer, around sides of the nose, and wherever you need just a little definition. This is the best shade of the bunch, honestly. At least for my skin tone.

* The light shade is, frankly, worthless to me. It gives my skin a pasty, chalky look and looks heavy. Yuck. I occasionally use it in tiny spots as a concealer, but as a contour powder, it just looks like I put on way too much setting powder or something. Instead, I use my lightest shade of matte eyeshadow (also a PF product) and a higher-end illuminator for highlighting. Those results are beautiful, frankly, even on my 38 year old skin.

All in all, PF's contour colors are suitable for pale skin, but may be better on other slightly darker or warmer skin tones, or on summer tanned skin.

title: Not Great for Thick/Wavy Hair. Pretty & OK for Touch-Ups
text:
My whole life I've needed to use a hair straightener. I have very thick strands of hair and a lot of it. Plus, my hair is poofy crazy curly. My hair used to be down to my butt, however, this past year I had to cut it all off due to getting a horrid matted mess. (If you don't know what it means to have matted hair - your lucky). It was a whole bunch of tears, pain, tantrums, home remedies, a ton of hair salon visits and a ton of money spent until realizing that I was s*** outta luck and had to cry as they cut my hair to only an inch in the back, but luckily had enough hair left / saved on top and on sides for shoulder length hair. So now more than ever, having short hair that's very thick and curly, I'm always looking for amazing hair straighteners and products in general.

I have wanted one of these heat and style brushes and finally decided to test this one out. I loved the color of this heat brush and it looked like a nice, high quality hair straightening brush in the images.

This brush has less options then I thought it would. I cannot control the temperature and I would like for it to get a little bit hotter. Since I have curly, wavy hair this doesn't heat up enough to get it straight. Or maybe it's not doing a great job because it doesn't have two "plates" like regular straighteners. If I straighten my hair with a flat iron, this is a great touch up tool for the days following the flat iron before I wash my hair again. SO - It does work, but it is NOT a miracle product. This hair straightening brush (& all brush type of straighteners) MIGHT work better / work faster / have better results if you have thin hair? Just a assumption.

One difference I noticed was the way my hair felt after styling with the Envy brush. When I use my flat iron, my hair is...flat. The flat iron leaves my hair very smooth but it doesn't seem to have much texture or body left after straightening. When I used the Envy brush, my hair was straight, but still had plenty of volume. I'm really happy I bought the Envy styling brush. I really like the volume my hair has after using this brush.

I had to completely comb through my hair to smooth it out before using this brush (obviously). I started out by just running the Envy brush through my hair. Once I was done brushing my hair, I sectioned off my hair for the best results. I sectioned off the top 2/3 of my hair, twisted and secured it to the top of my head. As always, I focused on the underside first. When I finished the under layer, I moved on to the middle section, and then the top. The whole process took me about 20minutes. Pretty close to the same amount of time that it takes me to use my regular flat iron.

An ion is as an atom in which the number of electrons and protons are not the same. When a hair tool has ionic in its name, it means that it can generate negative ions. Hair has high water content, making it positively charged. When negative ions come in contact with hair, the positive charge is neutralized. This leaves your hair straight, sleek, shiny and smooth.

Here is one crucial thing to keep in mind – not all flat irons are pure ceramic, many of them are aluminum. They are just coated with ceramic on the top. Such models are less expensive, but you need to be extra careful when using them. This coating can chip or peel, revealing less quality metal below. These peeled areas can snag your hair! So always try to find out if an iron is coated or not.
You can even find costly professional models that are not 100% ceramic. Solid or pure ceramic are words that you are looking for.

I'm not sure if this brush is ceramic, titanium or what..?!?

Titanium vs. Ceramic
In this battle, it is obvious that titanium is a winner. But does this mean that you should use only this type of iron? No. Many experts say that consumers should use ceramic for one obvious reason. Since titanium can get very hot and transfers heat better, it’s very easy to damage your hair if you are not careful. Also, this high heat is only advantageous for women with thick, coarse and stubborn hair. If your have thin or fragile hair, there is no need for high temperatures. In the end, it is up to you to find out what will work best for your hair. Now you have all the facts to make the right decision. If you are still indecisive, there is a simple solution! Get a flat iron that combines ceramic and titanium, such as Croc 2 Infrared mentioned above. This way you get ceramic’s safety and protection and titanium’s speed and efficiency.

title: Moisturizing eye cream, irritates my picky skin
text:
UPDATE: I have reduced my rating to three stars after more use. This cream turned out in the longer term to irritate my eyes, make them swollen, red, and painful. It's in good company though; I have found that everything designed to be an eye cream to help skin health and appearance has irritated my eyes (this is one of four products that have recently had the same effect). So while I cannot personally recommend this cream, my experience of it may be far from universal. I did like how it felt going on, and actually liked the jasmine scent.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (4 stars): The Penebella Brighten & Repair Eye Cream includes a lot of ingredients that are really good for your skin: retinol, hyaluronic acid, aloe, and Vitamin E, among others. It does also contain jasmine essential oil, which is an odd choice to me. I am sensitive to scents, and to floral scents in particular, but this jasmine does not bother me at all, which is surprising. I actually find it to be subtle and pleasant, but nonetheless would not choose to have any fragrance added to a product meant for some of your most sensitive skin around your eyes. It strikes me as unnecessary at best.

This cream does feel light and moisturizing. The very fine needle nose dispenser makes it easy to get precisely the amount of product you intend, which is important when using relatively small amounts of relatively expensive products. I haven't ever ended up with more product than I intended or could use well for application.

When I began using this product, the skin around my eyes were swollen and sensitive from the dry winter air and indoor allergies. After about a week of consistent use, my eyes still feel swollen and sensitive. Honestly, the much simpler, cheaper basic lotion I have for my eyes relieves that feeling better. However, this cream has ingredients that make it better for long term use and improvement. So I will continue to use it and appreciate it for the anti-aging effects, but won't rely on it for daily relief from irritated eyes. If using it longer affects my judgment of this, I will update my review accordingly.

I've been using this for well over a decade, as my go to curl activator. I agree that it blows everything else out of the water. The secret is to dip a fingertip in, and just get a dab, a small dab. Rub your hands together again, to move what's left to your fingers, then run them through a little. Apply Curl Keeper (Original) or a gel lightly. Then scrunch. Correct your part, if necessary. title: Probably performs as advertised
text:
I tried it out on my legs as shown in the marketing image and video. The surface of the product is like a fine silicone sandpaper, and it creates some not-uncomfortable friction against the skin as you vigorously rub in the area you want to eliminate hair from. I saw only minimal results with light rubbing so I rubbed up and down as shown in the video with more pressure until it became uncomfortable. I don't have a high pain tolerance, so it is entirely possible someone else with a higher one would be able to rub harder. As it was, I saw better results with this increased pressure, but it still only got about 1/3 of the hair from my leg, which is pale and thin with about 5 days' growth. My skin turned red temporarily, and I did end up having to shave per usual to achieve total hair removal. The product did not feel like it was individually pulling hairs out, so no sharp pain was involved, but ultimately I didn't like the sensation that would likely have been necessary to achieve results as pictured. I also tried this on my arm with similar results.
The product is easy to hold and aesthetically pleasing. It does work, but may require too much discomfort for the average person to negate the need for other hair removal methods.

title: Good razor
text:
I've used the Arcitec 1050 for about 3 months and like it with a few caveats. The shave is a good, close shave. Most days I shave as soon as I stumble out of bed at 4:30AM, without so much as washing my face. The shave is good, stubble starts to show by late afternoon. The days I shower first, 12 hours later it is like I just shaved. I am getting 25 shaves per recharge, better than advertised.

As stated by Norelco, it took several weeks for the razor to be really comfortable. May not have helped that those first few weeks were very cold and dry. I have used a Norelco for 15 years, didn't expect to need the 3 week break in, but I did.

I am not thrilled that the razor has to be washed daily, but it is easy to do. However, it means the razor sits open drying most of the time which is no real problem, but annoys me. On the plus side, after 2 months I poured a little isopropanol in the cup I got with Norelco cleaner fluid 15 years ago, stuck the razor head in it and ran the 1050 for 30 seconds. Much easier than having the take all the heads out and swish them one at a time as with my old 7825. The shave improved too, so periodic thorough cleaning is (as with all Norelcos) a must.

The trimmer is fair. It's fine for sideburns, terrible for my mustache. I bought a mustache trimmer, which works much much better than any razor's trimmer. So maybe that the poor 1050 performance was a good thing.

My one big concern. The first 1050 I bought died after 18 shaves. Just would not turn on. Would not charge. I returned it to the store and exchanged it, and the second 1050 has had no problems. But there are more electronics in the Arcitec than in my car. I suspect that caused the failure. So I am concerned about the robustness of the design. Although electronics tend to die early, or last a long time.

Oh, and the shape is the easiest I've ever handled.

It is hard to find a moisturizer with skin healthy ingredients and suitable for my skin type. I enjoy this product immensely because it leaves me skin moisturized without the heavy residue most intense moisturizers do. After two straight weeks of using this moisturizer, I have concluded that it works every bit as well, or better than the name brands I have been paying more money for at the department store. This moisturizer leaves my skin comfortable, soft, and matte all day long. The scent is delightful in my opinion and I find myself terribly addicted to the wonderful aroma. Even though it feels light on the skin, it helps my makeup glide on smoothly with absolute moisture. It feels like it disappears as soon as it is rubbed in, and yet it keeps my skin perfectly balanced and moisturized all day without the shiny greasy looking. I especially need something to help my sensitive skin stay hydrated and soft. This moisturizer seems to have just the right formula for that purpose without causing any breakouts.

This facial moisturizer is rich and creamy. I really appreciate that this product is not greasy or sticky. When using this moisturizer, I can actually feel it sink into my skin pretty fast. It instantly makes my face feel very smooth and it soaks in rather quickly without leaving any uncomfortable residues. I have been using this cream twice a day and always making sure to cover my eyelids as well. It is so gentle for my sensitive skin that my skin does not itch or turn red. It is not greasy, but the coverage is thick enough to sufficiently provide moisture for night time. I do not like oily or sticky moisturizers, but I do prefer certain degree of a good moisturizing coverage. This is a very good face cream compared to many other brands of moisturizers that I have used not to mention the fact that it is made by skin healthy ingredients and botanical extracts.

I have only been using it for two weeks and I have noticed that my skin is starting to feel smoother and firmer. The tone of my skin also seems to be improving and I could not be more happier. This is a good facial moisturizer that I find perfect for my skin type during the day since it has helped my makeup look natural and smoother. title: My journey of finding my love in wooden brushes
text:
Before I came across this type of brush, I was using those typical plastic brushes that you would buy at the store--that was at least 3 years ago, if not, more than that. Eventually, I got tired of plastic brushes because of the way it pulls, the static that it creates, and worst of all, the way it made my hair smell. I can't stress this enough, no matter how nice smelling my shampoo is, my hair would smell unpleasant (I cannot describe), almost like plastic after it dried. And so, I made my first step to healthier hair by changing brushes; I discovered about the boar bristle brush, and bought one that I found at the store. It was fine, it made my hair soft, but was it life changing? Kind of, but I grew out of it. I liked how it made my hair feel, especially at the ends, however I could not comb from root to end, because my hair type is thick and I was not feeling the scalp massage. I even thought about saving my money for a Mason Pearson, and had it on my wishlist for a while. I found an affordable boar bristle brush, but I never bought it yet, as it sits in the wishlist.
Another problem I had with my hair is that it is unmanageable. Everytime I got out of the shower, I needed to brush my hair, no matter how unhealthy it is, I needed to. Otherwise, my hair is all tangled and I will be irritable (just kidding). Well, brushes do no justice, so I went with a detangler, I bought one at the store (once again) for about a couple dollars, and I have used it for a while. You could say, I was trying to be gentle to my hair, by starting at the ends and work my way up. For now, it was the only way to keep my hair at bay, and I still use the boar bristle brush to fix my hair a little.

Until recently, I succumbed to realizing how important hair is, and so I watched videos and videos of hair routines, until I came across holistichabit's video about her hair routine/how to get long healthy hair naturally. I kind of regretted now, not watching it when I first found her channel, but now I am obsessed about her ways of maintaining healthy hair. When she mentioned about using a wooden brush, I was almost confused, but was curious as how it benefitted her hair. Though the brushes she recommends were expensive, she did hint that Europeans make the best brushes. That is when I began my hunt for a reasonable priced, yet high quality and came across this aethethically pleasing brush. Since it was made in Germany, I had to put it at my highest priority; a few days later, I couldn't contain my impulses and just bought this brush.

TL;DR
At first use, I'm totally impressed with how it distributed my oils, and I really enjoyed that scalp massage: it's amazing. I will say, that you do not need to apply a lot of pressure to your scalp, as it massage just effectively. I decided that I should wait until I shower after, that I began using. Today came around, and first use on wet hair, I was literally blown away! I was just in awe at how soft it made my hair, and I had been waiting for this moment for my scalp massage. I LOVE EVERY SINGLE MOMENT OF THE SCALP MASSAGE! A few hours later, and my hair feels so soft, it's almost heavenly. My hair strands and ends feel evenly distributed with oil, however, I'm not sure if the back of my head feels greasy and chunky because I use a sulfate-free shampoo, and it happens almost every time. Another thing to add, my hair smells of oak/maple wood; maybe I'm just weird but I do not mind it, in fact I appreciate the smell. title: 2 of 3 have micro glitter (mica). Sticky but not too bad. Moisturizing
text:
These come in a nice little box. They are vegan and cruelty free. They are made in the USA. I included the ingredients at the end of my review.

You get 3 glosses - a peachy pink toned one that has a strawberry scent/flavor, a more reddish toned one that has a grape scent/flavor, and a clear one that has a bubble gum scent/flavor. As for the scents, I can notice them when applying, not so much after the fact. I don’t really notice a taste really with any of them, but the ingredients do list “flavor” not fragrance/parfum, so it made me think they’d have more taste to them. Not a big deal to me though.

While 2 of them are tinted in color, the color doesn’t really translate onto the lips. They just look clear on the lips. They don’t change any color of lip liner, lipstick, matte lip, etc. that I put them over top of. So, I liked that.

The formula is nice. It feels nice and moisturizing on the lips, which I expected given they have nice moisturizing ingredients like Shea butter, coconut oil, and squalane. They do feel SLIGHTLY sticky on the lips. I hate sticky glosses, but these aren’t overly sticky. They don’t feel thick or heavy on the lips. They feel nice and thin. They are glosses so they do need re-applied often throughout the day. But, I’m used to that with glosses so it’s not a big deal to me.

The strawberry and grape both have micro glitter in them (mica). I didn’t know that when I got these. None of the product photos showed they had glitter and the description didn’t say it either. I’m not a fan of micro glitter in my lip glosses. I feel once the gloss wears off, it usually leaves behind glitter particles on my lips. Also, they can sometimes feel gritty. So, I was surprised when I saw 2 of the 3 had glitter. Luckily, these didn’t feel gritty. I do notice that there are some glitter particles on my lips after they wear off, but it’s not too bad. The glitter particles are really small, so it’s not really noticeable. So, I don’t mind that.

Overall, these are nice glosses with a nice formula. They might seem pricey when seeing the $30 price tag, but you’re getting 3 tubes of glosses, so that’s only $10 a piece, which isn’t bad. Of course, it isn’t great. You can get a tube of gloss that looks great and works just as well from the drugstore for slightly less. But, the ingredients might make it worth it to spend the little more. I give them 4 stars.

title: Worst Adidas Shower Gel I've Ever Tried
text:
Let me start this review by saying that I normally really like Adidas' shower gels. I've tried almost every variety in their men's line and none of them have come close to offending me like Water Sport has. Right out of the bottle, this shower gel stinks. It has a very strong, bitter chemical aroma, and it makes me think of both bathroom cleaning solutions and a hair salon. I have no idea what's in this that combats the effects of chlorine, but I imagine this ingredient is to blame for the foul smell.

Using the product, it feels thicker than it looks and goes a long way, like other shower gels from Adidas. As soon as I started to wash my body with it, the fragrance quickly turned into a very heavy single note of burnt hair. It smelled so bad that I was immediately checking myself out to make sure it wasn't chemically singeing my body hair off. Fortunately that wasn't the case, but it really did smell that horrible. title: Lovely Deck With One Gripe
text:
I pre-ordered this deck months ago and after much anticipation, it was very well worth the wait.

I'm slowly going through the deck card by card. The packaging is nice,easy to take out without destroying the box. It also comes with a Spread Sheet. Literally. *snerk* A sheet which illustrates different spreads on the front and back. Very handy for beginners. The deck is roughly 2"x 4" and included are two extra quick reference cards -- one for the majors, the other for the minors. Nice touch. I wish all decks provided this.

My only complaint so far is they provided a 70pg. LWB. Nothing more. No large reference book with extensive background on the cards symobolgy, like they've done in the past with the Celtic Dragon and ShapeShifter decks. Kinda disappointed (hence the 4/5 stars). But if I wish to carry this deck around, a big book would be cumbersome I suppose.

HOWEVER, what is nice about the LWB is they provide a mythical background on the creature, a divinatory meaning, AND magickal use of the card. Nifty! Never have I seen the Magickal Usage option before in a tarot deck.

So, card by card, I'm taking in what I think the symbology means then reading the LWB and finding I'm fairly accurate. Either I'm getting
better at Tarot or the deck really syncs with me like the Celtic Dragon and Fey decks do (ShapeShifter is a more difficult one for me to grasp now, but I have faith in the future it will become quite the tool for me when I'm ready).

Lastly, and one of the reason why I love Lisa Hunt's decks, is the Wands/Air - Swords/Fire connection. Few decks represent that and I've always been more intuitively drawn to that way of thinking, even before my Tradition's teachings reflected the same.

If you are a fan of Lisa Hunt -- get this deck.
If you are a fan of mythology -- get this deck.
If you are a witch or tarot reader who is more connected to the Wands/Air, Swords/Fire -- get this deck.
If you are like me and need a reference card now and again (lol) -- get this deck.
