title: You get what you pay for
text:
Buyer beware!
Pros:
Packaging was great. Nothing spilled out or burst open. Colors are gorgeous.

Shipping was ok. I got a message basically saying shipping was delayed due to my error of not providing the right address, yet I ordered 4 items the same day and provided the same shipping address. They supposedly corrected the error and got it shipped to me in less than a week.

Now, let's talk about the cons:
I can't say this product is a true polygel. When using the slip solution or isopropyl alcohol, the solution dissipated and the brush dried out within seconds. Once I was able to start smoothing the product out, I got one good pat before the product became extremely sticky and unmanageable due to the brush drying out. It definitely took some finesse to get it to work. Also, do not use the dual forms as the product is not thick enough to hold it's own without moving under the light. If you have paper forms or nail tips, you will have much better luck with this product. I will say it definitely took me way too long to do one set but filing the product was great and so easy.

After trial and error, if you want to take the time to make it thicker, put some on a smooth flat surface and add clear acrylic. Make sure to use a metal spatula to mix the 2 products if you so choose to. Also, THIS PRODUCT IS VERY STICKY. If you are not careful, you will get this product everywhere.

I would give more stars if the polygel was a thicker constancy and the brush didn't dry out seconds after dipping into the slip solution or isopropyl alcohol.

I will give this kit a try again when it's time for me to change my set, but I'm not sure I will purchase this kit again.

When I bought this product, I received both the cell stimulating body wash and the facial cleansing creme and I feel differently about each product so I will write my review accordingly.

Body Wash (2/5 Stars):

I actually bought this because I needed a new body wash. I was hoping that the mint and argan oil would make my skin feel refreshed and very clean, but it really didn't. The body wash leaves a filmy sensation after I use it, and the mint scent/sensation does not pack the amount of power I was hoping for when I initially bought this item. I used the body wash for exactly one week before I put it in my cabinet to gather dust, as my back-up "I forgot to buy extra body wash" bottle. I really didn't like it much.

Facial Cleanse (4/5 Stars)

The facial cleanse was just the freebie that came with the body wash I wanted, so I wasn't really expecting to replace my usual face soap. I was so disappointed with the body wash, I almost didn't try it at all but I am glad I did. The facial cleanser delivered the minty sensation that I wish the body wash had. It was reinvigorating and made my skin feel both clean and fresh, without leaving any residue. I definitely have kept this product in my shower and would definitely consider buying it on its own because I enjoy how gently it cleans and how well it removes my make-up at the end of the day.

Overall, I rated it 3/5 Stars because of the average review of both products, but I will never buy the body wash again; the facial cleanser definitely made up for the purchase for me.

title: "Sea" Mist is a Misnomer
text:
*Sigh*
This product received rave reviews, so I was very excited to purchase and test it out.
My hair is naturally very wavy. If the wave doesn't have product, it isn't tame. So, most mornings I dry/straighten it to avoid looking like a wild banshee at work.
However, I recently moved to Florida and because of the humidity, my waves are being a bit more cooperative. That being said, a product like this that would help hold the wave throughout the day and tame the "wildness" is desirable. Unfortunately, this has not worked for me as it is advertised.
There isn't enough salt to hold the hair in place. Instead of a subtle stiffness to hold the 'beach wave', my hair appeared a droopy, greasy mess that looks like I'd slept in a frying pan (with leftover bacon grease) rather than the just-off-the-surf look that I was anticipating.
Everyone's hair is different, so perhaps this product works better for others. My hair is long and thick. I would think that this may work better for people with shorter hair where gravity isn't fighting with the product all day.
Okay, so why did I give this more than one star? IT SMELLS AMAZING! If anything, I'll be using this as a perfume rather than a hair product. Seriously, I can't get enough of the coconutty wonderfulness in the bottle.

title: Kiss has the best nails! Instructions on how to make them last 10-14 days!
text:
These nails are GORGEOUS!!

Do NOT use the sticky adhesive as they make the nails not last as long. Simply:
1. Push your cuticles back
2. File down your nails
3. Lightly file your nail bed so the glue has something a little rough to hang to, it’s always easier than putting glue and a nail on a smooth surface and makes them last much longer
4. Find the 10 nails that fit you and lay them down in the order of the fingers you will put them own (pink-ring-middle-index-thumb-thumb-index-middle-ring-pinky) - they have numbers on the underneath of the nail on the tip, remember those numbers or write them down because that’s likely your size in all Kiss nails (for example, I’m 12-10-7-8-3-3-8-7-10-12, the smaller the number the bigger the mail)
5. When you’re ready to apply, place glue on the bottom of the fake nail about 1/6 inch from the bottom to the middle of the nail and make sure it’s dispersed even - DO NOT put the glue directly on the nail bed, for longevity it works best to put it on the fake nail
6. Align with the appropriate finger and place down, holding for 5-10 seconds.
7. There may be a little glue that comes out on the sides. Be careful not to smudge that on the nail itself. Just take a paper towel and dab that little bit of glue up as you go
8. Once all nails are on, file how you need/want them and you are set for about 10 days.
9. I usually get a solid 2 weeks of wear out of mine! I use either these KGN10, the almond shaped wine, or I’ll do a French or natural French short length from Kiss.
10. Carry around an extra nail or two that may fit a couple different fingers for emergencies, the glue, and the nail file. If a nail pops off and it’s not a broken nail, simply file your nail bed again and apply glue to either a new nail that fits, or the one you popped off if it’s salvageable.

Enjoy!

title: Loved this product. (Yes, it's just a stippling brush, but better than DIY.)
text:
I can't rave enough about this product. I've had it for a couple months now, and I've used it with mostly eyeshadow, but all sorts of colors. It's removed them all pretty much instantly! I will say that the only problem with this is that it will probably make people forget that even though it's taking off the pigment, it's not removing bacteria and such, so you should probably still wash your brushes once or twice a month.

And yes. I know that it's just a stippling brush in a little can. So if you want to DIY it, I'm sure you could. I find this a lot more convenient than trying to spend an afternoon coming up with a copy of this. Part of its use is the can: the stippling part doesn't move around (well, it rotates a little) because it's contained in the can. So I just have it sitting in a corner of my makeup box, and I can just brush my brushes towards the inside corner, and it doesn't move. Alternatively, you could put some hot glue or silicone on the top face of the lid, so when you put the lid on the bottom (like the picture) and had it on your countertop, it wouldn't slide, either.

Anyways, love this product! Also works with bigger brushes. I'm wishing I'd bought the duo, though, because it's supposed to work with creme make up.

title: Look no further you found your brush
text:
I had been thinking about getting a new brush for a while. I have had an Oral-B Sonicare for about 4 years. It still works, but I had been thinking there may be something better with the advance of technology the last few years. The Sonicare brush vibrated from side to side, which I have always like much better than the brushes that rotate in a circle so I was very nervous about giving this brush a shot. All I can say is, WOW!

This brush is amazing. The Sonicare never seem to brush hard enough, whereas the top setting on this brush is exactly what I hoped it would be. I was also always a bit confused how firm I should hold the brush against my teeth and the 4000 series essentially makes that dummy proof as a giant red light comes on when you are pressing to firm.

The best comparison I can make is to describe this as the cordless version of the brush your dentist uses. It's that swirling brush that leaves your teeth feeling like you just left Dr. Dental's office each day. For folks that don't like as firm or rough a brush, there's enough settings to tone it down, but I have found that most brushes don't have a setting firm enough rather than delicate enough. This brush solves that problem.

I read some complaints about the handle, the charger, etc. I can't imagine why people could even complain as it's the last thing I would notice nor do I think either are a problem. The charging stand is nice and you can remove the holding case that attaches to it if you're worried about counter space. You also get a nice travel case, which is a huge plus because every time I took my sonicare on vacation, I would have to bring it with my carry on or else the on button would also get pushed in the suitcase and end up basically dead by the time I arrive.

I had a tough time justifying buying a new brush when I had one that worked fine. I couldn't be happier I took a chance as I firmly believe this brush will leave me much healthier teeth. I have to believe the Oral-B brand will last as my brush from 4 years ago is still going strong.

What a great buy.

title: not the perfect shaver
text:
I have been using Philips/ Norelco shavers for the past 12 years; and for the past 5 years, I have been using the 8894 model. for no good reason, I wanted a change and assumed that the new Philips Norelco 1090 would be more improved than the 8894.
I was wrong.
These are the highlights of the 1090 in comparison to the 8894
1. Louder.
2. less power; 65 minutes verses 100 minutes
3. the shave is not better; practically the 8894 shaves closer.
4. Plastic casing; 8894 had a leather travel case.
5. Slightly lighter than the 8894.
6. All the 10 series, rate the same
Bottom line if you have been using the 8894 and want a change; my advice is stick to your old shaver and save the money. If you are buying a new shaver, go for the 7810 instead, as the 8894 is no longer in stock.

title: Great for camping
text:
This product was just what I hoped - simple and effective. I used it for the first time at home in the privacy of my own bathroom. I highly recommend a few "dry runs." Haha.

This weekend I took it on a group camping trip. I was one of only two females, so squatting would have been even more awkward and/or inconvenient. This device never leaked. Never. Even when I may have been, shall we say, a bit out of sorts. Even when I really had to go, this device could handle the pressure. I do recommend wearing a panty liner, unless you are using actual TP. The device does work kind of like a squeegee, but of course, doesn't take care of everything. I like that it is made of a hard plastic because it is durable. I fear that the more flexible silicone products might not last long. This little puppy seems like it will last forever. After use, I simply shook it off and wrapped it in a handkerchief. I kept in nearby at all times and never once smelled any unpleasant odors.

If you are a camper/backpacker, this is, in my opinion, the only device you need. It is light-weight, effective and durable. It made my camping experience so much more enjoyable. It's kind of hard to tell in the pictures, but it is about as long as your hand from wrist to fingertips. Easy to pack in an outside pocket on your pack, or to simply stick in the back pocket of your pants. I could go on forever about how much I love this. Happy peeing, ladies!

This prompted me to look more into the ingredient list which is shown and has a lot of things—most which are natural which is great however the last ingredient “Ethylhexylglycerin” which is a preservative and turns is not good for you especially if you have sensitive skin. I tried to include a image result of what google said but my review keeps getting flagged for it, but in short: “ethylhexylglycerin is not safe due to its performance as a contact allergen. People with sensitive skin and existing skin conditions are more likely to be impacted by products containing this ingredient”.
It did remove my makeup well but at the cost of a burning feeling around my eyes for over half an hour it’s not worth it if I only can clean half my face with it especially for $20…

title: Thank You, Earth Therapeutics!!
text:
My bedroom faces the east and has an uncovered half-moon window above the one with blinds. In the summer the light begins to pour in before 5 AM and, being a light sleeper, I would wake up and have a difficult time getting back to sleep afterwards, which eventually, led me to search for a sleep mask.

I purchased these masks and another, molded one that came with earplugs. This is my very favorite and I shared the second of the set with my night-shift working daughter, as I felt it might help her get more rest during the day as well. I've been using mine for a few months now and absolutely love it.

It does take a little bit of getting used to, just to the feel of something on your face and around your head. I've felt a little irritation on my ears occasionally but can easily adjust it to relieve that. It fits my face and stays in place quite well without having the band on tightly. I am a "tummy sleeper", and this mask is so soft that it doesn't feel uncomfortable against my pillow. It's just wonderful!

I have not noticed any scent on the ones that I received, and I checked because of the other reviewers comments. I've hand-washed it numerous times now, then let it air dry and it's ready to go again. If anything, it's just become softer but has not shown any signs of wear beyond that. I'm now looking to order more, just to have on hand when this one is ready to be replaced.

The other, molded one seems a bit bigger but sits off your eyes, if that sensation would bother you. I have a little more difficulty getting it to block all the light as well as this one, but it could be more attractive for larger faces or folks that are bothered by having something constantly touching their eyes like this one does. Just my thoughts on that. . .

I've read many articles recently on the importance of getting adequate sleep for your mental and physical health. If you are looking at sleep masks, you're probably wanting to improve your rest for some reason. I'd recommend you give this mask a try. I don't understand why some seem scented and some aren't, but I am 100% pleased with the masks I received. Most of those reviews are pretty old if you note that.

title: A Little TOO Old School for Me
text:
The PROS: This product does exactly what it says it will: it stiffens the hair so that it will stand up straight, which is why it is ideal for Flat Tops. It is not heavily perfumed, like a lot of hair products on the market these days. It has a very slight fragrance in the jar, but once you put it in your hair it is practically undetectable. Even though the jar is small, it will last a long time because you only need to use a little bit at a time.

The CONS: Because this product is petroleum-based, it is very heavy and sticky. In fact, it has almost the same consistency as Vasaline..perhaps a little bit thicker. Shampooing it out of your hair is like trying to clean up an oil spill. It will stay in your hair for a few days unless you use dish detergent (DAWN) to wash it out with.
Also, if your hair is more than about 1 1/2 inches in length, it will make your hair look greasy and stringy. As the label states, it is best suited for very short hair.

title: It's pretty ok. I tend to like products like this ...
text:
I am always on the search for a new brightening concealer pen, so I thought I would take a gamble on this one. It's pretty ok. I tend to like products like this to be pretty watery and light, but I would say this one has a slightly drier consistency than usual which makes it just a little thicker than I like. Despite the name is was also a little pinker than I thought it would be, which turned out ok on my pale irish skin but might be funky on someone with a different coloring than myself. None of these things are a huge deal breaker, but I seriously dislike the packaging. Most pens I have used like this have a dial on the end to dispense product; for this one, you have to click the end cap button a few times before applying to the face. The first time I used the pen I felt like I was clicking forever before any product was actually dispensed, which was very annoyed. Now the pen has no issue dispensing the product immediately, but it with the click mechanism I end up using more product than I would like.

tl;dr It's pretty ok, and not the worst choice for your money. But nothing special about it either, and the packaging is less than desirable.

title: Just kind of average
text:
I don't used to use skin-care products often. As a male, it's just not something I used to give much thought to. However, as I get older, I do suffer from dry skin in the winter months as the lower humidity in my house tends to cause my skin to flake and break out in spots.

So I thought I would try this vegan oil for dry skin and I'm not entirely impressed.

First thoughts are that the bottle is very nice. I love the green color of the oil. When the light hits it just right, it looks very pleasing. The bottle comes with a lid attached to a dropper for application, which makes it a little difficult to apply. You have to hold the dropper with one hand and apply it to the other and rub it in. My concern with this method is how difficult it will be to pull up more oil when the bottle gets low, but I guess that remains to be seen.

The oil itself is very greasy feeling. It literally feels like a lower viscosity motor oil and also has a sandy/gritty texture to it when applied. The scent is very strange as well. To me, it smells 100% like rubber. It's not a bad smell, but it's also not a pleasant smell. It's just a smell. If you've ever smelled rubber, you know what I mean.

As for its effectiveness? Again, not impressed.

I've been using it for about a week now, and I haven't really noticed any huge effects from the lotion. My skin is still peeling and dry in most of the places where I have applied this, but I would say there is a slight improvement. However, I'm not sure it's worth the price. I have used other, much cheaper, lotions/oils that have provided better results.

Overall, this is just average to me. I'm just not sure it's worth the price of admission.

title: It's okay.
text:
.

Wow, it looks like I'm part of a small minority here! I'm happy that this product works for all the 5- and 4-star reviewers. For me...meh.

For starters, this feels greasy on my skin and takes longer than other moisturizers to absorb. Certainly, it is an "okay" moisturizer, hence the three stars. ("It's okay.") But for me, it's sure nothing to write home about.

I very much like the flip-top tube -- very quick and easy to open and dispense with one hand. The texture is nice. And I do appreciate the absence of scent. But an hour after I've applied it, my face feels no different than itI did before I put it on.

Having said that, I will say that I have researched the use and effects of ceramide on skin, and it does seem that, in certain strengths and when used with certain other ingredients, ceremides can help skin retain moisture. So, this product will work for some people. It just doesn't do much for me.

This product is not overly expensive, which helps, but there are a number of lower-priced moisturizers that I believe most people would find just as good as (or perhaps better than) this one. I can't recommend it as a great moisturizer, and I honestly don't know how it gets such terrific views, but that's the nature of skin care: what works for some doesn't work for others. I just can't see this one as being any kind of a magic bullet.

title: THE BEST!  Better than Super Blue, Glam Seamless Tape, and Satin Strands.  Try it!
text:
I have had tape-in extensions for several years and these are BY FAR the BEST replacement tapes I have used. I only use Glam Seamless extension hair and these fit those pieces really well. I love that these can easily be split in half because when I place my extensions I use a single piece and fold it in half, rather than sandwiching 2 pieces, to put less weight on my baby fine hair.

I have tried many types of replacement tapes including the "Super Blue", and in a pinch the super cheap (quality, not cost!) Satin Strands, and these far outshine them all. With all other tapes I always lose 1-2 pieces every time I wash my hair (which is only 1x/week), and the rest slip a little with each wash. So because of that I always put them in as close to the scalp as possible. To my surprise, not only did I not lose any with this tape, they didn't slip at all, not even a little! So I had nearly 2 weeks of my extensions remaining really tight to my head! I almost pulled them out because they were getting uncomfortable, but I ended up sticking it out.

It has now been just about 6 weeks and I am going to pull them out and reset them within the week. They still haven't slipped very much, and I still haven't lost a single one! By this point with any other tape, half of them would have come out by now! I could easily leave these in another month without much issue, but my baby fine hair knots easily when there is any outgrowth.

This tape is a little bit thicker than other tapes, which is likely why it holds so well. When putting the two pieces together, really press down and squish them together to ensure there is a secure contact with both sides. Then heat set the pieces between a hot iron on low for 5-10 seconds - this is not in the instructions but is recommended on the product's website, so I did it, and got really great results!

Because these have such a strong hold, I just ordered the C-22 solvent to remove them. I normally use coconut oil, but suspected I might need something a bit more to remove these. I will update my review once I remove them and share whether or not it was more difficult, compared to other tapes.

title: Only meant for gel polish! Works well when used correctly
text:
This is ONLY meant for GEL polish NOT for acrylic powder, dip powder, Poly gel, or builder gel. Why? I don’t know. I’m guessing whatever chemicals in it breakdown the gel polish won’t breakdown the acrylic powder, dip powder, Poly gel, or builder gel in the same way.

This works great! I have tried other gel polish remover before and they just don’t feel right on the nail. It’s hard to describe, but it’s just a weird feeling I get in my nail bed when I’ve applied them. I’ve been trying out different ones hoping to find one that doesn’t feel like that and works really well…I finally found one!

This is easy to use.
-USE NAIL FILE TO REMOVE TOP COAT. This step is important. A lot of people think this step isn’t necessary with a gel polish remover like this. That it’ll remove the top coat too. It might, I haven’t tried it. But, I’m guessing it wouldn’t do it as quickly and easily. Just take a nail file and lightly buff off the top coat. It doesn’t take much.
-Apply a thin coat of the gel polish remover just like you would any nail polish
-Let it sit for 3-8 minutes. It will start to crack/bubble.
-Take a cuticle pusher and use it to push off the nail polish. It should push off easily. You can always add another coat of the remover if it’s not fully off.

I found for me with 2 coats of gel polish on, it usually took me about 10 minutes from start to finish. So much easier than acetone or even a drill! As long as you remove the top coat by filing it off before applying this remover and give it time to work and soften the polish, it’s easy to scrape off!

As a side note, even though this says it’s not meant for acrylic powder, dip powder, builder gel, or Poly gels, I tried it with dip powder. It worked well but did take longer for it to crack/bubble and I had to do 2 coats of the remover. It also worked much better when it was a solid color dip powder and not a dip powder with glitter in it.

title: Super hydrating
text:
I bought this mainly because it contains peptides and those are something I dont have in the rest of my skincare routine. The eye area is very delicate to begin with and as we age, the skin thins out along with the fat. This has been by far my biggest aging issue. :( I dont know why Ive been having such a hard time but around 21 the skin started thinning out rapidly. It may have been from being on doxycycline. Anyways, peptides help thicken the skin over time. It wont restore the fat loss but it can combat the thinning skin issue.

Nupeptin Restoring Eye Zone cream is PACKED with beneficial, anti-aging ingredients. I see various proteins, extracts, antioxidants, ceramides, and other natural sourced ingredients. This is a very thick eye cream and suuuuper hydrating. I like how plump and supple my undereye area looks while wearing this. You can tell by the ingredient list that it is very nourishing. Upon application, you can even tell by the consistency.

It takes a while for peptides to give full results. But the results are long term. Since peptides work similar to chemical exfoliators i would advise to wear a sunscreen while using this product. Also for best results, dont combine it with other actives (IE alpha hydroxy acids). The supple and plump effect should be immediate though! I am so pleased with this product. Its better than a lot of $$$$$$ ones ive bought.

title: good size. keeps my hair dry.
text:
My friend loaned me a reusable shower cap one time and I loved it so much I decided I needed my own. I wanted to find something in a solid color because so many of them are patterned and very loud and that just isn't really for me. I mainly wanted the silver and gold ones, so I gave the pink and purple to the friend I borrowed the cap from so she has spares. I've used them a couple times and they seem to work well. They're big enough to fit all of my hair and my ears in them and they do a reasonable job of keeping the water out. The elastic band lets in a little bit of water around the edges, but that's to be expected. It's not enough to be a problem. The main part of the cap keeps the water out nicely, and the satin layer helps reduce that very loud noise that is caused by water hitting plastic.

As others have complained about, the band is a little bit prickly on the head. I don't have overly sensitive skin, so I don't notice it very much, but if that is something that would bother you, these may not be the right choice. I think a little head prickling is worth it to have the color and style I want, so it really isn't a big deal.

While the size is great for me (I have about chin length, very thick hair) I'm not sure if it would work if your hair was much longer (unless it was very fine). I use up just about all the space in the cap fitting my hair in it, but I also think I have a slightly larger than usual head.

Overall, it works for me and I'm happy with it.

text: I like this clamshell but there are better options out there.  I give a lot of hot rock massages.  Start with some oil to loosen up the body, then use the hot rocks, then massage again after.  My last set looked almost like a crock pot.  You filled it with water, put the rocks in (of which, there were many different shapes and sizes), let them get to a temperature that the person being massaged liked, and you took them out and put them on their body.  The problem here is, there's no water.  There's no set temperature.  It only gets so hot and all of the rocks are round and grainy.  Even the largest rocks are not that big and I find that they don't sit well on a person's body.  If you're just buying this for fun, than, by all means, give it a go. title: Get the 130
text:
I ordered this wig in 10 inch, 180 density. I’ve had it for a little over 6 weeks. I cut mine more equal in the back, so it was more like a bob.

Pros
Very good quality hair. I’ve washed it a bunch, colored it three times (more on that further down), styled it with heat many, many times, and even slept in it a few times. It always goes right back to looking new.

Takes heat and can keep a curl.

The size of the cap is, in my opinion, perfect. It is big head friendly and long enough to go over the sideburn area in front of the ears. I’ve never owned a wig that fits me this well.

There’s basically no shedding, and it doesn’t have any matting or areas that tangle.

Very well executed ombré.

Pretty long life. I wear this a lot.

Cons
This wig is not cute out of the box. The curl that came in mine was honestly ugly. Thankfully it is not permanent. After the hair is washed and dried, it has a very nice slight natural wave.

This is not necessarily a con for me, but the lighter section is definitely brassy. I wanted mine orangey red, so this was a good starting point for me.

This wig does not dye well and the color will be mostly gone within a few washes.

The hair is not evenly distributed. I’d say the back half is 100% density, maybe 130. The hair on the lace is like no joke 400% density. There is so much hair on the lace. I’ve plucked and plucked and plucked and there’s no improvement. So the hair in the front is puffy because there’s so much hair. This wouldn’t even be entirely bad except that a lot of the hair on the lace is only 2-3 inches long so the thickness doesn’t follow through all the way down.

This is the biggest con. One of clips on the adjustable strap came broken, and I didn’t realize until I had started customizing it. Lesson learned there. I’m fine with doing some work on my wigs, so it’s not a huge deal. But someone else may not be comfortable doing so.

I give it three stars due to the weird hair distribution and broken clip. I would probably buy this wig again when this one dies. However, I would definitely recommend not paying extra for more density.

title: Really, really great soaps
text:
This changed my thinking about soaps. I had been using Dove for years before I received this (and the Orange Ale) as a gift. They sat in a drawer for at least a year until I ran out of Dove, so I gave them a try. Now I'm back to purchase more.

They smell great, but not particularly beer-like. They have a feel unlike any manufactured soap or body wash that I have tried in the past, and I greatly prefer it. Lastly, being of Mediterranean heritage, I have pretty oily skin. I've had pretty bad acne since I was a teenager, and only since I started approaching 30 a few years ago did my face clear up. My back and shoulders cleared up some, but it's kind of embarrassing to have bacne at 33. title: Awesome Detangling Brush
text:
I was really surprised with how much I really love this brush. I have owned many other types of detangling brushes, and this one is way better. It's was like magic.
It has a good weight to it and feels like a durable and great quality brush. The little black plastic piece that comes with the brush, clips onto the back side of the brush. There is two different spots that you can pick from to put the clip on piece.
I have 3A type of hair and this brush just rips right through the knots and tangles without causing pain. With my other brushes, the brush would be full of my hair after brushing all of the tangles out. With this brush there was very little hair left in the brush afterwards. Which was easy to clean off of the brush.
My daughter also doesn't run for the hills anymore when it comes time for me to brush her hair lol. Now she wants her own brush like this, so I will be buying another one soon.

Great Tip For Others: No matter what type of hair you have, you should always start from the bottom and work your way upward when brushing. Take your free hand and hold the section of hair that you are brushing tightly enough so that there is less pulling of the hair from your scalp. I usually place my free hand a little above where the brush is going through the hair. I also find that when you come across an area that is pretty tangled or knotted, that it works better to hold the brush in a vertical position to brush that area.

title: Base coat was almost dried up, but the powders  are AMAZING!
text:
The powders are beautiful. Since I wasn’t ready to redo my own nails, I offered to do my six year old daughter’s with dip for the first time. She chose the pink. The powder is VERY fine, and needed three coats to become opaque, and I probably could have done four. The fine powder smoothed out really nicely tough - I barely had to file, and was able to do it all by hand, without firing up my nail drill. Took a while longer than normal to dry, but that could have been because I had to use a different base that came in a separate kit that I don’t really like. The one that came with this one, while sealed, was very thick and past the point of no return. I was so disappointed about that. I do like that they included the extra brushes and pretty little strange case. I appreciate the slightly larger jars of powder too, though I noticed the white seemed to not be as full as the others. Sure enough when I put the other jars on a scale, they weighed in between 18 and 19 grams. The white weighed just over 16.

Not sure on staying power since we just did them this morning, but if they can hold up for a week on the fingers of a six year old girl who likes to climb trees and dig in the mud for worms, I’ll be impressed.

I have yet to try any other colors, but if they’re anything like the pink, these are my new favorite for dip powders. I’ll stick to Latrice for my liquids though. These weren’t bad, I’ll use them, I just like the Latrice liquids better.

Oh! Bonus - my daughter discovered tonight that the pink glows in the dark!! She was literally jumping up and down with excitement. I will definitely be using these on myself when my current set needs to be redone. Overall, I’m pretty happy, because the price was right. Just wish I had gotten everything I paid for.

title: I love snails!
text:
I love snail slime. I have been reading about it for a while and am so glad I pulled the trigger to purchase it. I get occasional acne and scar easily. After two uses I saw a profound improvement in my skin. Nothing works that fast.I am a believer and am buying up all the slime I can find. The use of snail slime to improve skin dates back to ancient Greece, where Hippocrates, the famous physician, reportedly prescribed crushed snails and sour milk as a way to rid the skin of inflammation. In more recent times, the use of snail creams started when Chilean farmers who handled snails for the French market noticed their skin was visibly smoother. Nowadays, it is the secreted slime discovered by these farmers that is harvested to produce snail cream, not crushed up snails.
How the Slime Works
When snails are agitated, they excrete a thick fluid as a means to protect themselves. It may sound odd to use something like that on your skin, but remember that humans and most other animals also excrete oils as a way to protect their skin. In fact, the oil your body excretes to moisturize your skin is made up of lipids, sebum oil, and dead skin cells. As a snail protects itself, the slime that is excreted from its body is packed with nutrients like hyaluronic acid, glycoprotein enzymes, antimicrobial and copper peptides, and proteoglycans. All of these nutrients are already commonly added to beauty products and are thought to provide many benefits to skin.
The science behind snail slime as a viable beauty cream is mostly derived from lab studies where the effects of the slime have been tested on a variety of cell cultures. In these studies, research suggests that snail slime will stimulate the production of elastin and collagen, increase fibronectin protein production, and stimulate increased proliferation of fibroblasts. While all of these traits could be beneficial for skin, there have yet to be significant cosmetic trials or research into how snail slime actually affects the skin, and how long those effects last. In fact, there haven’t been any significant clinical trials on how a specific beauty product containing snail slime actually works on this skin – just the slime itself.
One of the main difficulties in conducting clinical trials on the benefits of snail slime is that the market has not fully figured out how to guarantee the results of testing. After all, if snail creams are to be effective, then the slime has to have a consistent concentration of the various chemical compounds, but this is difficult to guarantee. Because the success of trials leans heavily on the quality of snail extract used, the concentration of slime and the way it is excreted and processed, test results can sometimes be misleading. Some companies that manufacture snail creams do choose to keep a steady supply of their own snails so they can better regulate the extraction and formulation of the slime.

title: Highly Recommended
text:
I replaced a different manufacturer's very old electric razor with the Arcitec 1050, and have been using it for about three weeks. My primary shaving method has been the razor blade, supplemented by the electric for a fast shave now and then. I am so satisfied with the new Norelco that it has become my primary shaver. It delivers results virtually as close as a blade, and sometimes I think it is just as good. I don't feel that I need to use a blade to get a close shave any more, and I'm really amazed by the results. I didn't think that an electric could ever come this close to a blade. I guess that the technology has improved over the last twenty years, like everything else!

The shaver is not perfect, but the disadvantages are minor in my opinion. It does produce hair shavings, so I just shave over the sink. I don't mind cleaning up a little. The trimmer is quite small, but it does work well enough to clean the sideburns with an up and down motion. I have found that the shave is quite comfortable if you don't overdo it - just shave until you are clean, and use an after-shave cream to avoid minor irritation. I would prefer being able to leave the plug in the shaver, rather than remove it right after the charge is complete. It's a small inconvenience for such a great shave. And it is more economical than blades in the long run.

title: Inefficient Razor that's Rough to Use: There are much better value bargain razors out there.
text:
The Acevivi Razor : A Test and Review
I only came across this razor very recently. It intrigued me because some seemed to like it and report that it was well made. Also, like the new Fendrihan razors, it has an unusual head: Closed comb on one side; open comb on the other. I think the idea is that it offers two levels of aggression. The Lutz slant offers a similar choice of two levels of aggression.

In use I found that both sides offered about the same level of aggression. Another reason for the test is that it's a low cost razor; under $13 currently on Amazon. I'm always intrigued by potential bargains!

A further unusual feature is the exceptionally long handle. Longer than the Futur, longer than my Mergress, Schick Krona, or even my long handled Gillette Starburst, (aimed at the ladies” market); longer in fact than any razor I own. To some this is a plus, to others not so. It may be useful if ladies wish to use the razor on their legs, or other parts. The razor is well balanced so the long handle presented no problem.

The razor comes with a box of five blades. I have no idea of their origin. But since the razor is Chinese, I expect China.

The Blade used for the Test
I chose to use the Rapira Platinum Lux. I've found this blade to be consistent and reliable in just about every razor (but there are some razors where it's an indifferent pairing, say with my RR Wunderbar), and it's always good for at least four shaves, often six, in just about any razor. It's sharp, smooth, comfortable, very cheap to buy, and easily available, and my personal favorite of the Rapira line. I've also used it every DE razor I own at one time or another, and I own over 50 DE safety razors . Not my favorite blade, but a very good one in most razors. I used a brand new blade

How I Used this Razor for the Test
When using an adjustable razor, (and following advice from others on this forum, including Jim Chandler, plus my own long experimentation) I've found the best way, for the smoothest and most comfortable shave is to INCREASE the aggression with each pass. It seems counter-intuitive at first but it really works best. It's like lowering the blade on a lawn mower to get a closer cut. I increased the aggression on each pass on this test.

Since this razor supposedly offered two choices of aggression I used the Acevivi in this way: Less aggressive WTG and XTG, then more aggressive ATG and for buffing. I'm assuming that closed comb is less aggressive, though as some have reported with the Fendrihan, this is not always the case.

Now in previous reviews, I notice that some people seem to miss this point. I really believe that this is the best way to get a very smooth, comfortable, and importantly irritation-free shave with an adjustable razor. I have a complete thread on this method. Please review the thread and give it a whirl, and report what you find please!

The Routine
For testing I go through the same routine. I clean my face and wet the beard by washing with a glycerin soap. I rinse off the soap, wet it thoroughly and apply two drops of a pre-shave oil.

By the way, I believe good pre-shave prep not only produces a better shave, but reduces irritation, and keeps you skin in good condition. I know of one rather famous reviewer whose skin frankly looks irritated, red, blotchy and awful, especially on his neck. I don't doubt he gets close shaves, but at what cost?

I use an Arko shave stick applied directly to the beard and lather with a Stirling Synthetic “Kong” brush. I rinse and lather again between passes. I thoroughly rinse the head of the razor between passes.

I remove the blade from the razor when I'm done. I dry it with a microfiber cloth. Naturally I dry the razor too when I'm done.

I finish with an Alum block, which is a good indicator of razor burn or irritation. Then after washing it off , I apply Thayer's Alcohol Free Witch Hazel.

The Shave
I shaved 22 hours before doing a test comparison of the Parker Variant and Ming Shi 2000s, so my face had a little less than average growth.

First Pass WTG: Closed Comb Side
Fairly smooth, reasonably efficient. Not good enough for a one pass shave.

Second Pass XTG: Closed Com Side
Not especially smooth and after the pass I wasn't especially happy with the hair removal. It still felt like there was a lot of hair, but I press on! Still not good enough even for everyday.

Third Pass ATG: Open Comb Side
Quite scratchy. I could feel the blade and I didn't enjoy the pass much. A lost of hair remained. Quite disappointing. Not a good shave at all.

Buff up and J-hooking
I would have had to spend an age buffing and cleaning up because the beard was still quite rough, and frankly my face already felt quite irritated. So I did not buff with the Acevivi. There are limits to my testing zeal!

Finishing the Shave:
Sometimes a specific blade is no good. In the interests of fairness, I took the blade out and put it in my most efficient razor, the RR Wunderbar slant (which incidentally is not a blade this razor likes a lot) and had to shave again, because the shave with the Acevivi was just not good enough even for everyday.

I then did another ATG pass, and boy, was there a lot to remove! The jawline and neck still had a lot of growth. The blade performed well in the Wunderbar, so I don't think one can't blame the blade.

Now I'm not comparing a $13 razor to a $130. That would be grossly unfair. I just wanted to see if the blade was to blame, and frankly I didn't want to irritate my face more than necessary.

I did a clean up and buffing pass, using the Wunderbar and got a BBS shave. However the feedback from alum block revealed a lot of irritation, not surprising given three indifferent and inefficient passes with the Acevivi, followed by another ATG pass and cleanup with the Wunderbar, though I don't blame the latter. No nicks, cuts, or weepers, but definite neck irritation.

Conclusion:
The razor is well made, and low in price, and I admire the innovation, but I cannot recommend the Acevivi, unless you want to get a very long handle that's well made for under $13. It's possible that it will do better with other blades, but my initial impression is that it's not really worth testing. It's a fairly mild and quite inefficient razor.

Is it good value? No! The Ming Shi 2000s Adjustable is cheaper (aroud $10 from China) and better in every possible way. The following razors, all under $20 are much, much better: The RazoRock (RR) German 37 Slant, the Phoenix Artisan Accoutrements Bakelite slant, the RR Slab, the RR Mission, the RR Old Type, the RR Jaws (if you can get it), and probably some others too.

It's a pretty poor razor, and even at the low price not worth it. I wouldn't recommend it to newbies, because it will put them off DE shaving. Here's one to pass.

title: Not Just a Name, The Shampoo and Conditioner Really Are Purple
text: I got this shampoo and conditioner for my wife--here is her review: I wanted this shampoo and conditioner because it said it worked really well for gray and white hair--as a senior I have plenty of both--and because it got good reviews re fragrance and how soft it left hair. When I was in the shower and squirted some shampoo into my hand, I was amazed to see that the shampoo really is a dark purple color. I asked myself if I could live with it if it actually turned my hair purple, decided I could, and lathered up. The shampoo did an excellent job of creating a strong lather, and my hair felt really clean when I rinsed it out. The shampoo has a soft floral fragrance that is very pleasant. I took a quick look in the mirror to see if my hair was purple, and it wasn't, so I then squirted out some conditioner into my hand. It was purple, too, although thicker and lighter in color than the shampoo. As I rubbed the conditioner into my hair, the wonderful floral scent of the conditioner filled my shower--what a delightful sensory treat! I checked my hair again when I got out of the shower and dried off--still no purple hair, thank goodness. However, when I squirted some shampoo into my hand to take a photo, there was a big purple stain on my hand when I washed the shampoo off. I squirted the conditioner in a different spot on my hand for that photo, and it did the same thing. I've washed my hands several times since then, and the purple stains are still there. So...even though the product information online says it works fine with gray and white hair, I look down at my purple stains on my hand and I have to wonder. Since I love the smell of this shampoo and conditioner and how incredibly soft it leaves my hair, I'm going to continue using it. If it turns my hair purple at some point in the future, I'll do an update and give everyone fair warning.

title: It's a keeper!
text:
This is well worth the price. I was looking for a low end electric toothbrush to see if I like having an electric toothbrush. I have been sold on the electric part and I really see no reason why I would need to upgrade to a more expensive toothbrush. I have been a manual toothbrush person forever. I had one other electric one a long time ago but it was loud and didn't hold a charge well so I was always skeptical. But this Oral-B toothbrush is great. It isn't super loud and it is comfortable to hold. The charge lasts for several days before it begins to lose brushing power.

What I really like is the 2 minute timer. It has made me much better at brushing for a the correct period of time. Some of the more expensive brushes beep every 30 seconds so you know when to switch regions, but I have gotten so used to this that I usually finish brushing everything within 5 seconds of the 2 minutes. In addition to a more thorough cleaning, I can definitely say that the electric brush cleans much better than a manual brush. The brush heads last, the entire assembly is easy to clean, and replacements are not that expensive. If you are trying to decide whether or not to try an electric toothbrush, this is a great one to start with. It is inexpensive and works great. There is no need to spend upwards of $100 for something like this. If you already have an electric and are looking for a replacement, well my dentist likes the results of this brush so this is a keeper.

title: Quality Reusable Glass Pump Container, Soap Lathers Well & Feels Good, Has Light Natural Scent
text:
This Cleancult liquid hand soap comes in a high quality, glass container that’s thick and strong with a plastic pump that works well. I’ve been using this coconut based hand soap daily and find it pleasant. It glides and lathers well when I rub my hands together and stays on my hands long enough to be thorough washing. This soap isn’t overly drying, though I almost always need lotion after hand washing. The lavender scent from essential oils is light, which is a plus as I’m not a fan of heavy scent. The container holds 12 oz. and the company sells 16 oz. refills (currently $6.95) in a paper based container styled like a milk carton to reduce plastic waste.

The glass container has a modern design that looks nice countertop. It has a beige or taupe color silicone (or similar) material on the bottom and lower sides that prevents slipping and adds breakage protection. The plastic pump is also beige and good quality but may not last as long as the glass container. Beige isn’t my favorite color but it’s neutral and the company offers a blue shade that looks pretty in the photo. This soap has coconut oil, olive oil, potassium soap, aloe juice, vitamin E, citrus acid, sodium chloride and a natural essential oil blend (not in that order). I assume “potassium soap” is potassium hydroxide (caustic lye), but believe it’s found in all liquid soap under various names. Overall, I like the hand soap and container. 4 stars.

title: Good and bad - But I have notes to increase success.
text:
I applied this to my 5 year olds blonde hair. I did not want to spend a future at a salon because.... she is five!
She DOES love the end result but I will say, if you want a successful process I have several important notes.
1. I can NOT speak to the bleach because we did NOT use it. I hear BAD things about it.... so, read other reviews if applicable.
2. Product is messy! That said; count on the NEED for 2 person application. Do NOT attempt to self apply this product. Will absolutely regret it and ruin your home and clothes.
3. Count on purchasing extra items AND plan for 3 hours from prep start to finish. I will explain why.
EXTRA ITEMS: This product will ABSOLUTELY stain hand, face and scalp. Purchase: extra gloves, vaseline, and hair dye removal!
GLOVES: It only comes with one crappy pair of gloves. For best result, swing by Sally's beauty and buy SEVERAL good pairs of gloves. OR buy some of those thick bathroom cleaning gloves that come to your elbows. this way you can use them and take them off and on easily to both apply AND rinse hair.
VASELINE: COMPLETELY coat ears, forehead, neck, etc with a THICK coat of vaseline to avoid staining
DYE REMOVAL: Swing by sally's and buy a bottle of hair dye remover BEFORE you start. This will get on skin and you will NOT get it off otherwise.
EXTRA TIME TO APPLY: I have applied this product in 4 different colors to both my own hair and others hair. I have NEVER gotten good coverage without having to apply it TWICE. (including this application. pictures attached are product of applying BOTH colors twice for an hour each time) For the vibrant color you will want, count on applying, waiting an hour to rinse. Blow dry and reapply for ANOTHER hour. Do not think you will "quickly" apply this product like a box of normal 20 minute color. You will be disappointed.

Overall, as I said, my daughter is happy with the turn out and I saved money so in my case, it worked out.
However, I have experience with this product so it was successful based on ALL the above notes.
Also, I DID experience severe staining to her scalp and it will NOT come off so far even with the hair dye remover. I did not apply it close to scalp but she is young and her hair is so thin, it bleed right through and left big nasty looking spots all over her little head. That said, I ONLY applied this to the underneath of her hair as an ombre look... so I can keep working on getting it off in the next few days.
I would be much more upset if I had this all over her head.

I could not be happier with both the body wash and bar soap. I own each scent and am obsessed with each of them; I keep a bar of “strength” in my car and “joy” next to my bed simply for aromatherapy! My family and I absolutely adore the products and feel refreshed and renewed after every shower.

The “hope” gift box was ordered for friends and was beautifully curated to include products and brand purpose. They had been eager to try the product after hearing about the brand and the gift box was a wonderful way to give a gift that kept giving this holiday season. I have also purchased various bar soaps over the past months to give as gifts to friends and each has thanked me for introducing them to the brand.

I am definitely going to keep buying products from The Right to Shower because I love the quality of their products, refreshing scents, and their purpose-driven approach. title: Works for Eye Puffiness & Amazing Off-Label Headache Relief!!
text:
This eye cream was far different than I was expecting -- but in a GREAT way. I'm 29-years-old, so the lines around my eyes aren't terribly deep, although they are probably deeper than many other females my age due to my sun-worshiping in earlier years. I do suffer, however, from severe seasonal allergies and am constantly plagued with dark circles ("allergic shiners" as they call them) and extreme puffiness of both my upper eyelids and just under my eyes (the infamous "bags").

To be honest, my impression of this cream at first glance wasn't too great. For starters, the jar of cream was much smaller than I had imagined, but I guess that's my fault for not noticing the (very) small-printed "0.5 fl oz" on the label in the picture. (I do think that this was a little deceitful though, because the size/amount of this cream is not listed anywhere on the product description.) In addition, while trying to read the teeny tiny print on the jar, I also almost immediately noticed a spelling typo on the front of the label that reads "Nautral & Healthy" rather than "Natural & Healthy." I know this seems like a rather minuscule and knit-picky detail to point out, but it did make me at least wonder about this company's quality control standards.

Despite my initial impression, I gave the company/cream the benefit of the doubt and have been using it for the last few days. With my first application under my eyes, the cream felt more on the "thin" side (similar to a lotion rather than thick cream), but while rubbing the cream into my skin in a circular motion, the moisture that the cream delivered was far better than I anticipated. It takes at least 3-4 minutes before your skin feels like the cream is completely absorbed, which gave me ample time to slowly massage the area during absorption (and felt very soothing and relaxing). I had absolutely no issues with any side effects or skin reactions such as burning, tingling, redness, or irritation. I noticed a small "immediate" reduction in the pores and fine lines of the areas I applied the cream, though not as impressive as some of the Retinol and Vitamin C serums that I've used in the past. There was no obvious difference in the dark circles or puffiness right after application, however, within about 30-45min, the puffiness started to visibly decrease and the area all around my eyes felt less tender/achy in general.

With each subsequent application, I noticed the same resulting decrease in puffiness as was observed initially. My puffiness did return each morning, but I expected because I'm still constantly being exposed to my allergens. (After all, the cream is meant to relieve a symptom of my allergies, not be a miracle cure for my chronic systemic condition.) I've noticed that if I apply the cream immediately before bed and spend more time rubbing it into my skin in the circular motions, I do have a noticeable decrease in the morning when I wake up compared to before I started using the cream. As far as the under-eye dark circles, I can't tell a difference so far - but in all fairness, I've only been using the cream for 4 days (twice daily) so there's still hope.

Now for the best part (in my opinion, at least). On the second night of using this cream, I had yet another one of my throbbing headaches (allergies are the worst!!) About 15-20min after my evening cream application, I noticed that my headache felt a little better -- I'm not saying that there was some miraculous change here, but it did feel less severe. This was very unusual for me, as I hadn't taken any ibuprofen or Zyrtec at that point (my usual go-to medications when my headaches are severe). The only thing I could think that I had done differently this time than any other time was that I applied the cream -- it was a strange connection, but stranger things have certainly happened to me. I went back to look at the ingredients listed on the jar and saw that it had rooibos in it. I had absolutely no idea what this was (and probably didn't notice it the first time I looked because I don't have a magnifying glass), but I looked it up online and read that it's an herb from South Africa with a laundry-list of health benefits -- including antioxidant properties and... headache relief?!?! Although still relatively skeptical that this was just a coincidence and that I had gotten "lucky" on my google search, I was still optimistic and proceeded to rub the eye cream on my temples and at the base of my skull to see what would happen. After a good 30-45min, my headache was almost completely gone. I know this headache thing sounds ridiculous and obscure, but I encourage anyone to research this mysterious Rooibos for themselves. I haven't had a headache as severe as that one since, but I have had a few headaches start to come on, and with each headache, I applied the cream to my temples, under my eyes, and to the base of my skull and the feeling has gone away each time within about an hour.

With all of this said, I couldn't rate this "eye" cream turned headache remedy anything less than 5 stars despite my initial less-than-thrilled first impression. Because the cream is light and only requires a very small amount with each application, I think the small jar will actually last me a reasonably long time, too. Between the headache relief and the disappearing eye bags, I would be confident in recommending this product to others. I was also fortunate to receive my first jar of this cream at a discounted price or free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: Use for 30 Days
text:
I am using this twice per week, and have only used it 1 week (2 times) so far. The instructions say that results will be visible within 30 days. I don't see much visibly yet, but I can already feel a difference when I run my hands over my face.
Also, the instructions say that the day after you use it, you may have redness. I have not really had that except for maybe a very slight flushed look that actually looks better than my normal skin tone.

As far as the way it feels, if any of you have a husband/boyfriend with prickly beard stubble rubbing against your face, that is very close to how this feels. It's very doable.

I am taking photos each week, and when I get to week four, I will post them. Based on my experience so far, I fully expect to have visible results in 30 days. Of course if the tool breaks, or if I experience any adverse reactions, I will definitely adjust my review accordingly. For now, I have December 22nd on my calendar as the day to update with before/after photos. Stay tuned!

title: Disappointed - went back to my T800
text:
I bought a T800 quite a few years ago when I found the Austrian-made unit on sale at the local Target store. It lasted very well, and I was somewhat disappointed when the battery eventually would no longer accept a charge, though it continued to work while plugged in.
After carefully looking into alternatives, I went with a T970 from Amazon.com, hoping for the same quality. Major letdown! This Chinese-made unit just is not up to the same standard as my T800. The charger is a seperate seperate and bulky transformer, instead of the simple cord of the T800. The T970 is larger, more awkward to hold and to use, and more fragile in every possible way. The vacuum, which was one of the initial attractions, works, but only marginally well, and the unit is unstable when laid down on a solid surface. If the mile-long charging cord is attached, expect to have to prop the unit against a wall to prevent it rolling over.
I spent $6.00 on a top-quality replacement cell for my T800 (shipping was $4.00, for a 700mA Sanyo AA), and after careful disassembly and reassembly, successfully replaced the ailing cell without breaking anything. Unbelievably, The T800 now outlasts the T970 two-fold.
I wish I'd stuck it out with the T800 in the first place.
.
Updated June 29, 2009.
After about two years of irregular use and the resulting regular complete self-discharges, the T970 stopped functioning even while plugged in, unless first given time to recharge. Initial time to start working after plugging in has increased to the point where it no longer works even being plugged in for 24 hours.

title: Love this deodorant!  Been using for about 2 years now.
text: I was on a quest to find a good natural deodorant about 2 years ago and scoured the internet, going deep in my dive of reviews.  This one had great reviews from guys and girls (it used to be called Primal Pit Paste, which was a name I thought was so fun).  Over the past year they rebranded and it's now called Pretty Frank, but it's the same great deodorant!  It works!  I never notice my pits smelling.  I love the variety of scent options too.  I use the Lime/Coconut one the most, but I've used the other ones and love them too.  The only gripe I have with this is that when they rebranded, they changed the packaging container to look like a more conventional deodorant container.  It used to be a cylindrical container with a twist off lid.  I prefer that one over the new one.  Because of the texture of the deodorant, it always seeps out of the lid, no matter how carefully you remove and replace the lid for each application.  It's definitely an obstacle for this deodorant, as it takes an extra step of cleaning the excess deodorant off the lid every couple days, but I'm confident they can come up with a solution over time.  Either way, this is a great natural deodorant and I highly recommend.

title: It is actually stretchy
text:
I had ready this wax is a flexible wax. Yes, all similar waxes flex to a degree but this one is supposed to be a bit more elastic. That's to help it wrap around tricky areas (ankle bones, knees, etc.). It's also supposed to work well for large areas. I prefer to wax myself, and I don't have assistance. I also like to wax everywhere. I waxed my own back with this stuff and it actually worked. I did larger sections, and was reaching behind myself to both apply and remove the wax. It did indeed stretch and flex well so there wasn't any wax or hair breakage. The hair on my back is the typically fluffy vellus hair. It showed up after I had my second and I just don't like it even if it's not super obvious (or even visible 90% of the time). Admittedly that hair type did make it difficult to see, but again this wax wasn't too fussy. I'm 100% positive I applied it in the wrong direction at times and removed in the wrong direction too. Still, worked great.

I also tested it out on my legs. The hair there really varies from fine and barely visible blonde to thicker and quite dark (and rather stubborn to remove in places). It did a decent job on most of my legs. In the areas where the hair is a bit more stubborn I really had to work in smaller sections to get a good result. But in areas like my thighs I was able to do wide areas with ease and little left behind. On my thighs I have small areas that grow in different directions for no reason. I thought I'd have to do second passes, but I rarely did.

All that aside, I don't think this is the best wax for everyone. If you have a lot of very fine or fluffy vellus hair on large areas. Especially if it's on tricky areas like the stomach or behind your shoulders, and areas such as my upper arms where the hair literally grows both up and down in the exact same spot. This will get the job done. If the hair is even a little bit stubborn, you will probably run into some issues. For those places I'd say the pink version (their Best Loved wax) is a fantastic option.

title: Great for under the eyes
text:
I bought this powder specifically to use under my eyes. What makes it different from most loose powders is that it contains cornstarch, giving it a smooth finish without being too drying. The only other loose powders I've been able to find that contain cornstarch are the Ben Nye Luxury Powders, and the Col-Lab Set the Stage loose powder from Sally's, which is sold on their website only. I've tried samples of the Ben Nye Luxury Powders in a few colors and liked them, but decided to try something different, and a little cheaper.

I apply this powder in one of two different ways. If I want a minimal makeup look, I'll use my ELF blush brush to pat the powder under my eyes, tapping off any excess from the brush before application. If I want my undereyes to look especially smooth, and my deep tear troughs less noticeable, I use a dry foam wedge sponge to pick up the powder, then stamp it under my eyes, and gently brush off the excess after a minute or two. It does not make my undereye area look or feel dry. Sometimes I use it all over my face, if I'd rather not use my usual matte pressed powder. I have fair skin, so the white color appears translucent on my skin, but I'm not sure how someone with deeper skin would fare.

Because I use this powder sparingly, this jar should last me a long time!

title: Versache meets the "modern" market...
text:
As the product is marketed for, it should only be used for casual affairs seeing as how while it is complex enough for formal affairs, it smells too much like something you'd wear with jeans as opposed to a suit and tie.

As previously mentioned this product is slightly complex featuring sharp characteristics that designer brands typically have, as opposed to more mellow notes commonly thought to be the key success behind marketing casual-use perfumes. In that regard I think Versache lives up to its name with this product: they manage to deliver something highly creative, if not long lasting.

It's extremely hard to define what the fragrance notes for this product are, I can only say that it is most certainly not velvety (not remotely), or musky as the designer would indicate. Instead it is extremely citrus and acidy... but this isn't to say it is too "sharp" for comfort.

So wait, absolutely no "velvet" characteristic like the designer noted? Well the mellow aspect comes with the highly distinctive scent of a "jeans" which is released over time as you wear, it making the fragrance a bit more mellow and yet still remain within the world of "distinctive" (and narrowly escaping being called "pungent" - a term I used to describe L'eau d'Issey by Issey Miyake, a characteristic I find extremely negative). Being highly distinctive and sharp from the get-go, I'd say that this product is pretty easy to forget about a few weeks after using it... seeing as how there are fans of such heavily distinctive fragrances (who obviously do not mind a sharp nose at first), this product should certainly be sampled by such individuals.

I like this product quite a bit so I'm going to give it a 4, hopefully encouraging others to try it. However as I previously noted it is easy to forget and I must admit that I do not wear it as frequently as I used to (I'd give it a 3 for a personal opinion if I could and a 4 for overall product quality and general appeal).

title: Great but, get the cheaper one. Just as good.
text:
Do you have migraines or Meniere's disease or just have a sensitive head? Don't get any of the pulsating Oral B brushes. They will just make you nauseous or trigger a headache.

I have used the classic Oral B electric brush for many years. A fantastic simple white design by Braun of Germany - since discontinued after Braun was bought by an American company. Now I have the simple low end non pulsing model. Essentially the same guts and head as the classic but with an ugly, over stylized, blue body.

When the battery started to die on my classic model, I picked up a pulsating Oral B. It is really banging away at your teeth and does as good a job as the non pulsatinging. But it vibrates your jaw and skull like, well, a vibrating electric tooth brush! After a month, it was just too much for me. I went back to the dieing battery original, but soon got its replacement as a gift.

The verdict: I'm in my 40s and I've had about 6 different dentists (moving from job to job) in 5 different states. One was a professor at a dental college. After each visit, they all proclaim my teeth are in excellent shape. I use the cheapest Oral B electric brush (non pulsating) in the morning and before bed with Colgate Total. I also floss just one time before bed and use the Crest rinse for night time. I get them cleaned every 6-9 months.

Save your money and get the cheapest Oral B electric toothbrush. I think it is on sale sometimes for about $10.

text:
Really nice feel in the hand and the little “fur pucks” we extract from our fuzz bucket come right off the brush head with two or three light button presses. This is easy to use with either hand and while it’s not a wand, it is easier to use than a brush that straps to your hand. In that case, the hand must remain in contact with the coat along with all the body contours. I would argue that with this item’s handle design, you bend over slightly less and you can reach most places by just shifting your wrist a little - probably my favorite feature. The length of the cleaning metal bits is substantial and also worth mentioning. They easily get through the undercoat and right to the skin.
Others mentioned “scratching” with the metal tips but I think my pup likes it, let alone minds it. I don’t go really hard, letting the brush do the work, and treats after. From light tangles to seasonal shedding, this brush has been a winner. Be sure to stand up-wind.

I have found that repeating one stroke with the brush followed by one swipe of your free hand really gets stuff moving and it’s like half brush/ half pets for better vibes. A couple of minutes of brushing when I take her outside has made a difference for sure. She has never flinched or shown any signs of discomfort or fear while using this brush and she has a significant undercoat which takes way less effort now to shake loose.

title: Ingredients don't match up
text:
As someone who suffers from chronic insomnia (and the lovely, inescapable dark raccoon circle eyes that come with it), I was pretty excited to try this. I’ve only used it for one day, and the gel is pleasant enough to use, but what I want to bring up is the disparity between the ingredients that are advertised for Nuju Revitalizing Eye Gel, and the actual ingredients. I’ll break this down the best I can.

Right off the bat I noticed that this product claims to be paraben free, but has a number of contradicting Ingredients: Ethylparaben, Butylparaben, Propylparaben, Isobutylparaben. This could be a major problem for anyone with allergies or sensitivities. This product also claims to have time released retinol, which is notably missing from the ingredient list. I’ve listed almost every ingredient in this eye cream, and its function, below. Personally I think this will be useful for moisturizing, and perhaps a temporary rejuvenated look, but it doesn’t seem to pack enough punch to tackle my under eye circles. Because of the disparity between advertised ingredients and the actual, I’m giving this two stars. Keep in mind I don’t claim to be a scientist. Just going off of easily available information.

Herbal Ingredients:
Cucumis Sativus (Cucumber) Extract (Skin Conditioner); Chamomilla Recutita (Matricaria) extract (thought to increase blood flow and aid in “congestion” under the skin); Camellia Sinesis Leaf Extract (Green Tea extract. Generally only high concentrations have substantial effects on skin, but thought to help reduce swelling and inflammation among other things)

Of Interest:
Ceramide 3 (part of naturally occurring skin structure, it helps retain moisture, regulates cellular barrier repair); Sphingolipids (naturally occurring in the body, it functions as protection for cells against environmental factors); Hesperidin Methyl Chalcone (naturally occurring bioflavinoid, often used for under eye circle treatments, helps combat free radical damage and inflammation); Dipeptide-2 (effective skin conditioner, believed to help improve lymphatic circulation and so often found in under eye cream to reduce dark circles); Palymitoyl Tetrapeptide-7 (helps reduce inflammation. Increases collagen production when paired with Palmitoyl-Oligopeptide, which is not listed as an ingredient for this product); Camellia Sinesis Leaf Extract (Green Tea extract. Generally only high concentrations have substantial effects on skin, but thought to help reduce swelling and inflammation among other things)

Everything else:
Cetearyl Ethylhexanoate (emollient and skin conditioner); Propylene Glycol (aids with shelf stability); Carbomer (thickener/controls gel consistency); Polysorbate 20 (emulsifier/solubilizer); Triethanolamine ( ph adjuster *a “moderate concern” level ingredient for potential toxicity*); Hydroxypropyl Methycellulose (used for sustained release of ingredients); Ethylhexyl (lubricant/makes skin look soft and smooth); Cocoate (derived from coconut oil, skin conditioner); Steareth-20 (surfactant and emulsifier, often found in eye cream); Butylene Glycol (solvent and used to make creams more easily spreadable); Phenoxyethanol (Chemical preservative); Titanium Dioxide CI 77891 (white pigment and sunscreen); Cyclomethicone, Dimethiconol, Phenyl Trimethicone (liquid silicone, creates a temporary skin plumpness)

title: The silver bullet for small breed teeth problems.
text:
We have a lot of dogs and they’re chihuahuas. They are known for having notoriously bad teeth as a breed even when you do everything right. Our littlest has been losing teeth left and right and is at the age where cleanings are too scary with her size. She would realistically need a cleaning much more often than yearly because the plaque builds up so fast.

I bought this as a shot in the dark, as we have burned hundreds on every product known to man. I mixed the product parts together in the large bottle and sprayed 4 of our dogs’ teeth as instructed. After a SINGLE application, our girl with the bad teeth had a 25% reduction in plaque. Our other three had a reduction of 40%, 60%, and 90%. I am not joking - this stuff has carbolic acid in it and it WORKS. The two components mixed causes some type of fizzy reaction and really works between the plaque and teeth/gums and between teeth. I tasted it first myself to be sure it wouldn’t be traumatizing to our pups and it tastes like flavorless alcohol free mouthwash.

Since, I continue to spray once or twice a day as I remember to and the plaque keeps disappearing. I did check with my dental tools to be sure it wasn’t just bleaching the plaque and it is not- it’s physically breaking off their teeth. I don’t know how we will get larger bottles of the stuff with the number of dogs we have but it’s true, it works. I paid my actual money and used it on my real dogs. This is not a paid or discounted review. Please give this a shot on your Littles!

text: I used to buy Vikki Lamotta Wonderlift YEARS and YEARS ago in New York, and then stopped using it to try a lot of other brands.  Hers was the original, and it still works great.  HOWEVER, you DO need to play around with it for a while to get it to look natural and so that your face isn't all powdery looking.  I use a very light moisturizing lotion on my face FIRST and let it completely absorb before I apply the Vikki Lamota Wonderlift, and then I let the Wonderlift DRY FOR HALF AN HOUR AT LEAST until it is fully firmed up, after which a slight white chalky look is on my skin...  THEN, I get my hands damp under the faucet (shake off all the excess water) and rub MORE of the moisturizing lotion into my hands and mix it with the little bit of water in the palms of my hands and then lightly PAT my hands all over my face where it appears white or chalky looking. I only use a tiny bit of make-up as a TOUCH UP ONLY on places that have blotches or redness, because you CANNOT rub makeup over your face once the Wonderlift has dried or it will simply ball up and take the Wonderlift OFF!  It takes some practice, but if you are dedicated to looking YEARS YOUNGER (as I am!!) then this will do the trick!
