title: Works surprisingly well
text:
I've seen these steamer machines that are used to remove gel nail polish and while I've always wanted to try them, I was very skeptical and unwilling to spend the money on a gadget that may or may not work. But, removing the gel polish is the worst part or the thing I hate about gel polish: it's time consuming and so hard on the nail bed. I've seen mixed reviews online about gel polish steamers but I finally decided to try one.
This gel polish remover machine actually works. It was easy to put together and I was able to completely remove my gel polish in under 20 minutes. First and most important is to file the top layer of gel down first with a nail file before using this device. I was not able to get the gel polish offf without filing the surface first. I put about two capfuls of 100% acetone (you can use less) into the little tray and turned the machine on. Once it beeps, you can stick your fingers inside. It gets a little hot but it's not painful. After five minutes the machine will beep and I am able to scrape off most of the gel polish. I have to do a second round to get certain areas that just won't scrape off. And when I say scrape off, I mean easily scrape off not scraping and hurting the surface of the nail. I guess I should say push off the gel polish to remove it. I leave the remaining acetone in the tray and either reuse it or dump it. I would say this is easier than using aluminum foil or plastic nail caps because you do the whole hand at once. With foil or plastic caps, I never get my whole hand done at once. This was easier and I didn't use any cotton balls and I used less acetone.

The device is a little pricey. It's basically a warming plate fitted inside a contained area with holes to place your fingers. It's worth the money to me because I hate the process of gel removal. I like that the company provides four replacement plastic pieces for the nail holes. It took me a while to figure out what the replacement pieces were for but after reading one of the reviews I now realize what it's used for. There is also a second plastic tray to put the nail polish remover or acetone in. My only criticism is that I wish the device was smaller as I have a lot of nail stuff and this will just add to it all. It's not the fanciest looking device but it does the job.

title: Same great smell I remember, just LESS of it.
text:
I started buying this when it first came out and because it became unavailable for time, switched to a different fragrance. A few years later (March of 2017), after finally running out of my previously ordered multi Apollo spray pack, I was reminded of the Kilo (after finding the Apollo was now temporarily unavailable) and and ordered it in quantity. After receiving it I noticed it had the same great scent I remember, that will always linger on clothes (always spray on clothes, NOT on skin), but also noticed it had been repackaged in a new kind of spray can. Knowing what I do about the corporate world of business I immediately compared the content amount to the previous can that still sat discarded in my bathroom trash container. Sure enough AXE had reduced the amount of content in the can by an ounce and redesigned it so that side by side it APPEARED to be almost the same size. Of course the slight reduction in price doesn't match up to the per ounce value (ROUGHLY previous price of $4.25 for 5oz vs now approximately, $4.34 per can; though buying in quantity as I did can reduce it up to$2.86 per can when purchasing an 8 pack). This is just the nature of the corporate beast. Promised profits + general greed = f the consumer.

None the less, if you need it I'd recommend buying it in quantity before they reduce it to 3 ounces. It's still a great product and a good value, when purchased in bulk.

title: I LOVE these!
text:
I just have to say it, I HATE WEARING A MASK! I have glasses that fog up terribly with most all traditional fabric masks. I have low-grade asthma and wearing a mask where I am breathing in my own air makes me very anxious and I end up being unable to breathe well at all. Thankfully I found that I didn't have to worry about any of that once I began wearing a face shield instead of a fabric mask. Because I began working in retail around the holidays and was required to wear a mask for 8 hours a day, I was able to survive with the shield. But I really didn't like the way that I had to wear the elastic band around my head over my hair, and it was much like wearing two pair of glasses, since I had to view the world through my glass lenses as well as the plastic of the shield.

One day I saw a woman in my store wearing one of these masks and I immediately became a fan. I found this seller online and I can't believe how much I love wearing this! It feels almost like I have no mask on at all - in fact, I was once heading into a store and the greeter there offered to give me a mask, not realizing that I had this one on until I got closer to her. It is great that you can sanitize this between wearings very easily without having to put it through the laundry, and I just keep it hanging from my rearview mirror and use hand wipes to clean it.

However, there are a couple of things that I'd prefer on this mask. The plastic is a hard, formed plastic rather than a pliable one. I no longer work in retail and am no longer required to wear a mask at my new job, but I feel like if I had to wear this one 8 hours a day like before, it might break within a few days. Although it does not fog up my glasses at all, it actually fogs up when I am wearing it outside. Once I enter the store and an ambient temperature though, the fog goes away and it is clear once again. I am sure that this mask would not be allowed on an airplane, but then neither are many other styles of masks out there. The other thing that is a bit bothersome is that when you are talking or singing with this mask on, it moves with the movement of your mouth since it holds onto your face with a chin guard that keeps the plastic away from your mouth. But all in all it is worth it to be able to breath and remain compliant with the current laws of my City regarding masks. For those reasons though, I gave it a 4 rather than a 5 rating.

title: A beauty industry expert's professional opinion
text:
Not all Obagi products are made at the same place -- but i found out that this formula is made by one of the top skincare labs in the US--one that manufactures high-end dermatologist and clinical skincare brands on the market today. So knowing this, i knew there would be *some* efficacy to this product. I actually LIKE that ingredients are straightforward and not full of fluff:

Water (Aqua), Dipropylene Glycol, Ethoxydiglycol, Caffeine, Malonic Acid, Zinc Carbonate, Arginine, Laureth-9, Copper Carbonate Hydroxide, Hydroxyethylcellulose, Sodium Hydroxide, Phenoxyethanol, Ethylhexylglycerin

To be honest--if you're looking to reduce eye puffiness and dark circles, this won't do much. If found no visible evidence of that in my use. BUT--it's really good at minimizing fine lines, plumping up the skin, and returning elasticity to the skin. That's why it's called "Elasti-derm", to help coax the skin into being more hydrated, refined, and pliant, thus reducing the signs of lines. Obagi's main active to do that is malonic acid, and I give a big thumbs up to the addition of arginine-- a powerful delivery vehicle to help drive the malonic acid further into the skin for more efficacy. As many in the skincare industry know, anything with arginine helps make the active ingredient even more "active".

The stainless steel ball is not just a "feel good" gimmick -- it actually helps to massage this serum into the delicate eye skin, further pushing the ingredients into the dermis. After using an entire bottle of this product, i definitely experienced a reduction in the signs of my fine lines. the skin was plumped up and the lines less visible, plus the texture more refined. Used in conjunction with a good eye cream and alternating with Vitamin C serum, this is a great addition to any anti-aging regimen. I would surely purchase again.

I take off one star because I do not like the plastic packaging, as glass is the safest material for stability, and plastic has a tendency to shorten the shelf life of a formula. Plus plastics are not as safe we think.

title: Best Hair Removal Experience EVER
text:
I have tried and owned it all: razors, electric razor, the original Epilady back more than 25 years ago, the Smooth Away system, Nair, and a really nice hot wax kit. I am very sensitive to pain, but my desire to be done with hassling with hair and mess overrode that. I expected less from this epilator than it has delivered. Yes, there is what I would call discomfort with the first and most ambitious hair removal, but I suggest that you do use the "massaging" head with it. That DOES work for a first timer. I now prefer the regular attachment for efficiency, but the massager is great on the remaining sensitive areas. I am flabbergasted at how many hairs it finds. A GREAT feature is the "Smart Light" that shows me the tiniest hairs. Very satisfying to watch them disappear as the epilator goes over them. It is also a very easy to clean device! I ran out of hairs to epilate (got a little addicted to the perfection of the process), so am now waiting it out. I have had smooth, smooth legs for DAYS. Worth every cent of the 119 dollars I spent. (Note: I've not tried it in the shower yet, as I'm happy about being able to set out a towel and watch tv and have a snack while I do this thing. You are not trapped in the bathroom.)

Tips: If some hairs are shorter than 2 mm and just can't get picked up, they are not visible in any case. Wait a day, and the epilator will get them. DO exfoliate. I recommend the "bath gloves" that you can get at the grocery store, but the Body Shop has terrific exfoliating bath gloves. If a hair is stubbornly being missed, be sure to stretch the skin tight right at that area, and try again.

text:

I was very, very skeptical... my implant (# 4 upper tooth) failed and i needed to wait 4 months before they will do another one. So, i decided to try this product. despite the contradictory reviews all over amazon, i bought it. the price is ok... it took me some time to understand how it is working *yea, you need to be creative on HOW you manage to place it... but, when you find your way, it does work. the good thing is, you put the fake tooth with the mold in the hot water and you can re-use it, if you didnt manage to insert it for the 1st, second, third time .

I do recommend finding a good youtube video for instructions. I was totally surprised, that it worked. definitely, it does not look 100% like the tooth that you are missing.. but it does serve the purpose: you feel comfortable talking and smiling, and a little bit of imperfection in the fake tooth is NOTHING in comparison with having a hole in your teeth ... I even didn't notice that it has been already three months since I started using it.
I am replacing teh fake tooth every day, as i am quick now with that. Other people i know replace it very two or three days. Dont chew on that side and dont during incredibly hot coffee/tea.

title: I love this toothbrush, but...
text:
1. I don't understand these reviews that complain about getting water into the battery compartment and corroding the batteries. I've never had this problem. It would seem that one would have to be really careless for this to happen. Don't submerge it or pour water over it, and you should be fine.
2. Don't worry about battery life. Get some Eneloop rechargeables, and swap them out anywhere from a couple weeks to a couple months and you'll be fine.
3. This does such a good job, my dentist assumes I'm flossing like I'm supposed to be. I'm not. I do use a waterpic, but only a couple times a week these days. My dentist gave me an A+ on my last visit (part of this is because of the fluoride rinse that's been helping strengthen my teeth, but that's another review).

So now to the reason I only gave it three stars.

I had one of these that we bought years ago. I don't remember how long, but it's been probably 5 years. I'm not exactly sure, but it's been awhile. It's always worked great and still does. We finally got tired of sharing, and when we saw they were only $20 on Amazon we got another one.

This second one has had to be replaced under warranty twice in about a year and a half. It just stopped working, both times. No corrosion in the battery compartment or anything. The unit looks pristine, it just stopped working.

The first one lasted about 8 months. The second one only about 6 months.

So while this is a great product (functionally) and I would still likely buy it again if my current one died out of warranty (can't beat $20) I'm getting concerned about the quality. Here's hoping third time's a charm.

title: it's ok but I would not recommend it
text:
It was tough to decide whether or not to give this product one or two stars, but I gave it two because it doesn't completely suck, it's just not as good as other razors that aren't as expensive The manufacturer recommends waiting 21 days before deciding to keep this product or send it back. I would also give the same recommendation to people who are looking at purchasing this. I bought it because I needed to replace my old razor. My old Remington titanium R9710 was a good razor but it ripped the hair out of my neck area and left me with very irritated skin. The thing about my old razor is that it had floating heads and it handled long hairs pretty well if I was lazy and didn't shave. This new Arcitec worked very well when I first got it but I really wanted to try it out and only had stubble on my face at the time. It worked very well with short hairs and left me with no irritated skin on my neck.

Well I wanted to see what it would act like if I let my hair grow a little and it did not perform like I thought it would. It took a long time to shave and I had to go over the area multiple times in multiple directions and with different pressures just to get a few long hairs. This new head style has really been a downgrade because when you apply pressure, the heads seem to pull away from your face on the outside part of it and it makes it harder to shave. It was either that or the fact that it doesn't have a hair collection area. It fills up with hair rather quickly so maybe that has an impact on how well it shaves. Cleaning the unit was very simple but I think I would have the cleaning system of one of the speed XL models over this. You have to pop open three separate chambers rather than flip the whole head up to clean each blade. A nice feature of this razor is the tube trimmer. You can take the razor head right off and pop out the trimmer. There really isn't much else to say about the trimmer other than I thought it worked great.

Overall, this is a very nice looking razor, but the functionality of the razor itself is pretty bad. It does come with a nice travel case and charging stand as well. The travel case is made of hard plastic and does not have room for the charger, but it does have the capability to charge the razor, so you do not need to bring along the charging stand. If you want to try this product I would say go for it because Norelco has such a generous return policy and maybe you will like it better than I did. If you think you like the functions of this razor but really aren't sure about it, I would not recommend it because it doesn't work like I think a razor should (it takes a long time to shave and it doesn't work well on longer hairs). It looks nice and has nice features, but I think its functionality isn't worth the high price tag.

They are NOT duplicates; they are INTERFERENCE MICA COLORS which I am super appreciative that these were included! INTERFERENCE COLORS = (lol, look it up for a proper definition but, BASICALLY =) dual tone white micas; white from one angle, and an interference color, for instance; flashes of blue OR red OR purple etc...when you look at it from another angle.

AS PICTURED, I think there are only two duplicate colors (bronze & red brown) but, I knew that by carefully reviewing the photo prior to purchasing. They happen to be colors I use a lot of so, I am happy with this.

For those concerned that the packages are too similar in color, each are unique with a slightly different character.
Take for instance a few of the golds differ from a rich deep golden or bright & shiny like finish or have a very subtle green hue, etc.

Other colors offered that you may be wondering about also have these slight but, for some of us, important subtle differences.

I do wish there were more variations of the blues, yet, it's okay! This is an affordable sampling set, delivered fast & in tact. (zipper bags keep the cost down of this nice variety of samples. I use & reuse over & over the tip of plastic cutlery knives as my mica scoopers.)

I'm taking a wild guess...& it could be due to some regulations on certain color pigments...True Red seems a bit hard to come by also. Let's see how the included red does.

The same batteries also power my living room hi-fi, using a 12 Volt DC to 120 Volt AC (house current) inverter.

The point, the yearly savings are about $40 total in electric bill costs during the, say, five year life of the razor. The same battery bank also charges about 20 rechargeable D, AA, and AAA rechargeable common batteries using a similar DC power chord with a high quality 12 Volt DC fast charger.

title: Ridiculously overpriced, but the performance is decent.
text:
I am conflicted about this product, same as I am with the sister shampoo. I think it's a great product in terms of quality and performance; I really like that it's sulfate free and not filled with a bunch of additives. I have noticed that my hair is very soft as a result of using this mask, so I will give credit where credit is due in that regard. It smells good, and it hydrates well, which is what it promises to do. I have no qualms with the performance, packaging, concept, or marketing of the product.

I am docking two stars, however, for the price point. I am all for luxury products and I am happy to drop money on products that work. However I think that the price is grossly inflated for the performance of the product. While it's a nice product, it's nowhere NEAR to being a $32 hair mask. With prices like that you're definitely in the middle of high end, luxury pricing for haircare products. To give you a few examples you could be purchasing Bumble & Bumble, Oribe, R+Co, and Kerastase for a similar price. I think for a mask that is going to be used regularly you need to offer a reasonable price for the product, especially given the fact that there are stronger, higher performing luxury products on the market. I also think that the packaging and the container is a bit cheap looking, considering this is a $32 product. If I'm buying something so expensive I expect it to have some really nice packaging. I understand that they are meant to look like yogurt containers, however I think that it's a bit silly to have a nice cardboard packaging on the outside yet leave the container for the product itself looking so bare and unappealing.

While this is a good mask and I think it performs well, I don't see myself repurchasing this at the price it's currently listed at. I think that for the amount of product you receive (a small amount, especially for the price) a more reasonable cost would be $20.

title: Loving These Locs!
text:
[[VIDEOID:f6fe2bb4d18d1094a8c2136bc198cd5a]] I've always loved dreads, so when I saw these, I ordered them immediately! I hadn't known I could simply *install* dreads without having to grow my own hair long and then proceed to do whatever magic (and damage) was necessary to create dreads. As soon the first set of 12 arrived, I was thrilled; I also knew that 12 strands was nowhere near enough to cover my head so I ordered a second set. Each set came with a bag of random hair accessories as well as what looks similar to a crochet hook. The hook is ridiculously small, so I don't know if it's intended to pull the hair through the top loop or if it's to help maintain the dreads as they're washed and loosen up over time. There were no instructions, so after my first set arrived I scoured the Internet to find photos of loc styles as well as tutorials about how to install them. I've included a short video with this review to help people realize that the most difficult part will be installing these on the back of your head. (I don't have a fold-out mirror and I don't trust myself to do a good job, so I've got to find someone I trust to do the back of my head for me.)

While this is the first set of dreads I've handled, they're not stiff and they have no odor. (While researching dreads, I discovered that a lot of synthetic pieces have those issues but THESE do not! I mean, I loved the first set so much that I ordered another right away.) I don't plan to have my entire head in dreads, but if I did I could easily get away with only 3 to 4 sets (with leftovers) because my hair is really thin and I'd pull larger sections through the top loop as I braided each piece in.

The ends of the dreads look a little scraggly BUT I think that makes them look all the more authentic; in fact, I was surprised when I hopped back online and saw these are synthetic! The top of each has a black rubber band just below a loop of hair and you basically pull a section of your own hair through that top loop, split that hair into two sections (so with the dread and your own hair you have three separate sections). Get the dread close to your scalp, then simply braid the three sections together to secure the loc into place. You'll need a small rubber band to hold the sections together where they end and it's that simple! You can attach the little hair accessories wherever you choose.

If you've been wanting locs, these are an excellent value and the perfect way to see if the look is right for you. I do think they should come with instructions, but that doesn't take away from the perfect coloring, length, and texture!

title: Just Buy It!!! Worth Every Penny.
text:
This wig is absolutely beautiful! I will be buying this one again and again. This was my first time buying hair from Amazon. I'd put off trying Amazon wigs for years. But wow! Huge mistake. I didn’t have to cut layers into it or really do anything other than set it. The hair quality was outstanding. The unit was soft and silky, hardly any shedding, no tangling so far, and it’s next to impossible to tell it is synthetic. My head measures 22.5 inches around, so the cap size was a perfect fit for me. I am SO IN LOVE!!! For the record, the wig did NOT look like this straight out of the package but don’t be disappointed. It’s not a “shake and go” wig. You will have to customize it a little, but it isn't hard. It's pre-plucked but you may want to thin the hairline out a little more if you want to pull the hair off your face. But a beginner could easily customize this with minimal effort.

What I Did To Mine:

The curl pattern is loose. But be advised, if you brush this unit out, it will explode. You really have to condition it first and train it. I washed and conditioned mine with Silicon Mix and Silicon Mix Conditioner to wash out some of the dye and get it ready for training. I wouldn’t advise washing synthetic hair with any other product. Silicon Mix makes it silky so it feels and behaves like real hair. This hair does NOT respond well to curling irons. At all. The curls droop quickly, even if you wet roll it and put it under the dryer. This wig requires wet heat for lasting curls. So I rolled it up with FlexiRods, boiled a kettle of water and poured boiling water on each FlexiRod. The bigger the rod, the bigger the curl. I DID NOT soak the wig in boiling water. I just wanted enough heat to seal in a loose curl. If it boils too long, the curls get too tight and they frizz.

I let it air dry overnight. As I took out each rod, I moussed each curl with Cream of Nature Style and Shine Foaming Mousse to avoid frizz. For hold and definition, I used Cream of Nature Moisture & Shine Curl activator lotion to seal in the curl pattern made by the rods. I finger combed out the curls, brushed them out and then rolled them around my fingers with my Denman Brush for definition and to shape the curl pattern. This was the result. If the curls loosen, just spray some water on them and brush them back into shape. The curls are permanent until you wet heat the hair again for a different style. The first three pix are dry curls, but the rest are wet-look curls.

I thank you, Thank You, THANK YOU, Andria for an extremely satisfying first experience with your products. I will definitely be buying more!

title: THIS WORKS!!!
text:
okay, i wanted to try this out for a while before writing a review, so here's the scoop:
first impression was awful. i REALLY do not enjoy the smell of this product. the second thing i did after i opened the first one, was pull off the seals of the other two to see if they all had that odor, and they did. there's just a really strange underlying scent that i can't put my finger on, i read all the ingredients and nothing stuck out to me. it's hard for me to describe it, other than calling it a funk. and somehow even a month later, every time that i apply it, it feels like the smell kind of catches me off guard! it's assaulting my nose! but it does eventually dissapate. so there's that. BUT with that being said, this stuff is great, i can't even lie. i've struggled with finding good antiperspirants, and struggled even harder to find good natural deodorants. although i like staying away from aluminum, as most of us do, i just could not justify spending another dollar on a natural product that didn't work. i work outside two days a week, and since i'm in customer service, people are all up in my space, so i can't reek of B.O. for their sake. honestly though even when i wear antiperspirants, i don't feel like i feel as fresh as i should at the end of my shifts. i'm also going to note here that i've had quite a few reactions to different sticks or sprays that i've used, bumpy and extremely painful rashes that almost look like pimples, so bizarre! i have not experienced that once since using this product!! the only other reason why i would even consider knocking a star off, apart from the rank smell, is the price. holy moly is this stuff expensive!! hopefully they will be able to bring their cost down because it's extremely pricey!! but i love this stuff and will continue to use!! praying they find a way to fix the smell!! 🤞🥲

title: Messy But Fun
text:
This is a fun set to have around for parties or kids crafting. The way it works is you place a stencil on your skin, brush on body glue with the brush attached to the glue bottle (much like nail polish), sprinkle some of the glitter on and brush off the excess with a soft make up brush (brush not included, but you can get one from the dollar store). Make sure the glue is thin, or the glitter gets clumpy, and brush the glitter off onto a piece of paper so you can dump the glitter back into the container. The kit comes with 2 bottles of "star glue", 36 glitter colors in a handy plastic case, 135 tattoo stencils, 2 pages of rhinestones and 4 pages of temporary tattoos.

Now the temporary tattoos will last up to seven days depending on where you put them. They fade much easier on your hand since there is a lot of hand washing usually going on in seven days. The glitter tattoo is only going to last as long as no moisture gets on the skin. It's basically gel glue, so it's not waterproof. You can expand the kit by buying regular stencils from a hobby shop like Hobby Lobby. You can also refill the kit by buying body glue off Amazon or gel glue (cheaper) wherever you buy glue, and buying fine glitter off Amazon or the dollar store. BTW, it's glitter, so expect a bit of a mess, but the results are worth it.

title: Sweet Dreams
text:
I love the Laura Mercier line, but I've found the sweet-scented lotions, like Creme Brulee, to be overpowering. I'm willing to keep trying, though, and I'm glad I did. I love the Ambre Vanille Souffle Body Crème

Ambre Vanille Souffle Body Creme comes in a heavy, clear glass jar. The silver lid easily screws off and on and the label is elegant and attached to the front of the jar. It’s pretty and I love having it on my counter.

I'm used to the thick texture of body butter, so I was surprised by the lightness of the Souffle Body Creme. It has the texture and appearance of whipped cream--only it smells much richer! The creme goes on a little white, but once it's rubbed in you can no longer see it. My skin feels soft and smooth and not at all greasy

I find this fragrance to be much more subtle than the Creme Brulee Hand Crème, but it’s still pretty strong. I'm not certain what Amber smells like, but I definitely smell the coconut, vanilla, and sandalwood. As much as I like this fragrance, I do think it's too much for me to wear during the day, so I've switched to using it at night. I drift off to sleep to the scent of Ambre Vanille

I suspect that the Ambre Vanille fragrance isn't for everyone and at these prices, you really want to make sure that you love the scent before investing in it. The souffle texture is a nice change of pace from my usual body butter.

text:
This is the worst eyebrow pencil I’ve tried at this price, and it’s even worse than the e.l.f. version that’s similar. I know that’s dramatic but the reason why I wanted to write this review is because I’m just so frustrated with the quality compared to the price. It’s just not okay!

I’ve been using the nyx precision brow pencil, but this was a few dollars cheaper at ulta at the time and so I got it because the nyx one is like 10 bucks. My brows are the makeup I wear most consistently, so I’m always trying different brow pencils to try to cut down on the cost. But I go back to nyx every time. Maybe the morphe one is okay but it’s pretty hard and waxy so not really. Now I know the importance of the extra two dollars for the nyx.

This pencil is so soft, it wears down so quickly and also because of how soft it is, it’s not precise at all. And it’s not pigmented either, so I end up using a larger amount of product because of that. To do both my brows, and I fill them in pretty lightly, I use about 1/8” of product each time. The nyx one I use less than 1/16” and it’s more pigmented.

I would compare this to the elf one in terms of pigmentation and texture. Except the elf one is like $3. So at this price point I expected it to be way better than something that’s less than half its price.

And after using it a few times, the spoolie end came off when I was trying to take the cap off to use it. The main body of the pencil cracked on that end. So now I have to use a spoolie from another brow pencil, good thing I have one. And this has just been on my desk, not banging around in a makeup bag or anything like that. So definitely don’t get this if you need to take it places it can’t handle it.

This is one of the few times I would return a makeup product, it’s just so egregiously bad.

text: I was really hoping this product would work and I wasn't disappointed.  It's amazing how FAST it works on gel polish!  In just around 2 minutes it lifts one to two layers of polish -sure beats the 20-30 minutes of soaking it off with acetone!  I expect the people who didn't have any results didn't follow the cardinal rule of removing gel polish - break the top layer of polish first (with a file).  If you do that, this product works just as it should.  If you don't first remove that top layer of clear polish, you won't get anywhere, no matter what method you use.  It even tells you to do that on the little paper included in the box.  I expect the people who didn't have results didn't do their do diligence and read the paper. By the time I remove my gel polish I normally have 5 or more coats on, so I use this product two times to get most of the polish off and then gently file off the rest. It's great when you just need to repair one or two nails and take off the polish completely.  Makes the repair very fast and easy.  I will definitely continue to buy this product to remove my gel polish from now on.

title: Large toiletry bag with some nice features
text:
The first thing you notice about this toiletry bag is its size. This thing is huge. It is much larger than it appears in the pictures. The size isn’t a bad thin though, if you have the space for it in your bag. It has plenty of space to put any items you want into it. It comes with a main see-through compartment and two removable smaller see-through compartments. The small compartments have Velcro on the back that holds them into place. They can be removed easily, in situations such as going through TSA security. On the top of the bag, there is a metal hook, which can be used to hang the bag. This is extremely helpful for travelers who commonly stay in places, which don’t have much counter space, such as hostels. At first, I imagined hanging the bag might cause the bottom bags to fall off, if the contained heavy objects weight. However, this does not seem to be an issue. My favorite aspect about this bag is the silicone travel bottles that come with it. They are awesome. These things won’t spill under any normal conditions. The tops of them stay sealed tight in the bag and I have yet to see one of them leak. They also have a cool feature on the cap that can be twisted to display what is in them. The labels that can be displayed on the caps are “Shamp.”, “Cond.”, “Lotion”, “Soap” and “Sun”. In addition, there are several blank spaces that can be filled in with your own labels, if you want.

Overall I think this is a good bag, large enough to hold anything you might need, and has some nice features (bottles, hanger, removable pouches). The only reason I did not give this five stars is the price. I do not think $39.99 is a good price point for the product. I believe it should retail in the $20-$30 dollar range.

As a disclaimer, I did receive this product for free for a fair review.

text:
I have thick, coarse..wavy hair. I have REALLY thick coarse...wavy hair. My hair is not that long, but since I have so much of it...when it starts to grow past a certain length..it can longer pomp up and slick straight the way i would want it to. I have tried Layrite (strongest hold), Imperial (strongest hold), American crew (strongest hold), Suavecito (regular & firme/strong hold)...I've also used some Murray's but that s*** just brought the waves out even more.

JS sloan has a very strong smell that I am not fond of...this product is definitely not worth me buying again. It may be good for peole with thin to somewhat thick hair...if you have really thick hair & coarse wavy hair then i'm sure you must use an extra amount of pomade to try and give the look you would want...but this product has an overpowering smell...i feel like my coworkers can smell it when I'm talking to them.

I've wanted to try other pomades, but when I hear that people with thick coarse wavy hair has had better experiences with the pomades that I tried and did not like..i'd figure there was no use in wasting my money.

I always keep on going back to Suavecito firme/strong hold.

It's the only thing that works best for my hair and gives the look (The closest as possible) that I would want to achieve.

for people with such hair, you must come to the realization that as your hair gets longer, it may become more difficult to achieve a hair style that's more suitable for people with straight hair (thin or thick).

Even so, I'd recommend Suavecito firme/strong hold...it's a very good price for a good product.

Also--I noticed that some people reviewed it by saying they had thick hair with great experiences...be advised that that not everyone has the same level of hair thickness as yours...to them it might be thick...but to you it might not..

I feel that I may have a thicker set of coarse/wavy hair...I'm going back to Suvaceto.

title: Smooth Teeth Afterwards
text:
Your teeth feel very smooth after ever session with the Oral-B Professional Care products. The question is which one to get? If you have sensitive gums, then I recommend the more expensive versions (3000 or higher) since they have sensitivity settings. If you are sharing the device with others in your household who may not have the same gum sensitivity as yourself, again, I recommend version 3000 or higher since you may not fully understand others' sensitivity levels. Plus the 3000 model (or higher) comes with a covered container for holding multiple brushes which will prevent the family from misplacing or swapping the heads.

I own the Oral-B Professional Care 1000 Power Toothbrush and now the 4000. I was perfectly happy with the 1000, but I had the opportunity to acquire the 4000 so I thought why not? The 4000 though gives you different modes as well as a easily seen red light letting you know if you are pushing too hard. I didn't really need these bells and whistles, but they don't hurt. I've always thought that if this kind of tooth brush was painful then I either need to stop pushing so hard or buy softer heads. That's just me, but I know others prefer having the feedback.

It's hard for me to spend $100 plus on a toothbrush, so if money is a concern, I recommend the 1000 or the 3000. I don't really need those extra feedback lights, and often I have to change the 4000 to polish mode to get it to behave more like the 1000 (which is ideally what I want). Note for me that the grip of the 1000/3000 feels better in the hand as well due to its smaller size compared to the 4000.

I further recommend you order at least two different kinds of heads so you can figure out the style you like. The 4000 does come with one head, and this is the type that integrates some sort of rubber/plastic in addition to having bristles (e.g., FlossAction). I think I prefer the heads that are made up of only traditional bristles but heads with the added plastic do seem to polish more.

Whether you get Braun or Phillips, do your teeth a favor and get a power toothbrush. Once you use these power toothbrushes, you'll never want to go back to the manual way.

text:
I bought this sunblock for a circus trip to the Caribbean, and it's perfect. The colors are thick and bright, and the "chapstick" style containers make it easy to apply without getting your fingers all gross. I promised my sister that she and her kids could have the rest when I'm back from the trip, and they were extremely excited. You can make a lot of neat designs with this many colors - much more than with the old tubes of nothing but florescent colors. If you have a small makeup brush (or a set of small brushes), it would be pretty easy to use this for creating more detailed "face painting" designs.

I really don't have any complaints about this sunblock. One of the tubes did sort of break, but it was easy to snap the piece back on, and it worked fine after that. The color stays put all day, and it doesn't sweat off or fade in water like a lot of sunblock does. At around $12-13 for 8 tubes, it's a better value than a lot of regular chapstick-style sunblocks...and it's fun!

title: Treat your face (or legs) to a classy shave
text: For quite a while i have wanted to experience an open comb razor, particularly since I have understood that they are more effective against multi-day growth. Sometimes i go four or five days, if not more, between shaves and, in general I prefer to use my butterfly razors because i can open, remove the blade, and clean them quicker than standard two and three piece DB razors. Also I have learned the hard way that one should not rush when unscrewing and reattaching the head pieces to the handle to avoid stripping the threads. So i approached my initial experience with the Shash open comb with more a little curiosity and anticipation. Well, i was not disappointed. It moves through the stubble with ease and a quick rinse in water removes the residue. I was pleasantly surprised with the ease and facility with which the razor travelled over my face. I must admit that I was very cautious the first time and even took precautions that I normally forego with other razors. I didnt spend much time on my chin and nose area which are my most problematic regions. For those I prefer to use smaller handled razors where I can have better control and access. But on those fairways which are a straight shoot downward to my chin bones, I was mowing the hair down like an Eastern European peasant harvesting grain. The razor also worked well on the straighaways from chin down to the neck.  It should be admitted that I have yet to put the razor to the ultimate test of a week-long beard growth, but i do not anticipate any increased difficulties with the later. The open comb facilitates easy cleaning whether rinsing in a bowl or under the faucet. As for the razor itself, it appears to be well constructed. I would guess it is a product of Germany which augurs well for precision instruments. It is probably the longest handled razor i own yet it functions well. It is reputed to be made of brass and chrome which should guarantee long life. The handle is striated enough to preclude slippage even when wet.  As a bonus it comes with three boxes of Astra blades (about 15 I believe) plus an alum stick and pre-shave oil. I can't vouch for the oil since I don't normally use it bit I can't see how it would hurt. And the entire ensemble is tidely packaged in a neat and attractive box. Certainly a fine addition to one's own toiletries collection and definitely something to consider for the upcomung gift season. Recommended.

My daily routine is to massage a quality beard balm followed by quality beard oil into the beard and skin. I then brush my beard with a boar bristle brush and comb my beard for a couple of minutes. I comb periodically through the day and generally do the Balm/oil massage in the morning and again after a bath or shower in the evening. All pimples, chaffing, beardruff, itching and irritation have gone away since performing this routine.

This comb gives a therapeutic feeling and the teeth do not scrape the skin like plastic combs do. I purchased this comb for my son who also wears a thick beard. He does not and probably will not carry this comb in his pocket for risk of losing or breaking it.

I stated in the video that instructions were included but I was mistaken. The sheet is on how to leave a review. I guess you don’t really need instructions with a comb. Durp! If you are interested in a thicker tooth spacing on one side and thinner tooth spacing on the other also check out Dream Bear’s comb.

Why the rating?
This is a high quality grooming piece which feels great on the beard and skin, and is a pleasure to use. This comb is easily a 5 star product. Overall, I am happy with the purchase. This product was received, and tested during a promotional period at a discount. I have attempted to give a thorough, comprehensive, objective, and honest review; I hope it has been helpful to you.

text:
I am always walking around barefoot. Not a big fan of socks, except in closed toe shoes, hence the dry heels. I used this religiously every night for about 1.5 weeks. I put it on, then put on socks at night (this is torture for me, by the way). While it is working and my heels are nicer, this has not "healed" the cracks (which were and are not that great or noticeable). It's definitely made my heels look better but no "healing" there.
I have also been having trouble with an awful looking elbow for years (cracked, bleeding skin and nothing's been able to heal it). I put this on and it's helped tremendously. It healed in within a few days. The only trouble is that I have to keep on using it, otherwise the dry skin comes back.
I guess the skin on the heels is so much thicker that it may take longer to heal than the elbows. I don't know. I have used other products for my feet and they work just as well as this.
In the end, paying $9.95 for this little thing just to use on my elbows - I don't know that it's worth it. As for the feet, you can get a $2 tube from Walgreens and you're better off.

U P D A T E: Three weeks of continuous use, every single day, sometimes three to four times a day, has not "improved" my cracked heel (I only have issue with one). It still works for my elbow, but if I miss a day, my dry elbow comes back with a vengeance. I will definitely not be purchasing this again.

2nd UPDATE: I've been using this for almost two months now, as directed. I am almost out of this product and nothing has really improved. The cracks are still there (just softer looking). In fact, another issue has propped up; tiny bits of skin on the bottom of both my feet are "peeling off" so badly that it bleeds under them. I have stopped using this product and I am going to see a podiatrist. I don't know if it's a direct result of using this, but I haven't used anything else on my feet other than the heel repair.

title: Why do I like this thing?
text:
I have used this for about a month and here is my take on it.

Cons:

1. I get a better shave with an old Sensor II Gillette razor.

2. I agree with another reviewer who complained about the recharger. It is flimsy and I am never certain the razor will stay in the holder. It looks and feels and works cheap.

3. I have a handlebar moustache and sideburns. Shaving near either doesn't work. Nor does the trimmer attachment work for me. I end up cleaning up with my trusty blade.

4. The gel packs work, but also seem cheap. I mostly end up using my normal shaving gel (Edge).

Pros:

1. I like the fact that I can use it wet.

2. The charge lasts a very long time, and the recharge is very quick.

3. It is very convenient to use. I find myself shaving more often than I did with a blade just because it is easy to use. For example I find myself shaving quickly before my wife comes home. Never did that before. :-)

4. The ergonomics are good. Good fit in my hand. Good balance. Easy glide over face, neck, chin.

5. I hav oily skin and find I get a better shave before washing my face rather than afterwards.

Conclusion: I like the thing and decided to keep it, but I will be darned if I know why. Oh, and I just truned 67 and haven't had an electric razor since the 60's.

The straightening brush has two different color options - light pink and white. The brush heats up quickly and the brush bristles are not hot to the touch. Temperature can be displayed in Celsius or Fahrenheit and the brush has an automatic shut off feature if it hasn't been used in 60 minutes. Auto shut off is a must have feature for me!! It really is as simple as brushing your hair. My hair is kind of short at the moment (above shoulders). The brush straightened the ends of my hair fine, but I struggled a little closer to the scalp. I really think it is because the length of my hair. I haven't given up on the idea of getting all of my hair straight. I've seen some great pictures on here with amazing results. I also think its super easy to be accustomed to the immediate (and damaging) gratification of a flat iron. Its too easy to twist and turn any way and have instant results. I can only imagine how much better the straightening brush is for the overall health of your hair.

title: Great for mixing oil blends for rollerballs
text:
I use fractioned oils to make rollerballs for my oil blends and for a carrier for various topical uses.
I have been wanting to recreate a muscle cramp relief oil from a major essential oil club and lucked up with a copycat recipe. These oils are over $30 for 5ml and, while it works great and smells amazing, I just couldn’t bring myself to spend that knowing that I have a box full of single oils.
When I saw this bottle with the pump, I knew it was time to try my hand and mixing this recipe. I had a few other rollerballs that I wanted to make (some decongestant and immune boosters since it’s getting to that time of year) so I inserted the pump and got to work. The oils mixed VERY well and the pump on the bottle made it very easy to dispense just enough into the small rollerball opening. That is SUCH a nice feature – manufacturer, please don’t remove that from the item. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve spilled my fractioned oil everywhere because it was difficult to contain since it’s thin.
Once I had worked through the 5 rollerballs for my family needs, I had enough room in the bottle to make a BIG batch of the massage oil with the rest of the fractioned oil. IT WORKED!!! I’m soooooo happy with this bottle of fractioned oil. I can easily pump out what I need to work out my sore muscles and apply to hubby’s back (he has scholosis and other degenerative issues). I would highly recommend for anyone wanting to use fractioned oil for their essential oil uses.

title: Will it outperform my 7 year old Norelco?
text:
I am generally happy with my new Norelco 7180XL, it is nice to have a new shaver, it is amazingly quiet, and gives a close and quick shave.

But I feel that Norelco needs to improve both their instruction manual, and their customer support. Neither of these were in tune with my first experience with the 7180XL, as far as initial charging, and what the green charging light and red low battery light were doing.

The manual calls for a 12 hour initial charge before using the shaver. When fully charged, the green light is supposed to blink. Well, on my initial charge, the light started blinking after 30 minutes. I did continue the charge for 12 hours anyway, the green light blinking the whole time.

I called Norelco support, and was informed the manual was not correct, and that I had not damaged my shaver by completing the 12 hour charge. But no further explanation.

Then I started using the shaver, and after just 2 shaves, the red low battery light came on. I went back to the Norelco website, and found a page on charging that said if the shaver did that, you should use it until the motor stops. They omit the obvious next step of charging it in these instructions, but say you will have no problem with the red light coming on too soon after following their directions.

Well, I have done that, and it remains to be seen if my new Norelco will eventually sort itself out and work right.

I must say I have my doubts after this initial experience, that it will last as long as my 7 year old model 5841XL did. I've used Norelco shavers for about 40 years, and never had any problems like this.

title: Do not buy during the summer months!
text:
These Live Bearded scents always take some getting used to; the combination of aromas are not as simple and straightforward as they seem. They never seem to smell quite like I expect, but I do tend to get used to them.

My beard is crazy. It literally grows in ten different directions and refuses to lay straight without a lot of coaxing.

This butter does a really nice job of conditioning my beard and taming fly-aways. I also find that it imparts some sculptability so that I can give my beard a little shape. I have to follow a bit of a routine in order to get it to cooperate, however.

I start the week out with a clean, freshly shampooed beard. I then warm it up with a hair dryer, to the point that it is damp, but not wet. I take a liberal amount of butter and rub it on my hands, warming it up, then I work it into my beard evenly. I use the hair dryer again with the flat concentrator attachment and a round brush to coax it into place. I have to brush it straight up and out first, which I find helps to straighten out the wavy parts, and then brush it into the final shape that I want. I also use a boar's-hair brush on my cheeks to get the fly-aways to lie flat. Once it is laying how I like, I use the cold button on the hair dryer to set it. I then do not wash it again for several days, (depending on how much I sweat or spill food/beverages), and only apply about half the amount of butter in the morning, though the brushing and drying routine remains the same.

I have found that this butter really does help my beard to keep its shape. It has a little bit of holding power, like you might expect from a pommade, but it is extremely light and clean, unlike pommade which tends to be sticky.

This is a great product, and one of the main reasons that I have kept using it is how well it works for me and the value/quantity when compared to other brands.

I will keep trying the other scents till I find one that I like.

Just a word of caution, don't buy this in the heat of the summer. The product I received had clearly melted and the resolidified, making one big solid mass of butter. It is described as being gritty and malleable, which I have experienced with previous purchases of this product. It still seemed to work alright, but was more difficult to use.

title: Powder gives light wash of color. Good for someone who doesn’t need too much.
text:
A little while back I got an eyebrow stamp kit like this and loved it! The only thing I wished was that the eyebrow stamp was a little thinner. When I saw this kit and saw the stamp looked a lot thinner than the one I had, I had to try it!

This comes with the brow stamp, 24 brow stencils, and 4 spoolie brushes.

Theres a whopping 24 eyebrow stencils included in this kit! That’s crazy! So, I’m sure most everyone can find a shape that they like for their brows among these stencils. Unlike most kits that have brow stencils like these, these have adhesive backing that sticks to you. Most kits I’ve gotten like these the stencils are plastic, so reusable. I like that they stick because you don’t have to worry about holding them perfectly in place while also trying to use the stamp to fill in your brows and worry about it moving some. But, I don’t like that they aren’t really reusable like this since once you pull off the backing and stick them on, they won’t stick anymore.

The first time I tried a brow powder stamping kit I wasn’t expecting much. I kind of expected this to make ugly, thick, blocky looking eyebrows. But, this actually works great! The product in the stamp is powder, so it creates a nice, light color, and you can dab more to build it up if you want. Once you use the spoolie, it looks pretty natural. You can also add pencil to if you wanted.

I don’t have thick brows, but I don’t have extremely sparse brows. My brows are thinner, where you can see skin poking through, but there’s basically an even amount of hair all the way across. I used to just leave my brows be, but when I do a full face of makeup I do feel like my brows need a little something. So, I started doing my brows. I usually do a little tinted brow gel. It usually gives enough tint to make them look a little fuller and complete, but not so much where they look too thick. I feel like since I’m just starting to do my brows, whenever I have them filled completely I think they look too thick and weird 😂 So, I like a middle area. So, using this stamp works well for me. If I’m doing full glam, I like to apply it to get a kind of light wash of color. Then, I’ll kind of go over the tail a little with some more powder to darken it a little more. Then, I’ll take a brow pencil and do a few kind of hair like strokes in the front. Sometimes I’ll go in and do some brow gel if I feel they need more defined. This fills them out nicely, makes them look complete, but doesn’t make them look too dark or full. If I am doing a more natural look, I’ll just use the brow powder in the stamp. I do feel that there isn’t a ton of product that comes out and I’m not sure how much product is in the stamp. I don’t mind that not a lot comes out, I actually prefer it. But, if you wanted more product, it might be kind of annoying for you.

Overall, I think this is a nice little set! It is a nice way to try different brow shapes to see what you like for yourself. The product works well. The brow powder looks natural and lasts nicely in the brows. I would definitely recommend this for someone who isn’t sure about their brow shape - what they like best on their face, what shape works best, how to fill in brows, etc. This set will help with those things! If you’re someone that just likes a little wash of color and fuller, more filled out brows, this would help with that. If you’re someone who likes a lot of color in the brows, you might not like this since it just gives a wash of color. So, I would recommend it but only if you’re someone who wants to try out different brow shapes to get an idea of what works for you or if you’re someone who likes a light wash of color throughout their brows.

title: Not good. Maybe okay for lefties.
text:
I almost never write negative reviews, but I had this set in my wishlist for weeks waiting for it to come back in stock and unfortunately I’m just not happy with them. The set I received only has 3-4 of the designs pictured which would be okay if they were of good quality, but they’re not. My set looks like horn and doesn’t have any raised lines down the sides which would indicate that they’re molded plastic, but they could simply have been sanded down to get rid of that.
Unlike other carved hair sticks I have, these are flat on one side and therefore you cannot see the dragon, bird, etc. from both directions.. Because of this, they only look good with the carved side out and most of them need to be inserted into the bun from the left to achieve this. If you’re left handed they might be okay but that’s very awkward for me and not the way I usually make my buns. Quality hair sticks that are the same on both sides are much better because they look great no matter which direction you choose to use them, as well as from the front and the back of your head. In addition to being decorative on one side and flat on the other, several of them are curved in such a way that if I were to put them in with the right side facing out they are curved away from my head rather than towards it, making them even more awkward to use. I don’t know if they’re made this way or if they warped during shipping, which would indicate plastic.
Overall, I’m unhappy with half of them and the others are mediocre at best, so they’re not the great value I thought they were. There are other sets of carved wood hair sticks that I’ve purchased here which are fantastic, as well as other carved horn sticks that are gorgeous and functional. The only way I can really use these is to make a bun that’s held in place with pins and then add one of these as a mediocre looking decoration. They’re just not very good at holding my long, thick hair up on their own. There are much better choices out there. Not recommended.

title: coming from someone whose had pro 28 full body laser removal treatments and 50 hrs of electrolysis
text:
Needless to say i have xp with hair removal. I was never really a super hairy but loved the feeling of being totally hairless from head to toe.

With all the sessions and hrs i barley have any hair but do have some spots on thighs, arms and other spots, that are fairly light even with all the professional laser treatments and electrolysis. IPL aka this device is NOT the go-to treatment for hair reduction but it does work.

Firstly, you need to use an electric razor or standard razor on the areas your zapping. Freshly showered, no oils or lotions on skin. If you dont feel heat your not killing hair follicles. The laser targets the pigment in the hair and absorbs the heat, so as they stated vampire skin, dark hair gets the best results.

If you have never gotten any sort of pro hair removal your hair is going to be fuller and courser. Like the subject heading states, ive had 28 full body laser hair removal treatments aka real hair removal that leaves you with red bumps, plus hrs of electrolysis and I still have hair grow back.

People it takes a long time to remove hair! This is not designed to be a one zap and the hair is gone. It will grow back finer and weaker, until it eventually is killed off. It literally takes years.

I zap each spot 5 times on the highest setting. The heat will build on each subsequent zap, meaning im actually hitting follicles. I would not recommend this if you have course hair or never had pro hair removal - build up to that, but this device is a nice supplement to the pro hair removal. It will never replace it and will take longer. For me its perfect and thats why i gave it 5 stars.

Once you zap the hair you should see a reaction, raised bumps, some redness, along the bikini line for example its very noticeable since the hair is courser - that means its working. It takes about 10 -14 days for the zapped hair to push its way out. Its not instant, the hair still remains in the follicle. You can expedite this by lightly exfoliating in the bath or shower. You may see little black spots in the follicle where the hair has been zapped and effectively targeted.

Hair grows in cycles, doing this every week is pointless, if the hair is not in the growth phase you cant kill it. Every 4 weeks, multiple zaps per spot and the hair WILL fall out and come back weaker. Different areas have different growth cycles but 4 weeks is a good middle ground.

This is used for hair reduction. If you want permanent (still takes multiple treatments( you need electrolysis.

If you want faster hair reduction result you need to use laser only found at the dermatologist or reputable laser spa. IPL is not laser treatment. This is not going to ever replace that. A combination of all three over 3 or 4 years will leave you hairless, so keep your expectations realistic.

Ok. So let me start by saying that until last month I had virgin hair. I went to a professional stylist to get my tips dyed rainbow colors. He used 3 different brands. One had stayed in nicely, the other two washed out in one wash with color safe shampoo and I was left with bleached tips and some random blue strands. So I decided to do it myself. I used splat beach however because there were several tips that my stylist had left untouched. I have black hair and the bleach lightened it to a medium blonde in about an hour (I wrapped the tips in tin foil to keep it off my skin) plus it didn't fry my hair! I then colored chunks of hair in random order using all 6 dyes. I wrapped the tips in tin foil again, put a plastic bag over my head and waited 3 hours. After removing the tin foil and washing my hair in cold water (which ran clear after 5 minutes at the most) I towel dryed my hair (the towel wasn't stained) and lo and behold. All the splat colors were vibrant and beautiful and one of the MP colors didn't even turn out. Those chunks are still bleach blonde. I love this stuff.
Now then. A few things to note. Even with 6 color packets on my counter I didn't make a mess. Nothing got stained. Nothing dripped. I just used latex gloves and a whole lotta patience. The stuff is pretty thick so if you're careful you can do this without staining your forehead :)

bee pollen granules

text: One of the best exfoliating moisturizers I’ve used... and I’ve tried many over the years of attempting to solve what dermatologists referr to as keratosis pilaris or “KP,” for short. It’s effective in exfoliating so if using daily my advice would be to be careful applying often in more sensitive areas such as behind the knees, inside of elbow, anywhere skin tends to be thinner and exfoliation can cause tenderness, sensitivity, etc. I most often use this exfoliating moisturizer after laser treatments that tend to make my skin dry and rough as it renews post treatment and also laser hair removal treatments which produces similar post treatment skin conditions. I have combined with highly moisturizing skin conditioners to help soften and condition the newer, fresher skin that is revealed by the exfoliating properties of the product and definitely recommend a high SPF application daily as the fresh skin revealed will be sun sensitive. But taking these precautions you’ll be highly pleased with the effectiveness of this product and certainly beats scrubbing with a loofah or grainy scrub!

title: So weird!
text:
I never thought I would sing praise to a sponge made from konjac root. The first time I had heard of these type of sponges I thought it sounded kind of weird, yet interesting. The only experiences I have had with konjac root was when I would ingest it, in pill form, to aid in a fuller feeling belly. Gotta love diet hacks. Anyways, an offer came around for me to try a set of discounted sponges for review. I thought, “these seem crazy and awkward. I must try them!”

The second I opened up the package to take a look my daughter gasped and said, “you got those? Can I have one? I have been wanting one so bad but they are expensive.” Well, with this brand, you get the same exact product that are sold in stores for insane amounts of dollars, for a screaming, affordable price. Two sponges come in a box so I handed one over to her. She was so excited.   I have slightly oily, sensitive and acne prone skin. My daughter has very oily and is also acne prone. This sponge cleanses and exfoliates without over drying. There is something about the way it holds water that feels really soft, gentle, yet effective. It is the direct opposite of what it feels like when it is dry - hard and scratchy. It does take some time to incorporate enough water into it, for the sponge to fully absorb the water, to be soft enough to use on your face. As you rub it across your skin it feels good and soft. I use light pressure while I use it for light exfoliation. I like the flat end for my forehead, cheeks and neck and the rounded end for my chin, nose, sides of nose and cheeks (near the side of my nose) and between my eyebrows. I feel like I am able to get a good cleansing in all areas. I use a small amount of cleanser. I use my hands to apply my cleanser and then use the sponge. My face is way smoother and makeup glides on nicely. My daughter reports the same thing. She loves the sponge and its benefits it gives.

My only slight criticism is the attached string. I do not see how it can be secure for long but who am I to know? I have never used one of these. It just feels a little like one pull could rip through the sponge. I do appreciate it having a string, though. It makes it super easy to hang-dry the sponge so all sides are/can be exposed to well circulated air. It does take quite a while for it to dry. Still, it is the only sponge of its kind and as weird as it is, it works.

text:
I have a love/hate relationship with this product.

I LOVE that it's travel sized and travel friendly; I brought it with me on my trip to Dallas and it took up like no room in my luggage which was nice since a hair straightener/curler is definitely a must need for me. I love the pretty rose gold color it comes in. I love the packaging, it's super girly.

I HATE the process... for lack of better word. You twist one way (and make sure you click it in place!) for straightener and you twist another way for curler --- this concept I actually love --- but I hate how the middle part you twist to choose which side you want feels like cheap plastic. It took me a few tries to figure it out because I didn't know you had to make sure it clicked into a specific place, I thought you just twisted in that direction. I also don't like how flimsy the barrel itself sort of feels. I don't know if it's because of the material or because of the size but it felt a little flimsy to me.

Overall, I did find this product helpful on my trip. It got the job done of smoothing down my hair or curling it and like I said it's a pretty cute and girly product. I'll definitely still be bringing it along with me on my trips. I sort of just wish that the barrel was a little bit bigger.

title: Give these a try!!
text:
I've bought 3 different styles of these and I had a hard time choosing which ones to get so I hope this review will help others. Sorry I don't have any pictures, I tried but I suck at that so I'll try to be as detailed as possible. First of all, these really do work if you make sure to put a couple coats of magnetic liner on, let it dry in between coats and before you put the lashes on. I bought the expensive liquid liner from Moxie and that seems to work better than the cheap stuff I've bought. However, I prefer these lashes over the ones from Moxie and they cost a heck of a lot less! I bought style 232 first and they are great for going out, they are long and thick but not so much that they touch my eyebrows or anything. I wanted a pair for everyday so I tried style 229. They are slightly shorter (not much) but thicker than 232 and do not flare or taper at the ends (same length lash all the way across). I really liked these also but they still seemed like a bit much for work, so then I tried style 234. These are perfect for everyday lashes! They are still decently long and full but they aren't too dramatic. They just look like you have a great set of natural lashes and a good mascara. (Keep in mind that my natural lashes are short and light.)

I had lash extensions for years and I loved them but they are costly to maintain and take a lot of time. I decided to take a break from them but they have taken a toll on my natural lashes and I had gotten used to the way I looked with them so I needed to find a replacement. I could never get the hang of using strips with the glue so when I saw the magnetic lashes I wanted to give them a try. I started with the expensive ones and loved the concept but had a hard time finding a pair of lashes that weren't too short or too long. I'm so glad I found these! I didn't give 5 stars because one of the pairs I bought had lashes that were 2 different lengths in the package (as a pair) so I cannot wear those.

title: great shaver, cleaning system superfluous
text:
This is my 4th Norelco, going back quite a few years. My last one was not very good, although the first two were great. The 8160 shaves very close and can handle a two day growth. How long an electric razor stays sharp is very related to how clean it is kept, as hair in the heads will dull the blades faster. To that end, Norelco ships this razor with a motorized stand to clean the razor heads. Basically what it does is submerge the razor in the cleaning fluid and turn it on and off occasionally. So you need not buy the XLCC, just buy the 8160 XL. You can submerge the razor in fluid yourself and turn it on and off a few times to do the same thing, and not have to worry about having space to store the stand. I'm experimenting with making my own cleaning fluid, which as far as I can tell is distilled water with a small amount of glycerine and a bit of an additive such as photo-flo which breaks the surface tension of the water so it will drain right off.

One huge improvement over my prior Norelcos is the ability to rinse the razor throroughly with hot water. It does an excellent job of cleaning the razor, and then the fluid bath is only really needed to condition the heads. You can also buy a silcone spray which lubricates the heads to have them wear better. So save some money but make sure the razor you buy is washable and water tight. I highly recommend the razor itself.

title: Great Hold and Light Scent
text:
I have been using beard oil for a while, but recently, it was not making the cut and my beard was getting a little too scraggly for work. I decided to try beard balm to see if it might be able to provide some hold and tame down some of my loose hairs. I was worried that I would need a significant trim if I couldn't find a way to bring it all together, but since starting to use this balm daily, I have been able to let it grow without any thoughts about the professionalism. Below are a few comments I have to make on different aspects of this balm.

Size: This is a fairly large container. If you are looking for some size comparisons, I would say it is about the same diameter as a coffee cup and 3/4 of an inch deep. I have been using it daily for a few weeks now and still have well over 90% of the balm remaining.

Scent: As someone switching from beard oils with fairly strong scents, I initially thought this balm was scentless. I think this can be a positive or a negative depending on your preferences. If you are using a beard oil or cologne with a scent you love, this will not clash with it, but will give you the hold and conditioning you are looking for. On the other hand, if you are looking for a balm that will double as cologne, you'll probably want to buy a beard oil or some actual cologne to supplement what this will provide.

Strength: The hold is great! My beard is about an inch and a half to two inches, and this has provided the perfect amount of hold for me. It helps me to be able to do a little bit of shaping when I need to, but mostly allows my beard to be itself. It has also left my beard feeling less dry and looking a little bit healthier.

Overall, this is a great beard balm and I would recommend it to first time users or those who have tried many before. Also, I received this balm in exchange for an honest review.

title: Easy and friendly on my skin
text:
It took a couple practice runs to get the hang of using this, but it did an awesome job removing both glitter and regular polish. What I figured out is this: Use a cotton pad to apply it to each nail. Make sure the nail looks wet when you have done it - the more soaks in, the easier it gets to remove. Wait a few minutes. Use the same soaked cotton pad to remove the polish. A little gentle rubbing will do it. Done this way, it takes a few moments, but it works. I usually leave it to soak a little longer after I've wiped the polish away, because it really does seem to do a great job of conditioning my fingers (which are otherwise prone to being dry and developing hangnails). Then I wash my hands and apply fresh polish.

It's quicker and less scrubbing than my old acetone-based routine, and it does a more thorough job on the hard-to-reach edges. It leaves my skin in good shape and my nails look happy.

text: When I started using mineral makeup I started with the more well known big brand line, I don't know if I can say their name, but the 'Bare' kind ;) But I'm a full-time student and reordering that brand was a little more than I wanted to be paying. And I had switched to the Matte formula which I loved but it was less product for a higher price. So I started looking to see what other mineral makeups were out there. I found another before IQ and they were ok, but when I tried IQ Natural mineral makeup I was sold. Great price, great product! I have been using them for over a year now, and I can't see me changing. As far as the product - great coverage from the mineral foundations (I use their IQ natural acne moisturizer before putting on the foundation and it works sort of like a primer, and it is great for my skin. I will be putting a review on that as well in a moment.) The mineral veil is awesome, I really feel that it helps give me the soft matte look I want. One of the reasons I switched to the other brand's Matte formula was to avoid the bismuth oxychloride in the original formula. I had heard that bismuth oxychloride contributes to acne, and I believe it does. IQ's products do not have bismuth oxychloride and I love that! One tip that I recently learned from a youtube video is after you put on your mineral foundation and veil slowly and evenly press the side of your powder brush on your skin to kind of help 'set' it. I use a kabuki to put on the foundation and a much softer large brush for the veil. I've been doing this for the last couple weeks and I think it helps keep the product on longer. Maybe it's crazy but it seems to work for me! I highly recommend this stuff!

title: Best bang for your buck
text:
I have used just about every type of hair extensions out there & tape ins are my favorite! I always purchased my hair from the salon so I knew the quality was up to par...but it's EXPENSIVE...I mean $600-$700 expensive. I kept those for a year each time because of the price. I finally broke down & gave these a try & I was pleasantly surprised. The quality is good...not great, but good. They are so affordable that I can get a new set every other time which is also a plus! $120(for 2 packs) is way easier to budget than $600!

Some pointers:
-wash with purifying shampoo. I know that's a no no for extensions but trust me, I've bought several sets & this is the best way to get off that thick coating they put on them to make them extra shiny... it makes them not look as natural.
-After shampooing, use a deep conditioner & let them set for at least 20mins.
-Remove the tape that comes on them & retape. Ok, TBH, I haven't used the tape that comes on them but the reviews I read scared me & I didn't want to chance them falling out or harming my hair. Sally's brand is ok to use & won't come out until you're ready.

Hope this helps.

I typically stay away from clay masks and may not have bought it had I been able to see inside and see that it was clay, but I'm so glad I couldn't! It's not a typical clay mask that dries you out, it feels silky and smooth like the thickest body butter you can imagine. All the things they say it does, it does. I have decent skin to begin with, but I struggle with some roughness on my cheeks, unevenness, some redness, and few small scars/sun spots. I applied this in a nice layer and putzed about for the 10 suggested minutes. (A tip from a professional: never let a clay mask dry on your face. You're pulling natural moisture out when you do this, which exacerbates the situation.) I removed it with a soft washcloth (in just 3 swipes) then rinsed with water. My skin looked nice, but I always see the real effects the next day...and I did. I'm nice and even, "glowy" (for lack of a better adjective), and my cheeks are smooth! The scent is a little too sweet for me (smells more like cocoa or vanilla than honey, but maybe that's it) but it doesn't last long and it's tolerable once it's on my face. I'm glad I gave this a shot, I really like it. There are no directions on how often to use it, so my esthetician training tells me probably 2 - 3 times a week, depending on skin type. It'll be hard for me to not use this more often, it's really nice.

title: Work great for fine, thin hair
text:
I have long, very fine, very thin hair so getting volume is always a problem for me. The only way I could get any sort of volume was to go the salon and get a blow out which, for obvious financial reasons, I can't do every day. I had a list of requitements for a round brush and this set checks every box!
They are sturdy and won't fall apart like the cheap ones you get at the big box stores. The hollow barrel is ceramic coated for better heat conduction without the extra damage to your hair you get from a metal barrel. The bristles are plastic but flexible and keep your hair smooth amd shiney. As a fun bonus, I adore the color! The set of 3 give you 1-1/4", 1-3/4" and 2" sizes. It also comes in an aesthetically pleasing box that is perfect for wrapping if this is intended as a gift.
If you don't know how to use a round brush I suggest looking up some tips. I was making it much harder than it needed to be! Biggest tip, don't try to do a blowout on wet hair! Your hair should be damp at best, like 80% dry. Otherwise it becomes a tangled disaster.
