title: Nice Gift Set for Price
text:
This gift basket of 18 moisturizing bath bombs is a great deal for the price of $21.99. I have to admit though that I got these for myself. But I would have no problem giving these as a gift.

These bath bombs are a bit smaller, 2.5 oz, than the 4 - 4.5 oz bath bombs I usually get because of my tub size. But there are 18 of them and they handled the amount of water in my tub just fine. With these types of gift baskets you often have the product just on the top layer and the rest is filling. There are two layers of bombs in this basket.

The gift basket didn’t have any broken or loose parts in the weave. The fabric lace accent is well done. There is a gift card attached with the message on one side and lines to write your personalized message on the other. The only issue I had with this is it was glued to the top. I had to remove it carefully so I wouldn’t tear the card or cellophane wrapping. Then the card wouldn’t just stick back on. I’d prefer the card to arrive not attached, but I suppose they do this to make sure it arrives with the bath bombs since there isn’t a box.

The bombs themselves are individually shrink wrapped to protect them and each are labeled with a tasteful sticker for the scent. They fizzed well in the water and gave a nice color to the water. The scents are really nice and lasted throughout my entire bath. I could definitely feel the oils during my bath, but they didn’t leave a lot of residue in the tub or make it slick getting out.

I’ve had these sitting on my bathroom countertop for several days, and everytime I walk into the bathroom it smells wonderful. It’s like having potpourri out. This was an unexpected surprise. I’ll also most likely reuse the basket once I’m done with the bath bombs.

This is a nice gift set for under $25 or a treat for yourself. I’ve been very pleased with these.

title: Not too oily, but it does feel like a film
text:
I've tried to transition from chemical based sun screens to more mineral based. The main issue I ran into was that they're super oily (not what I want on my face all day). I read reviews that this one would absorb better, and (bonus) act like a primer. All of that seems to be true, however 2 complaints. One tactile, and one visual.
Perhaps it's a side effect of the mineral aspect, but I can feel this sunscreen on my skin. Not as an oil slick in the crevasse of my face, but rather as a layer permeated into the surface of my skin. It doesn't simply wash off at the end of the day, and requires a somewhat exfoliating wash. I've been getting away with mild cleansers and a good face cloth wipedown.

Visually, it does blend in with my (super pale) skin after a few minutes wait. However it also catches on any dry patches (forehead, nose, etc.) and looks a little... unpleasant on close inspection. I'm inclined to believe this is an aspect of the primer element. I don't normally wear primer, or foundation. So maybe I'm just uninitiated and this kind of reaction is normal. It's definitely not my favorite thing, but it is relatively minor.

So far it's working, and I feel good about what I'm putting on my skin and it's environmental impact. Those are major pluses in it's favor. :D

*Update*
after revamping my skincare routine I find I like this sunscreen more and more. It was catching on any rough spots on my skin, but with a improved moisturizing routine that hasn't been a problem. Instead I feel like it acts as a light primer and it's more than enough "makeup" to get me through the day. You do still want to be sure to wash it off in the evening. But that's all sunscreens. I like that this not only gives me protection, but also evens out my skin tone and lightly covers any blemishes. It's not a replacement for foundation. But if you're like me and usually go bare face, it feels just a little extra nice.

This Exfoliating UltraMud Mask was pleasant on my skin and it felt nicer after application. I'm a guy and certainly no expert of mud masks but this was a pleasant experience. It has a thick consistency, slightly oily but that means it spreads nicely over skin.

I read the negative reviews of this Mud Mask irritating the skin and I believe them. You should read through them as that may be the case with you. Even though I got this product discounted for a review, I promise you i'm not altering my opinion and this product DID NOT irritate my skin at all. There is a warning on the bottle to leave on for shorter time or discontinue use if irritation is present. Perhaps some people left it on for longer than they should, especially the first time. It could also be the case that this might be irritating if you use a deep exfoliator in the shower, prior to the Mud mask. At that point the already peeled, sensitive skin may be severely further irritated by the mud. I recommend not using any facial scrubs before using this mud. You have to built tolerance to the mud, so start off only a few minutes the first time

This also says to not use more than once a week. So that tells you it's strong. I suspect people used facial scrubs in the shower before the mud mask and their face couldn't handle it.

title: Duped by the Chinese! They are on my Wall of SHAME again!
text:
When I ordered the HQ6 replacement heads for my Norelco Shaver, I knew that I was NOT purchasing a genuine Norelco product. So I was WARNED!

I installed the new heads and they immediately rattled around in my shaver and there appeared to be more of a gap around the Chinese replacement heads than my genuine Norelco head. So, I took them out and measured the outside diameter of the genuine Norelco head at .812" in diameter. My new Chinese replacement HQ6 head only measured .806" in diameter. (.006" smaller in diameter) This may not seem like much, but when you are dealing with a small precision instrument, a .006" difference is NOT acceptable. I'm not planning on returning the heads because it simply is not worth my time and effort, but it's another life lesson learned. You get what you pay for and I was told they were not genuine. This is JUST THE TRUTH!! Shame.

title: Reviews had me worried, but these worked great on 4100 Philips razor
text:
{I purchased these replacement blades directly from Philips, because I had a discount code. While not purchased from Amazon, these are the same blades I received from Philips.}
I used the SH50 replacement blades for a 4100 series Philips razor. I use my razor not just for my face, but also to maintain my shiny bald head! Therefore, the razor and blades get quite a work out. I wanted to replace the blades some time ago, but the negative reviews concerned me enough that I delayed. Finally, I had to move forward.
I wanted to make sure that I was not going to get blades made by a 3rd party, so I contacted Philips directly to ensure I was getting their blades. The box I received looks exactly like what you see here on Amazon. They also gave me a discount code when I contacted them, which is why I purchased from them.
Upon arrival, I over-analyzed the replacement process because of comments I had read here. At least for the 4100, the replacement was an absolute breeze, and I would have been better off not worrying. You do need to align each of the blades a little, but if you pay attention when you pop out the previous blades, it's simple. The next time I do this, it will take me less than 60 seconds.
In case I didn't like the new blades, I set the old ones aside. Then I waited--3 days--so there was a solid amount of growth to give these new blades a right proper test! As I write this, that test was just completed. The blades passed with flying colors. It's like the razor was brand new again. There was no pulling at all. The shave was smooth, and so is my head. I'm very pleased with how these blades work with the 4100 model.

title: it was a good buy, and certainly cheaper than everywhere else I'd ...
text:
I bought this item for my wife, as she was getting into DE shaving and wanted a brush & razor stand. I figured for $8, it was a good buy, and certainly cheaper than everywhere else I'd seen shaving stands.

Well, you get what you pay for.

There are several issues with this:

- The acrylic bowl is SMALL. It barely fits my Art of Shaving badger brush, which is smaller than most other brushes I've seen; my wife's Omega boar brush takes up all available space and she's unable to get a good lather going in the bowl itself.

- The neck to hold a brush? It doesn't fit any of the brushes I tried except for my small badger brush, which has a knot size of something like 18mm. I can get my wife's Omega brush to fit in the stand, but I have to bend the bars out, and it's just not a good fit.

- The two loops at the back to hold the razor? Apparently you have to have a REALLY skinny handle on it. It does not fit my Muehle R89 razor, my Gillette NEW open comb razor from 1932, nor my wife's Maggard MRP. I'm not sure what razor it WOULD fit...

I'd return it, but it wasn't fulfilled by Amazon, and it'll end up costing me more in shipping to send it back; I think I'm going to use it as a giveaway for a contest I've got going and see if someone else can use it; I'll be buying the wife a new razor stand that will, for sure, fit her razor and brush...

After a week in the sun we both got a light tan but did not approach the level of redness that we did when we used other products.  Also I am a runner and every day spent at least 30 minutes running outside. In the past when I applied other sunscreens I would always be rubbing my eyes during my run and trying to get the sunscreen off of my eyelids. Love Sun Body stayed in place during my workouts and did not migrate into my eyes. This is probably the only product that has stayed in place and I have tried dozens of products over the years.  I am a board-certified ophthalmologist and plastic surgeon. Many of my patients asked me for recommendations on products for their face.  This is my new go to sunscreen for my family and my patients.

text: Using this device as part of my weekly routine has been great. I have sensitive skin so I don't use it every day, as the instructions reflect. I'd say 2 or, at most, 3 times a week would be fine for all skin types. I did end up making a few red marks after I got used to it and got a little cocky (lol) but that was absolutely my own fault as the instructions also warn of this and how to prevent it. The discoloration (again, self-caused) went down with some icing and was completely gone by the next day with no issues since. I am AMAZED by the amount of GUNK pulled out of my "clean" skin every use, especially in my T-zone. I usually use this and follow with a deep-clean mask for my especially stubborn blackheads and I have to say the combination is without parallel. I've never seen such dramatic results with one single product and this device boosts the effectiveness of the products I already Iove by clearing the way for the next product to penetrate appropriately. I am so, so pleased and amazed with the results of this device, the gentleness (when used appropriately), and the ease of use/cleaning after use. The only question I might have is how to clean the little catch-all pad inside (a great design note as this prevents the "gunk" from clogging the vacuum itself), but that is likely easily remedied and I'm sure I will find a natural cleaning solution to keep my device and all its parts clean and functional for a long time. (Another side-question could be "what type of damage is the suction doing to the elasticity of my face?", though I've looked into it enough to learn this is viewed to be less damaging than some other pore excavation methods I've used.) Overall: I love this product and will keep it as part of my routine until the next beauty wonder is revealed!

title: INSTRUCTION FOR THOSE WITH FINE HAIR
text:
I have a full head of fine hair that needs product in order to look good. Keep that in mind, since products have different results depending on your hair type and amount. After testing out this Atlas Putty several different ways I’ve found that it has some great benefits if you use it along with other products as well.
I would not call it “thickening”. It does add some body and a little shine. And the unexpected surprise is that it also brought out the wave in my hair (most clays and other products I use tend to make my hair straighter).. It has what I would call a “soft hold” - easy to run my hands through band a feeling that there really isn’t any product in it at all. Yet it does keep my hair from being flat, which is its natural state without product.
The magic formula I have settled on is: After showering and shampooing, start with a thickening spray of some sort, like a sea salt spray with some added hold (some have it and some don’t). Once you’ve dried your hair then either go straight to the Atlas Putty, or use a little clay first and then go to the Atlas Putty. And go light with the Atlas. You can always add a little more, because it is quite soft out of the tin, and works into the hair quite easily. Sounds like a lot, but it takes me five to ten minutes to dry and style with all of these steps. And the results are really worth it. Whereas normally my hair is pretty limp, using these steps results in tons of compliments. Oh and yes, the smell is nice. An added plus.
I don’t think this will be a product I use every day, but it will definitely be in my rotation (OK - I’m a bit of a product hoarder). Worth the money and a great product overall.

text:
I heard this was similar to one of favorites, Bvlgari Man in Black. It’s not, and that’s not a bad thing. There is a passing similarity during the first seconds of the opening and then they quickly diverge. Frankly, I think it’s awesome.

To me this has some nice freshness in the opening. I was expecting spiciness so I was initially disappointed but I’ve grown to really like it.
It has some wine-like sweetness, similar to its name sake although their aren’t any wine accords listed in the notes. (I am familiar w/the unique alcohol used but I really don’t know how much that effects the profile)

As it dries down it interacts with my skin really well, it develops this really nice slightly resinous tone.

Personally I use this during the day. It can be used at night, although I have so many evening fragrances this isn’t my first choice but it could easily fill that role. It reminds me of sharing a bottle of great wine with friends.

In the end, I took a chance on a brand that isn’t too popular outside of Brazil and I believe it paid off. And to top it off the presentation is quality. The flacon has a nice soft-touch finish and the sprayer is decent.

This won’t appeal to everyone. It’s not particularly similar to today’s designer frags. But if you want something unique to add to your collection I highly recommend giving it shot. An affordable, unique fragrance with above average performance.

title: Easy and Comfortable to Use
text:
I was very hesitant to order this, feeling a little intimidated both by the technology and the potential for pain. Would it be "safe" enough to do laser hair removal on your own?

I was pleasantly surprised that it was both easy to use and virtually painless. You power on the unit, wait for it to indicate that it's ready, place against the surface of your skin until a light indicates proper contact, and then pull the trigger. Depending on the power setting you've selected, you'll feel anything from nothing at all to a brief surge of heat. Even on the strongest setting on denser patches of hair it wasn't unpleasant for me. I didn't notice any redness and didn't require gel or lotion after using, and I have fairly sensitive skin.

Making it even more painless to use, they've included a "cooling" mode you can switch on that will pre-cool the area where it makes contact with your skin, helping to make it more comfortable when operating. This is definitely a plus when working on sensitive areas or denser/darker patches of hair.

It has 5 strength settings and an "automatic" mode. I don't feel comfortable enough yet operating it to try the "automatic" mode, preferring to make sure it's positioned properly and ready before pulling the trigger, but I imagine it could make things go much quicker for large areas like the legs. I might give it a try when I'm a little more practiced.

The unit has two sizes of lenses - one for large areas (built-in) and one for small areas (attachment). The smaller lens is helpful when you need more precision.

It's important to read the instructions and tips before operating and especially important to wear eye protection (tinted glasses) which they've generously included. You should avoid ever looking at the laser during operation, and probably should operate this in privacy unless the people with you are also wearing eye protection. You shouldn't use it anywhere near your eyes to avoid risk of injury - I'd say nothing above the tip of your nose. One safety feature I like is that it won't operate unless the lens is pressed directly against the skin at a right angle, preventing excess laser light from "spilling out".

This isn't suitable for darker skin (including a dark tan) and also won't help with light-colored hair. You should also avoid using it where there might be a dark area on your skin, such as a mole or tattoo.

One thing I can't comment on yet is how effective this is at hair removal. It takes a few months to really notice a difference, and I've only had it for a week. My rating is based solely on ease of use, comfort, functionality, quality of materials and pricing. I'm optimistic on effectiveness, but may come back and edit this review if either it proves disappointing or exceeds my expectations. Assuming it performs as advertised, I feel comfortable recommending this with a 4-star rating.

title: Excellent quality rose quartz massage roller. White/very pale pink, with hints of pink.
text:
This is a typical rose quartz massage roller, but it's crafted with quality rose quartz and excellent manufacture. The presentation lifts it's value as a gifting option. While there is a natural variation of the rose quartz, and there's no way to tell if you'll get the same rose quartz colors that I got, I love the almost white/very pale pink color, with hints and shades of light pink interspersed faintly in the roller. The color is the first thing you notice about massage rollers, and this is an eye catcher.
This product is not perfect, though. The handle seems to be composed of a resin/plastic. It is very light weight. Use of the resin/plastic magnifies the imbalance of the product. The color matches the stone rollers, though. If the handle was also rose quartz, this would be at least a 5 star product.
The rollers have the plastic grommets that are found on properly designed/manufactured massage rollers. It serves to protect the stone and metal arm/axle from rubbing against each other. It also acts like a bearing, enabling a smoother rolling motion. The massage rollers without these grommets i place are sub par products. Thankfully, this feature is mentioned in the product details, and indeed is found on each of the connecting points.
Overall, the massage roller displays quality aspects and is visually impressive. Except for the resin/plastic handle, it's a fantastic product. For me, the balance is an important element. But, when I encounter a beautifully constructed tool, a structural miscue become more pronounced. Still, it's amongst the premium level of this product genre. As such, it merits a 4.75 - 5 star rating, with a very high level recommendation.

title: Great Horse Hair Brush
text:
This is my first horse hair shaving brush.. and a great one at that! Its said that horse hair brush is the medium between badger and boar. I tend to disagree more than agree. For me, it's a choice unto itself.

In any case, this is a great brush. The bristles are incredibly soft but nowhere near as thick as badger or boar. Which is to say that this bristles are more brittle in comparison. This is not meant to be a knock on the brush. Rather this means that you'll have to build your lather differently than those brushes (think painting rather than hard swirling).

The heft of this brush is noticeably lighter than other brushes I own. I believe this is due to both the light weight of both the acrylic handle and the bristles. While the weight may take some time getting used to, the brush itself has great balance and builds a formidable lather.

The smell was quite strong on first couple of shaves but will dissipate upon proper conditioning and continuing usage.

The one worry I do have is regarding the bristles. While this brush has been very good with hair loss, I do wonder about long term use since the hair is more brittle than badger or boar. So far however, it has not been an issue. In fact, its slowly becoming my go to brush.

At roughly 30 dollars, it's worth a shot.

title: Strong fragrance
text:
This was my first time trying shampoo or conditioner in bar form, and I had the opportunity to try both from this company's line of products. My first impressions were very positive - the ingredients looked clean and natural, as well as being cruelty-free and vegan, I love that it’s plastic free (both the lack of bottle and the packaging), and that the scent options were relatively gender neutral. The bars were a little smaller than I expected, but ergonomically they fit comfortably in the palm of my hand and don't seem to be shrinking too fast after a week or so of use. I'm glad that they have different colors, so that I can differentiate between my bar soap, shampoo, and conditioner!

My experience using them was pretty good. It felt odd at first as I've only ever used bottled products, but quickly got used to it and could definitely see myself using more bars in the future. I tried both running the conditioner bar down my hair and lathering it up a little in my hand and applying that way. Between the two, I felt that I got pretty good coverage and results. My hair felt less tangled and I was able to work a brush through pretty easily once I got out the shower. When my hair dried, it seemed softer and healthier looking than it had previously, and my curls had a little more life to them.

I only have two concerns - the first is that I'm struggling to find a place to put the bars in my shower where they won't get misted by water and disintegrate more quickly that way. The second is the smell. Although it's not unpleasant, it reminded me a little of a scented candle, and was very strong. Three different people commented on the smell of my hair that week, which is not something that usually happens to me. My husband thought that I smelled like cologne! I could see this being a pro or a con depending on how you feel about fragrances. Personally, I found it overwhelming as I'm more on the sensitive side to smells.

Overall, I would consider trying this or a similar product again in the future, but only with a less intense scent.

Finally, after over a year of having these, I actually tried them out! I don’t have get up close vision so it was a little bit harder for me to apply them than it would be for someone who can see better. I used a magnifying makeup mirror though and did fine. The photos of the eyelash after it was applied was my first attempt ever to do this so it’s definitely not perfect but it was much easier to apply than I expected it to be. I am sure my results will improve with practice. These are secured in place with magnetic eyeliner (I guess I am pretty ignorant about these things but I had never heard of that!). The eyeliner goes on smoothly; actually better than some liquid eyeliner that I’ve used in the past. It’s a little tricky to get them in the best spot. Like I said previously though, I think this will get much easier the more times I try them. It comes with tweezers to use but it was almost easier for me to apply them without using them. Once in place, I was amazed at how well they stayed in place!
They were easy to remove and the eyeliner did require makeup remover to get it off, but it also came off without a problem.
I didn’t wear them long. I will have to get used to how they feel; it wasn’t uncomfortable, just different for me. I have very thin, light-colored eyelashes so I think I’m really going to enjoy these!

text: I cannot say enough good things about this Retinol Serum. I have tried several things from the Baebody line of products, and they have all been very high quality and very effective. I am a huge fan of Retinol and how it benefits the skin. I am at a crappy age where I still get breakouts, and I am starting to get wrinkles. I hate having the same gross skin as I did as a teenager. And I have tried everything! Prescription meds, prescription creams, ProActiv, micro-dermabrasion, chemical peels, etc,etc. Nothing seemed to help until I started using this Retinol Serum. Retinol is just a fancy word for Vitamin A and apparently me skin is in desperate need of it. It acts on DNA to promote healthy epidermal skin cells. It does a great job of moisturizing my skin, which helps with wrinkles. And it also does a great job of preventing breakouts. If I do break out because of hormones, it helps clear them up without drying out my skin. Sometimes it clears up my skin within a day or overnight. Vitamin A is a really potent antioxidant that protects your skin from free radicals, generates cell growth, and repairs damaged cells. Retinol belongs to a family called retinoids, and is one of the only substances that is small enough to penetrate the outer epidermal layer to the layer where collagen and elastin reside. It is really strong at first. It is really effective and it is tempting to want to use too much too often, but it can end up irritating the skin. I started using it every other day at first and then built up to using it every day. I also like to use a Vitamin C serum, but using Vitamin C and Retinol together tends to decrease their effectiveness. And sunlight decreased the effectiveness of Retinol, so I use the Vitaming C serum in the morning and the Retinol Serum at night. I let it work it's magic while I sleep. title: Soft to the Touch
text:
I am only in my early 40's, Is there a need for me to use this cream? My curiosity has gotten into me ... besides, there's a fine line forming on my forehead so; I decided to give this product a try. I do not usually apply new products on my skin because I am prone to breakouts but, I dare myself to use this anyway.

So, I got the product with in two days after I ordered it. The shipping and handling was great and the #Miracalis product arrived in good condition. The product looks exactly the same as shown in the picture so; I am truly happy and thrilled to finally try it.

The Texture and Smell

The texture is creamy and I like the feel of my skin after the application. It is really soft to the touch and doesn't have that oily feeling or dry skin after every application. I just truly love to use it especially before bedtime. It makes my skin relax because it has that cool sensation. Anyway, after few weeks of using this product, the fine lines on my forehead are still there and I did not see any difference. If it is fading a little bit, I cannot tell if it does.

I will be brutally honest with you that when it comes to the smell, I am not a big fan of this product. I am hoping that in the future, they will add a pleasant fragrance to this anti-aging cream. It has a smell ... not strong though but, not really pleasant to my nose. It would have been perfect for me.

Does my skin look younger, attractive and glowing? That would have been very nice but, I cannot answer that at this time. All I know is that after each application, my skin is truly soft to the touch and I have no breakouts considering I have a sensitive skin.

title: Don't buy it for the vacuum
text:
This popped up in my gold box, and I decided to give it a whirl since the idea of trimming my beard with no mess had a lot of appeal. The vacuum does half work. Unfortunately, catching half the mess won't change the need for clean-up--there's less to clean, but you'll still need to do it. So my main recommendation is that you shouldn't let the vacuum "feature" be your reason for buying this. If anything, it's a slight negative, because the opening for the vacuum gets in the way when you are doing edge trimming without the attachment.
The next down-side is the "memory" rechargeable batteries. Basically, unless you let the batteries completely discharge before recharging, they will hold less and less charge each time. This is mentioned in the folded up piece of paper that passes for a manual--you will want to read through that. Which leads me to my final gripe: That piece of paper is extremely poorly done--diagrams with no explaination, unclear instructions, etc. So you do have to read it, but you're going to spend some time trying to puzzle it out before you actually figure it out.
For all my complaining, the trimmer isn't completely without merit. It does do a decent job of trimming my beard, which is of course the main point of the thing. I also didn't have any real noise complaints, which seems to be an issue for other reviewers.
On balance though, my main recommendation would be don't pay for the vacuum, because you won't be getting what you paid for.

I bought the Norelco 1050CC (shaver and cleaning system). Here is what I like and don't like:

Pros:

-I know others complained but I had less razor burn than other shavers

Cons:
-Beard/Sideburn trimmer is ineffective and located in a very poor place.
-The angle of the trimmer seems awkward to use.
-MOST OF ALL the recharging system is a complete disappointment. Basically you start the cleaning cycle and have to wait around to unplug the shaver so that the battery doesn't get ruined. It even tells you in the instructions not to leave it plugged in if your battery is charged--which is 90 percent of the time. VERY VERY stupid.

I would have kept this razor otherwise if it wasn't for the illogical charging/cleaning system. You pretty much have to choose between waiting 5 minutes watching your razor clean itself every morning or be okay with ruining your battery. It is enough of an inconvenience that I am returning it and going back to my Norelco quadra trac.

text:
This is perhaps one of the most difficult reviews that I have written in a while. Usually I know immediately if the product is a hit or miss, but Vitabrid C12 is different. I can’t decide. I’m torn. After using VC12 for about 3 weeks, I am still unsure of the results.

The concept: Vitamin C is slow released thru the skin by mixing a small amount of VC12, with water or a moisturizer, onto the face and neck. The results, brighter, smoother and firmer skin. The powder comes in a convenient small bottle (about the length of your thumb) with a small spoon (used for measuring). Simply mix the appropriate amount - I use about 2 spoonfuls since I put it on my face and neck- with a lightweight moisturizer. I didn’t notice any tightness, irritation or itching after I applied this to my skin (i.e., face and neck). I simply apply my makeup as usual. With that being said, I haven’t noticed anything bad either -no additional breakouts and no nasty white film (left on my face from bad blending). But I also haven’t looked in the mirror and said “wow” or “gosh, this is like a facelift in a bottle moment”. Not to mention that this product takes a little more effort than my usual skincare regime. I am not use to mixing products before I use them. **Therefore, I am going to give this product 3 stars BUT continue to use it for a little longer to see if I am wowed. After all each container is believed to last about 3 months. If I notice something earth shattering in the next month or so, I will amend my review. Otherwise, this review will stand.

title: Not tested in animals; Hypoalergenic and sulfate free!
text:
I'm a person that loves fragrances, specially natural oils.
I have a diffuser, I add natural essential oils to all my homemade lotions, shampoos, conditioners, body scrubs. My favorite scents are peppermint, sandalwood and argan.

I have tried a few other brands of argan shampoo, and as someone who loves skin and hair products, i'm always on the lookout for brands I haven't tried yet. The ones that work best for my skin and hair, I become a recurring customer.

I have other products from Pure Body Naturals; I like the fact that their products strive to use natural ingredients, mostly are hypoallergenic, and this shampoo is sulfate free.
This shampoo is very thick and dense, you don't need to use much to wash your hair; it doesn't lather - because it's sulfate free. I have no problem with it not lathering. If you think products need to lather to clean, you're mistaken. Sulfate strips your hair of it's natural oils, making it much weaker, brittle, and dry, that's why you need conditioner after a sulfate full shampoo.
I did not use conditioner after this shampoo, and i wash my hair twice, once to remove dirt, and second to rinse and coat my hair with the "goodies" in this shampoo; specially because i work in the elements and with animals, my hair and scalp need good cleaning.

My hair smells absolutely amazing, looks healthy, shiny, strong and clean. It brushed easily, no snagging, no knots. Very silky and soft.

I love the pump, a couple of squirts and no lid to close, and if it falls in the shower, it won't spill everywhere.

Very well made product, great natural ingredients, awesome smell! Highly satisfied!!! OH! Very important: NOT tested on animals!
Although i've received this product discounted, my review is an expression of the uses i put it through.

title: Good, but a word of caution for people with sensitive teeth
text:
The nice thing about this toothbrush is that it uses the same heads as most of Oral-B's other toothbrushes. This is a basic model, which probably cleans just as well as their other models. The battery lasted me about a week of twice a day brushing, and the battery indicator tells you when you'll need to recharge it a few brushing sessions in advance. Don't ignore it too long, because it takes about 18 hours to charge it fully, but charging it about an hour should be good enough for one brushing. The charger is small and doesn't take up much room in a drawer.

The small head really works well for cleaning the sides of your teeth and between them. Oral-B talks about the cupping action and it really works like the polishing tools most hygienists use. It even seemed to dig food particles stuck between my teeth(!), but you'll still want to floss where no toothbrush can reach. If you have gum issues, this may be the ideal toothbrush for you.

The dual clean head got my teeth acceptably clean faster, but it's noticeably bigger and the precision clean head worked better overall for me. It's nice that they included two different brush heads so you can see which you prefer.

Unfortunately, the slower pulsing action seems to irritate my teeth. A week or two after I started using this toothbrush, my molars started to ache. I ended up returning it and going back to my other Oral-B, whose head looks more like a normal toothbrush which vibrates up & down very quickly. It doesn't clean along the gum line quite as well, but seems to clean the grinding surfaces of molars slightly better.

Oral-B also sells softer toothbrush heads which people seem to like and may be better for my sensitive teeth.

I added another star for Amazon's good customer service and considering that most people don't seem to have sensitive teeth. In general, just about any electric toothbrush will do a much better job cleaning your teeth, removing plaque, etc., etc. - much better than a manual brush. Try one. If you don't like it, a different type may be better for you too.

title: A great falling sand picture
text:
In short, excellent product with well thought out characteristics. I am purchasing more.

I thoroughly enjoy the Golden Sun sand picture by Paradise Vision. It appealed to me so much I purchased it as a gift to myself. Now I am purchasing more for gifts for others. I provide below more details that may not be apparent in the product description or that are notable for me and might be important for others.

Mounting Features - The "picture" comes with design and parts for both table top placement and wall mounting. Frame is angled so that it will not stand on just the frame. Even if it could stand on the frame it is much too susceptible to falling over (and breaking glass) and the provided tapered frame prevents its support is important. It appears Paradise Vision also concluded this and, according, effected this taper. For table top support, a slightly flexible plastic "leg" is provided that supports the picture from behind. The leg attaches to the picture by press fit compression of the leg's two-prong fork feature to be around a sort of rubber grommet. If securely attached I find the leg does not come off when picking up the picture and placing it again on the table top in the same orientation. The leg must be removed and replaced 180 degrees on circular grommet/mount on back of picture if the picture is turned over for the falling sand effect. Bottom line, pick up picture, remove leg, turn over as many times as you want, when satisfied, reattach leg and set picture on table top.

Glass Face - Face is glass, not plastic. Perfect. Plastic is more susceptiple to scratching in my experience and opinion.

Great Scene - Picture has a perfect photograph for complementing the sand (OK this might be apparent in the Amazon photos). What appeals to me is that there is the photograph where other sand pictures that have no photo leaves the viewer seeing what is behind the sand when the sand settles. I find seeing whatever happenes to be behind the picutre less appealing. Also, in this (Golden Sun) version, the sand includes yellow and orange sand (small amounts of both) that complement the photograph and make the sand scene appear like the tops of hills/mountains still receive sunlight.

Great Frame - Solid frame with small grain/fatigue surface features, also painted a shiny gold coler (thing shiny dark gold gift bow). It might have a clear coat of some kind, but I am not sure. Tight, quality joints and surfaces at corners with no mis-alignment, mismatched thickness problems. I am nearly certain it is wood, but I cannot be absolutely certain.

Good Dimensions - Dimensions are big enough to accomodate more than one "hill/mountain". My experience with smaller sand pictures tend to create only one or none or more very small ones.

Air/Water Adjustment - Parts includes a blunt syringe and instructions for adding air or removing air contained in the picture. This is done by inserting the syringe through a normally blocked, one-way gasketed hole feature (about 1/8 in. diamteter) in the side of the frame. I have never seen this feature for users in water-filled sand pictures by other manufacturers. I will confess to not having tried adding/removing air because I don't want to alter the amount that seems to be working just fine as received from the manufacturer. Instructions for doing so are provided and I found sufficiently clear.

Tilt Angle Potentially Problem - The only thing I would have changed if I could was to shorten the slightly flexible plastic leg so the picture doesn't tip back , it appears, by only 10 degrees or so from vertical where it is easily tipped forward if bumped. If it falls forward, it could break, particularly if the glass strikes an object when falling. I would have suggested, perhaps, 20 degrees tip for a little more stability.

Slightly Flexible Leg Feature Good - I suspect the leg is slightly flexible, rather than rigid, so that, if the picture is bumped from the front or set down on the table top surface a little more "vigorously" that the leg will flex a little rather than, otherwise, possibly resulting cracking or breakage of the leg or picture. Great idea Rainbow Vision.

I know I have written a lot. I hope it helps.
Steven

title: you better have something to wash your mouth out with
text:
I used to dip a can of either Grizzly mint long cut or Copenhagen long cut a day for 10 years and have been tobacco free for a month now.I initially ordered this Beaver Chew and some Smokey Mountain straight, mint and wintergreen. I realized there wasn't anything that could replace the actual sensation of putting a real dip in, but I needed something besides gum and mints to give me the feeling that I had a dip in.

The Beaver Chew has a very weird texture and it sticks to everything. When you are ready to take the "dip" out, you better have something to wash your mouth out with. It spits ok, but your spit isn't that brown color that most are used to. There are two reasons why I gave this 4 stars instead of a 2 or 3. I feel like this stuff really helped me quit a terrible habit and the flavor of Beaver Chew is better than Smokey Mountain in my opinion.

Having said all of this, If I were you, I'd buy a few cans of Beaver Chew and a few different flavors of Smokey Mountain and see what works best for you. I am going to stick to Smokey Mountain straight or wintergreen because it spits just like real dip, its texture is as close as possible in my opinion to real dip and you can get used to the flavor after a few days of dipping it.

This stuff is fantastic for nail art! I am a super sloppy nail stamper, I get stamping polish all over my cuticles and the sides of my fingers. previously, I was using a q-tip or a brush dipped in acetone to clean up around my nails after stamping. The acetone dried out my fingers and I always inadvertently ended up removing some polish because I am clumsy and I have shaky hands. It was a hot mess. So I used a tiny funnel to pour a bit of this into an empty nail polish bottle that I had, then brushed it onto my cuticles and the area all around my nails, waited a few minutes for it to dry, then proceeded to stamp and be as messy as I wanted to be. I cannot get over how much easier this made the whole process. It just peels right off. I don't know how I've survived without it.
I don't know how well it would perform for any activities other than nail art...but if you are thinking of buying it for nail art, I cannot recommend it enough. title: It's not 100% human hair
text: So when you first receive this hair, it's super soft and smooth, but after about a week you can tell it's not real human hair.  I think this hair would work really well if you were maybe getting married or something and you put it in the day before the wedding. The hair would still feel nice maybe through a week long honeymoon. After that the hair starts to get really frizzy and has major breakage.  The hair becomes really dry and because it isn't real human hair, no amount of moisturizer will help because the synthetic hair doesn't absorb it at all. I'd like to point out that I've used extensions for years. I have a pair of clip in Remy extensions that are over 8 years old and still in amazing condition. I was able to get about a month of wear out of these before I had to take them out because they were driving me crazy. The tape they use is amazing.  It's almost over the top as the tape outlasts the hair. If you are looking for something long term, I wouldn't recommend this hair.  If you want something that is going to last you for 6 months to a year- you have to get 100% real Remy human hair.  I got a month out of these using every trick I know and they were still a mess by the time I took them out.  But if ur looking to use these for an event or short term, it will save u some $$ to use these. Just be prepared to fight to get the tape out! Oh and try to not wash your hair...like at all....if you can.  Once whatever they put on the hair to make them so soft washes off the hair, it's all bad from there!  Good luck!

title: Much better than expected!
text:
I bought this at a discount store, not on Amazon, but decided to review it since it doesn't have a lot of reviews. It cost me about $9, which is why I bought it. I was just starting a k-beauty routine and picked this out totally randomly, simply because I knew I needed a night cream and I liked the ingredients.

I liked a lot of things about it--how it feels thick and creamy, yet cooling, and it soaks right into my skin and doesn't leave it feeling oily like many other products do. I have dehydrated skin (live in the desert, at high altitude), but it also still gets oily at times. I like how this soaks into my skin and does not make it feel oily, even though I put it on as my final night step after several other treatments and essences.

But because I'm new to the whole system and trying several different products at once, I didn't realize quite how good this was. I thought, yeah, feels nice, not greasy, but otherwise unimpressive. But then I had surgery and wasn't following all the k-beauty steps as much as I had been, and particularly been not using this and I realized....wow, this stuff is actually pretty good. It was THIS cream that has been giving my skin such a silky feel! And I certainly noticed it when I wasn't using it--my skin didn't feel nearly as good, and I'd only been using it for a few weeks. So, guess I'm sol--it's really nice, at least as part of a multi-treatment skin care routine. I'm going to buy it again when I finish this pot. I do go through it fairly quickly, but I'm also putting it on my neck and hands, and it's not that expensive and really is a nice cream.

I do not live in a humid climate and never had this issue with any other brand. I will not be purchasing anymore of these. I know they are inexpensive but there are other cheap choices out there other than SXC.

UPDATE- Not two hours after my update was posted I received an email from the co-founder of SXC. He had read my review and thanked me for taking the time to leave an honest review. He was concerned about my issues and was going to forward them to the product development team to look into improving future batches. He also offered me 24 new polishes or a refund. I didn't write the review looking for that at all. I will still use the Polish so it doesn't seem fair to do either. I thanked him for his super quick response and taking the time to care (very rare in today's "detached, order online society). If customer service is important to you please purchase from this company, they want to make it right!!

title: An effective cleanser but awkward applicator
text:
This product certainly looks high-end with its black and gold packaging, the twist cap that turns through 180 degrees for on/off, and the raised ‘fingers’ for scrubbing your face, but that part doesn’t work too well.

The surface area of the head is too small, and the little bumps that are supposed to scrub can’t really be felt. Also, the dispensing hole is small, so it takes some effort to squeeze any product out. I found it much easier to put some on my hands and then massage directly onto my face - you’d be there all morning if you tried the applicator.

Other than that, the charcoal cleanser itself is high quality - it’s made in the USA (Seattle), the results feel as good as a scrub even though it’s not abrasive like a scrub, I'm told it does remove make-up properly, and it smells OK - not a strong scent, and I think it smells a bit like playdoh. Overall, I like it and will continue to use, but the brush system may need some rethinking.

title: Nice facial steaming product, with handy portable misting device.  Decent performance.
text:
At a spa, people go into the steamroom to relax muscles, open pores and detoxify. This device isn't a steamroom but aims at providing some of the same benefits to the face and neck, especially regarding the skin and pores. This device heats water up to 104F, creating steam which is expelled from the golden rim outlet. Unfortunately it cannot handle the addition of essential oils, recommending only pure water (or weak alkaline mineral water). This would have been a fantastic ability and function. Oh well. As a pure water streaming device, it is a decent performer.
It does not take long for the water to heat, about 30 seconds, and a fine steam mist is pushed out from the device. The optimum range is 6 - 10 inches away from the steam port. It's a good idea to start at a 12 inch distance, and ease your face closer, gauging your skins tolerance.
(Note: you can add toner that can fully dissolve into the water. The key is not to have a viscous liquid, or particulates, which will adversely affect the atomization.)
We found operation to be fairly simple and easy. Fill the water reservoir, put reservoir back into it's position. turn on the unit, within 30 seconds face gets a spa steam experience.
Is this as effective as those face steamers that have a cone that keeps the steam contained? No, because the steam floats freely. But, it's also multiples cheaper than those kinds of facial steaming devices. This is a credible portable device, that is compact enough that it won't take up much counter space. It's minimalist design will allow it to fit in with most decor.
It's easy to set up and operate. It's acceptably effective.
Also included with this steaming device is a mini misting device, a headband (with pink ears) and 4 skin care tools (intended to help treat acne and blackheads).
The mini misting device does not heat the water you put in it. Rather, via a rechargeable battery, a touch of the button will spray a fine mist. This is very handy in the summer, when you might want a spritz of water to help cool you when outside. It's an apt complement to the facial steaming device.
I found the facial steaming device to be capable of decent performance. If you have realistic expectations, you'll enjoy this product. And, I like the rechargeable portable misting device.
Overall, a worthwhile product set, which earns a 4.5 - 4.75 star rating, with a high level recommendation.

title: Good color match and full coverage without feeling too heavy
text:
I often struggle with finding foundations that are light enough and match my undertones. A lot of brands’ lightest shades are either too dark or too orange, and I jumped at the chance to try this after hearing good things about 000.

It arrived the next day with lightning fast shipping. I like the interesting design of the bottle, which has a pump that twists up and retracts. I would feel comfortable taking it on the go and hopefully not making a mess in my makeup bag.

While 000 is described by the manufacturer as a neutral shade, it did look very yellow when I first swatched it. But it looks more neutral blended out and appears to be a near-perfect match for me. It is very high coverage, almost more like a concealer than a foundation. I think a full pump is too much product for my entire face, so this will probably last for a long time as little as I need. While I’m not normally a fan of full coverage foundations due to not liking a matte look, this one has more of a satin finish that looks natural, and it really feels lightweight.

It does stick to very dry patches, so exfoliating and moisturizing prior to use is a must, and I wouldn’t recommend it if you have extremely dry or textured skin. On top of sunscreen and primer, it covered my pores and fine lines without making them more noticeable. I am a little concerned about some of the reviews that said the pump mechanism stopped working for them, but so far haven’t had any problems with it. I definitely recommend trying 000 if you are also pale and struggle to find the right shade match.

I like having my nails done but I have no patience with painting them and letting them dry. Even when I go to salons, I rush and at least 1 nail gets messed up. That being said I have started to use nail strips recently and love them. I usually use color street but I decided to try out these ones.

Separating the nail strips from each other is a bit of a challenge since the protective plastic is a little thick. Overall these strips were a little thick, so filing was hard. Lastly, the blue almost seems printed on, if you stretch the nails a little, the color shows up more white and it looks printed and not solid nail polish.

With all that in mind, I would say none of the negatives are deal breakers. I just wanted to list them so you knew what you were getting into. The sunflowers are nail stickers that I bought off Amazon.

title: Makes an awesome occasional pre-shampoo scalp scrub!
text:
As a facial scrub, I'd rate this better than average, and designed for oily (not dry or normal) skin, but where this really stands out from other products is as a scalp scrub, not to use every time you shampoo, but more like once every couple of weeks as a pre-wash scalp deep-cleaning. I have dryish hair, but my scalp tends to be oily. I have tried many scalp scrubs over the years, but they all left residue and/or just didn't seem to do much of anything.
The way I use this product is to wet my hair and scalp thoroughly, apply a small amount to my scalp, massage in (with fingertips or a scalp brush) for a few minutes, and leave it sitting on my scalp for a couple more minutes (not more than 3 or 4), then rinse, then shampoo and condition as usual.
What I notice right away is that my regular shampoo feels like it is actually cleaning my scalp instead of just sitting on top of it, and even many days later my scalp just feels healthy and clean. I've been using this scrub this way for over a year now, and it continues to work well for me. It's more effective and much less expensive than any "scalp scrub", and the small (1.7 ounce) plastic container, means it's very portable for travel.
One caution though - I don't color my hair (I've earned my gray hairs!), so I can't comment on whether this scrub would mess with the color of dyed hair. title: Amazing, natural product that delivers on its promises.
text:
I have been using this product nightly for 3 weeks and I can already tell my teeth are getting whiter! I have struggled with tooth sensitivity from whitening strips in the past, but this product gives me no sensitivity problems whatsoever. I'm so excited to have found a natural product that delivers on its promises!

I have not experienced any major messes as other users have. I find that when I follow the directions included in MMM exactly as stated, the product is virtually mess-free. My advice:
1. Use half of a scoop, as the directions tell you. Trust me, a little goes a long way. I hold my toothbrush over the pot as I pour the product on my toothbrush to waste as little product as possible and to avoid messes.
2. Buy an extra soft toothbrush to use exclusively for the Magic Mud. This product WILL stain the bristles, so no use in using your expensive electric toothbrush.
3. Brush the product on your teeth in small, gentle, circular motions, focusing on the outsides of your teeth (the ones you want white). KEEP YOUR MOUTH SHUT as best you can, once again, as the directions tell you.
4. Put on some fun or relaxing music while you brush - 2 minutes goes by very quickly that way.
5. Spit SLOWLY with the water running, spitting as close as you can to the drain. Less mud will splash up your sink that way.
6. Swish water around in your mouth to get extra mud out from your gums and teeth. Slowly spit again. I then brush with my electric toothbrush with toothpaste as normal.

title: Another stellar shaver from Norelco
text:
I've read a lot of bad reviews on this shaver and I just don't understand why it gets such bad marks. Granted, I've never shaved with any other brand than a Norelco, so I may not have a lot to compare it to. For the past eight years, I shaved with a Norelco Advantage/Cool skin. I wasn't in the market to purchase a new shaver, as I loved my cool skin, but after 8 years, it began to come apart (literally). I received this shaver as a welcome and much needed birthday gift. So far it has lived up to my expectations; its precise in the way it cuts the facial hair and it does provide a closer shave on the neck region than my Advantage/Cool Skin model. In order to avoid any razor burn, I dab some Lectric Shave on my face about 30 seconds prior to shaving (great advice for any of you experiencing razor burn). Unlike the Advantage/Cool skin model, the hairs fall into the blade area neatly, which makes cleaning a breeze. All it takes is some lightly running hot water and about 30 seconds. The arcitec 1060 also has a very powerful charger; I've had it now for over two weeks and have only had to charge it once.

Yes, this is an expensive razor and it may not be worth the price you pay for it, but getting it as a gift I can honestly say that I hope to be using this shaver for years to come. It's a quality machine that does what it is supposed to do: provide a close, comfortable shave.

title: Amazing Fragrances. Definitely Worth It! (Detailed Review)
text:
I’ve been on the search for a few fragrances recently, and was introduced to various reviews on YouTube about brands such as Swiss Arabian, Rasasi, Al-Rehab etc. I usually stick to Nemat’s perfume oils but this times I wanted to take a risk. Therefore, I decided to grab some samples. Initially I was intimidated by the fact that there’s the idea that perfumes that are manufactured in the Middle East can be heavy (which they can be), but great because they are long lasting. And let me tell you, I’ve fallen in love with these.

La Yuqawam Pour Femme is a definite dupe for Black Orchid by Tom Ford. It’s feminine, floral, peppery and spicy. This perfume is perfect for a night in the town, a date night, or to simply uplift your mood. This perfume is up there with Narciso Rodriguez’s For Her, Dior’s J’Adore and all the other popular perfumes that are titans in the perfume industry. I loved this very much. A must for fall/winter. 10/10

La Yuqawam Jasmine Wisp is sweet, floral and has quite an island-like feel to it. I imagine being on an island vacation. The notes of coconut and fruity notes makes this perfume a delicious addition to your collection. It’s quite the fragrance for a girly young woman but also has an element of sophistication too. I’d say that this is for spring/summer but can be used sparingly for fall/winter. 10/10

La Yuqawam Orchid Prairie is one that is so hard to describe..which is why I love it so much. I definitely get an enigmatic, unusual but a captivating impression from this perfume. I remember this perfume being described as “grape juice spilled over wet wood.” And I do think that’s quite true. Again, it’s hard to describe, but I imagine this smell as like being in the middle of a misty forest and you catch the scent of berries and rich, deep colored fruit mixed with moss and amber. I imagine this scent being something that is so rare, unusual, unique and exotic and otherworldly that people will definitely want to know about it, but you have to keep it a secret. Even if people don’t know you the wearer, they’d know that you were in the room. This perfume is exactly that. This perfume is definitely for a woman who is sensual, unusual, and rare.. a woman who is in the world but not of it. 12/10

In all, if you are looking for a captivating sample set of niche perfumes from the Middle East, these perfume samples will never fail you. They haven’t for me. So take a risk, take a chance and buy it. Also, you can always give these samples away as a gift if you don’t like them. These samples are just enough to carry in your purse, and just enough if you want to try out a scent without the full price.

Enjoy!

title: So easy and good, even a lifetime makeup-hater is hooked.
text:
Hi, I am Annelise (daughter of Jane) and I HATE makeup. I hate how long it takes to put on, I hate how easily it rubs off, I think it's so inconvenient that I almost NEVER wore makeup. I bought these to use once for a special occasion.

That said, I wear this stuff every day now (and no other makeup). It is ridiculously quick and easy to put on, even for somebody like me with unevenly-shaped eyes that tend to result in mismatched-shaped eyeliner. It takes me roughly 2 minutes to apply: just stamp, stamp, color-in, move on with my life. Moreover, it stays presentable all day with only optional touch-ups, even on my smooth, folded eyelid-skin that NOTHING stays on.

The only vague "criticism" I have for it is that, after 2 months, one of the stamps seems clogged and only makes a splotchy mark anymore, even though the brush at the other end still has plenty of ink. That's only a negative in the loosest sense, as it has lasted 2 months at less than $20 and I just use the other stamp now.

Completely satisfied and even delighted!

title: Functions well, but needs better instructions! Heavy!
text:
Seems to be made well, but wow, it sure is heavy! (I just went back and noticed that this warning does appear in the ad/order page, with solutions, but none of these solutions are mentioned in the product box itself.) It actually fits my large face, and the rubber around the eyeballs does block out the light rays. This might not be the case for people with other shaped faces. This all said, I found it to be quite uncomfortable I sat up and used it while watching TV. I actually found resting my finger under (in) the nose to hold it up during the session helped to keep the weight off of my eye sockets.

I have no clue as to what the electronic probes are for??? It mentions them in the little manual, but doesn't tell or really say anything about them. And yes, I plugged them in, and yes, they stung/hurt! THe little head strap in also fairly wimpy. I had to play with it to get it into just the right spot.

AND, the instructions are written really poorly!!! I know sometimes translations are a bit difficult to read, but I finally gave up, and just started to push the buttons to figure out what to do. They do give good "color" information, but I found a lot of it to be repetative, which makes me think I just need to hit the auto changing light!

No specific instructions on how long to use a given light, or its intensity. The device control is auto set at 30 minutes, upon plug in, but the ad (which I just looked at again) mentions 10 to 20 minutes a couple/few times per week. And, the control device does not have an on/off button, as far as I can see... you either have to slowly cycle down the minutes button, or, reach for the plug and pull it out of the socket while the mask is on. The other thing is that the control box itself is labeled "Facial Whitening Instrument." What's that all about? I am already too white looking! It is not mentioned in the ad or on the box.

I know that red light therapy is now touted as a good thing, but I am afraid that if the instructions are not good and thorough then it could also pose some dangers. I will look elsewhere to find information about how to use this device. I am sure it is actually a fairly worthy instrument, but the communication needs to be better!

title: Good but not perfect
text:
I bought this to replace a Norelco 5885 XL after the battery stopped taking a charge. I had the 5885 repaired at a Philips authorized place, but it still didn't take much of a charge, so I went back again and, in the end, still didn't have a razor that I could use for more than a few days. I finally decided to give up and get this. I paid about $40 for it (the price has since gone up) and the repair was $30, so I figured this was a faster way to get something that worked.

In general, this is a very nice shaver. It's super-quiet, noticeably quieter than the 5885. It shaves a tad closer and needs less pressure to do so, and it seems to take a few less passes over the same area to get a close shave. The trimmer is just okay -- exactly like the old one. It won't cut you, but it won't easily make a clean edge for your sideburns, either. It's nice to be able to rinse out the head under running water.

There are a couple of caveats, though. The design of the head is slightly different and it doesn't move as smoothly over my skin. For me, this is a noticeable and moderately significant disadvantage. The old one felt better. It took a bit more effort to get a close shave, but I enjoyed the process more.

There's no battery meter. The old one told me how much of a charge I had. It wasn't all that accurate, but it let you know if you needed to charge the thing before going on a trip. But the battery lasts a long time -- I've had it for three weeks and I'm still on the first charge (I don't necessarily shave every day, though).

I never cut myself with the 5885. With this one, I've had two nicks in the first three weeks. Using less pressure may help.

I bought this over the more expensive Norelcos because I didn't want to carry a charging base on trips -- I just wanted a cord. I would have paid more, but Phillips just doesn't make the shaver that I want, which would be similar to the old one -- no base, but with a charge meter. In general, Phillips makes way too many models and it's awfully confusing trying to sort out the differences.

Overall, I'm happy, but replacing my old one, for a dead battery, was way too much hassle and the result is a shaver that isn't quite as nice as the one it replaced.

A note for those of you who've never used one of these: you'll get a close shave, but a blade will always be closer.

title: Pretty amazing...
text:
I've been using this razor since it arrived, approximately 2 weeks ago, and thinking long and hard about the score I'd give it. I actually intended to give it 4/5, the reason being that, while it's an excellent razor, the price point is rather high. In the end, though, I'm so impressed that I really need to give it a full five stars in spite of the price, with the caveat that you may want to take a look at one of the less expensive, stripped-down models; this one is the flagship, but all the models should be similarly excellent (please bear in mind this is the only one I've used).

And excellent it is. While my feelings have already been summed up in the opening paragraph, read on for similarly styled (but moderate) hyperbole.

I've never gotten such a good shave with an electric razor. Norelco does recommend that you give the razor a full 21 days of your time exclusively (i.e. not shaving with anything else) before making a judgment. I haven't had the luxury of giving it a full 21 days, as I need to get my review in; however, I've already adjusted to it so well that I can't imagine going back to my old razors. It will only get better as I get more used to it, although I'm perfectly satisfied at this point and unsure if it could get any better.

Not only do I use it to shave my face (which is obviously what it was designed for, and it does a great job), I use it to shave my head. It's not going to give you as close a shave as a traditional razor, but it's also not going to scrape against your skin like a traditional razor. You'll also save money on shaving cream (the only extra expense is buying a new razor "head" for it yearly, the price of which I am uninformed of). It works "dry". This is nice for me, as it takes a lot of cream to shave both my face and my scalp, and it does, in fact, do a decent job on my head. It's a little stubbly, even right after shaving, but honestly the only thing that would do a better job would be a blade, and that's a difficult way to shave (I was previously using a Headblade). If it can shave a head, where my hair was very thick, I imagine it would be adequate for even the bushiest of beards, and, again, it's designed for faces, not heads.

If you look at the features list, you'll see that this model is full of bells and whistles. Truthfully, they are mostly extras you could live without; the lower-end models would likely be just fine, so I strongly suggest examining them as a money-saving alternative. The meter that shows you how many minutes of the charge are remaining is sort of handy, the icon that lights to remind you to clean it is somewhat useful, but to say they're necessary would be a grave overstatement. In fact, the "wash me" icon lights up after basically every use, so its necessity is particularly dubious. (As a side note, it's marvelously easy to clean.)

In the end, the product does receive my highest recommendation. I think if you tried it out, you'd be pleased, and even if you had to send it back and didn't like it after three weeks via their guarantee (it does take time for your skin to adjust), there would be little time/money wasted. I would, however, encourage you to check out the lower-end models. Ultimately, even the high price point wasn't enough for me to downgrade to four stars. I'm normally quite critical.

title: Nice Brush | Similar To We Love Doodles & Chris Christensen | Cats Love It | Easily Removes Hair
text:
If I didn't already own & love my "We Love Doodles" brand of big slicker brush, I would have rated this brush at a full 5 stars. Mostly what I don't care for this brush vs Doodles is the handle. It is a little more narrow so it's a teensy bit less comfortable to hold. I have carpel tunnel. I've been grooming cats furever & grooming English angora rabbits for well over a decade.

🐱For short & long haired cats, this brush works great. All of my cats love this brush & my Doodles brand. I can comb all of them except for my 14yo with a surprising amount of pressure & they roll around purring. Tons of hair gets picked up into the tines. Unlike some styles of brushes & combs, no hair is left behind around the tail area.

Removing the hair from the brush is very easy. Start at one side from the bottom to loosen & then move to the other side. Keep working your way around & it comes off in a nice clean loose mat. I actually prefer these types of slicker brushes over self cleaning brushes & also over brushes with the little plastic beads on the ends. If you groom your animal properly, you don't need little balls on the ends of the tines. Those balls also make it a little harder to get the brush fully clean of hair.

Cosmetically, I like the look of the brush much better than my Doodles brush. This is all black with a more classy branding in small white text on the head. We Love Doodles is blue & loudly brands itself on the head.

🐰I don't recommend this style of brush for English angora rabbits. I have found that my bunnies seem to be more comfortable with smaller slickers with shorter tines. You'd think with their dense long coats, you'd want something large with long tines, but it really doesn't work out like you'd expect. At least for me it doesn't.

🐰Recommended for English Angora Rabbits:

🐇Doggy Man sells a small soft slicker brush that my angora rabbits love. It's plastic with a little blue ring on the handle. I have purchased/replaced many of them over the years (the handles tend to break over time) because they work well.
🌐 https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B001NLVFH2
🐇I also recommend if money allows, a small slicker brush by Chris Christensen. I've never needed to replace it.
🌐 https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00GU7NKWW

Personally, I'd shop between this brand (Rita's), We Love Doodles, & Chris Christensen. Chris Christensen is top of the line. They are worth it if you have the money. We Love Doodles has been the middle ground for me. They were originally priced at $50, but the price has been a lot lower for a while now. Rita's is currently the second most expensive & probably the lowest quality of the three brands. However, I've been using it for the least amount of time, so it's too early to know for sure. So far I like all three.

A huge plus is this comes with an expiration date, mine came with an almost 2 year shelf life. This is something I haven't really seen before on body scrubs but I am pleased to say this is in effect for baebody.

The Arcitec doesn't allow you to do this. No amount of rinsing in the water will clean the Arcitec heads. Those who say "cleans easily" don't realize that rinsing the cutting head only cleans it superficially. Also as others noted the razor will not hold the whiskers when shaving and will make a mess. title: Great at removing makeup. Leaves skin smooth and doesn't dry it out.
text:
There are various important aspects that a facial cleanser needs to have or shouldn't have. The Simpir facial cleanser hits all the right categories for my skin and preference. This doesn't dry out my skin at all, which is a common problem for me. On the other hand, it doesn't aggravate my generally oily forehead. I haven't experienced any unusual acne since starting this and I didn't have any skin irritation or redness. It does a good job of removing makeup, and it rinses off easily. I have noticed a slight reduction in the size of my pores and number of blackheads on my nose and chin. I have been using this once a day for about 2 weeks.

I'm not a fan of the smell, but it's charcoal and should be expected that it's not going to smell great. I won't fault the product for that. Fortunately I don't smell it at all once I rinse it off. The pump works well and doesn't over dispense the cleanser so I don't feel like I'm wasting anything. I do prefer pumps that twist open/close rather than having to be pushed down and twisted to close because it's easier for travel. Not the end of the world though. I appreciate that the cleanser is made in the USA and uses organic and natural ingredients. You can never be too careful with something used on your skin regularly, and I feel a product of that quality made in the USA seems safer.

title: An excellent soap, and much less tempermental than I thought it would be
text:
I've been trying out new shaving soaps, and this was the latest one after trying Tabac (really loved that one too). From all of the reviews I've seen here I thought it would be tempermental to work with, but it wasn't that bad at all. In fact, if you can get a good lather out of Williams shaving soap (and yes, it can be done), then lathering with Mitchell's Wool Fat is a snap by comparison.

The big thing to remember is that just like Williams and Tabac, this is a hard-milled, tallow-based soap, and unlike the glycerin-based soaps of Van Der Hagen or Colonel Conk, a tallow soap needs to be used with lots of water, and the hotter you can get that water, the better the lather and cushion will be.
The big secret to getting great lather when I use this soap-or any other tallow soap-is to fill the bowl it's in with boiling hot water until it's about 1/2inch over the soap and let it soak for at least 5 minutes before lathering. After that the soap is properly hydrated and will work very well with whatever brush you use in your daily routine, just be sure to dump out the water before you lather up.

Some people have compared the scent to Williams, and it definitely has a "clean" scent, but it's not nearly as "cleaning product-y" to my nose. My wife REALLY likes the scent a lot, too, so it's a winner in my book. Will definitely buy again.

text:
I purchased this headband for my 4 month old. Her cousin was turning one and having a unicorn themed party. We all agreed that our little girls would dress up as unicorns for a photo op; this was perfect! I was really surprised by how well made the headband was. text:
When I first saw this product on Amazon, I was wary of all of it's good reviews. I have long hair that is prone to dryness and breakage, and have tried just about every shampoo and conditioner on the market to improve hair health. I am pleasantly surprised that this shampoo lives up to it's claims.

I want everyone to understand that this is, in fact, a shampoo; it is NOT a cleansing conditioner. In my opinion, that is a plus, as it's important to cleanse your scalp and hair follicles without adding buildup that a "cleansing conditioner" often imparts. This shampoo is sulfate-free and gives a mild lather. I feel like it cleans my scalp and hair sufficiently, without stripping. I color-treat my hair, and this shampoo has never stripped or lightened my color.

As far as moisture is concerned, this adds hydration without weighing my hair down. Yet, it is NOT drying to my hair as so many shampoos are. I have long, fine hair, so that's a significant point. If you read the ingredient list, you will see that this product contains many natural oils and humectants. Given that, I am continually surprised that it doesn't weight my hair down.

After use, my wet hair feels smooth and sleek, but I still need to follow with a conditioner for detangling. Again, this is a shampoo; it is not a cleansing conditioner. Since there is no matching Pure Body Naturals daily conditioner for this shampoo, I have been experimenting with some other argan oil conditioners sold here on Amazon.

No matter your hair type, I think this shampoo can add to your hair health. I highly recommend trying it.

title: Ingredients
text:
These have very little odor. They include a lot of currently popular natural ingredients along with a few ingredients not favored by those most into that kind of thing.

Barrier

It isn't quite like a protective glove. Probably does help with protection for a limited time, not a whole day of work with your hands, during which it gets absorbed, wiped away, worked out by other substances and so on. Takes a couple minutes to soak in, but it's not very greasy once it does.

Active ingredient: dimethicone.
Inactive ingredients: deionized water, stearic acid, propylene glycol, glyceryl stearate, isopropyl palmitate, Ricinus communis (castor) seed oil, cyclopentasiloxane, phenoxyethanol, ethylhexyglycerin, sodium hydroxide, mineral oil, Simmondsia chinensis (jojoba) seed oil, xanthan gum, disodium EDTA, acrylates copolymer, Aloe barbadensis leaf extract.

Hand cleaner

Looks like it has plenty of charcoal, it's so dark, but more of the grit--and it's very gritty--is from pumice than charcoal. Does't foam, cleans surprisingly well anyway, moisturizes a little.

Ingredients: aloe leaf juice, pumice, glycerin, sunflower seed oil, sorbitol, carbon [that's the charcoal], grape seed oil, lanolin oil, vitamin E acetate, xanthan gum, carbomer, 2-phenoxyethanol, ethylhexylglycerin, sodium hydroxide.

Hand cream

Not a heavy-duty cream but has some nice stuff in it that's thought to help with skin health, moisturizes for a while.

Ingredients: water, glycerin, stearic acid, dimethicone, sunflower seed oil, cetearyl alcohol, ceteareth-20, allantoin, petrolatum, hydroxyethylcellulose, aloe vera, Symphytum officinale (comfrey) rhizome/root extract, Calendula officinalis oil, tocopherol, diazolidinyl urea, iodopropynyl butylcarbamate, acrylates/C10-30 alkyl acrylate crosspolymer, sodium hydroxide.

Workman's Friend is a brand about two years old based in Texas. The hand cream and soap are made in the US, the barrier is made in Canada.
