[[VIDEOID:196aee9ee5552fd2737b70d726cb32cc]] I bought this as an electric shaver for my legs. I'm black and have coarser hair and I think it worked well. It's not as close as a razor but to the naked eye you can't tell. It kind of feels like the stubble from a day old shave. But like I said I was impressed. You do have to go over an area several times but it didn't bother me.

There was no discomfort. There were only a couple times when it seemed to catch and the pinch was very minor. I used large circular or long sweeping motions and it was like getting a leg massage. You can do it while watching tv. I shaved on dry legs (which were extremely ashy so don't judge me) but I want to try it in the shower since it claims to be waterproof. I also love the attachments. I used the trimmer blade to do my bikini area.

The only drawbacks are A) The housing for the blades is hard to open to for cleaning, especially the middle blade. You have to twist it counterclockwise and lift. It's also hard to put back in place. B) The instructions for removing the attachments isn't clear. I was scared I was going to break the thing trying to get them off the unit (turns out you just pull them out with a little force and pop them in, no twisting).

All in all for $20, I would definitely recommend.

title: This GUY absolutely loves this luxury body wash!
text:
I hate to say it, but I could care less about what kind of body wash I use and the ingredients it contains. My favorite brands to date are Axe, Dove, and Old Spice.

Having the opportunity to try this Hask Body Wash was an eye-opening experience for me. I really didn't think I was going to be impressed by a hypoallergenic wash that stripped away all the drying additives that I had become accustomed to applying to my skin on a daily basis.

The first positive impression was the fact that this Body Wash arrives as a pump product. It allows me to put it in the corner of the shower and not have to constantly turn the bottle upside down and squeeze out the contents.

The next positive impression was from pump to skin. This stuff is nice and creamy. It lathers very well as you sponge it across your body. For that reason, a relatively small amount goes a long way.

What impressed me the most was the lasting effect this Body Wash had on my skin after the shower was over. My skin wasn't dried out. It was smooth, with a refreshing coconut, vanilla scent.

title: SMALL but effective
text:
Ok, I know the photos of the product show the box that says "mini-curler" but nothing in the description indicates how MINI it truly is! I've never owned a 3 barrel iron before so I watched a few videos online while I was waiting for this to arrive. It looked easy enough, though I was questioning the size of the ones they used versus the what I ordered. The barrel is 3/4" so I knew that would make for a tighter curl regardless and I was ok with that. What I didn't think about was the overall size of the whole thing. It's tiny, like really, really small lol I attached a pic of me holding it, it's like a play curling iron for a child lol BUT it does work! I was able to curl through all of my hair in no time at all and it left me feeling like I got a perm in 10 mins (see pic of my hair straight vs curled)! Not something I'm going to want to do on a regular basis. I think I want more of a relaxed wave for that which means a much larger barrel size, but for special occasions when I do want my hair curly this will do the trick nicely.
A separate, tiny complaint is the inability to adjust the heat setting. I have very thin hair and I generally don't use very high heat settings on my other curlers/straighteners but this one was either on or off, no adjustment for heat so I had to make sure to not hold my hair in for too long so I wouldn't risk breaking it off. It's not the most ideal situation but it is a fairly easy fix to just err on the side of not long enough rather than too long.

title: Perfect Beginner Beard Butter, But Go Check Out the 10 Scent Sample Pack on Oak City Beard First
text:
I tried out Oak City Beard's products from their own website and Amazon, and both offered amazing deals for great products at affordable prices. The consistency is true beard butter, not sour cream like Maestro, and my two 4 oz containers came in without any grainy consistency issues. If you do have that problem on your order, you can fix the issue by checking out videos from people like Dan C. Bearded or Beardbrand Alliance on the topic. Finally, Snow Leopard is my favorite scent from what I have experienced so far as it's a very refreshing peppermint/sandalwood perfect for the evening. The scent lasts me a solid 8 - 9 hours as I can put it on at night and by the morning I can still get a decent whiff of it, but it's not strong enough to make it invasive if you're worried it's more like a cologne. (They also do sell solid colognes in the same scents if you like.)

Additionally, I would recommend getting the ten 1 oz beard butter sample pack from their website first. The cost is just right for $26 for 10 oz; you can try out almost all their scents in smaller doses; and the shipping is free and timely. I would have gotten the two 4 oz tubs I bought from Amazon on their website as well, but I had some left-over gift-card funds to make it cheaper here. However, I will gladly buy more of their products in the future.

title: Exfoliate your skin without ruining your hands
text:
This is a pretty great exfoliating pad/mitt with one key feature I have not seen before.
The thing that sets this apart from similar products is that the inside is lined with terry cloth.
That small addition makes a major difference when it comes to using the mitt because you don't end up exfoliating your hand the entire time you are trying to exfoliate you body.

The external material does a pretty good job exfoliating.
It's rough, but not painful, so it should work for a wide range of skin types.
Obviously, you can also pair it with soaps and scrubs to enhance its ability to exfoliate.
Personally, I find this gentle enough to use every shower, yet textured enough to remove a lot of dead skin.

If there is one extra change I wish the makers of this mitt would consider for future iterations,
it would be to add a loop of some sort to hang it by, so it can be left to dry on a hook.
Still, I can add something like that myself or just hang it over a towel rack, so it's not a big deal.

I would definitely recommend this mitt to someone in the market for one.
It's perfect for a bath or shower, offering good exfoliation for your skin, while protecting your hand from unnecessary wear and tear.

title: Captivating But Concerning
text:
Amore Pacific, based in South Korea, lists "alcohol" as an ingredient in its Color Control Cushion Compact with SPF 50. Since there are good and bad alcohols, I resisted jumping to a negative conclusion especially because I agree with AP regarding the impressive visible benefits conferred by their treatment foundation that has many fans atwitter and aglow.

AP's response to my inquiry was delayed, which I considered either bad (corporate communications) netiquette or bad news. After four workdays, I received a reply thanking me for my "patience" as a response from R&D "to ensure correct information and advice" had not yet been received. When I informed the company that I HAVE no patience and am spoiled by live chats, which provide instant gratification, I received an answer two days later. Apparently, bamboo sap, the primary moisturizing ingredient, is easily contaminated as it's stored for prolonged periods. To prevent "micro-organic pollution," anhydrous alcohol is used. This is ethyl alcohol, which some scientists who write for respected journals warn consumers to avoid because it penetrates the skin barrier and provokes short- and long-term harm, exacerbates oily skin and redness, and may even minimize the efficacy of good ingredients including those that protect against sun damage.

AP is the parent company of Sulwhasoo, which makes a Perfecting Cushion that also includes "alcohol" but not bamboo sap. I don't know what ingredient(s) this brand is protecting.

AP asserts that their anhydrous alcohol is dermatologist approved, but we have no idea who the dermatologist is and whether or not the doctor was paid. AP says that their anhydrous alcohol is patented, but this is just ethyl alcohol with water removed and can't be patented.

The respected Washington, D.C.-based Environmental Working Group (EWG) rates this alcohol a 2 (out of 10) and asserts that anything between 1 and 2 is "low hazard." The overall EWG rating for AP's Color Control Cushion Compact is "4," meaning that it is of *moderate* concern to human health. (The nonprofit group objects most strenuously to the sunscreen octinoxate and to the fragrances included.)

Our U.S. FDA approves the use of ethyl alcohol.

In 2008, the National Institutes of Health urged further investigation, but rigorous double-blind, peer-reviewed studies demand a lot of time and money. Meanwhile, concern lingers.

title: Makes Washing Your Hands When You Are On The Go  Convenient And Fun
text: Disney And Touchland Hydrating Hand Sanitizer makes washing your hands when you are on the go convenient and fun. The set includes four 1fl oz bottles with 500 sprays. The presentation package is truly adorable and instantly gift ready. The hand sanitizer is slightly larger than a gift card but looks like an iPod or simple cell phone with a drawing of Mickey Mouse that reminds me of an Andy Warhol sketch. There are four different fragrances: Pure Lavender Scented, Aloe You Scented, Citrus Grove Scented, and Unscented. One press of a button releases a fine mist. I ended up pressing the button two times to get a proper coverage per hand. The fragrances of the three are bright and strong. My hands felt clean, did not have any stickiness or residue remaining, with a faint perfume from the fragrance. I found that after multiple uses, I did not experience any dry or rough skin despite the product including ethyl alcohol. One negative I have is that there is no way to lock the button to keep it from accidentally spraying when in a bag, backpack, or purse. Another negative is that these adorable hand sanitizer containers cannot be refilled. Given the sturdiness of the product container and how cute it is, I really wish this was an option. When it comes to price, it is high but justifiable based on the sturdiness of the product container, the quality of the hand sanitizer, and of course acknowledging the tie in to Mickey Mouse.  The product is vegan and cruelty free. It is Made in the USA. I really love these hand sanitizers for not only their look but how well they cleaned my hands. These are a must have for any Mickey fan.

title: Good idea, bad execution
text:
I was excited to see this product because it seemed like a really cool idea. An all-in-one mechanical device that could be used a body scrubber for various uses. All the different attachment and the explanations of different power levels looked promising.

However, in reality this was not a great realization of that promise.

First the product itself isn't of the greatest quality. It has a 'cheap' feel about it.

Second, while it looks fine ergonomically and with tidy packaging, none of the attachments have labels for what they are used for right on the attachment. All the labelling is on the accompanying foldout. That would require you to always keep the paper fold-out with the appliance. That just isn;t realistic over time.

Third, I have to agree with a lot of the other reviews that the typeface on the instructions is too small.

Fourth, they promise different power levels, but honestly there does not seem to be appreciable difference in the settings. The setting is adequate for the face scrubber (not powerful enough to flay off skin) but nothing near to what you'd need for feet or nails.

In the end this is just not a really go execution of what should have been a good product,.

title: Tiny plastic covers on the bristles make it more comfortable for some cats
text:
We have three cats with three very different coats. The black cat's coat is sleek, shiny, and seems to have fine little hairs. He barely sheds, and his hairs are short. He loves being brushed with just about any brush, for the interaction, the petting/grooming connection and the scratching action. However, he doesn't really need to be brushed.
Our medium-to-long haired snowshoe Siamese seems to have sensitive skin; she Hates being brushed near her achy back hips, and will complain and whip around to smack at you if you brush her very hard at all. However, she sheds a TON, and needs to be brushed almost every day, so she doesn't get clumps by her arthritic haunches (she actually gets dandruff flakes that her hair clumps around and knots up). She is at least 14 years old (we're not exactly sure), and just can't reach to groom her back end well, any longer. She loves being brushed around her head and neck though, even with our old "scratchier" long-tined brush. You can fill that brush 2-3 times easily, brushing her for just a few minutes, every day. This one, because of the tiny soft covers on the ends of the tines, doesn't seem to dig at her as much, and you don't have to brush her nearly as gently - meaning that you get far more of the clumps out when they are small and just beginning to build.
Our orange cat has extremely soft, short-to-medium hair, and you hardly notice that she sheds much. But when you brush her with the longer-tined, flexible but sharper-ended bristles of our old brush, you fill up the brush surprisingly quickly, and she lets you brush all over. So, she may be the only one that we continue to use the old brush on.
Our old brush sort of pulls the bristles into it, towards the handle, when you push the button on the back of it, to clean it off. The bristles disappear inside the brush, and you can peel the hair off like a little blanket and throw it away.
With this new brush, it is more like the flat base with holes around the bristle seats, comes forward, to the end of the bristles; when you push the button on the back, it pushes that base away from the handle. This may end up bending the bristles less, and keeping the brush usable longer. But it also doesn't compact the hair and make it just "peel off" in one fell swoop. It is more likely that you will leave some hair behind on the brush with this one. It is Worth the trade-off of it being slightly less easy to clean well, because our older, sensitive cat likes it soooo much better, and she is the one who really needs to be brushed the most. This brush is lighter, and feels less substantial than our old brush. Again, we will keep the old brush for the kitten. But this new one is perfect for Sagwa (the old cat), and I am very glad we tried it. If it does crack or bristles break off, because it seems less sturdy, I would buy another one just to keep her happy.

And the fresh smell, which I expected not to like at all because any eucalyptus smell reminds me of cough drops, was actually one of my favorites. It reminded me of men that shower daily, shave regularly, comb their hair, and possibly go to the barber, and get all the ladies. This is what clean men should smell like.

title: Milk Perfume
text:
Just received Milk perfume by K.Hall Designs and I love it! I ordered the candle from this line earlier so that I could have an idea what the perfume smells like and I have to say that the two is very close in scent, except in the perfume I can detect a hint of coconut that I wasn't able to in the candle (even though it's suppose to be there, but maybe that's just me). Milk is not overly sweet at all, it is a perfect balance between creaminess and sweetness, a mellow concoction that is very comforting, a darling little scent that delivers creaminess with a hint of vanilla and coconut. Because it is not a serious scent, it might appeal to a younger audience or to those that normally don't wear perfume. I think it is excellent in the winter time when one uses moisturizers such as almond, honey, vanilla, cocoa etc. as it does combine really well with these scents. In fact, I bought Milk to go with L'Occitane's Almond line and I must say it layers very nicely with it. Like I said, this is such a simple scent, but by no means it is cheap, gaudy or car-freshener like, it reminds me a little of those baby-colognes that you can buy..but a little more grown up.

Update 1/30/2012:
..so, I've been using this perfume for a few weeks now and I noticed that it turns a little too coconutty. When I compare the scent of the candle and the perfume, I can definitively detect more coconut in the perfume, like I said before, and it just has a toasted coconut with a hint of vanilla scent. I much prefer the milky-vanilla scent of the candle, without the overload of the coconut. I think a more appropriate name for this perfume would be "Coconut".
As far as lasting power goes..it's not bad for a perfume.

title: Superior lasting colors!
text:
I've used a few SFX colors and have never been disappointed!

• Cupcake Pink: love this color so much, but definitely needs a very pale base (closest to white blonde, and porous, as possible) or it'll turn a salmon/peach color.
• Atomic Pink: the absolute best hot pink! Deep, electric, and long lasting.
• Sonic Green: more blue-based than I originally realized, I loved the green-teal color. Perfect mix of green with a bit of blue and fades almost minty. It covered over orange bleached hair well.
• Blue Velvet: a gorgeous deep denim blue that starts out deceptively dark and begins to lighten after a few washes. Easily applied over orangey bleached hair.

These are direct, veggie-based dyes, so it does NO harm to leave in your hair long. The longer you leave it in, the more difficult it may be to remove later when you want to change colors, but it'll also ensure you don't need to touch it up for awhile. I easily went over a month on the above colors without needing to refresh.

title: Not 100% Agran Oil, OK for Hair Use, maybe not skin or face
text:
This is no criticism of the distributor of this product, they do tell you the ingredients on the selling page: Cyclopentasiloxane, Dimethicone, Cyclomethicone, Butylphenyl Methylpropional, Argania Spinoza, Kernel Oil(Argan Oil), Linum Usitatissimum (linseed) Extract, Parfum (Fragrance). However, you expect this product to be mostly argan oil, and I don't think it is. First, 100% argan oil usually has a very earthy scent. This product is heavily perfumed. And, if you're trying to reduce the 'cones in your hair styling or skin routine, you can clearly see that Dimethicone and Cyclomethicone are one of the first ingredients, before argan oil.

I did use it on my hair after shampooing and conditioning. I'm not a "no-poo" person, so I don't mind using this for my hair. It did make my hair smooth and shiny with blow-drying. However, there is a lot of fragrance in this product, which stayed with me and on my pillowcase for quite a while. There is also a coating to my hair, unlike pure argan oil which usually sinks in my hair. Some people like that coated feeling on their hair, but I only use those types of products on days where I'll be prone to frizzies.

This product is just OK for me. I would use caution using it on the skin because there is a lot of perfume and additives, so spot check first. I'll just be using it for my hair.

text:
I recently purchased the Savanaah's Organic Argan Oil and the ELMA&SANA Golden Argan Oil because after reading the ingredients on MoroccanOil I wanted to see what the real thing was all about. I read a lot of reviews as well as watched a lot of YouTube videos before purchasing to know what to look for. I understand that the smell could mean nothing and be naturally occurring, but it may imply that the product has gone bad. The Elma&Sana argan oil does not have the most pleasant scent, but I can see where the "nutty" description comes from with the Elma&Sana and it is not off-putting like the Savanaah's.

From what I can tell though, despite the odor the product works well. Since the smell does linger I will not use it post-shower or on my skin, but I have mixed it with pure coconut oil as a hair mask and my hair felt great when I styled it and was much softer compared to when I just use the coconut oil alone.

title: 4/5 It's Not Bad....
text:
I've been using Bare Escentuals "Bare Minerals" mineral makeup since about 2002. I've tried other brands but till now I just didn't find anything I liked as much, let alone better. Lately though the BE makeup just hasn't been agreeing with my skin. I'm getting older and my skin is a bit more sensitive these days apparently. The one thing I never cared for with the BE makeup was their use of bismuth. Anything with bismuth it just makes my skin itch. I've been reading about the negatives of parabens too, and I decided I wanted to get away from that as much as I could.

BE doesn't have that but it does use bismuth, at least they did as of the last time I ordered a big kit. After perusing Amazon and reading ingredient lists I chose to try this kit. Mainly because of the fact that this makeup doesn't have any of that and reviews here already are mostly positive. Also because I liked the eye shadow colors in the trial kit. These are colors I'd use a lot so I didn't feel like I was wasting money on colors I'd never use just to get trials on everything else. The jars are about the size of a BE eyeshadow, a little smaller maybe. The brushes weren't bad but they are small. I put them in my purse kit. They're useful for that, but not for much else. But they're sturdy. They're not losing bristles and they seem fairly soft.

For the most part I like this makeup. It's about the same grind as the BE mineral makeup, feels a bit silkier to me actually. It smells about the same seems maybe a bit less noticeable, the smell. It blends as well, but doesn't feel quite as heavy. The finishing veil is good. I have combination skin and oil in my t-zone and it did a good job of keeping me matte all day. The foundation covers well and doesn't make my face itch at all. The bisque is okay but I don't think it's got quite the coverage of the BE bisque. I did have to use more of it to cover things the same way. I kind of wish this kit had come with sample jars of the colored concealers as I would have liked to have tried those combined with their bisque. I think it might have worked better with that combo. I'm admittedly at a point where a simple bisque concealer is probably not enough for me. I'm getting dark under eye areas and have some red I need to cover now and again.

Their "glow" mixed with the pink blush is my new blush. It's too much for me as a bronzer. I have very pale ivory skin and it just does not work for me all over. Just a little too much orange, a little too dark but it did work okay as blusher over the pink they send you. Combining both that gave me a blusher that worked well for me. The pink blush they give you is just way too light and frosted for me. It just doesn't show up at all. It was the one product in the kit I just did not care much for. I would definitely want a darker more mauve or cinnamon toned blush rather than this one. The pink on it's own is pretty useless. I had to combine the two or forget it. It didn't even look like I had any color on my cheeks.

The foundation colors are decent. Their Fair #1 is actually a near perfect match for me but I'd probably never use the Fair #2 unless it was combined with the Fair #1 maybe. My skin is never that dark, not even in Summer. But Fair #1 I must admit I like that one. It's hard for me to find a foundation that's fair enough that's not too yellow, but Fair #1 works well. Fair #2 is just a tad too dark and just a bit yellow for me.

Overall I'd have to say this kit was a positive experience except for a couple of colors being slightly off for me. I do plan on ordering a big kit but I'm also going to email them and ask if they might send a slightly darker blush and just the Fair #1 x2 instead since they're supposedly picking the cosmetics as they pack for you. Can't hurt to ask, and if they do then their "Fair" kit will work very well for me and I can see myself becoming a regular with this one. I did not expect this product to be as good as it is actually. It was a very pleasant surprise. I'm used to spending a lot more on the BE product. This is much less expensive and in some ways I think I actually like it better than BE so I probably won't be a BE customer much now that I've discovered this.

title: Comparison vs. SKII Facial Treatment Essence
text:
The AMAZING thing about this 'miracle water'? it actually doesn't bead up like water on your skin, but SINKS in and ABSORBS into your pores, what we in the beauty industry call "high skin affinity". Your skin just DRINKS it up. You use it as the first step after cleansing and toning -- this mineral rich, fermented water will act as your "reservoir" BEFORE you pile on the serums and creams, locking in all the hydration so that the essence stays in your skin and doesn't escape.

I have gone thru 5 full-size bottles of SKII over the years and every time i use it, my skin feels rougher and rougher and the hydration level doesn't seem to go up. This doesn't happen with Cremorlab. Moreover, Cremorlab's essence absorbs better than SKII. (SKII can bead up slightly, so you have to work harder at pressing it into your skin). Both SKII and Cremorlab have fermented extracts and good-for-you water-based ingredients; however SKII costs $100 and Cremorlab only is $40 -- and i like Cremorlab's performance more.

title: Realistic expectations
text:
After reading the mixed reviews of this razor, I decided to take a chance and purchase it. I don't regret the purchase one bit.

The positive things that have been written about this razor are true. So are most of the negatives. But I think the biggest problem most reviewers had are setting their expectations, so let me recap my experience.

I've shaved with blades, foil electrics, and rotaries all before. I have sensitive skin, so as much as I like the close shave a blade gives, even the best moisterizer leaves razor burn. Foils have never done anything for me. So I always find myself with a rotary razor. The last razor I *loved* was a Norelco, but after five years, the battery simply could not hold a charge. I tried a Remington last year and was disappointed. Better than a foil, but not my trusty Norelco. So I bought this.

First, there *is* an acclimation period to this razor. Even with my skin "experienced" to rotary razors, it took a month before I started getting *really* close shaves. So people that write and only gave it two weeks and were disappointed...take it with a grain of salt. The manual should say *at least* three weeks. To acclimate faster, you should shave daily. I know a lot of guys with thin or slow growing beards "cheat" and shave every other day, but it makes adjusting slower. Every day. For a month. You'll be happier.

Secondly, many reviewers comment about how this razor only works on stubble. This is true, and yes, my older Norelco (and so I assume the Speed XL's still) can tackle longer fur on your face. But a weed whacker is not a lawn-mower. The lawnmower you use on your yard is not the same quality as the lawnmower a golf course uses on its greens. It is about precision. This razor gives *the* closest shave I've gotten out of an electric. INCLUDING my old Norelco. This gets closer. It is designed for the discerning male who wants a device that grooms with precision and closeness. The trade-off is, to get that close, the lift-and-cut system simply can't handle longer hairs. If you shave daily (see above) then you'll never notice this drawback. But if you let your beard go a day or two at a time, you'll be disappointed. But this razor isn't for that man. If a man is okay with letting some fuzz go for a day, he usually isn't looking for that "perfect" shave, and won't notice the difference between the closeness of a less demanding razor and this one. So this is a device for the elite.

The small trimmer is another criticism. Again, the facts are true. It is small. It is not meant to chop down your entire face. Philips makes beard groomers for that. The trimmer, like every other feature of this device, is designed for the man who shaves daily. It's narrow blade makes grooming sideburns a breeze. Wider clippers make sideburn sculpting far more clumsy. You trim and sculpt, then take the razor to the skin and, since it doesn't do longer hair, you get a perfect sideburn. Again, a design for the man who demands the "perfect" look.

So why four stars if I love this razor so much? One word. Price. The numeric display is nice. The metal finish looks better than the finish on the 1050 as well. But neither of these justifies the $140 premium. I paid it because I think it looks nicer that the 1050, and if I had to, I'd pay it again. But it doesn't mean I actually think it is *worth* the price. I just spoil myself that much. Call me shallow. But the price, for the comparative lack of features does deserve a loss of a star.

--

In summary, if you want the closest shave from an electric ever then this is the razor for you. But it asks for some discipline in return. You have to put attention into yourself to get the most out of it. If you are fond of facial hair, like growing a goatee or chops, you'll want a groomer as well as this razor.

If you are less demanding about your shave then another Norelco device may be a better option. The Speed XL is essentially the newer revision of my old razor and I was perfectly satisfied with it for five years. It was plenty close (but not as close as this) and very comfortable, so really you just have to decide how close you want the shave to be. If you are a perfectionist, get this. If not, save your money and get a Speed XL.

12/29/16 Update:

So I've had time to use a fair number of these bath bombs since receiving them. My only real complaint is that they don't really fizz or bubble to the extent that many other bath bombs do, but I was prepared for that when I placed my order because I had read quite a few reviews on these already.

The saving grace for this product is that they make my skin feel super soft! Which I love.

The botanical pieces don't really bother me the way it seems to bother a lot of other people apparently. Yes, if you purchase these your bathtub may require a bit of cleanup if the pieces don't wash completely down the drain after your bath. Be prepared. This is a natural product, so you're going to get bits and pieces of the plants that were used in their creation. I personally enjoy that.

Would I purchase these again? Meh. I like the way that they make my skin feel, but I will probably look at other options in the future.

title: A nice standard wipe for just about anything you'll put in your mouth
text:
I don't have a retainer, but I do have a nightguard and I figured that since it's made out of the same stuff you'd see for some of the mouthguards and the like out there, why not give it a try? I'm always a little leery of brushing since I don't want to ruin my brushes or potentially harm my nightguard. Soaking it in some mouthwash is helpful, but then that isn't the same as a thorough clean.

The taste of this is fairly nice. I like that it's not extremely overwhelming. You can wipe your guard down and it won't be insanely strong. There will be a hint of flavor, but overall it's not going to be anything that will knock your socks off. This might be disappointing for some, but it's still a better thing to taste than the alternative. If you have a guard of any type, you know what I'm talking about.

This will get into most of the crevices and areas of the average guard. You'll have to cram it into the more small areas, but it will fit everywhere. It seems to do a fairly good job of cleaning as well. I'd read that it could help get rid of stains and other discolorations, which is the biggest thing that appealed to me. So far I've done a few cloths and it seems to be helping a little. It's not a miracle worker, but then I wasn't expecting it to be and to be honest, I'd be more than a little leery of something that would remove all the yellowing immediately. After all, what would it do to your mouth afterwards?

This is a pretty good option and I'm curious to try the soaks to see what they would do as well.

title: Much easier than glue
text:
This was my first attempt at using magnetic lashes; there's a small learning curve but oh my gosh - SO MUCH EASIER than the old eyelash glue that comes in a separate tube! They're very comfortable; like any false lashes they feel weird at first but after about 15 minutes I forgot they were there & wore them all day with no issues. They stay where you put them, they DO NOT budge until you pull them off. No glue melting or flaking off into my eyes, obviously that's a big benefit! They look super dramatic with pretty minimal effort.

I'm a little confused as to why it's best to apply the lashes when the eyeliner is half-dry but still tacky; is there glue built in to the liner as well as magnets? If you need to reposition them, you have to reapply the eyeliner because the lashes pull some of it off. The eyeliner is very wet when you apply, so be careful - you have to shake the tube before application, and when I pulled the brush out, it spewed eyeliner onto the wall (and it was not super easy to remove). So that's the learning curve part, now that I know I'll avoid those pitfalls.

The one unavoidable pitfall is that it is INCREDIBLY difficult to remove. I used 3 different types of makeup remover & still needed to scrub my eyelids for a good 10 minutes to get all of it. Not great for the eyelid wrinkle situation! I slathered on a lot of pampering eye cream afterward because my lids were a little sore. I guess I'm glad it won't wear off halfway through the day, but geez!

Anyway, despite the difficulty removing it, I'm pretty smitten. I used to love wearing false lashes but they were just so much trouble that I gave it up a few years ago. Now I love them again & they're easy!! I want to order all the lashes!

text:
I found this stuff locally, for only a couple bucks more. We had to make a bullet wound for my husband and radiation burns for me for halloween costumes. He was Abe Lincoln and I was Marie Curie.

[...]

Here's some of the results and instructions for use, the booklet that comes with the kit is better though and quite helpful.

I will say that you do need more than these three bottles alone to make your wounds. You also need a color wheel of makeup for burns/wounds - black, purple, red, browns. Since we were zombies, I also used a base layer of white paint to make my skin ashen. You will need wedges or a cheap brush to apply the gel. You need water slightly hotter than hot tap water to melt the gel before you can use it. You'll have to play with it to get the right temperature - too hot and it will run right off the area you want it to be in, too cold and it won't dispense. I had to blow on it a few times during application to get it to set, and it wasn't even that hot.

As long as you do a red/black layer of paint on your skin BEFORE applying this gel, it will look great. If you don't, the blood gel is too bright red when in a single or even double layer.

I also used some very thin fried egg white to make myself burned skin to stick on top and inside the gel. With the blood on top, it looked great.

If you don't set the results with setting powder, it will be sticky to the touch. Just use a light dusting and blow off the excess - any visible white powder remaining will disappear on its own after a few minutes.

title: Bought for use with UV Resin
text:
I didn't buy this for nails, but for curing UV Resin. And it works like a charm. I'm using resin from the Sophie & Toffee brand at the moment, and I leave it in for roughly 10min each cure. It's given me consistent hard cures each time.

The lamp is really lightweight and isn't any heavy duty plastic but if you're a bit careful and don't drop it, drop things on it, throw it, or otherwise abuse it I don't think it's a problem. It is a little big but nothing extreme, and in the case of resin work it's better that way because you can fit larger molds in. I'd hazard a guess that molds the size of the Mod Podge molds would fit (all of mine are smaller at the moment).

It's not noisy, it doesn't produce heat that I've noticed, and the bottom tray/panel does come out (it doesn't always slide easily). It did come with the bulbs packaged with styrofoam inserts to keep them from breaking. They were installed already and it worked straight out of the box. There aren't any instructions but they've got those here on this page so it's not an issue.

The seller then offered to send me a larger diffuser free of cost. We have corresponded several times and they have gone above and beyond to make my customer experience a happy one. I have rarely seen this type of commitment from a seller anywhere in the name of customer satisfaction.
It is quite a different set up than most other misters. This one includes a green red and yellow light for the interval you want the mist going. The first light (green) will turn off after 3 hours, the second light (red) will run continuously and then turn off automatically when water runs out, the third light (yellow) will run for 30 seconds, turn off for 30 seconds and cycle like this until it runs out of water and turns off automatically.
The diffuser and the remote work well and it has a very cute look with a wood grain base. The colors are very bright and pretty when lit.
Thank you Depree for working with me and I am enjoying my new free 400ml diffuser just as much!

title: Over [price] for a toothbrush?? It's worth every penny!!!!
text:
First of all, I am not a dental professional...
I didn't think much about it when my wife told me that she wanted a new toothbrush for Christmas...but I took notice when I found out how much the one was that she wanted. Around [price] for a toothbrush seemed a bit excessive to me at first! But we went ahead and got one anyway. My wife is a dental hygienist, and the dentist she works for highly recommends this product (and he rarely if ever recommends dental products!). As it turned out, we received a second toothbrush from my folks at Christmas, so we are the proud owners of two Sonicare toothbrushes.
I've been reserving judgement on this product until I've had a good chance to see how I like it. After a month of regular use I've got to say that it's GREAT! The internal timer is a good idea. It helps you to pace your tooth brushing, making sure that you spend enough time to insure adequate cleaning. Though one 2-minute cycle is long enough for a good brushing, I often brush for two of those cycles. I sometimes use the brush without toothpaste and sit and read while I brush for two or three cycles. The sonic cleaning really does a great job! When I'm done my teeth feel clean and smooth, as good or better than after I get done with a professional cleaning.
I can honestly say that my gums feel like they are in better shape than they used to be, and my teeth are cleaner on a regular basis.
After a full month of using a Sonicare brush I give it two thumbs up. Our children (ages 6, 8, 10) use it as well, and they enjoy it too.
The brush handle contains a rechargable battery, and the brushes are available in different sizes. I like the compact head better than the larger head. The handle takes a little getting used to, since it is much larger than a standard toothbrush's handle. It also takes a few brushings to get used to the rapid vibrations in your mouth -- it can really tickle -- and I imagine that if you have sensitive gums that it could cause some mild painat first, but will certainly firm up the gums and help their condition improve in good order. It really made my saliva run the first few times I used it, but that's not a problem now. Another thing that takes a little getting used to is the fact that you don't have to supply the muscle power to do the brushing. All you have to do is to hold the brush head gently against the teeth and the handle does the rest.
All in all, I'd say that Sonicare's brush is the best oral hygeine product I've ever used. Definitely in the 5-star category!
Brush on!
Alan Holyoak

title: Good, but no better than the cheaper Norelcos!
text: I have tested many brands of electric shavers over the decades but I have stayed with Norelco because I prefer their design and performance. My present Norelco, about 5 years old, is still going strong but needs a new battery so I thought I'd try the Arcitec 1060. It looks very high-tech with its articulated heads, but the bottom line is it shaves no better than my old model. I actually shaved half my face with the Arcitec and the other half with my old one. There was not the slightest difference in the closeness and I had the same amount of stubble on both sides 24 hours later. What's more, my old Norelco still has its original blades! It's also more solid and I think it's nicer to use. Also, the Arcitec has very little space beneath the cutters to hold the beard clippings, so you have to wash the heads after every use. Not a big deal, but I wash my old heads maybe once a week. So the Arcitec is going back. My advice to those in need of a new shaver: Try one of Norelco's cheaper models first.

title: But I bought this product because I received a REALLY bad perm at a salon and after dealing with damage
text:
USE THIS ON CURLY HAIR for smooth curls!!!!! I know this seems strange. But I bought this product because I received a REALLY bad perm at a salon and after dealing with damage, fuzz and frizz for about 4 months I was fed up and decided to give up and straighten it. The prices for a salon straitening treatment was outrageous. So I decided to attempt it myself.

When the box arrived, I loved how all of the products are full sized. I was going to wait until the weekend to do the whole straightening process but decided to go ahead and try out the clarifying shampoo and deep conditioners during the week. I could tell even after the first use of the shampoo and conditioner what a difference it made to the texture of my hair. It softened it and smoothed the curls and now I can run my fingers through it without it tangling.

So needless to say, the shampoo and conditioners alone fixed my fuzzy issues without having to straighten my hair. I love my soft curls now and am so grateful that I decided to "test" the shampoos and conditioners. It just made sense to me to try it because even though these are made to smooth straight hair, it can still smooth curls as well. So I use #1,3,4,5 every week. I went ahead and tossed #2 - the straightening solution.

They need to market their conditioners and shampoos to curly headed people!! Unfortunately I will have to buy the whole kit each time I need to replace the conditioner or shampoo since they do not sell the separate :-( But, this product has saved my hair so it is totally worth it.

UPDATE (05/08/17):

After leaving my initial review, I was surprisingly contacted by the seller who offered to provide me with either a refund or a replacement cap. I wanted to find out whether the first heat cap I received may have been defective so I opted to receive replacement unit. When I received the replacement, the first thing I noticed is that it is a different (seemingly updated) model matching what is now listed here. Compared to the original unit I received, this newer version definitely has improvements. The replacement cap fits much better than the original which greatly reduces the amount of heat that escapes. It also seems that this cap produces a better amount of heat than the original one I received a few months ago. The biggest improvement over the first cap I received is that this heat cap has a built-in timer which automatically shuts off after 15, 30, or 60 minutes of use.

I'm satisfied with the replacement cap I received. Kudos to the seller (Nilmee) for going above and beyond to make sure that this customer walked away happy with his purchase.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I'm torn on this heat cap, when it comes down to it, it's just okay. I've been using it here and there over the past few months and I'm just not impressed. The heating on the cap is inconsistent -- some areas get warm while others have barely noticeable heating. My biggest gripe with the cap is that it seems to be sized either for people with large heads or with an overabundance of hair. I have a shorter hair style and I either have to pull on the chin strap or lay down while using the cap, otherwise what little heat the cap emits just escapes through gaps.

If you have short hair or have a smaller cranium, you may want to explore other options.

title: Sorry, I choose Amazon
text:
This is my first time using Amazon.com for purchases other than books and software. So after carefully examining the various razors and reading previous purchasers critiques I decided to go all out and buy the "TOP" of the range product the Philips Norelco arcItec 1090XD Men's Shaving System.
This was not a snap decision as I also physically examined the model in Booths chemist. And after admiring the self cleaning aspects of the so called "SYSTEM" I gave myself a little treat and placed the order. This order also included an extra carton of cleaning lotion and a spare set of cutters.
I duly received the product but low and behold no cleaning "POD". How can this razor be accurately described as a shaving system. Surly a top of the range "Shaving system" includes the cleaning pod.

Enough of my woes but buyers beware. Once bitten twice shy.

On the razor itself I cannot say enough to express by satisfaction with this product.
I have over the pass 40 years always used an "electric" razor. Including 2 Braun and more recently 3 Philips or Norelco models.

The razor is a joy to use. It gives a lovely and almost silent cut. It looks and feels fantastic. The humble "electric" razor has certainly come along way and progressed to the development of this model. The design is so well balanced between the cutting heads and the main body it's as if the cutters were attached to the top of your thumb. The charging system does exactly what it say on the box and is fully charged in 60mins. It does remind you to empty and clean the cutter head after every use. But this is a relatively straight forward exercise and not as off putting as other commentators have suggested. The recharging stand complements the razor in both design and usefulness. It has suction pads on the bottom to ensure that the stand and razor won't move from its correct place. OK the trimmer is not as big as on my current model. But it does exactly what I need in tidying sideburns and trimming over ears etc.
Look it's a Razor not a hair grooming machine.

Would I recommend the razor? Most definitely YES, it's a man's razor. And thankfully as previous ladies have comment on its does not suit their needs. So hopefully I will not see my wife borrowing it either.

However be careful where you buy the product and don't get stung like me.
[[ASIN:B0014N0MFK Philips Norelco arcitec 1090XD Men's Shaving System]]

text:
This set of bottles come in a six-pack with blue, green, purple, pink, and two clear. They're fairly standard plastic travel-bottles; they squeeze but they're just a little bit thin and brittle in your fingers. If you want something that will stand up to serious compression, you'll have to look at the more expensive bottles with a more rubberized texture.

The pull spout is a good one; there's a ridge inside that holds it closed, and it takes some significant effort to pull it open. This could actually be a drawback for someone without a strong grip, but it does ensure the bottle won't leak easily and I like the feature. It will wear down over time, but I expect it to last a few years at least which is about as much as you can ask for this price, and the whole lit screws off for refilling and cleaning.

I would have given these five stars, except that the current image is not very accurate. The bottles are taller than it looks in the picture. The only complaint I have is that even at maximum pressure it is not as strong as our previous one. title: I liked the idea better than the product
text:
With four cats and a large dog, I am always looking for good grooming tools. I liked the idea of this brush, but the actual product really wasn't all that. First of all, this thing is much larger than any other slicker style brush I have. This is a great feature for my large dog, but it was just ridiculous trying to groom my cats with this large, unyielding wire brush. So, not a good choice for the cats.

Unfortunately, not a good choice for my dog either, as she has a short coat with little to no undercoat and she was really uncomfortable with wires dragging on her skin. She's more of a rubber curry comb type gal, I guess. Besides the size and wire bristle problems, the plastic itself felt a little brittle and cheap and when you add in the mechanics of retractable bristles... I think higher quality material would have been a better choice because that slider for the bristles is very basic. Finally, while I loved the idea of the easy-to-clean retractable bristles, they really aren't necessary and if those wires become crooked or bent it will cause all kinds of problems with the retraction. I've made it decades by just pulling the fur out of my slicker brushes-- it literally takes 2-3 seconds-- and while the thought of retractable bristles is nice, it totally isn't necessary. It's not a practical tool for me and doesn't work for any of my animals due to its size and the wire bristles. It also doesn't seem terribly well-made nor is it made of high-quality materials, and for the price it should be.

title: Now I'm too sexy
text:
Now that I bought and used the T980, my cool slacker goatee is attracting too many women. I'm not getting any rest.

Naturally, a product that causes grief should be down-rated, but I won't here because this shaver is just doing its job.

And, we all like things with "turbo" in the description, however loosely that term is applied. It makes it go faster with a cool noise, so even in a shaver that is attractive to many.

Electric shavers for beards sure beat the heck out of scissors! The Norelco has a wide range of cutting depths and my beard comes out a uniform length. I did not feel any pulling or other discomfort. The charge seems to last for days and the charger itself, like the shaver, is a decent and modern design.

The little detail cutter is easy to attach and does a great job of defining the beard area and also clipping any stray hairs under the nose where the big cutter head cannot reach.

Some people think the closest cutting position is still not close enough for that short-stubble look and that does seem to be the case. I don't want mine that close, but I understand those who do and I take off a star for brotherly solidarity. Actually, I'm sure that if it was to cut more closely, that would take it into the realm of regular shavers, an expensive world of high-tech blades and lubricants. Actually, if you press down a little, you can get closer.

The turbo thing works well. It vacuums almost every hair into the storage chamber. I didn't expect the vacuum action to work so well. I think the turbo button should be the only button, but there it is. The non-turbo setting is less noisy...

The parts detach easily and the little supplied brush works well to clean it out. The little travel pouch is nice.

The T980 works just as it should, for me, and the price is reasonable. I think it will last a long time and I am glad I bought it.

As for the women, I did exaggerate. One did make a favorable comment which is one more than before. That is an improvement, eh?

title: Excellent Kit!
text:
I'm just getting back into using a safety razor after decades of using a multiblade cartridge razor and/or really high end electric shavers, and I'm very happy with this kit. Functionality wise, is just excellent. It's easy to switch out blades, nice weight to it, nice grip. I also really like the brush and stand and the look of the whole set displayed in my bathroom. It's great when a razor works well, but it's even better when it looks great for the 23.5 hours per day that you're not using it.

The blades that come with the set seem decent, but I also ordered a 15 brand 2-blade variety pack, and will be going through each of these brands to find the one(s) I like the most.

If you're just getting back into safety razor shaving like me or if you're doing this for the first time, hang in there. Watching a few YouTube videos will help you. Most importantly, do not treat this like a multi-blade, lubricated cartridge razor. Safety razors are one-pass razors, do not apply pressure, and don't shy away from pre/after shaving skin/beard conditioners, lotions, etc. When you do everything right, this single blade will give you the best, closest shave you've ever had.

title: Pretty decent product but do your research
text:
Overall, this product isn’t horrible compared to others on the market. It is paraben-free, sulfate-free, EU Allergen free and uses minimal ingredients however it also contains alcohol, silicone and is not safe for fungal acne. After running this product through a cosmetic ingredient safety checker, it scored an 88% one the EWG Health Rating. Most popular, name-brand face lotions are around 65%-80% on the EWG Health Rating. I use the EWG (Environment Working Group) as a reference when checking products and try to stay away from the alarmist side. Only 8% of this product is considered “moderate risk” mainly polyarylamide, Fragrance (unnecessary additive; possible allergy) , alcohol denat. (Bad for dry skin, bad for sensitive skin, potentially block pores) and BHT (also found in edibles, rubber products and is banned in UK and EU due to limited research showing BHT is linked to cancer). This product is good for brightening, anti-aging and promotes wound healing. It also contains steric acid which can potentially block pores.

Keep in mind, everyone’s skin is different and what effects one person may not effect another. Learn your skin and what products work best for you. Personally, I would stay away from this product if you have very dry skin and/or sensitive skin. I have “normal” skin (no sensitivities, not overly dry or oily, limited acne, no allergies) and didn’t have any issues with this product so far. It has a light scent that isn’t overpowering but completely unnecessary (I HATE fragrance in beauty products; stick with essential oils). It absorbed nicely and didn’t leave my face feeling oily. I am giving this product 4 stars as of February 21, 2021 due to the minimal ingredients and will update this review once a larger amount of time has passed to fully understand how to works with my skin.

title: We Tried EVERYTHING To Get This To Work
text:
When it comes to styling devices, my family all has different preferences because we all have different hair. This looked like a really great product. Let's take a look..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This comes in a nice box, well packed in a fancy presentation and comes with a little manual. The device has four buttons on it which are power, temp up or temp down or timer. The bent curling iron is supposed to be more handy to use.

MANUAL
The manual is bare bones. It looks fancy but never tells what temperature or time would be good to start with for different types of hair. That was very disappointing. It does tell how to basically press the buttons and what they are for, however.

HOW DID THIS PERFORM?
We tried this several times on various occasions. Each time, we set the temperature higher and higher until we were at the top temp but very few of the curls we tried making worked. The hair simply had a light bend in it. When using a different curling iron with each person, the hair looked great. Finally after trying for the last time today, we have determined that this curling iron just does not work. I am not sure if we got a bad one or what, but it just does not do hardly anything except leaving a partial bend in the hair no matter how we wind it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although a great concept, this curling iron did not seem to curl hair properly no matter what hair we used it on or how high or low the temperature was set.

MY RATING
TWO STARS. Great idea, just didn't work at all for us.

title: Mowin' the five-o'clock shadow
text:
There was a time when I couldn't stand shaving my face. No matter what type of instrument I used-- single- and double-bladers, Norelcos, EpiLady-- after the act I usually found myself annoyed by skin irritation, razor burn, and nicks that took forever to stop bleeding. But when I tried the Mach 3, which changed the dreaded shaving ritual from a bothersome, dreadful task into... well, a less-bothersome, tolerable task. I got closer and cleaner shaves with fewer strokes than I did with previous depilatory implements, and my face didn't sting quite after the deed had been performed. I also experienced fewer nicks and cuts, helping to keep my styptic pencil bills down. Unfortunately, the max number of shaves I could ever get out of a single Mach 3 V 1.0 cartridge was six before the dullness set in (partially due to my coarse facial hair) and the lube strip began to poop out.
I was surprised by how well Gillette managed to improve on most of the Mach 3's designs with the release of the Mach 3 Turbo. Now it takes even fewer passes to get them cheeks & chin baby-bottom bare, and I've managed to make the average Turbo cartridge last through eight shaves. And thanks to the apparently-improved lube strip and that little face-stretcher thingy on the bottom part of the tri-blade, my face only feels a light sting in a stiff wind after a shave. Another great surprise: I didn't have to buy a new kit for the Turbo cartridges-- they snap right onto my original Mach 3 razor handle, no sweat!
Thanks to the Gillette® Mach 3 Turbo, that semi-weekly shaving ritual I once dreaded has gone from a less-bothersome, tolerable task to... an even-less-bothersome and even-more tolerable task! Boy, if Gillette keeps improving on this product, I might one day actually find myself enjoying the act of mowin' the five-o'clock shadow!
`Late.

title: I wear them everyday
text:
10 months ago, I cut off ALL my hair, (49 3/4 inches, so A LOT) to give to a coworker whose teenage daughter had cancer and needed hair to have a wig made. I had enough hair where she wouldn't need to even ask anyone else, so yeah, I chopped it all off. That girl cares more about the way she looks, then I do, at my age. But I remember being 14...and I cared at that age what I looked like. I cared a whole bunch. But now, not so much, and since locks of love and other charities don't give wigs to cancer patients because "their hair should grow back" (nonsense), her parents were looking for something affordable and found a place that would make a real hair wig, for about $1000, if they supplied the hair.

For the first few months after I cut it off, all was fine. I have never had short hair before and honestly it was nice. But as it grew out, it started to become annoying. I have a very prominent widows peak, so never had bangs, and it was getting long enough to get in my face which was super aggravating. Plus, having it on my neck...can't even describe how that cut the nerves....

I have never really wore headbands, so didn't have any, so started searching online for something to help keep my growing hair off my face. I read the reviews on this headband set, and many others. Focusing only on the negative reviews, because...thats what matters right? Why don't people like these? Only thing I saw on this set though was that people thought they were to tight.

I have an average size head, definitely not small, but don't think it overly large either...and since they were cotton, I saw this set as a win, win. They were the width I wanted, the neutral colors I wanted, and if they were a bit small, would be more likely to hold up the hair behind my head better. If they were TO small, they were cotton, so I could stretch them out. Plus, the price was definitely good for the number you get, compared to others I looked at.

So, I ordered them in June and have pretty much had them on my head everyday since. I didn't find them to small at all. Only problem I'm having is, I keep misplacing them! So, actually came on to order more, as I can only find two at the moment...but decided I would go ahead and write a review while I was here. It's still going to be a while before my hair is long enough to pull up in a ponytail, so until then, I am 100% reliant on these to keep my sanity, as my hair grows back in.

Makeup Eraser Claims:

Makeup Eraser removes 100% of your makeup with just water.
Removes mascara including waterproof mascara in just seconds.
Cloth is approximately 7" wide x 16" long.
All natural, no chemicals, and machine washable.

Makeup Remover Claims:

Reusable. Simply clean it in the wash for a brand new cloth, again and again.
Absolutely NO harsh chemicals on your face
Super soft material that is gentle on the skin
Clears away hard to remove makeup with less effort

Makeup Remover (purple) Pros and cons Vs. The Makeup Eraser (pink)
* Both cloths are soft and both sides feel the same as the other.
*The purple cloth is a tad bigger than the pink cloth which is nice.
* They both remove waterproof mascara easily along with other regular makeup.
* They both wash up the same.
* The makeup eraser feels thicker than the Makeup Remover but does not affect the makeup removers ability to remove makeup.
*The price is quite different. The Makeup Remover (purple) is around $13.00 and the Makeup Eraser is around $20.00 for pretty much the exact same thing.

If you are looking for a way to save money and want a cheaper version than the Makeup Eraser but performs the exact same, I would go with the Makeup remover. Save that extra money because this cloth performs the same thing as the Makeup Eraser.

text:
I've gone through a dozen concealers trying to find one that both matched my pale warm olive skin tone and covered my extremely dark circles. This concealer beats out all the rest, even the $60 concealer I tried out of desperation.
I purchased the lightest shade, Frozen, and it matches me extremely well. For reference, I'm about NC10-15. This would probably also work well for one shade darker in the Nars Sheer Glow (Gobi I think it's called?).
Frozen is not an olive tone; it's straight-up warm/yellow-based. However, since I use it to cover rosacea and purple/brown under-eye circles, the extra yellow doesn't clash with my complexion.
The texture is a thick cream---thicker than Nars Radiant Creamy Concealer, sort of like Tarte Shape Tape, but not nearly as chalky or quick-drying. It has a very natural luminosity and you have lots of time to work with it before it sets. You can achieve full coverage with just a small amount of product, and it builds well without getting cakey. title: MIxed feelings
text:
After reading on many shaving blogs about how much closer a straight-edge razor will shave, I decided to try it out. I got tired of using disposables and having difficulty cleaning them and dealing with the cost. Having never tried straight edge shaving before, I debated whether to buy a high end blade, a cheap one, or something in the middle. I decided to go for the higher end of the lower cost models and bought one of these.

My first impression on removing it from the box was that the gold embossing on the handle really detracted from the looks of an otherwise attractive blade. But it doesn't really matter what it looks like if it works well. Out of the box, it is not shave ready. I did everything I'd read about to prep properly (except hone the blade) and it just didn't produce a close shave and pulled quite a bit. By way of comparison, I went back over and got a much improved result from a three week old disposable afterwards.

I have no doubt that this will take an edge and function just fine, and I suspect there is some truth to the "snob" argument that a better blade will hold an edge longer, as is true of knives, but almost any blade can be honed to sharpness. In fact, I subsequently purchased a different brand of carbon steel blade that was pre-honed from the seller and it performed quite nicely. To be fair, I don't know that a more expensive blade won't have the same issues if not honed by the seller prior to shipment.

As stated by another reviewer, any blade will require maintenance and the skills to sharpen it if you plan to use it regularly. I will give a try at sharpening this one eventually since I will need to learn this skill. Just be aware that you may need to develop the skill or find someone to do it for you before you will get a good result.

title: Helps remove debris stuck between teeth, and deal with tartar/plaque
text:
[[VIDEOID:cbac90e8387083ce10f04b521f9fab97]] These stainless steel dental picks are well-made. The ridged areas of the picks help give me a secure grip.

Before I use any of the picks, I sterilize them as follows:
a) I boil water, then place the picks in them for 10+ minutes.
b) Then, I lay them on a clean plate to cool.
c) Once the picks have cooled enough for me to handle, I choose a pick to take care of my teeth/gums.

I use the dental pick with the sharp hook at the end to remove stubborn food debris stuck between my teeth that my toothpick cannot remove.
I use the dental pick with an end that reminds me of a chisel to pick away at the plaque/tartar.

The dental mirror gives me a good view of the inside of my mouth, so I know what parts need to be worked on.
I breathed on the mirror, and it did not fog up. The light is bright.
note: the product description page makes no mention of what to do if the light doesn't work. There was no user guide included with this kit when I opened the package containing these picks and mirror.

Overall, I find this oral care kit to be useful in helping me take care of my gums and teeth at home in between the times I see my dentist.

title: Works Good For Minor Stretch Marks
text:
Because I am a plus size woman, naturally I have stretch marks on various areas of my body. I have been using this Stretch Mark Cream by Luxy Beauty Care for a couple of weeks now, and I have had some pretty decent results so far using this.

I have stretch marks on my stomach, upper arms and around my bust. The stretch marks on my arms and bust are fairly small in size and more minor than the ones on my stomach. I have found that this cream is working well for my arms and bust, I am seeing progress in their visibility. On my stomach, the ones that I call my tiger stripes, they are a bit more stubborn. I think that if I use this cream for a while, and keep up my routine, results will come. I do recommend for those stubborn stretch marks to exfoliate the area a few times a week. This method in combination with this stretch mark cream has been my best friend!

I give this 4 stars, it is a great product, and one that I definitely recommend giving a shot if you want to treat your stretch marks. However if you have the stubborn ones, this will work, but it goes a bit more on the slower side.

Please note that I was sent this product complimentary to try out in my home in order to share my honest experience, thoughts and review.

I had to wet my hair and try to comb it out, but even that didn’t help it still looked gray and gross, leaving me to cover it up with a hat. I should’ve just washed it out completely.

I gave up today after giving it a try this entire week. I was hoping that I could find a green alternative and use this for travel because you’re not supposed to bring aerosols on planes, but this wasn’t worth all of the trouble it caused at all.

title: Beautiful, baby soft skin! Perfect for sandal season!
text: I have used these soft touch foot peeling care AHA acid peel socks a few times now.  I absolutely love them.  I have tried other Korean brands without any success at all and have always gone back to this brand every time.  I soak my feet prior to use for about 10-15 minutes to soften them up.  Then, I put the socks on and add in the liquid, tie them up and put loose cotton socks over them.  I sit and relax for about an hour and a half while the AHA does it's work.  After that, I just rinse my feet off and wait for the peeling.  Two to three days later, my feet will start peeling. Don't peel the skin off like you do for a sunburn.  Just let the skin slough off.  I like to soak my feet a couple more times during the peeling process.  When the peeling is all done (in about 5 days or so) my feet are so soft.  There are no dry heels, no rough spots, just beautiful baby soft skin.  It's recommended not to do these peels more than every 3 or 4 months.  I stick to that.  I normally do one per season.  But, I love the way my feet look just before summer and sandal season.  These foot peels are going to be a staple in my routine for some time.

title: Good overall quality but bad design
text:
This is the third of Norelco's waterproof series that I have owned.
The overall quality is just as good as previous models and other Philips/Norelco products.
The shaver is constructed well and is lighter and more compact than previous models. Charging and battery life also seem to be very good.

The main problem I find with this new design is that the heads/razors are floating and not encased as previous models and most other shavers. When using this shaver in the shower this is not a problem. However, when you use this shaver outside of the shower, the lack of casing around the heads means that as you shave, all of the hair pieces fall from the shaver to the counter or wherever else you may be (I would not recommend using this shaver in the car unless you don't mind getting yourself and your car covered with hair pieces). To me this is a major oversight and design flaw.
In short, if you only plan to use this razor in the shower this is a good choice, but if you need to use the razor outside of the shower as well, you may want to choose something else.

title: Love This Shaver
text:
I replaced my Norelco Spectra with this Smart-Touch 9190 XL and it works as advertised. I liked the Spectra, but compared to it the XL simply outclasses the old one.

The XL takes less time, shaves closer and is quieter. It also has a much bigger chamber to hold the cut hair. And the trimmer works well. According to the manual, it takes up to 3 weeks to conform to your skin and you may get some irritation until it gets broken in. I set it to sensitive and have had very little skin irritation from day one.

It has some nice features including a screen that tells you how many minutes you have used and how many you have left. Or, you can change the display to a battery indicator. It also tells you when to rinse, charge the razor and change the blades. Another nice feature is the travel lock. You hold the power button for 3 seconds and it locks which prevents it from accidentally turning on. The charging base has a little clock, but I do not see the point in that.

My old razor had the digital information screen so that is what I wanted in a new razor. However, if you do not need or want that feature then I would suggest getting the cheaper model. I think all the other features are the same on both, plus you would save a lot of money. Personally, I like the 9190XL but the choice is up to you.

Pros:

Faster shave.

Closer shave.

Information screen.

Easily rinses clean.

Holds charge for a long time.

Quiet operation.

Cons:

Pricey.

title: My cat lost his everloving mind...
text:
I wanted something small for grooming my short-hair cat & this was the best I could find. I'm glad I gave it a try!
It has a narrow metal comb, which works like every other comb, but it's sized right for a cat - no more stabbing him in the shoulders & haunches.
The second comb, with curved fingers, is what really makes this brush a winner. The teeth are plastic, so they're soft. My cat lost his mind when I started brushing him with it. I've never heard him purr so loud. He even made muffins. He never makes muffins. I have to hide the brush because, when he sees it, he starts patting me & looking at the brush. It's adorable. And slightly terrifying (no cat should be that smart).
There are a few downsides to the plastic comb. First, it doesn't hold the hair it knocks loose, so you have to follow each stroke of the brush with your hand to pick up all the loose hair. Second, it electrifies the cat. Every loose hair that you fail to catch floats up & sticks to you, until you look like Cousin It. And the cat looks ridiculous with such static-y fur - I've learned to keep a spray bottle or bowl or water nearby to kill the static.
Even with these drawbacks, I love this brush, if only for the joy it brings my cat.

I am fair skinned and often burn, even in the winter. My family jokes that I'm the only person they know who ends up with a sunburn on Thanksgiving and Christmas living in zone 6A. It's sad, but true. And if you've ever had sunburned lips, you know it's something you don't want a repeat of. Blisters and cracking are terrible, but on your delicate lips they make speaking and eating torture.

I'm quite pleased with these so far. Panama Jack is a great brand and known for their sun care products. The lip balm is excellent. It has a broad spectrum of sunscreen included, the scents are great and tropical, it goes on feeling smooth and moist, and it lasts! It need reapplied every two hours or every 80 minutes if you're in water, but it definitely helps! I can feel it on my lips, although it goes on smooth and soft, and I know it's working to keep me from getting burned. Honestly, I'm not sensitive to any of the ingredients and in a pinch, it's even great to put on my nose to protect it in the harsh winter, but sunny conditions here.

The multi pack was an awesome value. Seven balms cost less than getting three or four separately. My only negative was that the lid on my mango was busted, but it is still moist and I used an old balm lid to make sure it didn't dry out. I'll definitely get more of these. They don't really have a taste, but they smell amazing. They're clear to white in color and don't deposit any color or stain on my lips.

Reputable brand and skin protection! I can keep one in the house, one in the car, one in my purse, one in the medicine kit, and then extras for when I run out or lose one!

My Second daughter (8) and my son (5) also started to get a rash on their necks during this time, and then last but not least my husband.  None of our family have sensitive skin just fyi.  We finally figured out it was the sunblock and a few days after stopping it and treating with meds, their rashes are finally improving.  To be fair, myself and my 2 year old son did not get a rash, although we used it less as we stay inside more and try to stay in the shade as much as possible when out.  I read a few other reviews that mention this same issue, especially around the neck area and I just want you to be aware so that if this happens to you, you don’t waste valuable time and resources trying to figure out where the rash came from.

title: Great for Tutorials
text:
Lashes are a way of life when it comes to a make up routine. For someone who opts to go full force everyday, the thought of easier lash application was a no brainer. Not to mention, the ability to purchase lashes and liquid liner with one click of a button makes life that much easier. The application of the liner was easy and smooth, it went on very similar to a higher end liner. The applicator brush was a bit thicker than I’d prefer, but considering this little line was going to actually hold the lashes on, no big deal. I was thoroughly impressed when I began placement of the lashes. Each mini magnet grabbed right to the liner and wa-la! I had longer, more fun lashes.
But that’s where the magic ended. I always do my eyes first, and then the rest of my face, usually completing my routine within 45 minutes. By the time I was dressed and ready to go for my girls night out approximately an hour later, the lashes were lifting on both eyes and I had to take them off and reapply two more times before deciding they weren’t going to stick again this go around.
All-in-all, if you are looking for a quick way to have fun, flirty lashes during a makeup tutorial, quick pics, etc. grab a pair and have fun. But, if you’re looking for a long lasting night out, I’d opt for real glue.

title: I was so pleased that they gave customers enough credit to tell them ...
text:
So, first of all I was impressed by the level of scientific knowledge that they provide to the consumer when advertising this product. I have found that a lot of these skincare products either assume you know why you are buying this treatment over another, or don't have the scientific backing to emphasize their products effectiveness. Having worked in the makeup and skincare field for the last 10 years, I was so pleased that they gave customers enough credit to tell them how it works!

That being said, this product is really wonderful for adding luminosity and smoothness to the skin. It is rich, but not sticky, and leaves the skin feeling like you applied a moisturizer more so than a serum (which I appreciate being oily skinned and not always preferring to wear moisturizer under makeup). I'd call this a slow but potent product that will give you the results you want if you are patient (but nothing gives the results that going under the knife will give, so don't expect it).
