title: Very cheaply made. This is not a high quality item. Mine is defective...
text:
It is very cheaply made. Mine is defective. Gotta charge it from a computer's USB port... Before buying this, try to find other real reviews of people like me who didn't get a discount.

I have three problems with this item:
* The button that turns it on and the little white button that keeps it running are not working well. The big pink button doesn't always turn it on, and when it does - you have to hold it very strong to keep the device working. My hands get tired after 2 minutes, but my wife can only hold it for 20 seconds at a time and she hates it. The little white button holds the big button from going back, but it doesn't really work because at that point the device doesn't work.
* I ended up taking the device apart to fix the previous problem. I ended up making it a little better and now the white button keeps the device running, but you have to do it like 5 times to get there. As I was disassembling device, I discovered that they use the cheapest materials possible and the whole thing wasn't designed very well. It's made with the cheapest plastic that crumbles, has cheapest rechargeable batteries inside that will probably stop holding charge after 100 charges.
* Charging is slow. It charges from a USB cable… and there is no battery level indicator.

To be fair, there are two good things about this product:
• When you get it to work – it works fine. I highly doubt its better than any other products out there, but it’s not that bad. It gets the job done.
• It’s nice to hold and use. It’s kinda heavy and big, because it’s made cheaply. But that actually makes it easier to hold =)

Bottom line is – there are defective units out there, be careful. It’s cheaply made and charging will be painful. At $34.95 it’s a horrible deal. You can buy better quality stuff at a cheaper price.

I completely disagree with the reviewers who say that it doesn't perform better than the non-sonic brushes.

The first time I went to my dentist after having used it for six months, he sat back in his chair and asked me what I was doing differently. I told him nothing but changing to a sonic toothbrush ... when he asked me what brand it was, I told him and he said "Well, don't change a thing, because this is the first time you've had zero placque."

Its not supposed to be a substitute for flossing. Flossing once a week (which is considerably less than what the dentist wants) and using this brush have improved my dental health measurably enough that my dentist remarked on it, and I doubt you can do better than that for the money.

title: NOT actually silicone lined!!
text:
BE WARNED, THESE ARE NOT SILICONE LINED - contrary to what the listing says!!

I ended up purchasing these twice - when the first ones arrived and clearly did not have any silicone, I figured maybe they'd just made an error. Needing a product that was available with Prime, but finding extremely limited choices for this particular item, I ended up (stupidly) just trying again, hoping they'd get it right. They didn't.

I started to use these beads anyway, but am VERY glad I stopped after just a dozen strands or so! Because they don't have the silicone lining to protect the hair (and decrease slip) you're literally using needlenosed pliers to smash a tiny piece of unfinished metal in half, tightly around an already very tiny strand of your own hair, WITH another piece of metal in the middle! It's like a teeny tiny little car crash with your hair in the middle! If I'd tried to keep these things in for any length of time, I have no doubt they would have done serious damage. Just trying to remove the few I applied was extremely difficult and anxiety-inducing; none of the beads actually bent back in the opposite direction, like what you experience on a larger scale with the micro beads. When I could finally get each bead positioned to "un-crimp" it (getting it to stop slipping from between the pliers was no easy task) the only way they released was because they broke into tiny pieces, many took strands of my hair with them.

This is a long review for what probably seems like a totally inconsequential item, but I'm sure I'm not the only person who has made this mistake because they didn't know. Hopefully this will help prevent another DIY-er from having to deal with the same headache, and damage!

title: Great wig for cosplay or for day to day wear !
text:
Very good wig, required minimal styling.

I'm used to having to take a few hours to get a wig looking good, but this one was very nice right out of the bag. I didn't pluck the hairline at all, I just trimmed the lace and cut some baby hairs and I was good to go.

The color is pretty nice. It's a lot less of a crimson red than a lot of wigs on the market, which I really appreciate, but it still looks a lot oranger than I was hoping from some of the pictures. I'm going to see if using baby powder to dull the shine will help with that, I think it might. The hair feels very nice though, and it was easy to keep from tangling. The cut is also very nice, there are loose curls around the bottom that look very pretty and natural.

I bought it for cosplay, and because I thought it might match my own hair closely enough to wear casually. It's much brighter than my hair, not as ginger, but it is still a good enough wig that I might try it out for casual wear sometime.

Basically this is a really well made lacefront and I love how little work I needed to put in to make it look natural ♡♡

title: Afordable and easy way to stay tan all year long
text:
I have been using this product for about two months and honestly like it more than the other self tanner I was using prior that was double the price.

First off the smell is devine. Especially compared to previous self tanners I've used. Does not have a strong fake tan smell, and I also don't notice the smell lingering on my skin for extended periods of time.

The color of this product is great and never looks orange or gives me that too dark/red fake tan look I've experienced with other products. The color probably lasts me 4 days, depending on how often I wash my body, workout, and shave. As with all self-tanning products I don't find the "extreme" color to be very dark. I typically apply two coats to get my desired color, which is roughly 2-3 shades darker.

VERYY easy to apply. I use this with the [[ Premium Tanning Applicator Mitt Double-Sided Soft Microfiber Glove for Streak-Free Application]] and don't typically have any problems with streaking. I have noticed I can get streaky on my legs if I apply the product too quickly and don't pay close enough attention, but I don't know any self tanner that wouldn't be an issue with.

My only issue with this product is that I've noticed is coming off on my clothes the day I use it. Even if I use it in the morning and don't wear tight-fitting or light colored clothes until over 8 hours later it will still come off on them. I've noticed it the most on my light wash jean shorts. Fortunately, the color comes off in the wash, but be prepared to plan a head if you want to use this prior to wearing light colored shorts.

Other than that AMAZING product. Definitely worth the price in my opinion.

title: A True Gentleman's Walking Stick
text:
Alpacca is also named German Silver or Nickle Silver. Consisting mostly of copper, nickle and zinc content. In my brief research I find that Alpacca does not contain any actual silver. Though some may be silver plated. But do not think of it as cheap imitation silver. It is more akin to a subset of brass.

This Alpacca cane is the pricier big brother to the plastic headed walking stick of the same design. The plastic brethren of this stick was love at first sight. The flared head and modest fluting simply screams elegance. Nowhere have I found a more elegant walking stick for the 'top hat' era.

As reported with flared head sticks, it is better suited for show. The slightly rounded top makes putting any kind of real pressure uncomfortable without leather gloves. However, it does provide modest balance if weight bearing is not your walking issue. The silvery smooth head does not make the cane top heavy.

The rubber tip is pretty standard and is useful for standing the 3/4" wide cane on flat surfaces. On the negative side, it takes away from the distinctiveness and gives an "old man" quality. I ordered my cane through a vendor who does silver ferrules (plated brass tips) and upgraded the business end of this cane to become a "Gentleman's Walking Stick". Silver ferrules raise the value and elevate the distinctive beauty.

This Alpacca cane lacks the distinctive charm of a chrome collar. My vendor states he routinely heats up such heads for removal, but the extra cost hardly seems worth the upgrade. It was mostly due to removal of the head. Unlike the screw top plastic cane, the Alpacca head is hollow and intended for permanent mounting, using pitch.

As it stands, this cane is suited for mild assisted walking. Use it more for classy strolls, theater, special occasions and dancing. Do not forget the white leather gloves!

Addendum:
On Saturday, 2/7/2015 I finally revealed this walking stick for a big birthday celebration. My black and white clothing style makes me look good, but there is a "whoa" factor when seen with this stick and a pair of white leather gloves. It helps that I had the tip refined with a ferrule and small rubber tip. I love it.

title: If you used to Oral-B Glide floss, you would not like this!
text:
Product reviews on Amazon are something I always rely upon to make my purchase decision. Before buying this brand of floss, which was first time for my family (We usually buy Oral-B Glide floss at Costco), the straight 5-star reviews caught my attention so I thought this must be really good stuff. But as it turned out, this is nothing near the dental floss we expected - the line is too thin to hold on to; there is no waxing so moving in and out of the teeth gap is frustrating, not to mention the effectiveness of cleaning stuff in there. After a few attempts, we gave up using it and now there are 99% of unused packets. If anyone has really used this brand of floss and likes it, please let me know, so I can send them to you with no charge (but please send a prepaid return envelope). Hate to see the "5-star" stuff got wasted like this!

After all, even though the Glide floss quality has somehow gone down in recent years (the line become easier to break, which wasn't the case a few years back), it is still 10 times better. So I guess we have to stick with Oral-B Glide floss and pray they will improve their outsourcing process and bring the Glide quality back to where it was before outsourcing production to some foreign place where they don't give a damn to Americans' teeth.

Sorry, Flosscard maker and vendor, I have to do this to somewhat bring the review ranking to reality so none will be misguided again and make the same mistake we did. I know there are many Glide floss users out there who become unsatisfied with the worsening of Glide floss quality in recent years, especially with the tendency to break prematurely, and want to try something else. I was one of those and now I am here to tell you, my adventure has failed.

title: More Than Another Steelbook
text:
Review For Mondo X Limited Edition Steelbook

El laberinto del fauno (Pan's Labyrinth) is a fantasy film from the director Guillermo del Toro (Hellboy,The Devil's Backbone,Hobbit). Everyone should know the film but for those who don't i will quote the plot from IMDB "In the falangist Spain of 1944, the bookish young stepdaughter of a sadistic army officer escapes into an eerie but captivating fantasy world."

The Main Draw for me was the Steelbook itself, iv seen the movie countless time's and wanted to have a collectable version of the movie that would showcase my love for the film and del toro. Upon receiving this steelbook the first thing i noticed was the protective sleeve underneath the plastic, most steelbooks don't have these and you would have to purchase them separate and that it was included shocked me, the protective sleeve also has images and the information about the release and special features and a great touch. There are images on the front,back and inside of the steelbook itself and looking at pictures online don't really show how gorgeous the product really is, once you hold it as a collector i'm almost positive you will be more then pleased. There are two disc (One DVD, One Blu-ray) inside on the right side of the case, my guess for putting both disc on the right is so you can view the artwork on the left but still if you want to see the full image u have to take all the disc out. The next surprise is on the disc themselves, there not just disc from another version but there labels match this exact release and that really just seals the complete packaging into perfection. This review was more so for the steelbook, but i just fell in love with and had to share

title: WOW! Get it now! You won’t be disappointed!
text:
I’ve forever been a fan of the Real Techniques sponges. They’re soft, they work great, they clean well, they last pretty well, and they didn’t soak up too much of my foundation. So, they were a win for me. I’ve tried many other sponges, but never found ones I loved as much or more than my Real Techniques sponges…UNTIL NOW!

Initially what caught my eye with this sponge was the shape. I loved it had a thin, pointed tip I could use for concealer and areas like around my nose. I loved the 2 angled sides so I can apply cream blush or bronzer or for when I want to apply powder. The sides would work great to apply my foundation. I was hoping the shape would work as well as it seemed like it would, and it did! I was a little worried about the size. Usually, I like to use those little mini sponges for under my eyes. I just never found a sponge, even with a pointy tip, that gets under my eyes to blend my concealer as well as the mini sponges do. So, I was hoping this would still work as a great all around sponge, and, like I said, it did!

The sponge is AMAZING! It’s so soft, but dense so it doesn’t seem to absorb hardly any product. That makes it so easy to clean! I’m the kind of person that hates when my sponges have product stains on them. After I use them, I clean them and keep working at it until all the product is out of it and it looks new again. This can be hard on my sponges and cause them to tear after a few washes. My Real Techniques sponges held up well during my washings, but still would start tearing after about a month of regular washes. I LOVE that this sponge is dense enough that it doesn’t absorb hardly any product, so it’s easy to clean and I don’t have to scrub it for a while, but it’s still so soft and bouncy!

It does get bigger when it’s wet, and it’s already a good size when dry. But, the point on it is thin enough that it gets under my eyes to blend my concealer the way I like it! I don’t have to switch to a mini sponge to do my concealer! I love that!

The sides work great to apply my foundation. It blends it so easily and it looks so smooth and beautiful!

The angled edges work great to apply cream blush/bronzer/contour. It blends them out great and doesn’t lift product underneath it!

It works great to apply powder too!

This is such a great sponge that does everything I need it to and I don’t need to switch to different sponges to do different things! This one sponge has enough different shapes that it does everything I need! I definitely recommend it!

I am also planning on not washing them for three or four days. I plan to wash my face with a rag and just go as much around them as I can. If I remember I’ll come back and update the longevity, but no promises.

Update from the first week after dying my eyebrows. The stain lasted on my skin for a good 6/7 day before I redid the dye on my skin. I didn’t washing my brows (only the surrounding area on my face) for 3 days before washing them so the stain would last longer. Overall I’m happy not to have to throw on my brows every morning. This is a temporary fix until I can get them microbladed. Saves me 10/15 mins every morning and I don’t feel as rushed. title: It works and is not messy if you follow directions!
text: I am a firm believer in alternative medicine and non-toxic, organic cleaning substances; this is one of the reasons I was intrigued by this product. I'd already been aware of the benefits of activated charcoal for other uses, so why not use it to remove toxins in the mouth? I'd read many of the positive and encouraging Amazon reviews before purchasing it from my local health food store, and do not regret this purchase for one moment. Even though I've only used it twice, thus far, my teeth already look a bit whiter and feel cleaner than with any other product I've ever used. I was initially concerned about the "messiness", but there are specific directions provided to minimize the mess. A scoop is provided for those such as I, who prefer not to dip a wet brush into the container, but there's a better option. I have a set of small-increment measuring spoons (pinch, hint, dash, smidgeon), one which scoops out the perfect amount to sprinkle onto a wet toothbrush. This worked perfectly the first time I used it with no spills in the sink. You only need a tiny amount. I then "followed the directions" and kept my lips closed while brushing for the maximum two-minutes and keeping my mouth close to the sink drain. The directions also state to NOT "spit" it out, but rather allow it to fall out of your mouth, and use your hand to transfer running water to your mouth for rinsing. The small amount of charcoal residue left in the sink cleans up quickly and easily. So if you use a small enough amount, stay close to the drain, keep your lips closed, and refrain from spitting, this should be a pleasant and satisfying experience. So far, I highly recommend it!

title: Fades, but very vibrant color
text:
This color is pretty good for the price. There are a few pros and cons to it that I will explain below, but overall I don't think I will buy it again.

Pro:
Comes with 2 containers which is enough color for any length hair
The ability to adjust the shade you want by adding conditioner to the color
A little bit goes a VERY long way
Price is very reasonable
When it fades, it fades all the way out so it doesn't look like some weird shade of orange when it starts to wash out
You don't need any heat to get the color to stick
It doesn't smell like anything

Cons:
Fades INCREDIBLY fast - I had it in for maybe a week or two before it washed all the way out
You have to use a ton of conditioner to create a light soft pink color - the size of a dime with about 2 cups of conditioner do the trick
It will dye everything it comes in contact with - use thick gloves
If you are diluting the color with conditioner, it will take some time to sit on your hair
If you are diluting the color, you'll never need both bottles - it would take 5 years to use all of it

I think overtone color conditioner is an easier system to use and the color stays longer.

title: The Sdara Hydrating Sheet Mask is definitely worth a try.  I will be buying it again.
text:
As of today, I have used these Sdara Hydrating Face Masks on two separate occasions. The first thing I noticed was that it stayed in place on my face better than the mask from a different brand I had used previously. The Sdara mask seems to be of a somewhat thinner material and it is well saturated with the hydrating ingredients. Due to both these factors, it molds to the surface of the face more completely, as well as probably staying in place more easily.

After sitting with the mask on for a while, I experienced a noticeable soothing sensation on my skin. I found this to be pleasant and relaxing.

The directions on the back of the packet containing the mask say to leave it on for 25-30 minutes. From my two times experience with this product, I have to agree with that. One time I left it on for more than 30 minutes and noticed a kind of astringent sensation on my skin. The mask is not meant to be on for longer than 30 minutes.

The directions written on the back of the packet are clear and easy to understand. I was also thrilled to see that the mask is 100 percent biodegradable and cruelty free (no harsh laboratory testing on animals).

Looking at the results afterward, my skin definitely looked less dry and felt softer. I do plan on ordering a supply of these sheet masks again. Thank you.

title: Not A Bad Little Eyebrow Kit!
text: I ordered this dark brown Eyebrow Stamping Kit to see if it would be any better than using the standard eyebrow pencil.  Now, granted I have barely any eyebrows due to hypothyroidism, so finding something that looks natural is key.  I love this little kit.  It comes in a very handy little plastic zip lock bag which includes, the brow powder, 24 eyebrow stencils, and 4 eyebrow/eyelash brushes.  It was a bit difficult sorting through all 24 stencils but I narrowed it down to 4 initially, then down from there to 3, then 2, then 1.  On my right eyebrow(your left in the 4th pic), I did my eyebrow with the standard eyebrow pencil how I usually shape it.  I thought by doing one to compare to, it might make it easier to find the closest shape to what I do.  After finally selecting the stencil I was going to use, it was easy to peel it off the paper and apply to my skin/eyebrow.  I may have stretched it a little, I am not sure.  The brow powder applicator doesn't twist or push up.  It just has powder in the tip automatically.  Oh, I forgot to mention that on the back of the stencil box, there are instructions.  So, I kind of dabbed the brow powder on, but I do think it helps if you have eyebrow hairs for it to cling to in the first place!  I do at the start, but my ends are gone!  The brow powder is a bit loose and a small amount fell over the sink.  I then peeled the stencil off(was easy and didn't hurt).  I show the immediate results in pic 7.  In my opinion, it was a bit thick(I'm more "old school" and like my eyebrows thin), so I took a wet tissue and wiped a bit away and made it more narrow.  I also used one of the eyebrow/eyelash brushes to feather it out a little.  Then my final results are in pic 8.  I would say NOT BAD.  From far away it does look more natural than the pencil shaped one which is thinner and more precise.  Natural brows are not like that!  I will say though, it is not exactly "water proof".  Sure, if some raindrops got on it, it wouldn't immediately take it off, but it was easy to remove with a wet tissue and soap.  I think with both brows the same, I could get used to using this kit.  I am not sure how long the brow powder will last in the tube, but having the eyebrow stencils is handy and quick.  For the price, I would definitely recommend it!

title: Most Excellent
text:
This mask is unlike any other I've used. Unopened, it sounds like a heavy liquid when the container is shaken; I'm used to masks that are "solid" and extremely thick, but was looking for an exfoliating mask because my skin gets very dry and flaky in winter. Got this one because I was offered a discount in exchange for an honest review. Used it last night for the first time...

It should probably be well-shaken before each use, and it looks very strange. Kind of a greenish-grey pearlescence, and it is a "runny" mask. A little goes a long way, too! I was surprised. There must be at *least* 20 treatments in this little jar. Required less than two teaspoons to do my entire face and under the jawline.

It feels strange. Kind of an icy-hot sting in the beginning; interesting, but not uncomfortable. It doesn't feel as though it would do a lot of exfoliating, and it doesn't dry quickly (maybe it's not supposed to dry, at all). The instructions said to leave it on for 20 minutes, but I left it on for an hour. At that point, it was flaky. Rather than simply rinse it off, I rubbed it off with my fingers, and THAT was definitely exfoliating. This wouldn't work with any of the other masks I've used, and I really liked being able to easily/gently rub every bit off using my fingers. Post-rub, my face felt very dry, but after rinsing with warm water that feeling went away and my skin was SO soft.

Today when I awoke, my skin felt great. No dry patches. I did still apply my usual three or four drops of cold argan oil, just because the humidity is so low right now.

As-is, I like this mask much more than I thought I would when I first opened the jar (though it smells wonderful, again, it's very "liquid," which seemed strange before I'd actually used it). That said, I'll probably alternate between using it straight out of the jar and adding some bentonite to make it a bit thicker. Very happy to have this organic mask!

REVIEWS: Most of my reviews are 4* and 5* whether for items I received at a discount in exchange for an honest review, items I purchased at the regular Amazon price, or things I've bought elsewhere but like or hate enough to write a review. There are few bad reviews because I research every purchase I make, and junk even at a discount is still junk. I try not to buy junk (and I only exchange reviews for discounts with items I actually want and use). A bad review means I didn't do my homework (or fell for some crafty hype) and made a big mistake.

title: A Giant Leap Forward in Dental Care.
text:
I bought a similar model of Sonicare toothbrush about four years ago and I still marvel at how well it works. Honestly, when the price comes down everyone will own one of these.
I never used to enjoy brushing and I never used to brush my teeth as much as they needed it. I was just too lazy. My teeth were a little discolored and my gums were consistently a little puffy around the tooth. Then I bought a Sonicare toothbrush with the interval timer and now I'll never switch back to a manual toothbrush.
After the first few brushings my teeth were noticably whiter and after a few months I noticed the puffiness in my gums was gone.
At 30,000 strokes per minute it's like brushing hundreds of times with a manual brush. But all you have to do is "aim the brush" while it glides back and forth across your teeth. It feels like a vibrator in your hand. The timer pulses every thirty seconds to prompt you to switch from front to back of teeth and from top to bottom. After two minutes it shuts itself off after what is supposedly the ideal length of brushing time.
You can also take this brush with you when traveling as it works for more than a week without recharging.
Could it have any downsides?
Although I consider it easily worth every penny, the upfront cost is staggering compared to a manual toothbrush. It also requires a replacement brush head approximately every six months at about $15 each. But this is a sophisticated unit and is more like a medical device than a disposable supply item. The only thing these two have in common is the brushes on the end and I'm sure the Sonicare's brushes are higher quality.
It is important to note that the brush head will slowly wear out without any visible sign of wear. The performance gradually degrades until the unit seems nonfunctional. I know because I tried to save money by not replacing the brush heads according to schedule. I thought the battery had gone bad and I called customer service for advice. It turns out that the brush head was way overdue for replacement. Fortunately all the moving and wearable parts (including brush, magnets and metal connecting parts) are in the brush head and when they are replaced performance is restored to like-new again.
The first time you use this product it may make your teeth sensitive for a few days (because of the vibration) and while its permanent and rechargeable battery will last through most trips it is physically larger and takes slightly more space to pack than a manual brush.
Now I have never had to share the brush with anyone so I never had to switch brush heads on a daily basis. This seems to me like it would be an enormous hassle as you have to unthread and detach the head each time. While this is possible, I would probably buy two units instead if the finances allowed.
This is one of the best purchases I've ever made.
In summary, if you think you might like it and you can afford it, then go ahead and get one. They last a long time...

title: Pleasant Enough, Not Much Scent, Need a Lot of Product To Shower
text:
Like all too many organic soaps, this example ends up being a bit too subtle and bland in scent and power to justify its price point. I love vetiver but even with a generous dollop on the loofah, I get only the faintest scent of that fragrance here. The hemp / vetiver combo smells pleasant in a mild sort of way, but this is not what I expected at the price point and given the product name. If I wanted "fragrance free", I'd buy it!

Besides the really mild non-especially vetiverish scent, NH IH&V body wash also needs a lot of soap to generate any lather, and even needs a lot just to get through a whole body wash. Lather may or may not be to your liking, but having to reload the loofah halfway through your shower is no one's idea of fun. At the rate of product usage, I would be amazed if this 13 oz bottle lasts me for more than 2-3 weeks.

Ultimately, even if you want to stay organic, there are better choices with more prominent scents and better product consumption rates. EOs Cedar & Mint for Men works well enough and can even be used as a shampoo and shave cream for the undemanding. My personal favorite semi-organic products are from Every Man Jack. Their cedar and sandalwood (two separate types there) body wash have great smells and give adequate lather and cleaning duration with roughly half the product needed to get similar effects from NH IH&V wash. (I call Every Man Jack semi-organic as I haven't bothered to assess all the ingredients on their label, but they have no parabens or SLS derivatives, so they pass my personal screening standard.) Both of these product lines are much cheaper than Nubian Heritage.

For vetiver lovers who want that scent in their bath ritual, Provence Sante makes a good vetiver beauty bar soap, and also a rather expensive vetiver body wash. which I have not tried due to its high cost. I have tried the beauty bar, and though not cheap, it does indeed give the user a noticeable vetiver smell when applied, which is always a good thing when buying a vetiver named product!

title: Decent, but disappointed
text:
I have ordered these several times now, and they do work out okay. You need to make sure to have everything correctly sized/at the right resolution and set to A4 paper size before printing so that the images turn out well. You also need to apply the adhesive sheets with a lot of care and patience to ensure there are no bubbles or wrinkles.

When applied, the tattoos are shiny, as most temporary tattoos are. This can be fixed with a dusting of baby powder or matte makeup powder. The only issue I've had is that the edges tend to peel quite a bit if you place the tattoo near a joint/bending part, like your elbow/inner elbow, knee, etc. Any place that moves a lot. But as long as you put them somewhere that doesn't move so much, they last several days as long as you don't pick at them or fiddle with them.

My biggest complaint is that the last time I ordered these, I went ahead and printed my images, and then as soon as I went to apply the adhesive sheets (which is quite a process and definitely made easier with two people and a good amount of patience, if you don't want any bubbles), I found that every single one of my adhesive sheets were defective. I've attached photos so you can see what I'm talking about.

In between the adhesive layer and the yellow backing paper (which you peel apart to apply to the printed designs), there were tons of little black specks/dirt. They were stuck in the adhesive, which obviously rendered them useless, seeing as I don't want black flecks all over my printed tattoo designs. I am super disappointed in this considering how expensive this paper is, but I don't think I can get a return since I already printed on the sheets. I just can't believe that something of this price would have such a flaw in the quality, and despite having success with these previously, now I'm hesitant to buy again.

Keratin treatments rebound the keratin in your hair so that they are all put back into place. There are a lot of steps but don’t get discouraged because they’re quiet simple. To start of give 2 good shampoos with a clarifying shampoo (specifically the keratin complex one, then towel dry and blow dry the unconditioned hair. Once fully dry, make small sections and apply the treatment from roots to ends and comb through with a fine tooth comb to make sure hair is fully saturated. Let that sit for 30 minutes then blow dry again without washing out the product. Once fully dry the final step will be to straighten the hair with a flatiron so the keratin will set in your hair. After you’re completely done you won’t be able to wash your hair for up to 3 days depending on the strength in the solution.

title: Pretty good coverage for a powder
text: First time in 20 years I've transitioned from a liquid concealer to a powder, the coverage is obviously not the same but this is by far the best performing powder I've ever had. I'm lucky in that my face at it's not-the-most-tan tiny works well with the light color but I can see how the limited color choices can be a deal breaker for some. It's smooth and not cakey, it blends well, feels weightless, and stands up to sweating and long work days with great shine prevention and it doesn't come off easily (a little when you blow your nose etc). I do not like the porcelain doll look and this works well for me for evening out tones.  I am 35 and have very sensitive skin, several minor facial scars, and occasional adult acne and this doesn't have any negative effects on my skin at all. It washes off easily with gentle face wash. It allows for a few spot touches of stick concealer, blends well, and holds well. Mine arrived with no breaks/cracks and the sponge works well. I really like the protective inner plastic case between the powder and the lid and sponge. Will buy again! I previously used Revlon, Covergirl, Neutrogena, and JUNGSAEMMOOL Essential Star-cealer Foundation which I was happy with the first time and then the following two were slimy and just not working well. For reference my current face tone is a revlon 300-310, a covergirl 705-710, and Starcealer Light. After peak summer I'm a more 310-320, 710-715, and Starcealer Medium (almost, its still a little dark for me).

title: Another terrific Oral-B toothbrush!
text:
Anyone who is serious about their dental hygiene should consider getting one of these. I won't say it is absolutely necessary to upgrade from the Healthy Clean Precision 1000, which I also own. This one seems to polish just a bit better than the Precision, which is good, but I thought it might be only due to the head that comes with it being the 'Floss Action' design, which has these little plastic paddles that are supposed to get in between teeth, but also offer a better polishing experience in my mind. Before the Floss Action, I was hooked on the Dual Action which I used with the Precision. If you have a lower grade toothbrush than this one and want more polishing, you might give the Floss Action head a go. It seems to me that polishing would aid in bacteria-resistance since you are smoothing the surface so less bacteria could get in and reside, leading to cavities.

Your whole family can use one toothbrush like this as long as each have their own brush heads. The heads usually come with color-coded rings at the bottom so you know whose is whose. This model also comes with this lovely little plastic holder for 4 heads and a little lid to keep them dust-free. I love it - before, I was setting my head on a piece of tissue in the medicine cabinet. This is much more tidy. This is a great tooth-brush!

title: Arrived ahead of time which was super cool! I was incredibly excited to try this ...
text:
Arrived ahead of time which was super cool! I was incredibly excited to try this product out after seeing the buzzfeed video with them using it.
When I first opened the package, I was a bit shocked at how big of a bottle it was but how it seemed like barely half was full. When attempting to squeeze is out it was very much like trying to get the last of a product out of a container just as you're about to run out of it. All air, very little inside.
I did a small test area just to see if there was any kind of crazy reaction and I didn't have any issues. Goes on, peels off, wash away any little flakes that don't peel with it. However, when I went back to do a full mask I noticed that even though I had totally sealed it up tight, within about 20 minutes a massive amount of the product had leaked into the lid. I cleaned it up so it didn't solidify and placed the bottle upside down, so the lid was facing up instead.
The full mask itself went on nice and easy, just like the test. When I peeled it off, I did notice my skin felt fresher but it didn't really pull anything out. I checked the peeled off mask itself and while it had plenty of little itty bitty hairs from my face, nothing really noticeable. I checked out problem areas in the mirror and they looked basically the same, maybe with some blackheads and things closer to the surface and drawn up so they could be removed. The effect was minimal though and pretty disappointing.
I'll finish it off since there isn't much left and there is no point in not using it, but I won't be buying any more after this.

title: A good, no-frills electric razor
text:
I've been using this Norelco 6423 Reflex Plus corded electric razor for about 2 1/2 weeks now, and so far, I'm glad I decided to buy it.

My old Panasonic rechargeable razor didn't seem to be holding a charge for very long anymore, plus it was time to replace the foil and cutting heads again. For about the same amount I would have spent to replace the worn parts on my old razor (not even including the cost of replacing the battery), I got a brand new Norelco razor!

The first thing I noticed about the Norelco is that it's MUCH quieter than my old Panasonic. My Panasonic sounded like a Dustbuster when it was on. Another plus to the Norelco is that it does a much better job of shaving underneath my jaw line and on my neck. I have not had any problem with the cord coming out of the razor while shaving. It fits in there nice and snug. I also have had no problem with the razor grabbing my skin. Just make sure you don't press down too hard on your skin while shaving, and use your free hand to pull your skin tight while shaving your neck, as suggested in the accompanying booklet.

If you don't need a fancy, expensive razor that cleans itself or is rechargeable, give this one a try.

title: The fat
text:
This is a classic. Having tried a few hard soaps and creams and also having heard that "the fat" has a cult-like following, I had to try it.
The smell is nothing short of awesome. Kind of a powdery linen clean smell. And it's a pervasive smell too, that will carry with you after your shave.
But the magic of MWF is the lanolin, a natural wax that the sheep exude to protect their wool... The original Mitchell noticed that wool shearers' hands were always soft and supple, and thankfully decided to try a shaving product based in it.
You will notice the lanolin effect right after your shave as you're rinsing off your face. It will be smooth and moist and will feel awesome.
MWF can be tough to lather, but after a few tries and watching a few videos online you'll get the hang of it. For best results try skipping the bowl/scuttle and just face-lather. It'll create a luscious, moisturizing, delicious smelling lather that is like no other.

title: My favorite non-acetone remover.
text:
For this price you get 6 individually sealed containers of remover pads. They each contain 38 thin fabric-like removal pads that are soaked in the non-acetone remover. The containers screw open and don't seem to dry out easily. The remover contains isopropyl myristate, propylene carbonate, fragrance, and water. These are ideal for anyone who doesn't like the smell of acetone since they just smell flowery. They smell wonderful, I'm someone who doesn't like many scented things, but they are all very soft pretty scents that I love.

The pads remove polish more slowly than most acetone-based nail polish removers and require a bit of scrubbing. To remove a bright red (read-as nail polish that stains) manicure I use 3-4 sheets (more if there is glitter in the polish). They do leave your nails and hands a bit greasy feeling (which means they moisturize your nails rather than drying them out like acetone) so you should always wash your hands thoroughly after using the remover pads. Overall, great product and I will buy it again (once these run out, they last forever!)

title: Get rid of tinea pedis in 1 week.
text:
I went to doctor suffering with tinea pedis in my groin area. I had it for months and didn't know what it was (thinking it would just go away naturally). It finally got so bad that I had to see a doctor. He prescribed a topical treatment to use twice a day for 7 days. It didn't work. I went back and he prescribed a stronger topical treatment along with antibiotics to use for 5 days. It too didn't work. He was out of ideas and referred me to a dermatologist. While waiting to see the dermatologist, I decided to do some research on my own. I bought the following products and used them every day for 6 days straight so far. I am about 95% cured. I plan to use this for another week thinking I will be 100% after the second week.
This stuff works.
1. Product #1: Defense Soap Antifungal 4 Ounce Bar. [[ASIN:B01E0D6PIS DEFENSE Ringworm Treatment Kit - Bar Soap 4 Oz and Body Wipes 40 Count]]
Shower 3 times a day…once in the morning, once when you get home from work and once before bedtime. Use this bar soap 3 times a day for the infected area, once a day for your whole body including fingernails and feet.
2. Product #2. Wipes. (Link in above product description)
Use the wipes periodically throughout the day..every few hours and especially after getting sweaty.
3. Product #3: Antifungal Soap with Tea Tree Oil, Helps Treat & Wash Away Athletes Foot, Ringworm, Nail Fungus, Jock Itch, Body Odor & Acne. [[ASIN:B00HNWNXAW Antifungal Soap with Tea Tree Oil, Helps Treat & Wash Away Athletes Foot, Ringworm, Nail Fungus, Jock Itch, Body Odor & Acne. Antibacterial Defense Against Common Fungal and Bacteria Related Skin Irritations 9oz.]]
In addition to the bar soap, I used this product on the affected area once a day (at bedtime shower). When using this, lather well and let it sit on your skin for 3-4 minutes before rinsing off.
4. Product #4: Zeasorb Super Absorbent Antifungal Treatment Powder. [[ASIN:B005GM3LW6 Zeasorb Super Absorbent Antifungal Treatment Powder for Jock Itch 2.5 oz]]
After showering, completely dry off then use this powder on affected area.
5. Product #5: BUICED Liquid Multivitamin. [[ASIN:B00DSAA3L0 BUICED Liquid Multivitamin, 1-Pack]]
Internal treatment. Tinea Pedis condition can also be made worse by poor diet. I took a shot of this liquid vitamin once a day (when I got home from work each day).
6. Product #6: “Raw Organic Apple Cider Vinegar with the ‘Mother’”. [[ASIN:B00H4I4DRC Bragg Raw Organic Apple Cider Vinegar-16 fl. oz. Bottle]]
I don’t know how much this helped, but I read how beneficial apple cider vinegar is to your health so I gave it a try. I drank 2 tablespoons once a day (at night an hour before bedtime). I mixed it with orange juice and it wasn’t quite so bad.

I used these products for about 1 week and I am very pleased with the results.

title: Painless and easy to use, but the device gets super hot
text: I have been using this hair removal device for 2 months now. I used it once every 2 weeks so I've used it 5 times so far. Now, the sessions will be only once a month until all the unwated hair is removed. The manufacturer recommends using it once every 2 weeks for the first 5 sessions and then once a month after that, so using it multiple times a week won't change the outcome. The areas I use this device are my legs, under arms, bikini area and upper lip. The only difference I've noticed so far is the upper lip hair. It is growing significantly less, like almost 90% is gone. The rest of the body hair still grows the same amount, but the hair started to grow softer. I assume the hair is finally becoming weaker. I am half Greek and half Italian, I have olive skin color with dark hair, so it might take over a year for me to see some results. Overall, the device is very easy to use and it is painless, but it gets super hot to the touch after about 5-10 minutes of continues usage. I use the device on my legs first and then take a break until it cools down, and then I continue using it on other parts of the body and stop to cool it down again. I have to admit it is frustrating to stop the session to cool down the device. I don't know if other hair removal devices get this hot. This is my first time using something like this so I can't compare.

title: Works great, but make sure you understand how to control the device before use
text:
Of you’re looking to get your feet in shape fast, this is the tool. I have always had dry feet and large caluses in my heals and under my big toes in the ball. This is the first time a sanding tool has actually made my feet look and feel like new.

I have read reviews that say this product is dangerous and can burn your feet. Well that is true if not used properly. Here are just s couple tips that I have learned from a weeks use:

1. Make sure the device is on the lowest setting before use.
2. Do not make contact for longer than 1.5 seconds, even on hard caluses.
3. Use light contact and pull the device against the rotation on each pass.
4. Let the pad do the work, you do not need to push it into the foot. This is most likely the reason for the negative reviews reporting pain and burning.
5. This device is powerful! If you’re not comfortable using it right out of the box, practice for a few minutes on an Apple or other soft surfaces until your get comfortable with the control.

Enjoy your new feet!

title: Great concept - just falls short of the intended use!
text: I was really curious about receiving this product - as I LOVE the concept. I am constantly looking for a cover for my razors - both to keep them clean and to prevent my little ones from coming in contact with the blade. Unfortunately, this design just really falls short. There is a metal plate within the clamp like pod which the blade sits against when the pod is closed. I understand the metal was likely placed there to protect the blade and prevent unnecessary dulling and the build up of gunk. Most razors on the market today have a strip of lotion or emollient along the top of the blade. Unfortunately, the metal from the pod kept fusing to the strip causing both the strip to come off and the plastic of the pod to pull free - resulting in both a broken pod and a damaged and unusable razor. I would also caution this company regarding the name and claim of the product. Although the product is meant to provide a protective cover to the razor -  it by no means provides any sort of sterile environment.... thus I do think calling this a “steripod” might be a bit misleading.

title: Fine for Home Use; Not Professional
text:
I wanted a Nail Display Stand for the same reason others do; to hold full cover false nails in place while they're being polished and decorated with various nail art elements.

Nail stands are small by necessity; they have to be small enough so when a nail is affixed to one, it can be slid into a UV/LED nail lamp to cure gel polish and any UV/LED activated glue used to attach embellishments to the nails without scraping the ceiling of the lamp.

These Nail Display Stands (both the acrylic bar and crystal) work perfectly well for that purpose.

Nail display stands are also used by some professional nail techs/artists to display samples of their work at their place of business.

Clients prefer to select a design for their nails from displays of finished nails showcasing the designs offered by a nail tech/artist instead of a portfolio of still photos. Photos may not reproduce colors accurately, and can be edited to eliminate evidence of sloppy workmanship.

These Nail Display Stands should not be purchased for that purpose. The metal dots on the acrylic strip to which the five magnetized stands attach weren't glued on straight, so the stands won't form a straight line and won't be equidistant from each other.

The metal dot atop the crystal was also glued off-center.

So, while these Nail Display Stands are perfectly serviceable for home use, they simply aren't good enough if you're a professional nail tech/artist wanting to showcase your best work to clients.

I have been using this makeup brush set for a couple months now and figured that it was time to write a review on these guys. The reason why I didn't give this set a 5 star review is because none of the brushes in this set actually packs on eyeshadow -- it's definitely not a huge issue since I can just pack it on using my fingers but for sanitary reasons, I would have preferred a brush that was more dense for that specific purpose.

title: The BEST PRODUCTS EVER!!
text:
Ok fellow Amazonians, I have been on a search for over 2 years for the perfect shampoo and conditioner. I used to use Pureology, but then, a few years back, they started messing with their formulaes. I was definitely not happy as the new stuff left my hair lifeless or at worst created a snarled mess. My search brought me through over a dozen misc brands as well as the more well known such as Chi and Phyto, but nothing provided any stellar results. My hair would also somehow get used to a new shampoo and stop looking decent. No idea why, maybe it got bored.
Anyway, I am 50 years old, colored my hair forever, and have fine, thinnish hair. I found this brand on a random search and decided to give it a try.
I started off with their Lemon Scented set and OMG give that a try too. I had such incredible results, as in like nothing I have EVER tried. Within a few weeks of use I noticed new hair growth at my temples! That and my hair had a new body like it has NEVER had. A few weeks more and I noticed I now had to really work the shampoo down to my scalp BECAUSE there was so much new hair growth at the crown of my head. I gave a set to my daughter who has always had these very thin areas at her temples and she too has new hair growth that is VERY apparent. She would not wear her hair up because of those patches, but now, you can easily see all the new hair. This stuff is amazing.

Now, you get a jar that is gritty with the salt and very thick. This seems to confuse some people, but PLEASE, just dip a finger in, swirl it a bit, and scoop out what you need (You will figure out the right amount for you quickly enough)
You put the gritty(salt) stuff onto your scalp and start working it in and VERY quickly you will have a thick and luxurious lather as the salt and minerals dissolve. The scent is over the moon, enveloping you in a fresh zingy peppermint haze and the Peppermint creates the most incredible tingly sensation.
Trust me, you are going to want to try these products. The Lavender, while I love the scent, for me, it seems better suited to oily hair, but the Lemon set and Peppermint Rosemary are my favorites.
Earth Chemistry will be the ONLY products touching my hair from now on.

title: Great shave from an electric....solution to annoying unplugging.
text:
This new Norelco Arcitec razor provides a great shave with little irritation. I had a Braun Syncro previously, and it would leave little hairs everywhere on my neck. This new designed head flexs and pivots in all different ways to have more contact with the skin.

The jet clean station works good and is interesting to watch. It does a good job of cleaning the razor heads of hair and debris. There is however, one annoying issue. Norelco says you should not charge the razor until it needs it to maximize battery life. The jet clean system however, automatically goes into the charge cycle after cleaning and a two hour dry time!! If your like me, you will probably be at work two hours after shaving.

My solution to the unplugging is:

I picked up a plug in rocker switch at Home Depot to go between the wall outlet and the Norelco Transformer plug. I then shave a little earlier in my morning routine and clean the razor in the jet clean system. I then turn the switch off while the system is in the 2 hour drying cycle. This is ok since the razor is basically air/drip drying anyway. If it needs charged, I turn the switch on while I know I'm going to be home for and hour then turn back off. This is a bit annoying, but if I spent almost $200 on a razor then I want it to last. You could also just unplug it during the drying mode, but I like the switch so I don't have plugs and cords everywhere.

title: Hair glides through effortlessly
text:
I had my previous flat iron for many years and never had a problem with it despite the fact that my husband accidently dropped it in the toilet tank. I let it dry out for a few months and it worked like a charm until recently. The plates began to loose their finish and when I was done doing my hair I had a bunch of fly always and loose hairs sticking straight up. It was very noticeable which bothered me. It also became difficult to keep clean so it was time for a new one.

The peacock design is what attracted me, I thought it was pretty. This flat iron does a great job. It heats up quickly, it can heat up to 450 but I usually use it at about 400. I am Hispanic and have naturally frizzy hair but it also has a lot of body. I dye my hair it's it's a little on the dry side. This flat iron straightens my hair effortless. My hair glides through the plates easily, I don't hear dragging or crunching sounds and it does not pull my hair. It usually only takes a few pass-throughs until my section of hair is nice, straight and bouncy. The plates are ceramic so they heat up evenly meaning the temperature should be the same on the front tip of the plates as it on the center and back of the plates. The ionic technology reduces fizziness and fly-away hairs. The cord has a 360 turn and is long which I really like and it's very user friendly. The packaging is divine, it comes in a beautiful box with a magnetic closure with a comb and a felt type sleeve for travel.

I really like this product but there a few cons. My biggest con would be the cord. It's made up of very stiff plastic material that has a lot of memory and I'm worried that it will eventually crack. The curling iron I had previously had a supple rubber material and never experienced cracking or breakage but it didn't have the 360 swivel cord like this flat iron. The location of the on/off switch and temperature dial is located in between the plates by the hinge. I thought this was an odd place and worry it will eventually be effected by the heat of the plates. All in all I am happy with my purchase.

I was granted the opportunity to purchase this product at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest review.

title: Great body wash for sensitive skin!
text: I have very fair, very sensitive skin that is prone to itching and rashes.  Most bars of soap (and by most I mean 99%) are too strong for my skin so I am on the constant lookout for a product that I can use as a shower gel.  I asked myself "Who else has sensitive skin besides me?"  BABIES!!!  So I turned to looking for products created for a baby's skin.  I detest the scent of lavender and for some reason most baby products contain lavender.  Yuck!  I read the reviews on the Sweet Baby Shampoo and saw that some folks recommended it also as a shower gel.  I'm a FANATICAL ingredient reader and I was pleased with the ingredients.  So, my first purchase was the Coconut Baby.  I liked what the product did for my skin as well as what it did not do.  It left my skin feeling soft and not irritated.  I loved the way it lathered, not too much but not too little.  It made a soft, creamy, bubbly lather.  I just wasn't crazy about the scent.  It has a faint plastic play-doh smell.  But then, to my nose most coconut scents end up smelling that way.  I was just hoping this would be different.  My next venture with Sweet Baby was with the vanilla scent.  The scent is a soft, buttery vanilla.  When I smell it, it makes me close my eyes and say "yum".  I haven't used it on my hair and I probably never will so I can't comment on it as a shampoo.  For now, this will be my staple shower gel.  By the way, I love the baby lotion as well!  I would definitely recommend both the shampoo as a shower gel and the lotion.

text:
I just picked this up this evening and unboxed it a few minutes ago. I'm already a bit disappointed with it so far. I had read the reviews here on Amazon, and knew that some people were finding a rough shave with it. I haven't had a chance to try that yet ... but the cleaning system is a bit of a disappointment.

First off, the cleaning solution that they provide contains no alcohol. My Remington with cleaning system had an alcohol-based solution, and I was always sure my razor was clean and sterilized. But this? No alcohol? Hmm.

Secondly - my Remington (and the Brauns, too) had a small filter packet that was supposed to catch all the little bits of whiskers that were going through the cleaning solution. This one? No such thing. So you mean weeks-old whiskers are going to be floating around in the non-alcohol based cleaning solution? No thanks.

The "unplug after it's fully charged" thing will probably be a bit annoying - but I have a feeling some people are worrying a bit too much about this. I left my Remington in the stand constantly for 5 years. Eventually the battery burned out - and I realize it was probably my fault (I didn't read the manual) but I don't think you need to get obsessive like some reviewers have here and get it unplugged *immediately* after it's done with its cycle. When you get home from work in the evening would probably be find. Just give it a full charge once every several days.

Even though I haven't even given it a full charge yet, I have a feeling it's going to be going back and I'll be buying the Braun instead - even though my face seems to prefer a rotary.

title: Good, not perfect, but really nice
text:
This is now the second makeup removing towel of this kind and I will admit I was a skeptic about this magic towel concept, but I was offered the opportunity to review it at a reduced price and curious to compare it to the other brand I have tried. The towel itself came with instructions to wash before use, after washing I immediately noticed when I pulled it out of the washer the towel felt nearly dry already.Which is the same experience I had with the other towel. So instead of drying it with the rest of the load, I left it out to air dry to see how long it really takes to dry. One of the things I was really wondering about this towel is, if it works, could it be something to take on a long trip, where I will be packing up and moving locations every couple of days. I wouldn't want to through a moist towel into my bag and end up with a musty bag of cloths for the entire trip! This did take a while to dry, maybe a couple of hours, but that seems far less than a regular washcloth or towel.

The washcloth itself is super soft and plush, and when you get it wet is holds ALOT of water, which might be part of its magic. The directions say to get the towel wet and rub the towel with tcircular motions. Once done you can choose to flip the cloth to the to exfoliate. This towel feels really nice and gentle on my skin, and and it definitely took off the BB foundation and undereye concealer I was wearing. As for my eye shadow, eye liner and mascara, it did a decent job, but there was definitely residue left over that I felt I needed to to back over with a little soap and water. I actually went back over my face with a wet wipe to see if there was any other make up residue left behind and did find that a light amount of my face cream still wiped off, but it was a very small amount, it seemed that it was mostly my eye area that needed a little extra wash.

Overall I really like this washcloth. The idea of rarely having to use soap or chemicals to get a clean fact is really appealing. I am prone to stye’s so I will always be more vigilant about cleaning my mascara and eyeliner area more, but overall I am presently surprised by this product.

text:
I'll start with the best things about this curling iron. The heating element is encased in plastic so its easy to use without burning yourself. I am not sure why most of the deep wavers these days got away from that and now its all this exposed hot mettle that one wrong move or a slip of the wrist and you are burning your neck or face or hand with it. But not with this one. Its nice that way. That's probably one of the biggest reasons I went with this one. Its very attractive and sleek looking with a nice swivel cord. It shuts itself off after an hour which is nice as I have left it on by mistake before. Gives you peace of mind if you can't remember if you left it on after you've left your house which is awesome.

Now it works alright and you can make nice waves with it if you are careful to align the waver properly because its like they went a little cheap on the waving plates. You really have to think about it and position it right each time because you have one and half wave on each plate as apposed to two full barrels on one side and one full barrel on the other that fits between the two on the one side, which makes it easier when trying to align as you work your way down your hair each time. But with this one if you don't do it right you end up sort of straitening an area that you were trying to produce a wave. And then its hard to fix it. I suppose you would get used to it over time and it might not be a big deal but I didn't like it. I kept trying to not let it bother me but it bothered me. Also I didn't think it went as deep as I might want sometimes. With the one I posted on here in the photo which is a Bedhead waver, you have that option to go deeper by leaving it on longer and also it has hotter settings that this one doesn't have. This Wessopan iron that I am reviewing only goes to 200 degrees. It takes longer to do my hair for sure. My new one which is a Bedhead goes from 250 up to 400 degrees. Much easier to use and faster. Its only half enclosed in plastic for some reason but it has a plastic nob on the end to hold if you need it also. Its pretty good, I only burned myself a little on the side of my face once. Ugh. How much extra can adding the other side of plastic casing really cost anyway? Seriously. But I digress.

title: Endless sea of curls!
text:
[[VIDEOID:e7a30e00ac346d7528a89979e60ae651]] This curler is big in size compared to most classic curlers. That doesn't stop us from using it in our house though! It does come in a variety of colors and I chose pink because it is my favorite color. It just takes a couple of minutes for the curler to get hot and the best part about that is you can control how hot you want it. The curler has a nice display to show you what the temperature is and there is a nice on/off sliding switch to it as well. The other buttons on the handle are for the temperature settings, curl direction, and the time setting. The curl direction is pretty flipping neat as you can control which direction it will curl your hair. You can have it make your curls go right, left, or set it to auto curl. The time setting is pretty easy to figure out, it controls how long you want the curler to actually hold the hair and how much of a curl you want. You can set it to hold the strand of hair that you are curling up to 15 seconds. You hold the blacker part toward your head when you are curling and you can start anywhere you want to. If you want more of a curl, you will go closer to the base of the strand. If you don't want a lot of curl, then you can start in the middle. It is pretty simple to use, all you have to do is slide the strand of hair into the curler and clamp it down. It will automatically gather the strand on the inside of the curler and set the curl. It is quite an amazing little gadget! You always want to make sure you are using a type of heat protectant on your hair to keep it healthy. The other thing is that it will automatically shut off after non use but always try to remember to unplug your stylers. I honestly wasn't sure what to expect but now I am going to have to fight with my daughter to use it!

title: I highly recommend this product if you have curly, dry, brittle, dull and frizzy hair
text:
I didn't buy this treatment from Amazon, but I thought I'd review it since when I browsed it before buying the product I wished it had a good review.

This keratin treatment did truly what it said it would, my frizz has been 99% tamed and my hair looks and feels soft. It's silky, smooth and shiny. The down side was that my hair was weighed down after washing the treatment. I hope this will go away in the next wash cycle or so. I followed the instructions provided, if your hair is resistant or virgin to keratin I recommend shampooing with the Anti-residue Shampoo (Step 1) twice making it work in your hair for 5 minutes each time. You can then let your hair air dry or blow dry it with either cool/warm/heat setting up to 85-90% (I used a cool setting here). Then apply the treatment (Step 2) with a fine comb after sectioning your hair, make sure not to get it too close to the scalp unless you're combing it upwards fast. The key thing here is to not let the solution drip down to your scalp or skin otherwise it will burn and cause irritation. A bit of an advice here, if you have vaseline I'd recommend applying it to the skin area that's close to hair line avoiding touching any of your hair (of course this is optional). Try not to over saturate, once all your hair has been coated well with the treatment without over saturating use the cool/warm but NOT the heat setting in your blow dryer to fully dry the product before using the flat iron. You can use your fingers to help with the drying and not a brush/comb. The ironing step is crucial here, you want to make sure that every strand is straight and coated with the heat from the iron 8-10 times. This ensures a straight hair after washing the treatment, so move the flat iron on each section 8-10 times on a perpendicular angle from the scalp. Once it's all straight, you can go ahead and wash your hair with warm water ensuring to scrub your scalp with your fingertips to get rid of all the solution out of your hair, then towel dry (no water dripping) before applying the "Repair Mask" (Step 3). With the last step, apply the mask generously all over then massaging it to your scalp and ensure the ends are covered too. You can wrap a plastic/shower bag and warm dry towel (I warmed my towel in the dryer first) and leave it on for at least 30 minutes or longer (I left mine close to an hour). You can comb the mask to make sure every strand is well covered.

In case you were wondering, you don't have to keep your hair straight when you apply Step 2 (Keratin Treatment), in fact once you've done a section you can swirl it back and clip it. For me, when I coated all my hair I took the clips out and combed my hair again before blow drying. Then after washing the mask thoroughly I left my hair to air dry, but you can use a heat setting here if you want to.

title: You get what you pay for
text:
These plates are just cheaper (price-wise and quality) versions of Konad plates. You get 21 plates for about $18, and shipping is free, so that's quite an irresistible deal, but I have to say, these plates CANNOT compare to the Konad plates.
First of all, there is no safety backing on the plates, as many people have written already; the plates are very thin, and can be very sharp. I resorted to pasting the plates to index cards so it's less likely to slice into my fingers, and to prevent the plates from scratching each other.
Secondly, the designs of the plates are not as intricate and well done as the Konad plates. I have a bunch of Konad plates, and the BM designs definitely don't come close. The BM designs are not as detailed, and just are not as "pretty" as the Konad designs (but of course, you get what you pay for). Also, some of the plates I got, seems like there were manufacturing flaws. The designs on the plates appear smeared, or smudged, and when I tried to stamp them, the images do not transfer properly, if at all.
Thridly, the full nail designs don't actually fit on your whole nail (unless you have really small hands, or are a child). I learned that if I'm very precise on how I stamp, I can get away with stamping the "full nail" designs from my index to my pinky. Thumb is definitely out of the question, lest you end up with a half stamped thumb, or you're good enough to stamp in two halves (you have to really match up the designs). I've never had this problem with Konad designs.
Fourthly, some of my plates arrived with water and rust stains. I don't understand how this happens, since there is a thin Saran type film ontop the plates when you first get them. This must mean that the plates have somehow gotten wet during manufacturing process, but before the packaging process. This doens't interfere with the stamping process, but I just find it annoying to have rust and water marks on my plates.
Overall, these plates are dirt cheap (under a dollar for each plate), compared to Konad which are between $4-7 per plate, but you get what you pay for, and Bundle Monster plates definitely do NOT compare to the quality of Konad's.

title: An Evolutionary Upgrade That Pays off BIG
text:
I've used Oral B toothbrushes for years now. I have always been more than satisfied. I purchased my most recent professional series over 6 years ago. I've always watched them and from appearances, nothing seemed to change. I was wrong! When the brand new 4000 series came out it piqued my invest. I bought one at announcement and when I opened it I was pleased by several differences:
1. The new spare toothbrush holder is better thought out and works much better than the old 'stand up' one.
2. The charging base itself is flatter and more attractive.
3. Unlike the old charging base, there is no where for gunk to pool and become unwashable. Sounds like a small thing, but who wants to look at a mess on their kitchen counter?
When I used it I found out that the improvements were more than skin deep. This is a better toothbrush. I cannot quantify it, but it does clean better, not a little bit, but a lot. In addition there were some positive functional changes.
1. The standard two minute cycle with beeps every 30 seconds has been augmented with a ' deep cleaning' cycle that simply uses the same brushing action with a three minute cycle and beeps every 45 seconds.
2. A separate polishing cycle has been added.
3. A sensitive cycle has been added. For people first converting to an electric toothbrush, especially kids, this is a plus.
4. A pressure alarm light that is easily visible has been added. This was a plus for me since I saw that I had been brushing too hard at the very back of my gums.
Is this an entirely new and revolutionary product for cleaning your teeth? No. Is a very real upgrade resulting from refining that which was already good? Yes. If your Oral B is several years old, you may want to consider upgrading.

title: Great alternative to brow gels, pencils, and powders.
text: I've been using the dark brown tint in this brand for years and have never had a problem.  My hair color is lighter than 'dark brown' but darker brows look nicer on most people because it gives more definition to the face.  The only thing you want to be careful with is making sure you give yourself enough time after application to get it off the skin.  Some people use a cream or Vasoline around the brow, so it doesn't tint the skin.  I apply it at night, remove it with eye makeup remover (oily liquid on a cotton round), and then the next morning wash my face. It comes off the skin without issue for me and the skin around my brow isn't raw from scrubbing.  Whatever you do, if it's your first time using a brow tint,  don't apply it right before an event, date, or work.  Give yourself time to learn how to use the product, i.e. not end up with brows too dark or with tinted skin you are panic scrubbing to get off.  Sometimes, when I want a more dramatic look or the color is fading, I will still manually define my brows, but for my everyday look, the brow tint is enough.

title: Great for putting moisture back into your hair.
text:
Like a previous reviewer, I also received steamer in a box labeled "O'Hair Steamer," but that didn't bother me because all 3 of the models I researched appear to have the exact same design. There must not be an active patent for this device. It was delivered via USPS and arrived in perfect condition. The instructions read like they were translated from another language. I didn't bother with the diagramed instruction booklet, I found a YouTube video from one of my favorite natural hair vloggers, Nikkimae. She provided step by step video instructions on to assemble a steamer that looks exactly like this model. Make sure you have the tube that connects the bonnet to the base connected, as well a as the tiny plug that is located at the base of the bonnet, or you might get leaks. It took less them five minutes to assemble. It took about 3 minutes to start producing loads of stream.
Because the stem that connects the bonnet to the base is not adjustable, you can't adjust the height of the bonnet. Fortunately, the counter I placed mine on and the chair in which I sat provided the perfect height to allow my head to fit under the bonnet so the steam came in contact with all of my hair. I still had to wear a narrow elastic headband so the back of my hair could come in contact with the steam.
I used my favorite deep conditioner and after 20 minutes under the steamer, my hair felt soft and was much easier to comb and style. I like the results much better than using a heat cap for deep conditioning.
The unit doesn't fold down for storage like a bonnet style hair dryer, but fortunately, I have the space to store it fully assembled.
So far, I am very pleased with this. The jury is still out regarding durability, so my opinion may change over time.

title: Unique product, tastes good, and it works!
text:
I know this candy is expensive, but it does what it says it will, which is a big deal for me. This candy is actually sort of a life-changing product for me, and I'm so excited it's available in the US now.

I sweat easily and profusely. It's an embarrassing problem, but this candy makes it much less so. I shower and use underarm deodorant, obviously, which helps the situation there, but the rest of me sweats too... just a general moistness of the skin all over, which often has a somewhat sour smell. Yuck. I'm always the first one in any group to start to sweat if it's warm or we're doing something vigorous. Usually this leaves me feeling really self-conscious and I will stand apart, etc. I've even avoided certain activities with friends during the summer because I knew this would happen. For this candy to help me, I just eat a few pieces an hour or two in advance! Then, when I start to get warm my skin will give off a subtle lovely smell instead of the usual sour smell. I can't tell you how excited I am about this! Also, a side bonus, it has a nice effect on the breath that lasts longer for me than any breath mint I've ever used.

Maybe it's just the way it reacts with my own body chemistry, but I don't think it smells particularly like roses, or even flowery... it's hard to explain, it's just a subtle clean & fresh smell that comes through my skin. You know how some people just smell good, not like product, but just like a nice skin smell? That's what this does for me. A friend of mine ate some and I thought she smelled more flowery, more reminiscent of roses, though not quite. I'd expect it's going to smell a little different on everyone.

Oh, and since it's a candy, I should probably mention: It's delicious! The very first taste when you pop it in your mouth is a little "rosey", meh, but that is almost immediately replaced by a very nice tangy tangerine flavor. I have to keep myself from eating them all up so I'll have them when I need them. :) I buy the regular sugar-sweetened kind, since I don't use artificial sweeteners, so I can't comment on the taste of the sugar-free ones.

title: Some Flaws, But I'd Buy It Again
text:
I bought this to replace a nearly identical Norelco 5825-XL that I used for 12 years until the NiCd battery faded.

This one indicates battery level with 5 LED's, which is nice.

The nylon carrying case is flimsy or "lighter and more compact" depending your viewpoint.

The marketing geniuses at Norelco decided on a rather feminine light blue color for this model.

Other than that, almost nothing has changed in 12 years.

This one's made in China. I see nothing sub-standard about it once you get beyond the insult of paying $70 for something with a manufactured cost around $10.

According to the manual, this shaver will cost you an additional $ 395.40 over 12 years because you should replace the razor heads once a year. The heads on my old 5825-XL went 12 years with no problem, thank you.

The Norelcos might not shave quite as close as foil-headed reciprocating shavers, but they're quiet, comfortable, and good at tackling 3 day's growth and/or difficult parts of your face.

If I lost this shaver, I'd buy the same one again.

text:
This has some pluses and minuses.

The pluses:

This doesn't irritate my skin and even if it doesn't do anything for bumpy skin, it does certainly make my skin very soft. I'm not entirely sure about its claims about dealing with skin issues like acne, as I'm a bit nervous to put this on my face. I figure that it could certainly be used for the occasional acne that shows up elsewhere (we all get it), as tea tree is well known for being a good way to treat acne. Still, I have heard that the base oil is good for skin as well, so that is a plus as well.

The main minus I have here is that while the smell here isn't awful, it's still strong enough that it gave me a bit of a headache. (That's another reason I probably won't be using it on my face.) I was able to deal with this by putting it on in small bits, which seemed to work well since the strongest part of the smell faded away pretty quickly. The remaining scent is honestly pretty nice and mellow.

I do have to commend the company for their packaging. While the bottle did leak during transport, the company was aware that this would happen ahead of time and packaged this well. I do wish that it didn't leak, but barring this I do appreciate that it was properly packaged so that the small amount of oil that leaked didn't get everywhere.
