title: Interesting Gritty Texture And Strong Clove Scent
text:
This Spa-Da Immunity Support Soap is one of the more interesting soaps I have tried. You get a pack of 6 small shield shaped soaps in a resealable plastic bag. The soaps are about 2.75 inches in length.

The scent is strong when you open the bag and especially in the shower. Some of the oils and ingredients included are cloves, cinnamon, oregano, peppermint, parsley, eucalyptus, and rosemary. If you don’t like the smell of cloves, then do not order this because that is the most predominant smell in my opinion. I like it though- it has a nice spicy kick.

The soap definitely feels different than I expected. It doesn’t feel really smooth like many soaps. When dry, they were slightly powdery when I ran my finger across. They are slightly gritty feeling which I noticed more once the soap became wet in the shower. This could be nice if you like a slight scrubby feeling. I typically rub it onto my mesh bath sponge or silicone sponge so I don’t really care about the grittiness either way. I found that it lathers and suds up very well with both my mesh and silicone sponges.

I just started using, so I’m not sure how many showers I’ll be able to get out of each bar. Honestly, I thought they might disintegrate and get used up fast simply based on how powdery they felt when dry. I don’t think it will last as long as some other soaps, but I was still surprised that I could somewhat see the outline of where the shallow cross was imprinted on the soap even after my first shower-and I did intentionally scrub my sponges all over that side pretty vigorously. I took a picture of what the soap looked like after one shower compared to unused bars.

Anyway, my skin feels very clean, perhaps even a little moisturized after using and I haven’t experienced any irritation to my sensitive skin (I have eczema).

I like that this soap is natural and free from harmful chemicals. I also love that it is made in the USA-Ohio specifically, which is where I am from.

I’ll be sure to update my review if any issues arise like if I find that the bars do in fact get used far too quickly. I hope my review was helpful in some way, and if so, I would love to know- thanks!!!

title: Over all really good, once you get the hang of it.
text:
The scraper is plastic so you don't have to worry about it scraping up your plates. I've seen people using just old credit cards to do scraping but because it's free why not use it, plus it fits in your hand easily so it's easier to grip, which is great if you have small hands like me.

The stamper itself, is made up of two parts. The squishy thing to actually transfer the stamp to your nail, and the tube thing that holds it. They do come apart so it's easier to clean (or whatever).

And now for some things I wish I knew sooner:
1. You do not have to press as hard as possible when scraping the plate. Just as long as you move the excess polish out of the way you're good.
2. Newer polishes work best. I know there are specifically polishes for stamping but I don't have those. I have tried to stamp with several different polishes and I've found that newer polishes are easier to pick up with the stamper because they are more liquid like.
3. Move quickly-ish, no you don't have to race to get the polish on your nail but remember that it's a very small, thin amount of polish that dries very quickly, so don't wait a millennium.
4. Roll the stamper over the plate. Start with one side and roll to the other, I've found that this works best as opposed to just straight down on the plate.
5. Remember to use the clearness of the thingy, it's easy to forget that it is clear so remember it is the diffrence between a straight design and crooked design.

read what else I found:
If you haven’t been using makeup primer, then you’re really missing out.

Whether you wear a full face of makeup everyday or you prefer to keep it simple with BB cream and tinted lip balm, makeup primer is a godsend when trying to combat shine or create a smooth base for foundation.

Yet, many people often skip this step because they believe they don’t really need it, are unsure of how to use it or don’t think it’s worth the investment. However, using primer underneath your makeup will make everything last longer, whether that’s on your skin or in your cosmetics bag. We asked two beauty experts to discuss the ins and outs of primer and why it’s a must-have. Here’s the deal.

Makeup primer is a base for foundation or face makeup that allows it to go on smoother and last longer.

Formulas are available in cream, gel and powder. While moisturizer softens skin, editorial and celebrity makeup artist Stephen Dimmick points out that primer prepares skin for your favorite tinted moisturizer or foundation, giving it something to hold onto so it lasts throughout the day.

Many makeup primers are formulated with silicone-based polymers like dimethicone because of their ultra-smoothing effects. But for those who struggle with cystic acne and other skin conditions, do a patch test or check with a medical professional before use, as there have been reports of allergic reactions to dimethicone.

Physicians Formula’s celebrity makeup artist Joanna Schlip adds that makeup primers can also help smooth any fine lines, wrinkles or large pores. If you are searching for a face primer to help color-correct rosacea or conceal acne spots, Schlip’s go-to is this light green primer as that hue cancels out redness.

Primers are even available just for your eyelids to prevent creasing. “I’d recommend pairing a primer with extra long-wear [eyeshadow or eyeliner] formulas for a look that will really stay put,” says Schlip. If you have oilier eylids, Dimmick advises that you use a mattifying eyelid primer.

Using your fingertips to apply makeup primer allows you to really work the product into your skin.

Schlip thinks it’s best to apply primer with fingertips for areas larger than a quarter. “If only using for small areas, I’d recommend a brush. I like to use a concealer or lip brush for this,” she said. This spot-treat technique gives the look of a more natural finish, according to Schlip.

Taking this routine a step further, Dimmick considers the process “an exercise for the face.” He explains that massaging primer onto skin with fingertips helps “to get the blood flowing underneath.” We’ll consider that the next time we’re meditating while putting on makeup.

Primer is a life-saver for getting your makeup to stay-put in extreme weather.

If you live, visit or plan on traveling anywhere that experiences hot and humid or cold and dry temperatures, Schlip suggests having primer handy to help your makeup wear longer. However, Dimmick advocates for using primer year-round. “No matter what the weather is like outside, this extra step will save you a lot of time and effort.”

Primer can even be worn on its own.
Love the fresh no-makeup look but want to look a bit more polished than when you first woke up? Primer is your answer. The product can be worn on your eyelids and double as a light eyeshadow, or it can serve as a lighter alternative to foundation.

title: Super cute AND functional!
text:
With 4 kitties who share our home- two of which are super fluffy and all four are super 'sheddy' - I'm always on the hunt for ways to manage the fur tubleweeds that roll through our home! I ordered this brush because....well....I had nothing to lose! And boy - I was happily surprised!

Pros:
* The brushing area is nice size - it allows me to brush a large area at one time, which is key when dealing with kitties who don't love to be brushed.

* The bristles have tiny rubber tips, which is a small detail that makes a huge difference! This little 'bumper' seems to be much more appealing to our older kitties - perhaps their skin is more sensitive or fragile. Also, for our younger more rambunctious crew, it's not unusual to find minor 'battle wounds' (don't worry, nothing serious and always in good fun). Having this little rubber tip protector prevents from tearing off any scabs as they heal.

* It works! The 'self cleaning' aspect of this brush DOES work! With a wide variety of fur lengths and textures in our 'pack', I can attest to the fact that it catches it all, making it so much easier to keep clean. No more digging into the spikey needley prongs, ruining your fingers as you try to fish out all the pieces of fur! Hooray!

Cons:
* This isn't TRULY a con, but rather a small detail that would have made this tool even better....a cushioned brush. Several brushes that we've liked have 'cushioned' brush heads (where the bristles attach). This allows the brush to contour better to the kitty's body. That's the only thing I can think of that would have made this brush better.

Overall, this cute brush earns 15 paws of approval from our Pack! (One is a tripawd....)

title: solid antibacterial, astringent and anti inflammatory qualities
text:
Tamanu oil is extracted from the seeds of the Calophyllum inophyllum tree (a large evergreen native to East Africa and some regions of India and Australia). Long used in certain systems of traditional medicine (including African and Asian traditional medicine), tamanu oil is applied directly to the skin.

This tamanu oil is manufactured by Gio Naturals, and is 100% PURE ORGANIC COLD PRESSED & UNREFINED! The oil comes in a 4 ounce amber colored bottle with treatment pump. It is USDA & ECO Certified Organic. Tamanu oil is renowned for it's skin regenerating and healing properties. Since the oil is proven to have solid antibacterial, astringent and anti inflammatory qualities, you really can't go wrong by adding it to your facial care routine. I make a night time facial serum from Grape Seed Oil, Tamanu Oil, Argan Oil, Rosehip Seed Oil, Lemongrass essential oil, Tea Tree oil and Vitamin E oil. Tamanu oil absorbs quickly, even though the oil is thick (and dark green). It does have a strong nutty / earthy scent but the lemongrass in my recipe kind of masks it, plus you get used to the scent with continued use. It is pretty strong if you use it as a stand alone oil, but again it is highly effective so you need to balance the pros (many) and cons (scent) to decide if it is right for you. Personally it is my go to oil for facial products.

Tamanu oil is touted as a natural remedy for the following conditions: acne, athlete's foot, eczema, psoriasis, and sunburn. Since tamanu oil is said to alleviate pain, the oil is also used topically to relieve the pain caused by conditions like sciatica, shingles, and rheumatism. Some proponents also claim that tamanu oil can help aid in the regeneration of skin. For this reason, tamanu oil is thought to help reduce the appearance of stretch marks and scars. In addition, tamanu oil is said to promote the healing of burns, blisters, cuts, and scrapes. It is a great, all-purpose therapeutic oil. Works well for my sensitive, acne prone skin.

I received this product at a discount. I have provided an honest and unbiased review based on my personal experience with this product. I am not affiliated with the company in any way and my star rating is based on my personal experience and use of the product.

title: Works well, easy to use, one drawback is tricky to take apart and put back together for cleaning
text:
We purchased Pet Electric Hair Clipper: professional tools for your love pets/grooming clipper, from Caleegi.

Everything appears to be quite well made, of sturdy construction. The scissors and nail trimmers came out of the box sharp, and have a good weight to them. The nail trimmers have a good locking mechanism, metal, not plastic; I think it will last. The set comes with a convenient little storage pouch, which I hadn't noticed on the item description specs list. I like the colors of the pouch. They're cute. The pouch easily fits everything in the kit, except the brush. You can make the brush fit, but I dont think you can make the brush and electric clippers fit. I couldn't. The electric clippers come with a usb powered charger cord, but not a charger block. This is not a standard charger. If you lose this charge cord, you may be hard pressed to find a replacement.

The brush is of good construction, and the ergonomic handle grip is a joy to hold. For real, it just feels good in your hand. I like the push button hair dislodger for easy brush cleaning. Our dog is fairly short haired, straight and wirey, and our cat is fluffy but on the short side of medium length hair. It took very little hair off them, and I haven't found a product better than the Furminator for brushing them. But I've had and worked with longer haired dogs, and for a Great Pyrenees, Burnese Mountain Dog, or Saint Bernard, I think this would be the perfect brush.

The nail file worked great. The comb I intend to keep for myself- it's perfect for my wiry, sometimes wavy, sometimes curly, always disobedient hair.

The electric clipper charged fairly quickly, enough that I could take it for a test spin about 15-20 minutes after plugging it in. I love the electronic digital display, showing how far along in its charging it is, and the RPMs of the clipper blades. I love that it came with a little bottle of lubricant solution for the blades (none of my personal trimmers ever have). The little obligatory cleaning brush to sweep between the blades looks much the same that any electric trimmer does, but I found it shed a wire or two with every pass throughthe blades, which my personal trimmer brushes do not.

I tried the electric clippers out on myself first. I was a little bummed that the nearly universal gaurds that come with clippers designed for people did not fit. The clippers are much more quiet then most clippers, which is good for not startling pets. I used the clippers with the guard on the sides of my head and with no gaurd to shave my face. It went easily through my hair, had no trouble, and gave me a close, even shave. And I went a little rough to see if there was any danger of maybe cutting a squirming or struggling pet, and it seems very safe.

The clipper blades came off pretty easy for cleaning, but were kind of tricky to put back on, and in trying to do so, I hit at a funny angle and the entire clipper assembly fell apart in to 4 pieces. That was annoying, but after messing around with it for about a half hour, I was able to put it back together, and it still worked fine. I would be hesitant to take it apart for cleaning again, though I'm sure I will. Despite this one design flaw, I still think overall this is a pretty quality product.

title: Not just cotton and silk - contains polyester
text:
I won't say the product is necessarily bad, but I certainly do not like it and am not pleased with the disparity between the description and the actual product.

While the amazon page says these eye-covers are made of cotton and silk, the product packaging and tags both indicate the product is cotton, silk, AND polyester. I would not have bought these had I known this as my wife reacts to polyester. This just leaves me with another useless set of eye covers that my wife can't use.

Also, I personally find these uncomfortable. The silk is nothing like my nice soft silk shirts. It is still a shiny and smooth fabric, yet also an uncomfortably rough (I'm not sure how better to describe it -- it's like running your skin over tiny closely spaced wires), fabric that is very hot to wear on your face. Furthermore, I found that I got a headache both times I tried wearing these.

My wife has previously made some passable eye-covers out of cotton socks that we both can wear -- and I find significantly more comfortable. She's suggested that maybe she can try taking these apart and using the straps and cotton parts and making better cotton-sock eye-covers. I'm skeptical and am considering returning these. I'm certainly not happy.

If you like the really slick-abrasive feeling fabrics like cheap silks or cheap satins, and if you don't have any issue with the polyester in these, I can't really see a problem with them. They could probably benefit from being a bit larger, but they're 'pillowy'-enough (for lack of a better word) to block out most of the light and fill in the gaps around the edges. Mystery as to why they give me a headache, but they've enough good reviews that it can't be common.

I'm giving them 2 stars because I think the description is misleading and I don't like them, but also because I think a more moderate rating would get this lost among rating of people who are happy with the item. I always read some of the reviews and I wish I'd seen a review like this before purchasing.

title: fine but the container has flaws
text:
The gel soap seems fine - the cedar scent is strong but nice and not flowery (which is what I wanted) but the container has some serious flaws.
The bottle is attractive made of smooth metal - so when it's wet it becomes very slippery (which is the normal status when taking a shower). However, when I pressed the button to dispense the soap - nothing happened - no soap came out but the button didn't really depress, so I thought it must be locked and I'd need to twist it to unlock it.
Wrestling with this slippery wet bottle with my wet hands didn't seem to be working - I couldn't feel any give or clicks as I tried to twist the very small nozzle button in the wet - and without my glasses on I couldn't see if there were any markers or arrow directions....but I braced the slippery bottle as firmly as I could and kept trying until I suddenly noticed a stream of foamy soap coming out and dropping to the floor of the tub.
As I proceeded with my shower, I continued having challenges. This bottle has a VERY firm button. It wasn't actually locked, but my small 54 yr old female hands didn't have the strength to manage it at all (one handed). Especially as the bottle was wet and smooth and dang slippery! I ended up having to brace the bottle with one hand and push the button with the other - which left me with no palm available to catch the actual soap coming out. I wasted a bit of soap before I figure out I needed to twist the hand holding bottle to catch the stream of soap which let me catch about half.
There's definitely a design flaw in choosing that bottle and button dispenser!! It's very attractive but the tension spring for the dispenser button is crazy strong. Maybe they took the idea of masculine soap too far and have chosen bottles that can only be used by men with stronger hands too? Added with the smooth but hard bottle (metal doesn't provide any give when you squeeze hard) that becomes super slippery when it's wet (which is the expectation when taking a bath or shower) this doesn't seem very well thought out. Bad operations and marketing choices!

title: Norelco is great, this one is just OK
text:
I have used Norelco shavers for many years and prefer them to all other models I have tried. This review comes from much experience with the brand.

This Arcitec design looks fancy and works well, but gets three average stars because it really works no better than the previous non-space-age, less expensive designs. The 1050, 1060, and 1090 all operate the same, they just have a different display: none is better than the other, and don't waste money on the Cleaner accessory. It is fairly comfortable to hold (I prefer the feel of the original model because this is one is smaller), and looks fancy sitting on the counter, but it does not do a better job. It requires cleaning after each use as there is no space for the hairs. I have always cleaned my shavers after each use anyway. Unless you just want the apperance, it is not worth the extra money.

Technically: The triple-blade per round head (each cutter has three spinning blade areas) does not do any better than a double cutting blade. Kind of like a Saturday Night Live skit in the 70's, Jim Belushi said, "Buy a triple bladed razor. For those that will believe anything". Lift-and-cut is a ridiculous concept and a marketing ploy, but Norelco's do a nice job. Norelco went back to more diagonal openings with this model, which is good. Many other newer models have lots of little pin-holes which are worthless, as the hairs have no time to enter a small hole with shaving motion. You would have to set it directly on a hair to cut it. The less pin-holes the better.

Feel: The head design feels better on the neck, and has not caused razor-burn if I do not stretch the skin tight like I need to with the original model. It takes the same time to shave as my older unit, and I get no better results, no faster. It takes the same time to get a smooth shave, and the same persistance in some areas.

Function: It is a little bit easier to shave under the nose, above my mustache, but not a major difference. It is much harder to trim my sideburns with this unit as the heads almost cut my hair on my head above the ears the way it is shaped. Very poorly designed trimmer, so I use my older shaver for that.

Battery: Early, new battery life is good, as with most new battery devices. But, it states to not over-charge. Meaning, you need to be around when recharging to unplug it after it is charged; not good for those that shave and must go to work. The other units would shut off after charging.

Cleaner/Charger: Again, one needs to be around when it is finished to not over-charge. The cleaner is not necessary and a waste of time, money, and chemicals. I use a razor brush from an older unit, brush it out quickly over the wastebasket (one can't blow it out without getting hair dust all over the bathroom, and it can't be shaken into the wastebasket as easily as the older models), and I spray it quickly with Remington Silicone Lubricant (I can only find it at Wal-Mart, which is the only thing I ever go there for, by the way).

Overall: Buy it for looks and keep your old one in the drawer for sideburns. Nicer on the neck.

I would return it, BUT, it was a gift, AND I like the look of it. I know, I know!!

Update 12-29-07
I purchased a Braun 9595 through J&R on Amazon, and it has a 60 day trial return guarantee. This is the first micro-screen razor I have used and it is better in all respects to the Norelco Arcitec except for the fancy styling. It is fast and comfortable, and my face feels razor smooth. I was able to return the Arcitec and am really happy with this Braun 9595 model.

text:
These come with 3 product boxes wrapped with plastic around them holding them together. All 3 of the outer product boxes look exactly the same, so initially I thought they had sent me the wrong thing - 3 foundations - instead of 2 foundations with sponges. But, once I took off the plastic wrapping and felt the 3 boxes, I could tell that 1 had sponges in it. Kind of weird they put them inside one of their foundation boxes. Not sure how comfortable I am with them not being wrapped on their own, but rather handled someone and placed into a foundation box? But, I guess either a machine or person normally handles makeup sponges in order to get them in their packaging, so this isn’t that weird 🤷‍♀️ Then, I took the sponges out and they looked like they had lint/paper or something all over them. I always wash my sponges before use anyways, and these felt soft and bouncy, so I figured I’d give them a try once I washed them. They worked really well so I’m glad I didn’t toss them right away. They are really soft and bouncy and increase in size once wet. Even though I really like them, I took a star off for them coming in a foundation box and having paper/lint all over them.

This comes in a thick frosted glass bottle with a dropper to dispense. It’s a nice clean way of dispensing product and to be able to control the amount of product you get out, which I like.

It claims to be made from natural ingredients. The ingredients are listed here on the product page and on the box. I put them at the end of this review. There were some ingredients that were listed oddly. When I first saw them listed I didn’t recognize them, so I looked them up. I’m not sure if they had to be translated and they got messed up that way or what, but they just weren’t written completely correct. Like I said, I put the ingredients at the end of my review. First, I put them exactly how they’re listed on the product page and the box. Then, below that, I wrote out what ingredients I felt were written the wrong way and wrote out what they should have been written as. If you want to look them up, it definitely makes it easier looking them up written the right way, at least for me it did. The ingredients can come from natural things. It does include parabens (methylparaben and propylparaben). I know a lot of people now are against parabens and now a lot of companies are producing “paraben free” products, but parabens are used preservatives. If they aren’t using parabens, which have been used regularly in products for many years, for the preservatives, they’re going to be using something else. Methylparaben occurs naturally in a handful of fruits (like blueberries), but it can also be created synthetically. Propylparaben is also a natural substance found in many plants and some insects.

I had gotten another foundation from Amazon that came in a glass bottle with a dropper to dispense similar to this one. I got that one in the lightest shade and it ended up being way too warm for me. I got this one in #2 because looking at the swatches it seemed lighter than #1. #1 seemed darker and warmer than #2 and #3. #2 and #3 seemed to be the lightest shades, with #2 looking more pink and #3 more yellow. I decided to go with #2. I always hate when companies make their #1 shade darker than the ones that come after it! I never understand that! But, I’m glad they had swatches to look at!

#2 is light enough for me, and like it seemed in the product photo of swatches, it has a pink tone to it. I did a swatch comparing this foundation in #2 to Maybelline Fit Me Matte+Poreless in 110 Porecelain. As you can tell, Maybelline one is more warm toned and this foundation is more cool toned.

It gives a nice natural, slightly dewy finish. It gives okay coverage. One thin layer just evens out my skin tone, but you can build it up some and/or use a brush instead of a sponge and get more application. With a foundation like this, that is a thinner consistency, if you want the most amount of coverage you can get from it, I recommend using a short haired, dense foundation brush. If you want to blend it seamlessly into the skin where it just evens out skin tone, you can use a sponge or use a fluffier brush to blend it onto the skin (I like using a fluffy dual fiber brush or my luxie 522 brush - it’s called a tapered highlighting brush, but I love the look it gives when I use it to blend in a thin consistency foundation! It just looks so seamless!). I usually don’t powder my face completely, only where I absolutely need to. But, with this foundation, I definitely recommend powdering! If I do a thin layer and powder, I don’t get much transfer at all.

Overall, I think it’s an okay foundation. If you like a natural but dewy finish, like a foundation that you can even out your skin tone with or build it up for a little more coverage, and don’t mind that you have to powder it to keep the transfer down, this would work for you. Personally for me, I like how hydrating this feels. It doesn’t cling to dry patches at all. Where a lot of foundations, even dewy ones, will sometimes look dry or cakey (like between my eyebrows, no matter how hard I try I can’t get foundation to look smooth and good there 😠), this one doesn’t do that! It looks nice and smooth there! I like using it on days where I just need to even out my skin.

INGREDIENTS
AS LISTED ON BOX AND ON AMAZON PRODUCT PAGE
Water, glycerin, propylene glycol, poly two methyl siloxane ring five, titanium dioxide, palmitic acid ethyl ester, liquid paraffin, PEG-30 two poly hydroxy stearic acid ester, poly two methyl siloxane cross-linked polymer, petrolatum, C12-15 alcohol benzoate, magnesium sulfate, avocado fruit fat, beeswax, rose flower extract, lanolin, magnesium stearate, polysorbate -80, methylparaben and propylparaben, phenoxyethanol ethylhexylglycerin, rose oil, iron oxides.

MY CHANGE OF HOW SOME INGREDIENTS ARE LISTED
“Poly two methyl siloxane ring five” - Cyclopentasiloxane D5 (Cyclo = ring, penta = 5, dimethyl = 2 methyls)
“PEG-30 Two Poly Hydroxy Stearic Acid Ester” - PEG-30 Dipolyhydroxystearate (di = 2, stearate = salt or ester of stearic acid)
“Poly Two Methyl Siloxane Cross-Linked Polymer” - Polydimethylsiloxane

title: Long fine hair has shape and style!
text:
I have abundant long, fine hair which is stick straight unless it’s on vacation in say, Sanibel Island FL, Cancun, or on summer days in Washington DC. I work from home most of the time, so my hair is generally air dried and worn down, but I wanted a tool that would help me style my hair - some way, any way! - while on business trips without devoting precious carry on space to both a blow dryer and a round brush.
This device has given me exactly what I wished for! I pack it in my bag, air dry my hair as usual, brush it out carefully with a hair bristle brush, and then start hot brushing. I don’t do anything fancy, just turn my head upside down to get some volume at the crown, then run the brush through my hair to get it orderly. I might wrap a few ends around the barrel to get some shape, and style it away from my face, but this device is far less technically demanding than a round brush/dryer set up or a traditional curling iron. I like that I can use this spontaneously, so if I get sucked into some other task while my hair dries, I haven’t missed the chance to style it. My fine hair is prone to tangling so I am an admitted frequent user of silicone, so it was important to me that I not style my hair every day - just when I need to look nice.
Two caveats: I tried to add volume at the roots by wrapping my hair around the barrel all the way to the bottom, or wrapping just the bottom, but both approaches led to terrifying tangle-ups. As someone who has had to have her boyfriend physically cut the bristles off a round brush to free her, perhaps I’m just lacking technique. But if you get your hair wrapped around this barrel going two directions, you’d better turn this baby off quick or your roots will get scorched.
Secondly, having learned how to use a straightener to create attractive curls, I’d hoped that the straightener feature of this device combined with the bristles would allow me to follow the same procedure with smoother results. Not so. This didn’t work for me at all. If you used this device in straightener mode to achieve curls, I may need lessons from you. It might just be a matter of how willing my hair is to hold curl (not very).
Anyway, while this device didn’t let me create straightener curls, it’s otherwise been great!

title: Unique. . .Maybe Too Unique
text:
This is a really neat razor that has one possible issue, which I'll get to later.

The handle is big and heavy, and its unusual shape is very stylish. It gives a nice shave, too. If you have a small face or tight features, the large head might be a bit tricky to use in some areas, but that hasn't been a major issue. I usually use an old-school double-edge razor, not a flexing cartridge razor, so the fixed head angle isn't an issue for me. If you're used to a razor with a movable head, this one might take some getting used to.

The included shaving foam smells good and works well. You don't get a lot, but you don't have to use a large amount of it.

The "stand" is just a heavy metal cylinder with a round hole in the top and a pad on the bottom. The hole is wider than the razor handle, and just deep enough that the razor doesn't topple out. It's kind of weird, like the stand was designed for something else, but I guess it works.

I'm not sure why they call this package a "travelling razor kit." It comes in a large gift box, and doesn't include any sort of travel case or bag. Plus, it's the biggest, heaviest razor I've ever seen (aside from folding straight razors). I wouldn't even think of taking this thing on a trip.

Despite all the good things about this razor, there's one major red flag: At the moment, replacement blades aren't listed on Amazon or on the Suprent website. The package includes two cartridges and a card to get a third for free, but there's no guarantee that more will be available when you need 'em. While the included cartridges are definitely good for several shaves apiece, if that's all you get, you'll soon be left with a very expensive paperweight. I rated the product based on my use of it, but recommend that you verify the availability of replacement cartridges before buying.

title: They recommend to use it in the morning on DRY skin
text:
I bought this serum from ScienceSerum directly and returned it after 3 weeks of use since it dried out my around eye area beyond repair. Skin in the corners of my eyes started to crape, lines and wrinkles became more deep and pronounced because of the dryness, puffiness and dark circles appeared. It has been 4 weeks since I stopped using it, but I still have been able neither to quench the dryness nor diminish puffiness no matter what I do. I went to my derm, he said I have severe allergic reaction and prescribed steroids to combat the symptoms.

At the time when skin care layering is paramount, this product is a huge logistical failure.
It is very difficult to incorporate the serum into either- morning or night - routine. They recommend to use it in the morning on DRY skin, which means you would need to cleanse your face, wait for it to dry, apply it, then wait again for the serum to dry. Who has time for that much waiting in the morning? Another issue for me was that I could not leave my skin dry for that much time without applying toner and Vit C. But then, when the serum was dried, vitamin C would be washed off along with the serum. I wrote to the company and asked them how to properly layer it with other skincare products I use (Vitamin C, Retin-A, essences etc) they had no idea!
Another problem - it is extremely difficult to get it off your skin completely without pulling and tagging your delicate eye area. But if you do not pulling and tagging, the product stays on your skin and destroys it very rapidly.
If you have a question and write to Scienceserum, be prepared to contact them at least three times before they respond.
If you are going to buy directly from them and decide to return the serum, you will be responsible for return shipping AND they are going to withhold 20% of the serum cost for the original shipping. Returns are processed only on Mondays, so do not expect the return money to be on your account soon. The last drop was when I wrote to them about my experience, I received back one line reply consisting of the return address". No word of apology or concern.
Overall, it is a dangerous, damaging product, please be very cautious before buying it.

text:
I like at home spa treatments and have enjoyed most I've tried. I was offered this Molequle Glow & Go mask and thought I would try them out. At time of review 3 masks cost $24.99.

The masks come well sealed as a set inside another bag. My set did not come with instructions for use. The back of the packet only has ingredient information. I had to look on the Amazon product page and with my phone I could not read the instructions on the one picture they have of it- as it was blurry. So from what I think I read you use these masks daily for 20-30 minutes. 1 star was taken off for lack of instructions- there's no real reason it couldn't have been on the packet itself. I'll say when I buy these at home treatments I tend to lean more towards mud masks, gels, and lotions, the biocellulose masks are never very comfortable or fit my oval face well. The eye holes are never big enough and the masks never sit right. This is sadly no exception, I would keep pushing on it while I wore it so another star taken there. Now, the effects: they were pretty good, my face definitely had a glow about it when I removed them. Likely over time and with extended use my skin would lighten more. So at least what they said is very true. They are pricey but if they do what they say and this is the result you want they would be worth the cost. The solution had no smell, absorbed nicely, and felt good, no irritation to speak of. I'd be interested in trying their other masks or more of these even with my small gripes.

title: Patience required, and rewarded, by good results.
text:
Does exactly what it is supposed to do. A couple tips and tricks I've picked up along the way:
1) There is a continuity buzzer that will let you know that you have completed a good circuit (remember the saltwater on your fingers!)
--> The buzzer length is about 8 seconds and then repeats. You can use this to keep the probe in for the recommended 15 seconds (two long beeps)
2) The tweezers are just ok. A person with 120 grit sandpaper and a bit of patience can get the surfaces mating perfectly and give the tweezers a positive grip
3) There are two included probes, and the super-thin probe wires are reasonably stiff, but also brittle. I've broken one already trying to straighten the wire after I bent it.
4) The process is NOT instantaneous... after treatment the hair will still feel firmly attached. Give it an hour or two for the chemical reaction you created to break down the follicle.
5) The process will almost certainly only kill "many" of the hair producing cells in the follicle, but not "all". You will see regrowth, albeit much finer hairs, which should fade with additional treatments.

text:
Common sense right? Well, it’s not that I didn’t try, but it’s not exactly made as easy as it could be.

Regarding the seller: Don’t buy these without being 100% sure they’re for your clippers, because you can’t return these.

Regarding the manufacturer: Wahl doesn’t do a great job identifying their physical products. I bought a clipper second hand, thinking “Great, it’s hardly used and all it needs is a new blade.” Turns out, if you don’t have an exact model number it’s extremely difficult to figure out what blade kits will work because Wahl doesn’t actually put the exact model number on all of their products. There’s also slight variations for common parts, like screws. Not sure why you’d spec an entirely different screw when manufacturing a like part used in multiple product lines, but hey, what do I know. You might only get the name of the series or product line, or in my case, an abbreviation of it. title: Excellent for eczema
text:
I have sensitive skin due to eczema, and I have tried so many body washes making sure they do not contain sodium laureth sulfate (this is ingredient is a trigger for a flare up). But after trying this cleanser my flare ups have minimized considerably.

This is what I do to minimize flare ups:
1) use unscented laundry detergent for sensitive skin. Dropps or Tide are both excellent brands.
2) DO NOT use fabric softners or dryer sheets, they are toxic for our skin.
3) use 1/3 cup baking soda as fabric softener
4) use unscented body wash and lotions and make sure they do not contain SLS (Sodium Laureth sulfate)
5) avoid tight fitting clothing whenever possible, especially when sleeping.

title: Major price hike, small quantity.
text:
The listing is for 3 sheets of 18 graduated sizes of stickers attached to a central strip, so 6 stickers of any given size. The "54 strips" refers to the quantity of individual stickers, not the quantity of sheets. At $13 USD, that's $4.33 per sheet and $0.24 per sticker. Since most people don't have 9 different sizes of nail beds on every finger, you'll go thru the ones that fit pretty quickly and have to either trim down or throw out the ones that don't fit.

In Sep 2018 I ordered a pack of 40 sheets (720 stickers) from Dashing Diva for $25. That breaks down to roughly $0.62 per strip of 18 and $0.03 per individual sticker. They worked well and I felt happy with the results. Although they've tweaked the product in the last couple years and the stickers are now a thicker material, and 2021 is a different world in terms of supply chain costs, I'm not convinced a ~587% price increase in less than 3 years is justified by slightly thicker material.

Although these strips are effective at protecting your natural nail and easy to use, the value for money is not great in my opinion. Unless the price comes back down I can't see myself ordering these again, and will have to find more cost effective ways to keep my nails healthy.

title: Definitely Worth It
text:
Great comb! Never bought a comb for myself before I started growing out my hair. Short and sweet:

Pros:
- Style: Comb is beautiful. You can see the details of how it was made, with slight markings where whatever tool they used to form the teeth made contact with the horn. You can't see it unless you inspect it closely, which IMHO adds to the authenticity of it. Also, the coloring of the comb is just fascinating. On mine, you can see the differing blends of color throughout, and between each teeth you can sometimes make out the gradient transition.
- Weight: Very light. I sometimes check my pocket just to make sure it's even in there and hasn't fallen out when pulling out my wallet or keys.
- Function: As advertised, I have never experienced any sort of static buildup or discharge when using this comb. It's especially nice when you just woke up with some severe bedhead and don't want to fuss with taming stray statically charged strands of hair.

This product is exactly as advertised and shown in the images. This mini system does not come with color, so be prepared. The packaging is attractive, and the products came very well packaged and arrived safely in perfect condition. This gel nail polish kit has a little different texture than some of the kits available these days. This system has a complete nail prep and foundation product line-up much like the really great gel nails from 20 years ago. I'm hoping the long term quality of the nail growth and health with this product line, is as good as the old products as well. As well all know, products can help your nails or destroy them, and this product line, the formulas remind me of the better products that were once available and were very expensive to buy.

The thing people may not be used to is the last step of using the finishing wipe to remove the sticky layer once the manicure is complete. Some top coats are completely set and free of any tackiness right after the curing process. These products cure quickly with some heat, and 60 seconds seemed to be plenty of time. After the top coat and final removal of the tackiness, the nails are perfect. This kit doesn't come with color, so I experimented with a milky white and some blue ink, using the wood tools included in the kit to move and swirl the pigment around. It's a fun, creative way to change up polish. I think stencils could be fun, and I do have mica powders, some bling pieces, to play with as well. I like these products, and the box came with a nice catalogue of other products available.

This product is easy to use, I've experienced no irritation of my cuticles or nail bed, no itching or discomfort at all. The light is really cute, tiny and it works. Just one easy button and it turns off automatically in a minute. I pressed twice to get 2 minutes but found that 1 minute was enough, which is great. title: Great scent, great lather. And a great price (at WallyWorld).
text:
Palmer's/E.T. Browne has a lot of above-average products in its line. This is one of them, for sure.

The scent is scrumptious. Not much like "coconut sun-tan oil at the beach" … much more like "fresh coconut cream pie desert!"

I say above-average because, if you scour the ingredient list on Palmer's products, you will typically find SOME natural & luxurious ingredients … and also some fairly common chemicals. So many of their products are of a higher quality than common store-shelf items … but not exactly in the category of seriously premium and/or upscale products.

For example, this product's main ingredient is Sodium olefin sulfonate. That's a common ingredient in bath & body products that used to make them lather. And Palmer's has been very generous with it, in that this shampoo really REALLY lathers up! The next major ingredient is coconut fruit extract. Many manufacturers won't use coconut oils or extracts in their bath & body products because straight-up palm oils and extracts are cheaper. After that there's a list of many other common chemical sounding ingredients. But also there's coconut oil, Tahitian gardenia extract, keratin-protein and glycerin. Those too are premium ingredients that common bath & body products usually won't contain. And this shampoo contains NO sulfates, parabens, mineral oil, dyes, gluten or phthalates.

That's a lot of quality, given the price … that being $4.36 at WallyWorld for a 14 ounce bottle… and, as of this writing, with instant "$2 off" coupons attached. That's a lot less expensive than other "big brand name" shampoos that offer less and cost more.

There's also a matching body wash product. In use, and in the ingredient list, they are almost exactly the same product. And there's a matching bar soap, though I found it far less interesting - meh - than this shampoo and its matching body wash.

This shampoo seems far better suited for dry hair; it conditions, moisturizes and protects. But I have oily hair. So I sometimes resort to using my bar soap on my hair as a first pass, to "cut through" a lot of the oil, before actually using this shampoo as a second application.

In any case, for a mere $2.36, you can pick up a bottle of this stuff at WallyWorld and see how this shampoo suits you yourself.

title: Helps My Sensitive Skin
text:
My skin is ridiculously sensitive, so finding products that won't set off some kind of irritation, breakouts, etc., is nearly impossible. I hadn't used a cica cream before, but the reviews were positive enough that I wanted to give it a try.

The texture is interesting - it's less a cream and more like a gel that's almost runny. It absorbs fairly quickly into the skin and doesn't leave behind any kind of greasy residue. It does help with redness and dry patches, and at this point, it doesn't seem to cause breakouts.

I have to say, though, that I was hoping for longer-lasting, even cumulative results, because I apply this at night and right after I rinse my face off the next morning, it's almost like I never used the product at all. Maybe it's a matter of me having to use this twice a day (at least), but given the high price point for what is, in fact, a pretty small tube of product, I feel like I would go through the cream much too quickly that way.

Still, it does help a bit and doesn't seem to cause any issues, so this is one of the very few products that I can see myself continuing to use long-term.

title: Lovely oil with so many uses
text:
I love apricot kernel oil. It definitely one of my favorite carrier oils because it has so many uses. It's nice to have a 16 ounce bottle of cold pressed oil to work with. Here are just a few of the uses for this wonderful oil:

1) Apricot kernel oil for Skin
Apricot kernel oil is good for people with sensitive skin. It is non-irritant and soothing for the skin. It is light and quickly makes the skin soft and smooth. Apricot oil penetrates deep into the skin. It is easy to apply on the skin as it quickly spreads on the skin. It soothes irritated skin. A massage with apricot kernel oil is good for dry, parched skin. It can be used post shower to lock the moisture into the skin. Since it is light, it wont leave a greasy residue. Once absorbed into skin, it provides moisturization for hours. Apricot kernel oil is one of the best carrier oils for massage as it penetrates nicely into the skin and also improves the delivery of essential oils and other herbal agents. This oil is also good for infusing with herbs and absorbing their essence. It can be utilized for various kinds of massage that require an oil.
2. Apricot kernel oil for Hair
Apricot oil is loved by many people around the world for their hair care. When applied to the hair shafts,it helps to detangle hair. These are the health benefits that organic apricot oil provides to hair. It promotes hair growth because of the nutrients in it, especially Vitamin E. It reduces dry scalp problems and helps to achieve gorgeous shiny hair without any greasiness. When used as a hot oil treatment, it conditions the hair and provides them nutrition. It softens the hair, so that they are more manageable and easily combed.
3. As an Under Eye Cream
Apricot oil can be applied just like almond oil for healing under eye skin. It aids in reducing dark circles, puffiness and helps to strengthen the skin around this region. With regular application of apricot kernel oil, one can reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles around the eyes.
4. Face Oil
Apricot kernel oil is a nice face oil, especially when compared to other heavier oils. It helps to improve skin tone, nourish the skin and lower the appearance of aging signs, like wrinkles, lines and blemishes. However, this oil should be avoided by people who are suffering from acne or are prone to acne. That is because it has a comedogenicity of 2. This means that the oil is mildly comedogenic and it can clog skin pores. This may result in acne breakouts and blackheads.
5. Heart Health
Consumption of apricot kernel oil can be a healthy choice for the heart and the cardiovascular system. This oil has demonstrated the ability to lower the risk of heart attack in rats and can possibly perform the same function in humans. You can use apricot oil as a salad dressing and by using it for cooking certain recipes that go well with the flavor of this oil.

text:
About five months ago, I was offered a free Zakora Head Shaver for review via the Amazon Vine Program, and I accepted.

This head shaver rocks! It's super easy to keep your head clean shaven with this. I've been using it regularly for the past five months and I've travelled with it more than a few times, no problem. I've been using it in the shower and it only takes a few minutes a few times per week. It runs smoothly and quietly and the shave is close and comfortable. The shaver itself is light in weight, fits well in the hand, plus it's very easy to maneuver and maintain. After using it, I rinse it under the water then shake and let it dry. The easy to read LED display shows both the approximate remaining battery life in minutes along with the time spent shaving. It runs for about 80 minutes on a single charge, so you only need to charge it occasionally (depending on how long you use it, of course). The extra brushes and trimmers are all very nice and work well with the exception of the nose hair trimmer... it doesn't work well for me at all. The shaver has a travel lock feature so that it doesn't accidentially turn on in your bag. The build quality is very impressive, especially for the price. title: Doesn't fade but bleach is rough
text:
I have been using bright hair colors for about 18 years. In the past I used Manic Panic and it faded - this stuff does NOT fade very quickly at all! I dyed my hair purple in October 2011 and it was still there nine months later! I bleached it and it STILL stayed, except it turned pink. This color will show through even if you dye over it, so be sure you want that color!!

I currently have white hair with blue and pink on the top. The pink is still vibrant and the blue is very dark.

Two words of caution:
The bleach is rough. Really really rough. Not too bad on the hair but very bad on the skin. It makes my whole head burn. Other bleach kits do not do this and I do not have sensitive skin. It does not, however, seem to do damage to the skin. No redness or anything. It just hurts till you wash it off.

The second thing is that you will think this is all washing out. For the first five or six washes, you'll see a LOT of color in the sink. If part of your hair is still white or natural color, protect it the first few washes - coat all the hair except the colored portions by rubbing in conditioner while the hair is dry. That way, when you wash, you won't get the color residue on the other hair.

I give this product four stars simply because of the bleach - the color itself is great. I have used purple, blue, and pink.

After trying most sunscreens on this continent, I decided to look to Japan for my sunscreen needs. As fair skin is so highly prized in their extremely technologically advanced society, you'd think they would have some exceptional solutions to blocking the sun. They use amazing ingredients that haven't been pushed through America's expensive FDA drug approval processes, but are no less effective and harmless.

I ordered 8 different sunscreens from various Japanese brands in my search for the new holy grail sunscreen that moisturized & worked well under makeup. This one is IT my friends! Protects so well and just sinks into your skin--no whiteness at all. Everyone I've gifted it to loves it as well.

I have dry skin, so this is perfect for me (and I'd say most people) but this brand (Rhoto) has an oily skin version called Sarafit that was my favorite before I found out they made a dry skin version. The Sarafit was also the only sunscreen that my boyfriend liked out of all of them --"not sticky!" he actually likes how it feels so has become a daily-applier. I'm so proud! A testament to this brand's excellence.

I've bought many tubes, each one lasts a long time but they take a friggin month to get here via Amazon so plan ahead and order two..

title: Niceeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee!
text:
Have had a dozen cheap low end 10 buck nose hair trimmers Norelco, Conair, and 10 other no names (in the last 20 years). None lasted longer than a year. All didn't trim worth a darn. This is a well made, strong motor, cuts very well and has bested every other one I have owned - and get this - it's less than 10 bucks. Just used for the first time, if it lasts longer than a year I will be thrilled - It feels sturdy and I think it will. Will update if it doesn't - but for now 5 stars isn't enough - would have given 9 if it could.

Not quit a perfect 10, would have like the charge port to be USB - but I knew that is wasn't USB when I ordered - so no surprises.

Others have said - LED light doesn't go off to indicate fully charged - instructions say charge for 8 hours. For less than 10 bucks it probably doesn't have the "smarts" to tell you it's charged and go into a trickle charge so that it doesn't overcharge/heat-up or shorten the life of the battery. So simply time it - plug I in when it slows down and charge it for no more than 8 hours - tick tock, set an alarm on your smartphone for 8 hours.

Others have complained - no storage case - what do they want for 10 bucks ? If you want a case there are dozens of soft cases for sale on Amazon that would work - don't care about case to store the trimmer and the charge cord.

Great price for the quality. NICE.

-The tube lasts much longer than it says. I'm on my second now, and the first lasted 4 months using it every day. (Long enough to see if it works on you).

title: The razor does what it was designed to do
text:
Having used the disposable razors now for 25 plus years i decided to try an electric razor again, given the fact your considered a terrorist if you have shaving cream cans in your luggage while traveling, the electric razor seemed like a viable solution. After much reviewing i decided to go with the 9160xl at christmas, it was almost march before i recharged it, and after a few days of use, i was used to how it works, its much faster to complete a shave, trim my mustache and gote, and off i go with no worries of water on my shirt, or shaving cream to wipe off. You can also shave while walking around as your not tied to the sink and running water to clear off the razor. The key to any battery operated device is to properly charge it when you first place it on the bathroom sink. And do not return it to the charger until the shaver shows low battery, that way you keep the battery life good. And yes its quiet. Does not sound like a small airplane nor does it make a high pitched whinning noise. Comments about not having power or cutting of skin are ridiculous, i have never had a problem, all i do is clean it out each use, and rinse the head out when the razor indicates it wants a water cleaning. title: Works well overall - but "bristles" vary in length year to year, become brittle and break off too easily.
text:
It is difficult to find a large barreled curling iron/brush. HELEN OF TROY offers a broad range of assorted sizes, and they work well. This is my third or fourth purchase of this same model in about 10 years. Even though I purchase the same model, I find that the hard plastic "bristles" vary in height from year to year. The short "bristles" sometimes place the hot barrel too close to my skin, especially when the "bristles" break off (which is fairly easy and common, possibly due to overexposure to heat). The models that arrived with longer "bristles" are more suited for longer hair, however they sometimes "tangle" in the hair -- and THEY, too break off all too easily. (I have recommended to the manufacturer that they add something slightly more flexible to the "bristles" to keep them from getting brittle and breaking, or perhaps design the barrels so that new sets of bristles can be installed, however -- why would they take my suggestion when consumers can simply replace the entire unit with a new one?) The heating elements in these units have never failed; only the "bristles" are problematic.

Overall, I like this model, but I find that I need to replace it after about 12-18 months of use due to loss of "bristles".

title: Not bad!
text:
I've always been wary of electric razors, but I have to say this one works pretty well for me. It took no time for my face to get "used to" this razor (in the past it was hell to try to get through a couple of weeks with other kinds). The first day I used it I got a nice, close shave with no irritation.

A single charge lasts me a couple of weeks, so even though I've brought the charger with me when traveling I've never had to use it (I'll be leaving it home the next time). I haven't actually used the cleaning system yet, because you can run the entire razor under hot water and clean it out no problem. I just leave it on the counter to dry until I come home from work.

My only complaint would be that like most other people (and all other electric razors that I know about) it doesn't get all of those hard to get hairs on my neck without several passes, and the trimmer doesn't get close enough to my sideburns. Not a problem though, I just keep a disposable razor in the shower and touch up---just a few seconds with no lather so not a big deal.

I would recommend this product to anyone looking to make the switch.

text:
For the longest time I've wanted to be able to throw my hair up into a cool looking messy bun ~ but with very thin, fine hair, was never able to pull it off. This messy bun hairpiece, however, provides the volume & fullness my hair absolutely needs...

This hairpiece is very large; it enveloped my entire head. So, to create the messy bun look I was after required a 3-step process: 1. Put my hair up into a pony tail with a hair elastic & wrap it around into a tight bun using just 2 bobby pins. 2. Place the scrunchie hairpiece on, securing it with a couple more Bobby pins. 3. Pull the hairpiece together, & stretch a 2nd hair elastic around, over the top, tucking it under. This makes it just the right size ~ & viola... instant messy bun! Love it!

For reference, the underside of my hair is a natural, medium brown color, & the top is dyed a #8 medium blond shade. I purchased the #27T613 Sandy Brown & Bleach Blonde messy hair piece.

title: An Honest Review
text:
My friend introduced me to epilating about 5 years ago. She had a double headed one from Spain it was amazing you could barely feel a thing. I searched for one similar everywhere and did some research that said the 40 dollar epilators do just as good as the more expensive ones. So I settled and bought a 40 dollar one, it did the job yes and I got use to how it worked (I usually waxed though since the epilator never removed every thing) Well it died about 4 months ago after, I decided that I wanted an epilator that would last and actually get the job done.

I went back to researching, I read so many reviews and many of you probably have and will. It is from my experience it depends on the person and the day that makes the review (I am having normal day.)

I decided in the to buy the Braun 7281 and crossed my fingers. Since I had grown use to my last epilator I was extremely surprised that this one felt so much better and barely noticed any pain; as well as I don't have to wax anymore saving so much more money now by spending more on the better epilator. But I decided I would give myself about 6 weeks and see how it did pain wise. It didn't feel the worst but it did sting for a few minutes and then I got use to it again. I must say that it still didn't hurt as bad as the 40 dollar one did and it still did just as good as a wax would. (Any epilator is going to sting if you haven't waxed or epilated in a 6 weeks +, I recommend waxing if you have sensitive skin before you jump back into epilating.) In the end I would even say this one is equal if not better then one my friend had and would recommend it to anybody. Added bonus is that it comes with many different tops as well as an electric razor.

If you are still on the fence about buying this one verses the 40 dollar one you have also been looking at. Buy the 40 dollar one first and in a few months when it dies, come back and buy this one. But if you want to save yourself time and money then make the jump and buy the Braun 7281 you won't regret it.

Also if you aren't familiar with how to use and epilator read the instructions it doesn't work like a razor and if you use it like a razor it will hurt. I feel it is the only reason people would complain about this epilator.

title: My Hair Feels Alive!
text:
First impression review:

A reducer was added to the bottle to prevent accidental over-pouring, so now you can shake it to get a few drops out and don't need to worry about over-pouring and losing product.

I used to have a handlebar 'stache and long goatee, and would use a product called the beard "jelly" (halfway between balm and oil) by Bossman which was quite effective. I shaved them off, yet would still use a little bit of that stuff on my head hair before applying pomade as the two seem to work together well, the jelly almost functioning as a pre-styler. Once I tried the Outlaw Soaps Magic Elixir, however, I realized that it does much more for my head hair than the jelly was doing. It instantaneously tamed my curly-wavy hair, but working *with* the curls in a way that mirrored how I style my hair anyway -- it actually felt "magical." Also, it stood in for itself without me needing to use any additional product (was on my way to hot yoga and didn't want pomade liquefying and pouring over my face). Also, the smell, like all Outlaw stuff, is intoxicating and legitimate aromatherapy -- the manly, woody, nutty scent put a smile on my face. Also, it's subtle and can act as a "base" for other Outlaw products such as their solid colognes and hopefully the upcoming DEODORANTS! (While the scent has it's own woody character, it seems to provide a foundation whence you can take off either in a "woodsy" or a warm, bourbon-ey direction.)

These guys are artists -- the impeccable harmonic synthesis between quality/effectiveness and out-of-this-world scents that they've achieved sells itself. In fact, when somebody wonders what it means for a product to "sell itself," Outlaw Soaps, for the most part, is the definitive example.

title: Interesting idea ... smells great. Cheap packaging.
text:
At first, I was a bit skeptical about baby cologne. The act of spraying down your smelly little bundle of joy with cologne seems a bit weird. Are babies supposed to smell like anything but babies? So, we actually bought this spray for us, figuring the ingredients would be healthier if it was meant for youngsters. This does smell pretty darn good!

When the bottle arrived, it came capless in an envelope. The bottle feels like very lightweight plastic and cheap. Not sure why they did not go with a thicker plastic or even glass given the price point of this being not exactly on the cheap side. The packaging does not match the price or quality.

I wanted the white blossom/citrus version, which was unavailable and worried lavender would be cloyingly sweet and feminine. A few squirts from the bottle and my fears were gone ... this leans more towards feminine but could be worn by a man as well. The note I smell most is orange blossom followed by a faint lavender. It is fresh and captivating and I do get the mediterranean influence ... it smells like Spring on the Amalfi Coast. It's classy and well balanced ... I am a huge fan of colognes/perfumes and have lots of the high end Creed, Aqua di Parma, etc. and while you'll never mistake this for a luxury scent, it's better than a lot of the cheaper colognes and perfumes.

I wish I could tell you how babies like it, but mostly my 40 year old girlfriend wears this. It's a splash she puts on after the shower or before heading out when she wants something not as strong or distinctive as perfume. This doesn't last a long time ... maybe an hour or two. Nor does it project incredibly well ... it sits close to the skin. But for the price and how refined it is, it's worth keeping in your overnight bag or gym locker.

The ingredients seem to be similar to a normal eau de cologne. I am not sure I'd spritz down an infant with this too often ... but it seems to be a slightly scaled down version of bottled perfume. It still contains alcohol as the first ingredient but feels lighter on the skin.

Overall, despite the cheap packaging, this is a nice light scent that is good for adults and probably kids. Orange blossom is one of my favorite smells and it's high on the list of basenotes here. I'd recommend keeping a bottle of this on hand for a quick refreshing spritzdown. It smells nice and seems high quality.

title: I am a new fan!!! Love, love, love this straightener.
text:
Okay, this might be a long review but I hope it helps!
Back in the mid 2000’s, when the Chi was selling like hot pancakes, I had such a hard time finding one available, that one day I ended up buying a Paul Mitchell iron. I fell in love with it and never again tried to buy a Chi. After 13 years of using my PM, it finally started having issues with the electrical cord. My sweet husband, seeing how much I was struggling to flat iron my hair, got on Amazon and bought me this Titanium hair straightener. I didn’t want to stop using my Paul Mitchell (was kinda sentimental about it), but I finally put it away and gave this one a try... BEST decision ever!!!! I hadn’t realized how long it actually would take my old straightener to do the job. I though 20-30 minutes straightening my hair was normal. This titanium iron is the real deal. I have super long (almost to my waist), medium thickness hair. Not thin, not coarse... but if I don’t flat iron it, I look like a lion on a bad hair day. Very frizzy. This iron heats up so quickly and it goes up to 450F. I have seriously straightened my whole hair in less than 15 minutes. More like 10 minutes. A little more if I want to flip it and curl the ends. I seriously love this titanium straightener. And no, I didn’t get the product for free just to review it. Like I said, my husband did his homework researching and bought me this for my birthday.

The only thing that I would suggest is that you might have to wear a heat glove if you are using it to curl your hair, since the outside of the plates does get hot, and when you use it to curl, you have to grab the hot end.

Anyway.. I hope it last 13 years or more like my old straightener!

It is also very easy to maintain--we were able to brush through it with a paddle brush no problem and it was so silky and smooth.

The only issue was that the clip would not stay on my daughter's clothing. You have to clip it vertically in order for the colors to show the way they do and for it to look like a tail. If you clip it horizontally, it looks weird. Our fix for this was really easy. My daughter had a belt that had a two hole pattern that went all the way around the belt--I was able to clip the top two prongs of the hair clip into her belt and it stayed perfectly. She put it on and twirled about and was shaking it all over the place and it didn't budge. So, I recommend doing something similar if you want it to stay in place and to have have to work about it falling off or getting caught on something and pulling off.

For Example, 5 Volts Input Minus 3.4 Volts LED = 1.6,  1.6 Divided into LED 0.020 Milliamps = 80,  So in this case You would need an 80 Ohm Resistor if you were going to power this LED with 5 Volts.

text:
So far, so good! I've got very sensitive skin & this is great.

My routine:
1. Wash with 'cleansing water'. (Soaps are too much.. even sensitive ones!)
2. Wet my skin. Make sure it's dripping wet. Don't skip this step!
3. Squeeze a little hyaluronic acid onto your fingers and rub around your wet face.
4. Let it dry.
5. To finish, smooth lotion or oil (whatever you prefer) on top of your now-dry face.

This gives the hyaluronic acid moisture & locks it in. You'll love it! You can even do this at night as well.

NOTE:
This is not magic. It will not repair years of sun damage or neglect to your skin. However, if you take care of yourself & take care of your skin, this will really help with your crows feet or frown lines or general wrinkles that we all get as our skin ages.

Enjoy! Don't expect miracles... but take care of yourself and take care of your skin. Plus, this is vegan. Hooray! You can nourish your skin without hurting animals. I'm nearing 40 and this is really helping my crows feet & fairly-large frown lines.

The gaps on the finger clippers are more prominent, and I always get the white spots on all of my fingers. I'm not the type of guy who gets manicures, so I just want to do clean, even clips and be done, and not spend time filing if I already did a good, even cut...but I know women are particular about nails, so it bothers me that they may notice these white spots if I don't take the time to get rid of all of them.

I took a guess and let it sit for one hour. I applied a line of the gel over the threshold of the shower where the door seal sits. This area often accumulates mold. The smell is not as strong as other cleaning solutions I have used, but there is a light chemical smell. It comes with a pair of disposable gloves but I did not use them. Since it is a gel it is fairly easy to handle without making a mess. After one hour I wiped it clean with a damp cloth. On the tile it works about the same as soap and water. It still required some scrubbing in certain areas. On the door seal it performed much better. The areas where the gel was applied cleared up not only the mold, but also the soap scum which would not wipe away with just the wet cloth alone. Overall it seems to work fairly well, but it is hard to say how well with no instructions provided. It may take some trial and error to maximize the performance of the gel.

title: Nothing spectacular. I have received more... for this price.
text:
This Hair Removal Device by Ulike just as well as a couple of other IPL devices I have that cost much less. It comes packaged nicely, though I kept trying to open the flat two-sided green piece that covers the accessory side. It doesn't open.
The device does look quite fancy, and I was interested in skin rejuvenation, which is in one of the photos (that is mentioned in the other listing that shows this exact same device). The instruction booklet contains about as much as the empty listing page that I ordered it from. That page has no bullet points, only one photo.
They do have another listing for this same exact device, showing the accessories, extra photos with bits of information, and bullet points telling a little about it. I got my information from there.
The device does have the cooling feature, as many others do, which helps it not to zap too badly. It also comes with a razor and eye protection.
What it lacks, that many others include that are in or around this price range, is more attachments for the device. There needs to be at least one smaller light head for use around the lip area, as it's very hard to use the main one with the device being so large.
This IPL device works pretty much as well as any other, with none having the ability to make you completely hair-free at any point in the future. As far as the studies that I have seen, with diligent use, home IPL devices can only offer a little better than 50-60%-ish less hair.
My preferred device, which costs very little more than this one, has several attachments, including some specifically for skin rejuvenation. You do get a fancy box with this device, and it looks nice, but I don't think it provides any more or less than devices that cost much less.
I haven't found one yet that really only takes 10 minutes to do your legs, but if I ever do, that is the one that would probably take the cake! If you like fancy boxes and a sleek-looking device, I would recommend this one.

title: High quality, great colors and right size
text:
I received this product at discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.

This is the second set of hair clips I bought from Shemay and I am very pleased that this set is as high quality as the first one. The clips came in a zip-lock bag on the scheduled delivery date. The colors and patterns are exactly the same as the picture shown. The alligator clips are hot-glued on the bows.

Here are the reasons for my 5-star rating:

# I found glue leftover or unclear-cut ribbon on hair clips sold by other sellers, this product does not have that issue. The ribbons are securely attached to the clips and I didn’t see any fraying one. They are well-made.

# I like that they are NOT single solid color clips but a mixture of two colors. My daughter has dark hair so I do not put dark color clips such as black, brown, navy or dark green on her. Also, the color white is for funeral in my culture so I don’t put white, ivory or beige on her either.
Very often I see solid color hair clip sets that have the perfect size and good price and I really like to buy them, but I know I am not going to use at least one-third of them. I end up keep looking on the market or bought them anyway yet gave away those colors to friends who have lighter color hair or who do not have the cultural believes.
I am glad that this is not the case and this set fits my need.

# They are the right size for my daughter. She is only 14 months old now and is really tiny. Big ribbon bows are just not matched to her size. I found that she gets more compliment when wearing tiny hair bows than wearing bigger ones.

Bottom line:
I am very happy with this high quality hair clips and I think I will buy a second set in the near future to make pigtails for my daughter.

title: Not a bad set!
text:
One star removed because of the limited sizes, packaging the adhesive tabs, the odd number of nails included, and the fact that I think the transparent nails would probably look better with a white background instead.

These nails came in 10 sizes - 0 to 9. Other brands will usually come with more (smaller) sizes. I do have small hands, so this might not be a problem for most folks. For my pinky, I had to file the size 9s to fit.

One of the two sheets of adhesives came a bit crumpled. Though I didn't use the tabs - I use liquid, which wasn't included - I still think it's important to package everything a bit more carefully.

As for the odd number of nails, not every size came in a pair. I believe size 4 had only one nail, and 7 had three.

After applying, I do think a white background, rather than transparent, would have looked great. But, it's up to you. I would have painted the well side with a white gel polish or acrylic paint first, if I wanted to try again.

Application was pretty standard, nothing out of the ordinary. They're a bit thin, and flexible, making them easier to shape around more curved or flat nail beds. Despite how thin they are, they still feel sturdy. And because they are transparent, it's important to make sure ALL bubbles are gone if using liquid glue. I feel the tabs would be very visible, so glue is probably the best option. The length is great as well, these would probably be considered medium-long in typical drugstore brands.

Also, please note that these are more of a burgundy color, not red as shown.

Anything that keeps me from shaving is a plus.
There is a bit of "pain" like needle pricks but after repeated use, it gets less noticeable. There is a precision guard that also helps buffer a bit. The cord is annoyingly clunky. Not sure why it's so bulky. There isn't an on/off. Unplug when you're done. It's a bit large for travel, especially if you're keeping it in the box. No glasses, surprisingly. Some small improvements would definitely make this a 5 star review for me but certainly not a deal breaker. High 4 stars for performance and ease of use.

first review:

My specific need for this shampoo was try to help with extreme stress induced hair shed. The brand promises to "stimulate keratinocytes for renewed hair growth", and there were some anecdotal reports of it helping with hair loss I found in my research, so I gave it a try. I've been using it for a little over a month now, twice a week, and cannot definitely see any difference it might be making in my hair regrowth. It didn't prevent any further hair shedding though. My hair keeps falling out at about the same rate it did.

The positive is that the shampoo didn't seem to do any further damage either. It does produce a thickened look. My hair is naturally fine and even in its best days i could hardly get any volume at the root. This seems to be helping with the texture and fuller appearance. I would not call the effect "silky", as the thickening effect is achieved by making the hair coarser than my natural state. This means i have to be extra diligent with my conditioner to aid smoother results along the entire length. Oh, and it also tangles quite a bit in the shower.

All in all, I think my search for hair regrowth solution continues.
