title: 3.5 stars
text:
Philips Norelco Arcitec 1090 is my first electric shaver ever and I've been using it for 7 months now. I had been pondering on whether to take Brown Pulsonic or Philips Norelco for quite a while, when ultimately it was probably the looks of the latter that prevailed so I ended up with it.

All in all it is a pretty good shaver, but not great. Perhaps I should start off with mentioning that I am NOT one of those with a thick and bushy beard, so I usually shave every other day. Normally I spend about 5 mins on shaving. At times my skin gets slightly irritated, which might result in light-red patches under my chin. Most of the time it's fine though, and I can get a decent shave. However, not always is the shave that clean. Sometimes certain hairs (esp. on the side - around my jaw and around my whiskers, or under my chin) will be left out, so I'd have to trim them separately with the trimmer.

Oh yes, the infamous trimmer. It really is more of an aesthetic feature on the shaver than a tool serving its real purpose. It's just too small and inconvenient. At times I'm having difficulties accessing parts of my face with it, unless I took off the shaving heads.

The shaver also comes with a neat LED display that shows how many minutes of shaving time there is remaining. Great. This was one of the features that won me over about this shaver. But what I resent is that it's inaccurate. Well it does accurately show how many minutes you have shaved, but when it comes down to 0 mins, one would expect the battery is about to die, yet usually I can still squeeze several shaves out of it (which means additional 10-15 mins). In the instructions manual it says that after 3 charges it should display the remaining shaving time accurately, but I've already charged it at least 5 times now, and no difference. The highest shaving time is supposedly 65 mins. What is rather curious about all this is that on each charge I've actually been gaining additional minutes to the proposed 65 mins, so the numbers have gotten up to 81 mins on my most recent charge. I would be perfectly happy with getting those additional minutes if that means that the shaver will eventually display the time properly so that if 0 mins is remaining, then 0 it really is. (Perhaps once I've have charged it 10 or more times the display will finally get normal, as suggested in the manual? If it does, I might as well mention it here.)

Anyway, speaking of the battery, this is one of the features I am really content with. I can get numerous shaves out of one charge; therefore, there's nothing but praise on this part.

I also like the fact that the shaver is easy to wash. You simply open the shaving heads and rinse it.

One thing that I as well dislike though, is the On/Off button's silver paint peeling off already after only a couple of weeks' use. But alright, that's already going into details now.

Pros:
- attractive looks
- long battery life
- light and not too loud
- easy to wash

Cons:
- trimmer
- doesn't always shave ALL the hairs clean
- sort of inaccurate LED display
- paint peeling off of the On/Off button

If I could, I would give this shaver 3.5 stars. However, for a 4, I guess it will still at least have to get the LED display straight. So if after 10 or so charges it does, then I am giving it a 4. We shall see.

The information on the pamphlet that came with the eye drops was interesting; it stated one ingredient keeps the eye moist, it is naturally found in the eye, body. Another ingredient is a vitamin that doctors use to help the cornea... heal.
So I figured these might be good for pollen, mold exposure allergy increased by airplane fumes (low flying jets that go to the airport over my apartment.) and 2 other chemicals in our air; neighbors e-cigarette and drug pipe vaping fumes and laundry mat constant white cloud blowing out into the air, into our apartments; bleach, chemical soaps...

Many of my neighbors have the same uncomfortable feeling. Increased in spring, late fall by certain pollens. We live next to a marsh.

I been taught by natural eye doctors to avoid eye drops. But; for the first time in my life I thought I might try these until my eyes, nose get used to the air here (if that is possible), or I am able to move.

The drops felt nice the first night; but next day I had extreme dry eyes, dizzyish, crawly kind of feeling in head, sinus. Then much itching! I was walking to the store and on the way sniffled. The itching seemed to spread from the eyes tear drainage system into the nose and up into the sinus by the nose/eyes and forehead. Awful strange, strong itching.
Next day (I never took the drops again, have thrown them away); the eyes are very soar and sinus has extreme pressure, crawling feeling and pain. I think the eye drops caused the pollen, mold, chemicals to flow through from the eye-tear drainage tube into the nose, then up the sinus when I was sniffling in the rain yesterday. Today pain still bad but itching less. Following day two; no drops for 3rd day; pain, itching less. Pain gone after days no eye drops. Went back to using humidifier.

Maybe the drops are good for other conditions a doctor might apply for. I do not know. I definitely have decided to go back to my usual use of a steam humidifier, natural food, natural methods, natural medical and eye, nutrition doctors advice. And to keep looking a for a better place to live. After 2 moves in last 3 years; I think this time I know how to avoid a bad real estate deal.

Eye doctor, driving test recently says eyes, eyesight is very good. But got allergy to whatever is in the air. And the air’s chemicals can cause dry eyes.

These eye drops definitely do not work in certain situations, and can make a eye, sinus pollen, mold.., allergy... worse.

title: Won't Compete with Norelco Triple it's Styled Like
text:
UPDATE: This does get a little better with use, or I got a little more used to using it, or a little of both. My Norelco is a little old and needs a new switch. I use the Rozia most of the time now when I shave. I dump the whiskers out every time I shave. The assembly that mounts the shaving heads will come loose from the driving assembly that is the lower half of the shaving head replacement part. It then has to be reconnected to the little metal hinge and latched. That's slightly difficult to get right.

It's competent but misses many improvements incorporated into more expensive razors twenty years ago. The Norelco that this one looks like has a suspension system with integrally spring damped "driveshafts" connecting each head to the motor(s). That keeps the heads in contact with your face more effectively, making shaving quicker. This one lacks that important advance and seems a little inept in comparison. My Norelco has a broader range of head flexion. At rest the Norelco's three heads form a more convex shape together. When pressed inward against a face there is also more deeper (concave) movement allowed.

The heads on the shaver being reviewed seem to pull on my whiskers when shaving around mouth and chin. I suspect the slots aren't as rounded at the ends, rather coming to a point where a whisker catches. There is no sensitivity setting as well. But it works. I will use it occasionally and keep it as a backup. If I didn't know that better equipment exists I might be more satisfied with it's shortcomings. Of course the better equipment does cost four times or more the price of this one.

title: Color, ingredients
text:
The frosted glass looks good. The color of the plastic and silicone parts is darker than in photos, though. Judging from the website it's supposed to be off-white, actually called "classic linen," but the ones they sent out seem to be more beige. If that doesn't suit, there's also a "midnight blue" color available, which is a sort of medium gray blue judging from the photos (which may or may not be reliable).

Or you can take the silicone skirt off this--it's made so it's removable, good for occasional cleaning--and replace the push top with whatever color you want. It's a standard size. I think it looks better without the skirt even with the beige top. Just be careful not to break the bottle. It feels pretty sturdy.

The scent of the soap is lavender with citrus. (Not coconut--that's in the photo because it's where some of the saponified oil comes from.)

It washes well, doesn't leave any noticeable residue for me, though I suppose the aloe juice is intended to moisturize some.

It comes oddly over-packaged but in cardboard that can be recycled or biodegraded.

The ingredients given at the website are:

Saponified coconut oil, saponified olive oil, potassium soap, aloe juice, citric acid, sodium chloride (table salt), natural essential oil blend, vitamin E.

It's not clear why potassium soap is listed separately from the saponified oils, since that's what potassium soap is, oils turned into soap by the addition of potassium hydroxide (potash).

title: STICKY SITUATION
text:
When I first received the item I was pretty excited. Tried opening it out of the outer plastic bag, but it was sticky. I thought it might have been a leak, and sure enough the product had sticky goo all over the cardboard packaging. It was pretty bad even for a leak, so I examined it over the sink, but then realized the ENTIRE top half of the spirit gum adhesive bottle had broken off and half the glue was filling the clear plastic cover attached to the cardboard.

At this point I was worried about glass cuts but I tried to salvage what remained of the glue. Using a scissor, I tried extracting the glue remover so at least I can use it to clean up all the stickiness resulting from the sticky situation. When I cut the packaging open, all the glue started dripping out into the sink. Long story short, the glue got everywhere and it was a mess cleaning up because THE REMOVER DIDN'T WORK EITHER! As there was a lot of glue, I also applied the remover liberally, including pouring out enough to cover my hand and soaking a cloth to scrape with. I had to later resort to using citric acid using lemons and that seemed to work better but still tough to remove.

I considered buying a new one but at that point I really didn't think it was worth it given my experience. All in all it took maybe 2 hours to clean up, and to begin with I have an extreme dislike for sticky substances on my hands.

title: Review of 51S foil and cutter for Braun shaver
text: Just my .2 cents. I have a Braun model #8985 Series 5. After a year of satisfactory use, I thought I should replace the foil and cutters. I got the one recommended for my shaver, the 51S. I started to use it, and after just a few shaves, I noticed the shaves were not as smooth, and more irritation to my face, than I was getting with my original shaver I had for the past year. Now just after a few shaves, I noticed my cutter was starting to dull. I stuck with it a few more months, and then I started looking for a better cutting block for it. I came on Amazon and read some reviews, and there were many satisfied users of the 30B kit. . I even called Braun, and told them my situation, and asked if I could change over to the 30B, instead of staying with the 51S. NO WAY said the rep, use only the cartridge recommended by Braun, the 51S. Well, I decided otherwise, and went to "Target", and got the 30B replacement foil and cutter. Boy, what a difference. It fits right in, no problem with the foil or the cutter fitting, I even like the foil better than the 51S, seems to roll over my fact smoother. The shaves seem so much better. Now to be honest, I have not used the razor much yet, but I'll get back to you with my thoughts when I do. On my #8985 there is a light that comes on, and it says "change foil", which came on right then when I changed the foil over to the 30B, it lite up. There is a reset button right there, and if you push it with a pen or pencil point, the light goes out after blinking a few times. Maybe the 30B is the way to go, and the 30B is about $15 cheaper than the 51S. I don't know what Braun is doing, but it is not making me buy a new Braun. If I get upset with their shaver, I'm not going to buy a new Braun, I will switch brands. Hate to say this folks, but every manufacturer out there is trying to rip us off today! Regards, TC

title: The good and bad about Easy Feet
text:
My Easy Feet $14.95 purchased on their site (EZ Feet site) (buy one and receive one free plus "handling" and postage) cost a total of $30.97 (with their handling fees) shipped to the house, with their standard slow delivery which I approved. The good: EZ Feet seems very well constructed for what it has, and so far the bristles are holding up for me (owned for 2 weeks now). EZ Feet cleans MOST of the bottom of your foot and in between the toes, satisfactorily. With my size 12 foot, the REAR bottom of the foot is rather hard to clean with the EZ feet.

The bad: (as I see it) is that the EZ Feet doesn't clean any of the sides of your foot, being there's no bristles on the side, only on the bottom and the front part of the foot. I can't push my foot in far enough to get the rear BOTTOM of my size 12 foot. I have to wash most the top of my foot and all the sides of the foot after using the EZ Feet. It is easier cleaning my foot with the EZ Feet unit, ultimately.

EZ feet should positively add side bristles so the sides of the foot can be washed, and a larger footprint (or raise the top bristle armband slightly) so as to allow larger feet to clean the REAR bottom of the foot.

title: The coverage is pretty darn thick
text:
The coverage is pretty darn thick, definitely for people who are into normal to heavier coverage. It has a sort of matte but moist finish, which I really like because it lends a nice glow to my skin, and definitely lasts all day - huge staying power. It does slide into my fine lines, and does not really have many pore-filling qualities. It will minimize pores at first, like right after you finish applying, bu by the end of the day your pores will be rather obvious. BUT, in pictures your skin will look flawless and fairly matte regardless of how odd it looks up close in person! So at least you'll always look on point in pictures, and as long as nobody stares too closely. The product has also been a little pore clogging for me, but I find that it's somewhat manageable with dedication to a skincare routine.

The cushion inside does dry out a little faster than one would expect, but that is probably also because of the product being thicker than most cushion compacts. The puff applicator is so pleasant and soft to touch, but for me it also deposits way too much product onto my skin. I always have to go back with a beauty blender and try to make the coverage thinner, because when I don't the product looks SUPER cakey.

As for the sun protection purpose, it works pretty well, and is convenient for when traveling or running errands on a sunny day, if you're like me and like to carry a cushion around in order to reapply throughout the day. However, as I said the product can, and consistently has, been cakey when applied with the puff that comes with it, and is already a rather thick/borderline cakey. So even though it's supposed to be convenient, it's also a little counter intuitive.

title: Cute, Functional and High Quality!
text:
The Choo Choo Stripes Adult Shortall is an amazing, cute, functional product from Baby Pants! I bought these as a birthday present to myself a year ago and they have held up very well through play and washings. After looking at the sizing chart on the website I had originally ordered a medium, but had to exchange them for a large because even at the lowest shoulder strap length they were too tight around the waist and too short on my legs. I had to cover the 25% restocking fee and return shipping, but Baby Pants was very professional, and quick in processing my exchange. That being said, I would consider choosing the larger size if you're on the fence about what size to order.

I agree with LollyLaLaz's comments in her review about the Baby Pants patch logo on the back and recently decided to remove it myself so that I would feel comfortable when discretely wearing these in public. This is a common feature in the few Baby Pants products that I've bought, but it is very easy to remove without damaging the fabric.

There are six snaps in the crotch and three on each side by the pockets, each labeled with the Baby Pants logo. These logos on the snaps are a nice touch and are not noticeable unless seen up close. Also, the five pockets are deep and functional as well.

Overall, I would definitely recommend these to anyone considering buying these super cute, childish, practical shortalls! Enjoy!!

title: I'm not seeing it
text:
These are essentially giant temporary tattoos very similar to the ones you sometimes get as novelty gifts and promotional material.
Like those, you simply peel off the protective cover, press the design where you want it, then wet the back of the paper holding the tattoo, until it transfers to your skin.
Rubbing alcohol helps wipe the tattoo off, if wear and tear and sweat don't take it out first.

The reasons I personally did not care for these:
- A lot less vivid on my skin, than in photos or against the paper
- There is no precut opening for your mouth; FYI, you get the best result cutting (carefully) an opening after you put the tattoo on, not before
- Very difficult to line up with your own mouth
- If you wear these over your mouth, the activity of talking, drinking, eating, etc... rapidly degrades the tattoo, causing wrinkles, gaps, tears, etc...

In my opinion, the best use of these temporary tattoos would be to create the illusion of a fake mouth somewhere else on you body, like your tummy, neck, back, hand, etc...
Honestly, I was just really disappointed with these all around.

title: I tested this controversy
text:
SEE BOTTOM FOR MY UPDATE: Is the 51s foil and cutter really terrible? Is the 30B foil and cutter really better for your Braun Series 8000 shaver? Is there an Original Equipment foil and cutter still available for the Braun 8985 shaver? Answers: no, no, and no. I have the Braun 8985 shaver and bought BOTH of the foils and cutters mentioned in these reviews: the 51s, which Braun sells as its only replacement now for the 8000 series, and the 30b, which is supposed to be for the Braun 7000/4000 series shavers, but some buyers are saying it works better for the 8000 series shavers than the so-called "terrible" 51s replacement. Both foils and cutters fit my 8985 shavers, and I've shaved serveral times with both. The 51s does NOT pull, cut or irritate my face and gives a very close shave, particularly if I have a 2-day beard. The 30b also gives a good shave, but perhaps not quite as close. Some reviewers say the 51s wears out quickly, is prone to dents and starts irritating your face. If that happens, I will update this review, but so far, so good.

I ordered the 51s by mistake because the seller's web listing did not mention that its "Braun 8000 360 Complete Foil and Cutter Block for Models 8995, 8985 and 8975" is really the controversial 51s replacement. When it arrived with the dreaded 51s name on the package, I immediately ordered the 30b foil and cutter and planned to return the 51s, but I waited until the 30b arrived so I could be sure it worked. It does, but it buzzes differently and didn't shave much closer than my 3-year-old original foil and cutter. The 30b DOES give a more comfortable shave -- it glides over your face like nothing is happening. The shave is fine, what you'd expect from any electric. But Braun is better than "any electric." The 51s is giving me that exceptionally close shave I expect from Braun. You DO feel the 51s a bit more than the 30b, but it's not irritating. I am keeping the 30b in case my 51s goes haywire on me, but for now, the 51s seems better.

UPDATE May 6, 2012: I'm glad I kept the 30b because the 51s did indeed start inflicting red marks on my face, and it stopped shaving as closely. Very disappointing. So now I'm using the 30b, the red marks on my face are gone, and the shave is close. So if I had it to do all over again, I would recommend getting tthe 30b foil and cutter instead of the 51s.

title: Mitchell's Wool Fat Shaving Soap
text:
I have been using this soap for the last few months and I love it. This soap produces a rich lather and I never need to reload my brush for subsequent passes. This soap takes a lot of water to thin out (which seems to be a common characteristic of good shave soaps). The soap has a soapy scent which some people like or don't like, but it smells good to me. It doesn't seem too strong of a scent to me either, but some people think it does based off of what I have read about it before I bought it. Even if you think the scent is strong, it doesn't seem to linger like Tobac does, but provides as good of a lather.

Perhaps the greatest characteristic of this soap (at least boasted by the brand) is that it is made using wool fat, which has lanolin. Lanolin is a wax secreted by sheep (and I guess other "woolly" animals) that helps protect the animals skin and wool from the environment and is often added to soaps (among other things) as a moisturizer. That being said, I don't really notice any huge difference in moisturizing, but I don't have really dry skin either. So, who knows? I can't tell you whether or not it will help you with dryness, but it works well for me and may work well for you too.

If you have dry or sensitive skin, I would recommend looking for a review written by someone who also has dry or sensitive skin. Even though the company boasts the qualities of lanolin, there are other ingredients that may be a problem for you (maybe even the lanolin itself).

title: Order Ahead~
text:
The good:

Packaging is very much discreet, and inside the box was another pretty box. They sent it to me in a little black box, with some really pretty tissue paper around the jar. And a little business card.
Speaking of the jar, that's discreet, too. The label peels right off, leaving you with a simple black jar with a silver lid. The cream is filled to the TOP of the container, and it smells so wonderfully of vanilla.
Without the label, it can easily pass for any kind of body/face cream on the market.

Applying it, you really do only need a little bit, like a fingertip's worth. It's very creamy at first, and even with only a small amount it looks like you used way too much with the way it just spreads out, and then it feels and looks very oily before finally absorbing. Now I understand why 4oz is sufficient for a month supply.

I might edit in later on to share any results, seeing as there aren't any other reviews on it at all... Presuming anyone requests it anyway. (No sense wasting the time writing it up here if no one cares to know. ;p)
Their site says you can 'see results' within 2 weeks, but we all know how much that varies from person to person. However, it has Pueraria Mirifica in it, and that stuff is strong, so who knows how fast it'll work.

The bad: Delivery.

There is no "fast" option - when you order it, your only option is 5-8 days.
I placed this order July 6, on a Saturday, and it was expected to go out the following Monday or Tuesday.
It "left the facility" on Wednesday, July 10th.
It was expected to arrive between Thursday, July 11 - Tuesday, July 16.
It finally got to my post office July 18th.

Considering that I had to PAY for the shipping, unlike a good 95% of my orders on Amazon, I can't say I'm impressed with the seller's delivery speed. Of course, I don't know if their shipping is always like this, either, and it was only 2 days off of the estimated date, which is why I only docked 1 star. But for future orders through them, I will order a week or two ahead of time -- just in case -- and I suggest you do the same.

********

ETA: Second time around it arrived one week later on the dot. I ordered it on the 7th (with a new shipping option of 3-5 days) and it arrived on the 14th. No business card this time (maybe because I've bought from them before?) but it arrived in the same pretty box with the same pretty tissue paper.

title: OK, but outperformed by a $10 foil electric
text:
I got this shaver in early January of 2007. For the first month or so that I had it, it worked decently. The shave was relatively close and it did get most of the hair, but it did take a few passes over the skin, and a touch-up using the on-board trimmer to get the ones it missed. I also found myself having the stretch the skin quite a bit to get a close enough shave. However, it did offer an irritation-free shave (I have sensitive skin, thus why I stay away from blade razors).

Over the next few months, though, I noticed that the shave started to get more irritating: more 'pulling' instead of cutting (had always pulled a little, but got more frequent), takes more passes to cut what it once would, etc. I changed the blades after 3 months (short period, yes, but I tried anyway). It helped a little, but it still wasn't as good as it once was. Then, I started to realize that the shaver wasn't holding as strong a charge as it once did. It would come off the charger and be 'full power' for less than one shave, and would need to go back on the charger after 6 shaves (far less than the advertised two weeks). A call to Norelco led nowhere, as they said it was 'expected' for the battery to wear down over time (4 months?).

I kept using the razor as I wasn't about to waste the $90 investment. On a trip in late July, I had forgotten to pack the shaver, so I purchased a $10 Remington battery-operated foil razor at a local convenience store. Sad to say, but from Day 1 that foil razor has outperformed the Norelco by leaps and bounds in all areas (closer shave, gets all areas better, less passes needed, etc.). Also on a sad note, the Remington is kicking the bucket (a year later), and I am forced to go back to the Norelco for the time being while I look for an acceptable foil shaver as a replacement.

In short, this razor performed decently at first, but it seems as though compared to a $10 battery operated razor, this $70 shaver isn't a good value for the investment.

This hook is perfect for a smaller towel or even a larger body towel, I like that I'm able to dry my towels off and continue using them until they are ready to be washed. The hook looks great in my bathroom and matches my already placed decor, the stainless steel is polished and sleek giving my bathroom modern accents. The representative was very polite and helpful,and I explained the problem,and admitted to having lost the receipt,and he STILL said that they're replace it right away,if I would agree to send the broken one to them promptly,postage prepaid by THEM. The new razor arrived in a sealed new package,like they have at the store,and they also sent a postage paid label,and instructions to send the old razor and all accessories and a copy of the invoice in the box the new one came in,and I could then just put it in any UPS drop box to mail it.
I would buy Norelco again,ANYTIME!

text:
I was given the opportunity to review Keeva's tee tree oil shampoo and fell in love with it right after first use. I wasn't around to when they were selecting reviewers for their conditioner but now that it's available for purchase I'm glade to say I've bought it for full sale price being 20 USD. Like it's shampoo counterpart the bottle is 28oz total.

Texture: White and creamy
Scent: Pleasant and definitely not reeking of tea tree oil like it's shampoo sister
Slip: Slip is a product's ability to allow one to detangle hair effectively and not need to use too much product to do so. For the amount I used which is pretty standard across the board with all conditioners I've tried, this conditioner is rated at 5/5 for slip
Moisture: Next to none but that isn't a real issue due to most of the oils being found in Keeva's tea tree oil shampoo
Standout Ingredients: hydrolyzed keratin ( protein ), argania spinose ( Moroccan argon oil ), cetearyl alchol ( fatty alcohol )

Cons:
Cocos nucifera ( Coconut Oil ) isn't listed as an ingredient, however it is featured as an ingredient on the front of the bottle.
Melaleuca alternifolia ( Tea Tree Oil ) isn't listed as an ingredient either.
Both of these oils is on the front of the bottle being featured however, the product doesn't list the oils as ingredients.

Overall, I believe this to be a quality conditioner even better than some brands found in salons. Price of the bottle is reasonable for the quantity received. This conditioner does provide one with good slip and it doesn't leave hair feeling heavy or weighted down after rinsing. I feel that when used with it's sister shampoo, you'll benefit from this conditioner most .

title: Ni-Cad battery dooms it
text:
I really wanted to love this trimmer. Especially given the hefty price tag. It trims as you would expect and the vacuum works well and is a must-have feature in my opinion.

Another must have feature is either Ni-Mh battery or the more expensive Lithium ion battery. This has Neither it is the bad/cheapo/old Ni-Cad (Nickel Cadmium) with all the memory effects and shortened life span that implies. For a device like this where you can't swap the battery yourself and you can't leave the job half done you will have to partially charge and then finish your trim. Then you will recharge it fully, boom instant battery memory and shortened life. Or maybe you re-charge it after every use? That may be even worse... I've been through this before, you are doomed to a useful life measured in months before the battery (and therefore the whole trimmer) craps out.

I researched on line and couldn't discover what type of battery it was so I went in person to my local WM and looked at the packaging, still no hint. So I bought it thinking they couldn't possibly sell it at such a high price point with such an unsuitable battery.

I got it home and found in the instructions that the battery is Ni-Cad and soldered into place and must be disposed of properly. I'll be returning it and looking for a different vacuum trimmer with a battery that will be useful for longer than a few months.

title: Great metallic nail polishes
text:
I just got these and had to test out most of the colors right away. This was my first time using any Kleancolor polishes so I had no idea what to expect. I was very pleasantly surprised on the quality. For polishes that came to less than $1 each, they cover very well with just one coat. Usually with polishes that inexpensive they are very thin/sheer and don't cover well, which is not the case at all with these.

I knew that not all the colors were going to be to my taste/ones I would actually use (just a preference thing) but I'm happy with the majority of them. Some were better than I had hoped they would be once I tried them out. (They look better on your nails than in the bottle.)

The white metallic doesn't seem very metallic to me and that was the only one that seemed too thick like it was an old bottle. It might be better going over another color than by itself, or maybe that one bottle was just a bit of a dud. And the black seems fairly flat with very little hint of metallic. The rest are very shiny and metallic, which is just what I was going for. I was really into the Sally Hansen chrome line from years back and still have the ones I bought - but since it's been a long time since I bought those most of them are getting too old/thick. Fortunately, some of these colors seem very close to the ones I had bought back in the day. There is a little bit more of a glitter undertone to most of these compared to the other chrome polishes, but it's not overwhelmingly glittery.

I will say that these polishes have a stronger smell than most polishes I've used but it dissipates pretty quickly.

They also seem to dry pretty quickly as well.

Overall, I'd highly recommend this set to anyone who likes metallic nail polishes. The variety of colors is great and the quality is much better than you'd expect for how much they cost. I can't say yet with regard to how long they can go without chipping. I honestly don't expect it to be long for my fingernails but that's just the case with ALL polishes I find. If they chip within a day or two, then that's just par for the course for fingers. Though I'm too lazy to ever do a topcoat, so maybe it would last longer with a well applied topcoat. I do expect they'd last a good while on toes though since that just seems to be the nature of the beast.

title: The only thing that holds my hair up properly
text:
I have long, very thick hair. My hair breaks heavy-duty ponytail holders regularly. My hair laughs at barrettes and clips. Every time I've had a professional updo for a formal event, the stylist has used multiple dozens of bobby pins to hold my hair in place. And I have never been able to do an updo myself and get it to stay in place, no matter how many bobby pins I use. My hair just spits them out, and the updo falls down. I'd even tried those Magic Grip curved plastic hairpins -- people claimed those held up long hair -- and if anything, they worked worse than regular bobby pins in my hair. (And yes, I used them right, first aiming them out of the bun and then twisting them around to tuck them into the bun.)

So I was skeptical when a friend recommended Spin Pins. I figured they would be another disappointment. But they are BRILLIANT.

It takes four Spin Pins to hold my hair in a bun (the package instructions say to use two, but they're written for people with normal amounts of hair). I literally just screw them into the bun so that they catch some of the hair that lies against my head, along with catching the bun itself. I figured out the best technique by my second try. I promise these aren't complicated to use. The instructions have pictures.

And once they're in, that bun stays until I take them out. I can walk, dance, shake my head around, and the bun will stay perfectly in place. I usually need to use a couple of bobby pins to tuck in a few stray ends here and there, but the Spin Pins hold the weight of my hair -- and believe me, my hair is heavy. I've made buns at the nape of my neck, on the back of my head, and on the top of my head, and all of them stay perfectly in place with these pins.

I've used them regularly for probably a year now, and they haven't bent or broken or anything, despite the large quantities of hair they are forced to hold up.

Don't panic too much about interlocking them (despite the dire package warnings). With four Spin Pins in my hair, they can't help but interlock a bit, but I have never had the slightest problem unscrewing them from my hair again. They also like to interlock in storage, but again, I've never had the slightest problem just unscrewing them from each other again.

I'm glad I was able to get the 3-pack, because now I have a couple of extras in case I lose one.

If you've never been able to get bobby pins to hold your hair up properly, do give Spin Pins a try.

title: My favorite natural fragrance lotion: No Sensitivity problems for me!
text:
It does smell like an orange creamsicle in the best way (yummy!), but if I get a big direct sniff of my hand right after putting it on, it does have the smell reminiscent of eating a really good tangy, fresh apricot, too.

Even some lotions that advertise “natural fragrance,” I have sensitivity to, but this one is no problem! No sneezing, wheezing, or headaches from it. It’s a delicious smell, but not too strong or overpowering, and not fake smelling. The scent subsides quickly after a short bit of time passes, but is still there if you sniff the skin directly. I’ve tried their lavender & lemon coconut (both tend to be favorite scents/scent combos for me when done naturally), and those are nice, but this is my favorite one, unexpectedly.

I normally make my own really moisture intensive thick creams & lotion bars (with beeswax, cocoa butter, shea butter & olive oil.) These I usually apply to my hands every time I wash, because my skin dries out so easily. It keeps cracked hands at bay. This lotion is not a replacement for intensive creams like that.

But this lotion is lovely when I want something that *doesn’t leave my hands feeling greasy*, applies easily, soaks in nicely, & smells good. It’s kinda my “treat myself” lotion. I can also put it out for guests who are used to more traditional lotion consistency, and have them like it, while not being a problem for my breathing. It works great to include in a gift basket, too.

I can’t say this will work for every person with scent sensitivities (and don’t assume it’s okay if someone’s told you no scents...some people have dangerous health reactions to even natural fragrances, among other possible serious concerns that need to be respected), but it is definitely one worth looking into if you are the one with sensitivities, trying to find scents you are okay with. It is 1000 x better than most of the lotions with synthetic fragrances, and even some of the stronger ones that claim natural fragrance.

title: After 1 year of using the product, great traveling shaver
text:
First of all here are some points to put into consideration before buying. This shaver is for...
1. Someone who is looking for a TRAVEL shaver that is small and convenient to carry. It comes with a neat carrying case, and only requires two AA batteries that can be found anywhere. One set of batteries can approx. last up to 20 days/shaves-ish. It will still go on, but I can feel the motor running at lower speed.
2. Someone who prefers WET shaving experience whenever possible. (Wet shaving with this product is great. Dry, not so much.)
3. Someone who needs to shave everyday or simply want that clean shaven look everyday. ( It's still a foil electric shaver, it's fast, efficient, everyday.)
4. Someone who needs his travel shaver to have a trimmer. (Frequent long trip? just like me.)
5. Someone who doesn't want to spend 15 minutes cleaning the shaver. Who wants hassle-free and easy cleaning shaver.

This shaver however isn't for someone who is looking for a blade replacement shaver. I say, wake up, electric shaver will never give you that baby "skin" shave like you get from a proper blade shaving method. However, for $15 this shaver can deliver a very decent shave, very close, but definitely not alike. It also isn't quite for someone who plan to use it 7/365 days. You will probably be better off buying other wet/dry panasonic shaver that is rechargable, and have more than one moving blade, linear-super fast motor and on.

It's been a year and I still use it on every one of my trip. no problem. Impeccable reliability there, and well made.

--------------------

If you decide to buy it, here are my tips and tricks for you. It's based on my experience with it so perhaps it will help you get a better shave with this shaver.
1. YES, it will take up to 2-3 weeks if you are coming from blade for your skin to adjust. This is normal and all you need is patience to get through it.
2. It's miles apart better wet shaver than dry. DO NOT shave dry unless absolute necessary.
3. With that said, all the techniques in wet shaving apply. You should shave in the shower, or right after you come out of it. Your skin should be clean prior to shaving. One trick is that this shaver works better if your shaving gel/foam/cream is "light" or "not dense". Lather up too much or a very dense cream can make the foil/blade hot during operation. (Thick cream will cause more friction and blade moves pretty fast.) Last, don't forget a splash of cold water to seal in and a good aftershave.
4.DO NOT press the shaver, or foil against your skin. You will only get irritation out of it. The trick is to shave everyday, go against the grain, let it GLIDE SLOWLY on your skin, rinse it whenever you feel there is too much foam in the shaver, use trimmer to take out long stubborn hair like those on the neck, and under the chin. DONE.

Thank you for reading my review. I know it's long but this shaver, for $15, deserves a decent review from me imo.

title: A nice, all in one set
text:
Everything in this set is clearly labeled, and most everything that you need is included. (I also used a dish to mix the dye, toothpicks, Q-tips, and some cotton pads.)
Because my eyes are easily irritated, I don't like wearing mascara for more than a couple of hours and started dying my eyelashes. However, this was my first attempt at a lash lift. Let me just say--if I can do it, you can do it!
If you are an expert at this, the directions on the back would probably be enough. I watched a couple of YouTube tutorials and found one where the presenter did this herself, which was very helpful. Because I was doing this to myself, I did one eye at a time, which worked out fine. Also, I didn't want anything too dramatic for my first time, so I used the Medium-1 lift pad; next time I might go a size smaller.
One thing I noticed is that the solution times for this set are longer than some. (Perm/#1--18-20 minutes; Fixation/#2--10-15 minutes; Black Dye/#6+7--25-30 minutes.) Because I didn't want to fry my eyelashes the first time, I didn't leave the solutions on as long. (#1--12 minutes; #2--8 minutes; #6+7--5 to 20 minutes.) One reason I think less time might be okay is that I dyed my first eyelashes just over 20 minutes, but for the second eye I must have gotten the dye a little too close, and my eye became irritated. I washed the dye off after only about 5 minutes, but both sets of eyelashes look the same depth of black several days later. The lift is also staying quite nicely and looks better than mascara for me.
This kit comes with supplies to do 5 eyelash and eyebrow treatments. Only using this for my eyelashes, I think I'll be able to do this at least 12 times. (And doing this only every 6 weeks, it's going to last a while.)
Finally, I'd recommend using Castor Oil as part of your daily routine. Applying it to my eyes/lashes once a day has helped keep them healthier (even with treatments) and has helped my lashes grow longer. Anyways, have fun!

title: Decent Tools for OK Price, Useful Also for Crafting

There's neither anything special nor anything disappointing about this set.
What sets this set apart from others is the lighted mirror. Otherwise, you can actually get larger sets for a lower price, with wider assortments of picks, scrapers and that even include tweezers.
However, since I needed these tools for crafting/tinkering purposes and not for teeth cleaning, a smaller set with a lighted mirror was suitable for my needs. The tools and mirror help me reach into and look into spaces, helping me to scrape or remove flashing, pry things, pick out broken parts, position parts when epoxying, etc.
The tools are strong and durable. The mirror has a sharp image and the light is very helpful as I'm using this to peek inside small cases and enclosures. I don't doubt these are more than adequate for tartar removal, they're a strong and precision crafted stainless steel.
Overall I give the set 4-stars, it suits my needs at a fair enough price.

title: Splat works best for me!
text:
I feel like I've tried every single pink/purple color on the market and I still come back to splat.

I do NOT bleach or use anything in the box except the color. I don't mix anything. Just straight color only my medium brown hair.
The pink makes my brown hair a burgundy purple-ish color, whereas the purple (lavender!) color makes my hair DARK dark dark purple.
Purple is my desired outcome - and the pink color achieves that best for me.
& splat lasts the longest for me! It will actually stay in for months! My roots grow out way before anything washes out - although it will leak color every single time it's wet and stain your clothes, bed, etc forever.

Now with splat I have noticed that it stains the heck out of my skin - whereas other brands wash off skin better - splat will stay on my skin despite prep before and scrub after for days! weeks even! it's a disaster to get off the skin.
HOWEVER- it actually rinses out of my shower and doesn't stain that as bad as other brands do (some turn my white shower pink!)!

So to sum up in comparison to other brands -
lasts longest for me. best color. stains skin horribly. doesn't stain actual shower as bad.

title: Eh, meh, nah.
text:
I got these a month ago when I saw these featured on a YouTube hair video from a YouTuber I follow and generally, her advice on products is solid but these French pins?

The IDEA/CONCEPT is simple and tried and true. So no way to really mess it up, right? Well...

What I do like is the color and the paint or coding hasn't faded or chipped off. The slight curve allows for the in to rest against the curve of your head. The length is nice, and allows more versatility.

What I don't like is the material. For $10 at Target, I wasn't expecting something industrial but the material is very, very flimsy and not remotely sturdy. Not only that, maybe it's the coating on the pins, these things don't stay in for long, or at all sometimes. I have fine, long hair and these pins won't stay put if I don't use product. I usually use a leave-in conditioner so that helps to create texture and the pins seem to stay in longer. These might work better with coarse, thicker hair. It's too bad the material isn't sturdier--so don't think you can do anything while wearing them. The minute you start anything other than sitting and look pretty for however long you wear them, they will fall out without even trying. I had my hair half pined up with a barrette and then pulled the rest up in a twist and made sure the prongs were under the barrette so that it was more secure but it didn't even last half a day and I sit in a cubicle for 8 hours staring at a computer. Just getting up to get a cup of coffee or a printout from the copy machine or other basic tasks would easily loosen the pin.

These are merely okay if you're doing absolutely nothing but sticking a pencil to keep your bun in place work just as well. It's too bad since they are pretty but these are not that functional.

title: Pretty Good
text:
I've only ever owned this epilator, but in the 4+ months I've had it, I've been pretty happy with it. The epilator itself is very well built, it's very sturdy, I've never had problems with the tweezing mechanisms, and it has a nice, solid feel. I chose this epilator because it was relatively well-reviewed, though I was worried by some of the negative reviews. I wanted to be able to epilate my legs and underarms, and this product performs pretty well. There are a few notes:
The light, this makes all the difference, and I never thought it would. I can see EVERY hair growing out of my legs, even if I'm in a dimly lit room.
The trimmer works fairly well, and it's nice to have a device that is so multifunctional (great for traveling).
Some have complained about the battery, but I've had no problems. Even when I was just starting and took forever trying to get every hair, it lasted till I was done.
The noise is fairly loud and menacing, but it's one of those things you get used to. Roommates may get annoyed though.
I don't have any trouble with ingrown hairs, but some people do, so be mindful of that.
I really wanted the wet/dry capability, but the wetness makes the tweezers slide off the hair, so the hair ends up getting pulled pretty hard but doesn't come out. This feature didn't help me in the least. Also, it's harder to get a good grip on the device when it's wet.

Yes, anything that takes your hair out by the root will hurt, I don't think the best epilator in the world could stop that, so don't ever expect it to feel like a massage. Everyone who is saying the first time is the worst is absolutely right - when I did my underarms the first time, I was seeing spots it hurt so bad. My legs were a little difficult but after awhile it was easy to keep going. I tried the bikini line, but couldn't get more than a few hairs out until it was unbearable. It is a good idea when you're starting to epilate to epilate every few days for a week so that all the 'cycles' of hair can be initially epilated. It got much less painful very quickly each time I'd epilate, though I still can't do the bikini (upsetting because I was planning on completely doing away with razors). Now, legs are no problem, though my underarms still hurt some. Tip: make sure you don't have any deoderant on your underarms when you epilate, it makes the hairs slick and the tweezers don't grip well.

I really love having underarms with no stubble shadow, and they feel much smoother. Even when the hairs grow back, they are tapered, so they are much softer than shaving stubble which would irritate my skin. Similarly with the legs, tapered hairs are much less visible than blunt ones, and I do think it is growing back slightly more sparsely (I've heard with routine use, you can stop a lot of growth permanently).

I also had the same issues with 1) never getting a just-shaven smoothness 2) the finer hairs do break - these are best to attack with the slower mode, which is easier on the hair 3) the hair grows back faster than I expected. I have a fair complexion with fine hair, and my hair doesn't grow particularly fast. I have to epilate my arms once a week, and my legs every other at best, so 4-6 weeks is a pretty blatant lie.

So, I'll give it four stars because it does as good a job as any epilator could, most my complaints have to do with epilating in general. One star penalty for misleading description and useless wet/dry feature.

title: Where Has This Stuff Been All My Life???
text: Oh. My. Word. *Excuse me while I go throw away all my regular nail polish.* This is a Game. Changer. I'm a busy mom and honestly, I just hate going to the nail salon, and who has time to wait for 300 hours (Ok, maybe not quite 300) for your regular nail polish to dry, only to smudge it or have it chip within 2 hours? I had pretty much given up on nail polish and just been resigned to the fact that I would have boring nails forever. This stuff is seriously incredible. You just paint it on, cure it, wipe the top with the cleanser to remove the tacky finish, and VOILA! Perfect nails! I did mine last week with this set and they still look AH-MAZING. When this set arrived, I was a bit bummed to find that there's no color included, just base and top coat. I live an hour from the nearest mall and so I couldn't just pop into the store and get a color, and yet I wanted to try it out... Like, right now. I did some reading and found that you can actually use regular nail polish to make a "Gel-y" sandwich. Once you have the base coat on, cure it, then paint your regular color over the top and wait the "300 hours" it takes to dry. Then paint the top coat over the regular color, cure, wipe with cleanser and enjoy your stunning, long lasting nails! The only thing I would change about this set is the light. I wound up buying a larger light because the one that comes with this set is quite small and I wanted to be able to fit all my fingers or all my toes in at once. This light is great for storing and being portable, but I personally wanted something bigger. Overall a fantastic set. I'm never going back to regular polish ever again!

title: Provides subtle, consistent improvement. Effects aren't striking -- but it works.
text:
I received a discounted sample of this product to provide a review on amazon.

I am a healthy 64-year old male with skin that appears tighter and healthier than that of many peers. While I tanned during the first half of my life, I phased it out during the second. I only use lotion under my eyes where skin is noticeably loose and darker than the rest. Over the past five or six years -- part of this is genetic -- the skin at the front of the neck has become especially loose, while the furrowed lines on my forehead have begun to look alarming. I wanted to try Puressant Neck Firming Cream to see what effect it might have on these two issues.

After a three-week trial, during which I applied the product at least once per day, I've seen a subtle but real tightening of the skin on my neck, which appears to have reached maximum effect. I will assume that to continue this trend I might have to use the product indefinitely, but received no indication from product instructions about this. In any case, there are few products I use indefinitely and particularly those with such an extensive list of known and unknown ingredients. Having said that, I might use the product at intervals to reduce symptoms periodically.

The product has had no effect on my wrinkly forehead, at least not yet. I'll just have to live with it.

The cream has a clean, subtle fragrance (I wish it had none) and rather heavy consistency: A little goes a long way. I've not yet noticed any staining of clothes after application nor any side effects. If not for its moisturizing qualities, I might have awarded this product three stars, but it generates enough cosmetic improvement at a low price to merit four.

title: Beautiful Summer Polish
text:
While this has been discontinued and hard to find, if found at all, I did purchase it when it was available. I am a China Glaze fan and have purchased many of their polishes here on Amazon and other places, and have been given bottles of China Glaze polishes. My hobby is nail art, and I have many bottles of polishes from many brands, but for the most part China Glaze is one of my favorites. I love it because it allows me to grow out my nails because it contains a nail hardener in it which I appreciate. I used to have acrylic overlays and when I removed the overlays, what was left were weak, damaged nails that would bend and break into the nail bed--very painful! However, while using China Glaze polishes, it strengthened my nails enough to grow out and now they look amazing! For this, I will always love this brand.

I love spring and summer colored polish. In fact, most of my vast collection are mainly spring and summer colors. The color of this is what drew me first. I use it in the Summer with my teals and aquas. It is a textured polish and contains a glitter-ry finish-highly reflective as is, and even more so when top coated. Without top coat it leaves a rough finish as all textured polishes do. With top coat because it is porous it absorbs the top coat and more than one coat is needed. I have worn it both with and without top coat and in the sun this is really beautiful. My only complaint but not just aimed at this polish, but all textured polish is removal. It is most difficult with regular polish remover like glitter so I use acetone to remove.

I would recommend this if you can still find it. I wanted to buy the whole set because of the colors, but was only able to get two and no luck finding the rest at present time. It sold out and was discontinued some time ago. However, if you can find it and like textured polish, again, I would recommend it.

title: Works great, added free bonuses but they don't sell the file refills
text:
Before you buy this...
Make sure you can buy replacement files for it. I cannot find that this company sells them. I see that Amope does sell them and although I do not know if they would fit this file, I have a strong feeling they would fit. Many times beauty gadget dupes are almost exact replicas in my experience so other brands of replacement items do normally fit (i.e. clarisonic off brand brushes, amope off brand file rollers, etc). I checked the Amope refills & at the time of writing this, they sell for about $10 for all 3. I normally won't comment on price but I find that to be ridiculously high considering it is just a piece of plastic with basically a sticker on it with a rough or smooth edge. Regular emery boards are so cheap so I am surprised the refills would go for that much. Now that is for the name brand of Amope. If dupe companies make them, they should be cheaper.

Pros...
* Includes AA battery, 3 heads (file, buff, shine), soft top separators, nail clippers & bag to keep it all in.
* Works good.

Cons...
* I think this company not selling the file refills is a HUGE NEGATIVE. At the time of writing this, I searched the internet and cannot find anywhere that they sell them.

I read some reviews about how some people didn't feel it was powerful enough. I felt the same thing when I used it but really it is powerful enough for just filing your nails. You wouldn't want anything too rough for that.

This vs Amope...
I do not own the original Amope so I cannot compare the two directly. I looked closely at the photos and they look identical to me. This brand you do get the added extras of the clippers, toe separators and bag. With the Amope brand, you are able to purchase the nail file refills. With this brand, you are not able to purchase the nail file refills at the time of writing this. It is likely the amope refills would fit this. My advice is if you are wanting an electronic nail file like this, go with the Amope version because you know you can buy refills & they will fit. I normally will not comment on price but I will say that I am taken aback that this Amope dupe is priced as high as it is. Even though this brand is at a lower cost and you get the added bonuses, I am still a little surprised that there is not more of a price drop to remain competitive since they do not have the name brand recognition.

I like to write product reviews & because I rely heavily on what other people write when I am buying items, I try to write reviews that highlight the good and the bad. I rate things from as low as 1 star up to 5 stars. I base my judgment on my experience with a product and not on the price, since the price value of an item is ultimately up to the buyer (what is a good deal for one person might seem expensive to another). That being said, I did receive this item at a discount in exchange for my honest, unbiased opinion.

title: Not 100% human hair
text:
This wig isn't 100% human hair.
I tried to lighten it with powder bleach using a strong developer and saw hardly any results at all.
It lifted / lightened maybe 2 shades after processing for almost an hour.
To no avail, I covered the test strand with foil and used my blow dryer to help it lighten. Nothing happened.

Using the same formula, I would've gotten completely different results on a 100% human hair wig or on living persons head of hair.
I have 39 years experience in the hair industry, including coloring human hair wigs and hair extensions. I have never had this problem before.

I wanted the wig for a chemotherapy client who had curly hair, same length with a center part. The only problem was the color.
Unfortunately, I went by what the description is of the wig, which is 100% human hair. I ordered it, recieved it on time. Tried to lighten it as promised for my client with a disasterous result.
Now I have the upsetting task of telling my client that I can not achieve the same hair color she had because the wig isnt processing the same way human hair should.
This is after I reassured her I COULD achieve it given the facts stated and description of the wig.
My personal conclusion and professional opinion with 39 years experience is that this wig is not 100% human hair.
Theres no reason why I could not achieve a lighter color for my client other than that the wig is made up of something that resembles human hair, and not 100% human hair as the description states that it is.

It's not an overly thick wig, but has enough hair to scrunch and create a full look.
Curl formation is smooth.

3 stars for the style, curl and length of the wig. Pictures of it are somewhat accurate.
0 stars for the misrepresentation that its 100% human hair.
In addition to me, I will have a very upset client.
I'm at loss as to what to do now as she wanted and I reassured her that she could have this wig for the holiday.
It's too late now to order a different one and start this process over again.

These are made in China, and there is no clarification on the package that I can find. So I don't have a clue what these are made of.

They are not quite as soft as the ones that come with their own serum that I've tried. But they are fairly sturdy. You can rip them if you start ripping in a corner, but they don't rip as easily as I would have thought.

So these are acceptable dry face masques, but their product page and labeling needs some improvement.

Some of the sandwiches are already pulling apart and do not feel sticky. The hair itself smelled slightly synthetic while I styled it, and I noticed the ends bubbled up with heat application like synthetic would. I also noticed several strands of super thick, plastic-feeling pieces. I pulled one off the weft and it snapped apart like it was plastic. Tried to take a picture of the bubbled ends as well as one of the thick pieces.

I've used other inexpensive brands that have had better tape, and don't mind synthetic when you know it's what you'll get. I will probably take these out and return them as-is or have to buy better tape to fix them.

title: Decent cleansing conditioner for dry, damaged hair
text:
I have very dry, very damaged hair, and am CONSTANTLY on the search for the "perfect" products for my hair. I have now tried just about every shampoo and conditioner available, ranging from very cheap drugstore products, to very expensive salon products. I've also tried a few infomercial products. While I have found several products I do like very much, I am still on the search...

Having heard that Pantene Co-Wash might be a good alternative to my expensive infomercial cleansing conditioner, I purchased the large bottle and gave it a go. After following the directions to wash into my hair and then let it sit for a minute before rinsing, I towel-dried my hair and then let it dry naturally (my wavy, frizzy hair usually does better air-drying than it does being dried via hair dryer). My hair was definitely easy to brush, but I feel it didn't get my roots very clean.

So I tried it again. And then again. Each time, I felt it did a good job detangling, but not such a good job cleaning. My hair looked fine for about 8 hours before it began to look greasy. Getting my very dry hair to look greasy is not an easy feat!

Overall, I would say this is a decent cleansing conditioner for dry, damaged hair, but it might leave some people's hair (mine included) looking a bit greasy, especially after a few hours.

Although this product is marketed for African-American hair, it works for other textures of hair, as well. I have very fine, dry, damaged Caucasian hair, and it works for my hair texture, as well.

text: I tried using this after 30 days of using Walmart's eyelid scrub towelettes. The Walmart eyelid scrub towelettes have the same ingredients as the OCuSOFT LID SCRUB ORIGINAL PRE-MOISTENED PADS but are about 30% cheaper and much larger in size. The Walmart towelettes really improved my eyelids, but I still had a bit of residual itching, so I tried the OUST cleanser to see if I could do better. I wash my hands thoroughly and apply a small amount of the OUST foam to my fingertips and work it into the eyelashes, eyelids, and eyebrows and then rinse it off by splashing cold water on my closed eyes. After that, I wipe down the eyelashes and eyelids with a small cotton pad soaked in saline water solution, the stuff that comes in a bottle for rinsing out contact lenses. This does a good job of clearing the OUST solution from my eyes because the tea tree oil in the solution does sting a little (not much) and you want to make sure you completely rinse it out -- no pain no gain if you want kill those mites and clean your eyelash pores. When you open the lid of this lava scrub, you'll think you just stepped off the plane landing in Hawaii. It smells so tropical, so dewy, and so tasty I almost tried it. And it's no wonder, with ingredients of coconut oil, papaya extract, and macadamia oil.
I tried it a few times on my face (mixed with soap, of course), and it was a little too strong for me. The sugar crystals are large and sturdy, requiring a vigorous scrub to dissolve. It didn't cause me to break out, but I did notice that the rest of the day and the following day, it looked like half my skin got taken off. Dips, discolorations, and small zits that were hiding beneath the surface were all visible - but after a couple of days everything went back to normal. Those of you who have tried chemical or acid peels on your face know what I mean.
I get it, if there are that many impurities on my skin, it's a good idea to scrub them away. But I don't really like looking at my face like that in the mirror. So... now I've switched it to a body scrub and use it in the tub. Perfect! Arms, legs, and chest are now totally smooth and smell great.

title: Good toothbrushes, terrible chargers
text:
I bought 2 of these, received them Wednesday night. By Friday night, one of the chargers was completely broken. It wasn't manhandled or anything, just normal use. The charging port itself was crooked but whatever. Then 2 of the prongs that make contact to the toothbrush broke off. It also kinda whines when charging. The toothbrushes themselves are good, but I don't feel they will last very long with one charger already broken within 1.5 days and having to share the other charger

Update: the other charger broke now too. The prongs on the charger create a caustic blue substance (I'm no chemist, I'm sure there's a name for it) while the toothbrushes charge and then they break off. All fine if two prongs make contact with the contact points on the bottom of the brush, which are both on the same side, while there are 4 prongs on the charger. If two prongs on opposite side break off, you're out of luck. I'd like my money back for both of these. Even if they sent new chargers, they'd have the same flaw. The toothbrushes really should have either a better charging design or a secondary way to charge them.

I'm pretty novice with hair styling, only recently cutting my hair in a manner that requires drying and styling to look at its best so if I can take this brush and make my hair look beautiful then anyone can. This brush is excellent for beginners so I imaging people with more experience can do even more with it too. This brush is actually really nice. It is lightweight and goes through hair with ease. It doesn't knot up or pull my hair at all. It wraps around it and helps to dry my hair with a cute flip at the ends like I like. It has a comfort grip handle and is easy to manipulate. After I apply my products and dry my hair to about halfway, I section my hair off and begin drying around the brush section by section. It handles a pretty large section at a time and I use a concentrator nozzle from here on out. It goes pretty quickly as I manipulate each section to add a little flip or a more pronounced curl at the ends. This brush will allow either one with minimal work and also helps to keep hair smooth and frizz free when finished. I am really please with it. Like I said I am beginners level at best and only have a few style know how's in my arsenal but with this brush I am able to try a few new things and have control needed to perfect what I already know. Using it the first time was easy and natural and the positive reviews that convinced me to try this inexpensive brush are spot on. I really cant think of a negative or something I wish it had that it doesn't. I think it's pretty perfect and I recommend trying it. For the price you can't really go wrong.

title: Helps to detangle my wet hair in the shower but not as good as my Heeta brush
text:
These brushes are actually like eight combs strung together. I had to set the extra piece that comes with each brush to separate the tines. It was not easy to get the bar across the "combs" but eventually I managed. There are only two places the bar should be put and that is where the holes are on the back of the "brush." I assembled these brushes on the lower holes. My biggest issue with these brushes is that there are only two holes to lock the bar in place when I prefer four holes like my Heeta detangling brush (product number B0836XT7J8 since the Amazon embedded links are not working).

Once this is assembled, it glides through the hair and detangles. It works well on dry hair but even better on wet hair. I love the hard tines as it is like getting a massage on the scalp. The handle provides an okay grip but I would have preferred a silicone grip. Since the combs are separated, this brush can act as a vent brush for blow drying even though it is not of circular design. Hair can be removed easily since the tines are flat with no "ball" tip.

The only reason I rated this three stars is because of the hard time I had assembling the rod in place on each one, the lack of four holes for a secure fit, and the lack of silicone grip on the handle. Otherwise they work well. The current price of $8.99 is reasonable for two detanglers.

title: Noticeable Difference in Days
text:
I'm a mother of two, and needless to say, my skin isn't exactly what it used to be. I suffer from redness, large pores, and a loss of elasticity. I've tried numerous remedies, including facial peels, moisturizing lotions, etc. and while they left my skin feeling smooth, they never removed the redness or shrank my pores.

The first time I tried La Deessa, I was skeptical, as I am with any product. I opened the bottle and sniffed--no odd smell. It actually smelled somewhat like aloe, which is the second ingredient listed on the bottle. I used the little glass dropper to add a few drops to my face, neck, and chest, and I rubbed it in. As the serum began to dry, I could already feel my face getting tighter. It was pretty impressive. I didn't notice a big difference in the redness and pore size right away.

I continued applying La Deessa Vitamin C Serum twice a day--once in the morning before I applied my makeup and once at night after I removed my makeup. Over the next few days, the changes were noticeable. My pores were smaller, and my skin had more of a radiant glow. After a few weeks, it was even better, and you could literally see and feel the difference in my skin.

I am incredibly satisfied with LaDeessa Premium Anti Aging Elixir, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a pick-me-up for their skin. It works!

The silver properties are excellent for first aid as well and in my opinion make better use of the ointment (based on cost effectiveness for purpose). It’s good for minor skin irritations, cuts, abrasions and especially burns.

It came in handy initially as I managed to burn myself promptly after receiving it. It helped the burn heal much faster, while keeping infection at bay, than if I had just let nature take its course.

I learned about the healing properties of colloidal silver about 20 years ago when my daughter burned herself as a little girl. The ER doctor sent us home with colloidal silver cream and it fixed her right up.

I like to keep it on hand now for just such emergencies. Highly recommended.

title: Halloween Or Messing Around Okay, But Serious Wear, Not So Much
text:
I have been working with wigs for quite a few years now. One thing I know is a good quality vs not so great quality wig. Let's take a look at this one.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?

HAIR
This wig has some great hair. the colors are definitely platinum white and what I would call light auburn base hairs. The white hairs are about 1/3 or so longer than the auburn hairs. There is a nice kink to the hairs.

THICKNESS
That is where this wig is sadly lacking. At the top, the wefts of hair are way too far apart. The lace in the cap is a very light butter colored yellow. The hair is not too thin, but it is not quite thick enough to cover hair below. Yes, this comes with a nylon cap, but it just is not comfortable with those. If you have dark hair it will definitely show the bright colored lace and elastics through the wig when the wind blows.

BANGS/STYLE
That is where this wig is just not practical unless you don't mind looking stupid for a party or Halloween. The bangs are WAY too long for anyone to wear. That usually would not be a problem, but what you will get instead of the cool light ends on the entire head is chopped bang that is bland looking and then these white cool looking ends around the head. The bangs are best cut painstakingly so that the auburn is cut way shorter (about 2/3) than the white hairs. That takes a lot of time but worth the effort. Then you have to cut them at a staggered manner.

Other than the bangs being hard to trim so you can at least function with this wig on, the overall style is fabulous. I love how it falls and looks while on the head.

ELASTIC BANDS
Inside the wig, there are elastic bands with hooks to help hold the wig on the head. You might want to take them down to the spot you like it in as the hooks have a tendency to come undone during wearing.

WHAT I WANT IN A WIG
Believe it or not, I would actually wear a wig like this with the right outfit, and not to be silly either. I prefer wigs that look authentic,, and can be worn realistically as well as for fun.

1. I have to be able to see out of it
2. I have to be able to wear it comfortably without fussing
3. I want it to not have my real hair showing
4. I want it to look realistic
5. I want it to last for quite a few wearings

DOES THIS WIG PASS THE TEST?
I am giving this wig THREE stars because it is hard to wear and see. In order to trim this in a realistic manner, I have to take a LOT of time and that takes stars off for me. I happen to love the style and coloring, so I am wiling to put the work into it, but honestly, I think it should be a bit shorter in the bangs area since it is so hard to trim and keep it looking real. Also, the wefting on the top is just a bit too widely spaced. I wish also that the cap was made with light auburn lace and elastic instead of the icy yellow colors.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want to wear this for fun, it will be hard to see and hard to trim and not look silly in this. It is comfortable and the style is epic, but there will be work required. You can bandana it to help, but it still will look a bit floppy unless trimmed a little bit in the bangs/fringe area. I like this, but it takes work to wear and not look silly for me.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. The trimming of the bangs is VERY time consuming since we only have one shot at it and if it is screwed up, then the wig is toast. I wish there was more hair on top and that the lace cap did not show as easily. A darker cap underneath (light auburn color) would have been much nicer with this. I will still use this, but it could have been a bit nicer with small inexpensive changes.

title: Versatile and comfortable
text:
Many times wearing a mask also comes with the discomfort that the elastic bands can cause to some one’s ears. I found that the Zelaxy Mask extenders do help with the comfort level.

The pack of Mask extenders I have contained 5 extenders; black, white, pink, green and blue. The Eagle (it has little ‘wings’ that the elastic strap wraps around) model that I have is made out of soft silicon which makes the extender comfortable to wear around a person’s head.

The extender is stretchy enough to get on fairly easily, it also has multiple ‘stops’ in order to control tightness of a mask and the extender is thick enough so it won’t snap under normal use.

The ‘standard’ way of wearing the extender, that being directly behind the ears, works fine. This extender is also versatile enough to allow the extender to be worn around the neck so that both elastic bands from the mask fall below the ear while still providing good support.

There is one unexpected issue; longer hair can sometimes complicate putting on the extender as longer hair can more easily get caught up in the ‘wings’.

The bottom-line is that, for me, the Zelaxy extenders are comfortable to wear and they do help make it more comfortable to wear a mask throughout the day.

title: I had to try it for myself.
text:
After reading all of the bad reviews on this new Norelco shaver, I swore I was not going to buy this unit.

Well, a few months ago I realized my local stores didn't stock my HQ5 Norelco replacement blades anymore and I about had a heart attack. Oh, darn, I am now being forced to upgrade and I was quite happy with my current shaver.

I have had a Norelco 5885XL for the past 13 years. I love this unit and it suits me well. This only noteworthy things about this old unit is that I have had to have the batteries replaced only two times, but this is normal since they wear out every 6 years or so.

Here is my 1050x review.. it was painful to write, but here goes..

--This is a noisy shaver folks.. I graduated to a 5885XL a long time ago and was surprised of the whisper quiet shave it delivered. The 1050x is about 2-3 time noisier than my 15 year old Norelco, WTH? This is not good. I simply cannot accept a noisy shaver. This thing is inches away from my ears at 5am and that is very annoying. I need peace and quiet at those early hours, and this would not work long term.

--What a bad shave. Starting with a 2-day shadow growth, I shaved half of my face with my trusty 5885XL [using 1.5 year old blades] and the other half with my shiny new 1050x unit. I actually had my wife feel both shaves afterwords to confirm I wasn't being overly critical of my new toy.

As I suspected, she confirmed my 5885xl produced a better shave, in about the same amount of time.

As I shaved with the 1050x, I realized that I was going over the same growth areas without making things smoother, especially around the neck. I was getting tired, frustrated, and irritated. The pivoting head technology is clearly inferior to Norelcos older units.

--Here come the skin irritations: Ahhh!!!
Just a few minutes after my shave test had ended, my 1050x side was now irritated and not feeling comfortable [like my 5885xl side was]. Having used Norelcos all of my shaving life, about 25 years, this irritation I feel is not normal, and I do not find this acceptable; even if there is a break-in period; not for me there isn't. no thanks..

--Bad charging system! What the heck is it with this terrible charging system. I should be able to plug the unit in directly and not have to lug around more junk to lose or break while on travel. The AC adapter cable does not even fit into the travel case, how stupid is that!?! I can see this cable being the 1st thing I lose on a business trip because it does not have a place to be stored.

Gosh, I wanted to love using this shaver. I was excited and wanted to prove all these other bad reviews wrong. Sadly, they are correct in every way.

My guess is many of the good reviews are being written by persons who have not had the pleasure of trying one of Norelco's older shavers to notice the amazing quality they can provide. Folks, do yourself a favor and get an older model, preferably something from the late 90's IMHO.

Norelco, come'on buddy.. Your losing me big time here.

It's back to my 5885xl, and I have found my HQ5's here on Amazon, clicking buy; and it's byebye to my 1050x.

:(

F.
