title: WOW. Great exfoliation!
text:
So I've never had a professional microdermabrasion session and can't compare to that, but this is definitely the most amazing exfoliation I've ever had! The written instructions with mismatched photos for setting up are pretty bad- probably should've checked-out the video, but I was too impatient! Not sure I got the little disk filter thing in right, but onward and upward!

I used the diamond tip- medium size- and suction level 2 (I have pretty thick skin). I did give myself a little hickey next to one eye before I realized I could change the suction level while it was already in use (since you set the timer and the suction and then start it, I thought it was locked-in). But even that already looks a lot better 24 hours later.

I started with just one side of my face (line right down the center) so I could see/feel a side-by-side and while, of course, it's not like all my fine lines or hyperpigmentation disappeared after one session, my skin on the side I did was BABY SMOOTH while the other side was my usual not so smooth (Though I exfoliate a LOT)! Just keep in mind that your skin may be a little tender in some spots and you DO NOT want to use any chemical exfoliants (like AHAs) for a bit! I'm not a professional, so I don't know the time to wait, but I'll try a bit of my usual AHA serum after 48 hours. For now, I'm just using my hyaluronic acid and peptide blend serum and DMAE moisturizer and my skin is super glowy and nice!

title: Not as Strong As I Hoped
text:
I am relatively new to solid colognes. I own this sampler set, Oak City Beard's Sandalwood Bourbon, and a sample set from another company. The other company's set was my first venture into solid colognes. I liked the variety it offered, and their colognes usually lasted most of the day.

I expected the same from this set.

I will admit, I liked variety that this offered, which is why I ordered it. Now that I've had time to try out each one, here are my thoughts. (Please note, cologne can smell different on each person, so what didn't work for me, may work for you.)

Barista - I don't drink coffee, so the thought of smelling like coffee all day was not a selling point for me. I figured this would be my least favorite of the four. When I opened the tin, it smelled like a 30-year-old motel lobby. A powerful scent of cheap black coffee, with a hint of musty cigarettes and pleather couches. I was not impressed. Still, I put it on and the smell changed to more of a 1990s coffee shop. Fortunately, the cocoa smell came forward more once it was on me, and the coffee was not as strong. I don't hate it as much as I thought I would. In fact, I kind of like how it smells on me.

Woodland Ranger - My favorite out of the bunch. While you may think it would make you smell like a Christmas tree, it's more of a clean outdoors scent.

Snow Leopard - I love me some sandalwood, so this was the one I really bought the set for. It says there is peppermint in it, but I can't smell it. Also, I feel like the vanilla overpowers the sandalwood. Not as good as I had hoped. Not bad at all, just not what I expected. (This one also seems to dissipate quicker than the others.)

Uncle Jack - I smell the bourbon and a trace of tobacco, but once again, the vanilla is the stronger scent here. It's definitely not a bad smell, probably my second favorite of the pack.

As I mentioned in the headline, the colognes are just not as strong as I hoped for. I mean, I don't want to overpower everyone in my general vicinity, but I do like to smell the cologne throughout the day and none of these do that. Perhaps I'm not putting enough on. Like I said, I'm new to this whole solid cologne thing.

title: (Check wikipedia if you are unclear where this stuff comes from -- way cool. ) Anyway
text:
I once bought a kilo jar of flakes from some craft outlet. The flakes are neat because you can see that the chip still have the imprints of the palm leaves. (Check wikipedia if you are unclear where this stuff comes from -- way cool.) Anyway, the 1 lb bags are the same quality Carnauba wax but more finely powdered. Probably that is good for some things. I am using this stuff two ways. Use 1) I use an electric iron to saturate very thin cloth and make collages. It is a neat effect. Most recently I have used the same process to cover very thin plywood to make pieces for a mobile. See pictures.

Use 2: Melt in a double boiler 1 part Carnauba wax to 2 parts walnut oil. The result is a hard paste wax that is terrific for finishing wood. Don't use much, just rub it on, wait an hour, and then buff with a clean cloth. The stuff doesn't contain any drying agents like commercial paste waxes so it doesn't dry nearly as quickly. But it works great. It is a little stiff for lubricating screws for power driving but it will do the job. Furthermore, I have used it has lip balm -- perfectly safe -- but to be honest bees wax melted with olive oil works better.

text:
I practice magic, and I do many bathing rituals to rid myself of unwanted negativity and to cleanse myself of lingering residual energy that others might have left behind on my person. One of my bath rituals called for Florida Water, so I went out to find a bottle. Let me tell you, not only was I shocked when I found it in my tiny suburban CVS, I was even more startled at the $3.89 price tag! I fully expected to have to order this stuff online, but it seems like it's an item that's easily obtainable at your local drugstore. Like another reviewer had mentioned, it was on the isle with the products from Mexico. Didn't have to look far to find it either.
It smells pretty good. I was expecting something lighter, but it definitely has a more 'masculine' scent to it. Not very feminine, in my opinion but that's ok since I don't bother with women's perfumes to begin with. I'm not a 'flowery scent' type of girl. For some reason it makes me think of my ex-boyfriend who is a sailor and is constantly around the water. Reminds me of the smell of the ocean mixed with a spritz or two of citrus lemon fruit. I got the Murray and Lanman 7 1/2 ounce bottle of this stuff, and I LOVE that it's in a plastic bottle. It's going to be on my altar and I have a curious cat who wanders around nosing things, so if he knocks it over it won't be a problem. There's a good deal of cologne in the bottle for the price you pay, so I expect to be able to use it in my rituals for a long time before I have to buy another bottle. At the price, you really can't complain.

title: Better Than I Hoped For
text: I purchased this B3 gel in desperation. I am 70 years old, have rosacea, facial eczema, and rosacea-related acne, redness and sensitivity, and very congested pores. Also, the age-related sagging and wrinkling that most women have. My complexion was very nice when I was younger, so all these problems have been challenging to say the least. Most creams, etc. make me break out or redden. A rosacea website suggested B3. In the past, I used a B3 cream which made me break out badly from the added coconut oil to which I am very sensitive. However, this brand has fewer ingredients,  no penetrants to inflame my eczema, and comes well-reviewed. It was also not terribly expensive. Most web reviewers note one must use B3 10% faithfully for three months to get full benefits. On the third day of use, however, I noted the redness of my facial skin subsiding, including my acne scars. By the end of seven days, my pores appeared smaller, even on my nose, and the overactive sebum glands in my T-Zone were shrinking. White heads were either coming to the surface and easily extracted after a shower, or shrinking below the skin. I started using this on my neck and noted increasing firmness (which I badly need). I am not much concerned with wrinkles, as I had oily skin until menopause, and have not yet noticed any difference. Because this gel is thick, I first spray with a non-alcohol toner, and then put one or two drops on my fingers and spray three times with the toner before applying. This amount covers my whole face, neck and eye area. I then apply a lightweight moisturizer  after the B-3gel has sunk in. At first, I only did this one time a day There is a very tiny bit of flaking from this gel--it is drying a little. That, I think, is why the acne scars improve. However, this flaking is not noticeable after I apply the moisturizer. I can use mineral powder makeup with no difficulty. I now use the B3 two times a day. The Zinc in this gel appears to prevent my acne from forming like any antibiotic. I will have an undersign cyst begin to form, but by the next day it is gone. I plan to keep using this product and have ordered oral B3 vitamins, also, but have not yet begun taking them. I feel I must be deficient in this vitamin to have such a positive response topically. I should add that I usually have to take extra oral zinc when I break out badly, because I had a bad, life-threatening staph infection six years ago. The breakouts I have from rosacea often become infected now and scar badly. This Topical treatment, however, means I no longer have to take zinc orally, which is much better for my system. I hope this very detailed review helps someone else who suffers from demagogical problems as I do. PS: I also may begin using this gel on the tops of my hands at night, under my hand cream, just to see if my aging skin improves there, too. Retin A appears to thin my skin, but this B3 seems to thicken the protective layer even when the gel is not applied. Try it!! UPDATE:  April 19, 2019. I am on my third or fourth bottle, buying them now for friends. I regret this review is so long, but so afraid the company will go out of business since their founder died. These are wonderful formulations--especially this one. I've not found anything as effective at any price. Started using the caffeine eye gel last night and saw a difference immediately.

This filler has a negligible hint of scent; however, that goes away almost immediately and is not at all offensive. In fact, the scent will probably not be detectable unless one is trying to determine if it is completely odorless. The product goes on smoothly, and it takes a very small amount to cover a nose, blotches, etc.

This is a small bottle. The net weight is listed as 10g/0.35oz. If it is applied on specific areas, and not the whole face, it should last for lots of applications. Just a note of observation, the product I received was in a small bottle with a plunger type dispenser. The one in the advertising and use brochure is a tube and the application instructions are for the tube.

title: Can't use if you're undergoing fertility treatments or tanned.
text:
“Do not use if you are pregnant, nursing, or undergoing fertility treatments.”

“Do not treat if you have tanned skin. Tanned skin is at an increased risk of adverse effects with light-based devices.”

These are warnings that NIRA doesn’t indicate in any of their marketing, but which are included in the booklet you receive with purchase. The tanned skin comment is contrary to information on their website saying it's for all skin types.

I purchased the device (not the serum) directly from the manufacturer for $200. They seem to offer a lot of promotions, so don’t buy this at full price (current msrp is $400, and they seem to offer 30% off all the time if you give them your email, my 50% off was a link from an influencer’s page on youtube). Tried reviewing on the main device page and got this notice: “Amazon has noticed unusual reviewing activity on this product. Due to this activity, we have limited this product to verified purchase reviews.” So that should tell us something about the quality of the reviews here. I can’t offer a review myself of the actual product because of the surprise contraindications. I had to give a star rating in order to post this review, so I just plugged in 3.

Also, the website says to wait 1 minute before re-treating an area; the warning label says to wait at least 1 hour.

title: This vs. Clarisonic Uplift?
text:
I haven't been using this item long enough to report on any discernible difference in my face but I can speak to a couple of other interesting tidbits.

I know that these have been in use for generations and they must work because people swear by them. If that weren't proof enough, I use my Clarisonic Uplift daily, and it comes with an attachment that does the exact same thing that this roller does, only with using technology. The instructions on this roller is to use it for 5-10 minutes a day, 2-3 times a day. That's a lot and I don't know of many people who care to carve out time to do this, but if you're sitting quietly watching TV or even reading, you can do it absentmindedly. With the Clarisonic, you're supposed to use it with a moisturizer or a serum but with this, you use it on a dry face. With or without a lotion, the massaging affect is exactly the same.

The jade roller feels cool across the skin (even if mine does squeak a little) and it feels wonderful. I'm not sure it does anything if you're rolling it on your chest, but it feels amazing if done with a bit of pressure. It comes in a nice little Asian-inspired embroidered bag, so it doesn't look bad if you want to leave it on your bedside for easy access. I'm going to continue to use the Uplift each night but this item doesn't require a battery and I can whip it out anytime.

title: Product Name is Misleading
text:
I read all the glowing reviews and decided to purchase this product, and decided to use it daily for a month before writing this review. If you are considering purchasing this product be advised that Vi-Tae will send you emails encouraging you to post a review (hence, this one for my purchase -- but not the positive rating they were soliciting), and offer you incentives for good reviews -- Amazon promo codes for discounts on other Vi-Tae products. I did not go to their website to fill out the form to get discounts, nor did I register for their $250 sweepstakes.

The name of this product is "More Than Clean: Blackhead Remover, Pore Minimizer & Unclogger;" It is a misnomer to call it a "blackhead remover" since it does not remove blackheads; I doubt there is a product out there that does.

Perhaps it does minimize and unclog pores, but I am rating it two-stars for two reasons: (1) because of the "blackhead remover" claim, which was the reason for my purchase; and (2) the Amazon price of the product, 4.46 oz for $39.95 (list price $69.50).

title: Steep learning curve
text:
I tried these with several other bridesmaids to see if they might make our hair easier on the morning of the wedding. I'm glad we did it ahead of time, because they would have been a wedding morning disaster.
First of all, the pictures show these straightened to make waves and the package of ones I received cannot be convinced to hold that shape. This wouldn't be a big deal, except they are difficult to put on as spirals. You have to thread the hook through first, but the tube is much longer than the hook. If I'd been capable of sprouting a third hand, putting these on would have been the moment it happened. And that's only the first hurdle.
It takes some extra work to get a good curl out of these. Make sure your hair is damp when they go on or it won't hold the curl (after a lot of success in my life using regular foam curlers on dry hair, this was the most disappointing thing). Keep a spray bottle handy, because they take long enough to put on that your hair will dry before you get done, at least the first couple of times. Make sure the hair isn't tangled or twisted or it won't curl properly. Don't snag your hair section with the hook or you'll find out.
A good curl cream is a must because these don't make a curl that holds as well as-- pick a standard type of curler. Make sure you have a God hair spray to set them with, too. If you don't have a quality product or three in your hair to force the curl to hold, they will fall within a few hours and then you've got whatever your hair texture is with too much brushing and a few weird bends.
Also, these pull your hair at the root pretty hard if you try to sleep on them loose, so make sure you have a good cap/bonnet/kerchief/babushka (whatever hair covering you use) to keep them arranged into something fairly comfortable.

text: I bought this product after seeing a beauty blogger's review about it. Since I have hyper pigmentation from not using sun screen in my youth, I've been trying to find ways to stop or reverse it. I also bought and tried out other products in conjunction with this one as part of a skin care routine, but I noticed that my skin would break out in very small pimples sometimes. After testing and leaving out products to figure out what was making my skin like this, I discovered that when I stopped using this product, I no longer got those small pimples. My skin is somewhat sensitive, so maybe that's one of the reasons, or some ingredient I'm slightly allergic to? I'm not sure. But I wasn't completely surprised as I did notice my face felt just a tad tingly and extra sensitive after using it (even with just one drop, no more than two, each night). During the time I did use it, which was for a few weeks, I have about half the bottle left, I didn't notice my spots lightening or even staying the same. Actually, they got very slightly darker; even though, I used sun screen. I don't necessarily attribute that occurrence to this product though, but certainly I was disappointed that this did nothing for me even after being patient and using it consistently for a while to see its effects. title: It isn't even close to natural bristle
text:
I wanted to try a synthetic fiber brush since it is impossible to dry your natural bristle brush sufficiently before packing it up on the day of travel. I was looking for a brush that I can use, shake out and pack within minutes. For use at home, I've had over the years a couple of natural badger brushes of varying quality, ranging from lower grade black only brushes to very fine silvertip. So, trust me, I know how they feel.
This brush is for me virtually unusable.
When i try to lather up, i spray water and soap all over the bathroom. Try as i may, i couldn't prevent the spray. When these synthetic bristles are deflected even only a little, they spring back with a snap. It appears that the spring back force increases linearly with the amount of deflection. And all the fibers move almost in unison.

This is very different in natural bristles where more force bends the hair further, but it isn't like a linear increase in force. During the lather, the bristles conform to your face and the circular action seems to gently bent the hairs in one or the other direction. The brush also spreads a bit, as fibers are pushed and bent a little. Once you lift the natural hair brush off your face, the bristles don't string back all at once. Some fibers may return to their approximate straight form, but the water and soap mixture will clump some of them together.

I want to be clear that I don’t object to a different brush feel. As long as it does the job of lathering up and isn’t so coarse to feel like sandpaper, I’m fine. This synthetic fiber, on the other hand, are best compared to very playable, soft steel springs. Even when I tried to lather up very slowly and gingerly, each fiber literally snapped back to its original position. When you lift the brush off your face, all the bristles are back in place as if you just upacked the brush.

In summary, this brush is far from coming close to the feel of badger bristles. I cant use it without spraying soap all over and I wish I could return it, but it appears I’m stuck with this thing.

title: Cavin Schon Fuller's Earth & Bentonite Combo Clay (3 Pack)
text:
Cavin Schon Fuller's Earth & Bentonite Combo Clay is chemical free, preservative free, metallic free, pesticide free, peroxide free, ammonia free, and cruelty free. It is used to leave skin and hair softer, as a deep pore cleaner that draws out toxins, and as a treatment for acne and scars. One package (this comes in a set of 3) weighs approximately 100 grams. The product is made in India. Each bag of clay comes in a resealable pouch to keep it fresh (and from making a mess). The directions say to not use a metal bowl when you are using this product (probably due to absorption issues). I used a styrofoam bowl and plastic spoon which I discarded after use. First of all, I believe the directions say to use 1-2 teaspoons of clay to equal parts water. I recommend using MUCH LESS. I followed these directions and had leftover clay that lasted for two weeks! (I kept adding water to the remainder to soften the clay each time I used it). The clay is fairly easy to mix as it is not sandy or gritty - but becomes more of a "putty" type mixture. I used the clay on my face only, as I did not want to deal with the mess of having it in my hair. On each application, I left the clay on for about 15-20 minutes (recommended amount of time). After about 10 minutes, you can feel the clay tighten on your skin. This doesn't hurt, but just feels strange, and at least for me - was a tiny bit itchy. The clay comes off fairly easy with a warm washcloth. There is one thing to note about this clay and it is even mentioned on the product instructions - this clay can (and did) make your face appear red after removal. I encountered this issue each time I used the product - even decreasing the time to about 12 minutes or so. The redness looks like a very light sunburn and doesn't hurt. It takes anywhere from 30 minutes to 1 hour to go away (at least in my case). Since it didn't hurt and was only appearance - I didn't worry too much about it, and just followed up with moisturizer afterwards. After the applications, I noticed that my skin felt much smoother, but the feeling only lasted that night (and sometimes only for a few hours). If you are not used to clay masks - this will make a mess! When applying the clay, I had some that fell off of my fingers and plopped into the sink. When trying to clean it up, it only smeared - making matters worse. The product does as it is intended, but I do not think that clay masks are for me. I did not like the tightening feeling when it was drying, after the first application- the redness was a little weird, even after reading the warning/precaution, and I prefer easier/simpler techniques such as creams, ointments, or serums. I have seen some reviews that state that the clay does not smell. I have to differ on this, as it does smell like - well CLAY! It has an earthy, dirt smell to it. Nothing bad or extreme, but it is noticeable. After using the product for 2 weeks straight - I did not notice much of a difference in my pores. The amount of product that you receive (3 bags) should last for quite a while! I had the leftover in the bowl that I mixed, and I still had 3/4 of a bag left from the one pack. I gave the rest of this bag to my mom and sent the other two sealed bags/packs to a friend.
I received this product in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: i wish i knew how to use ALL the brushes...
text:
I was so excited to receive this set. I already had a brush set from Mary Kay, that I love; but, I it only has 5 brushes.
Since I like to contour and highlight (subtly), I mostly needed brushes for this.
Researching sets produced a huge price range. One could spend upwards of $70.00, with comparable brush sets. Yikes!! This set is much more affordable. The brush handles are solid and bristles are firmly attached. Some brushes are softer than others.

So, if they are quality brushes and the price is reasonable, why am I only rating them 4 stars? I had no clue what each brush was for, and the internet wasn't very helpful:(
If the brushes had been labeled, or there had been an insert explaining the function/functions of each brush--it would have received 5 stars. Add pictures/diagrams for tips on use, even better. I would be willing to pay a little extra for an easy to clean roll-up case for the brushes. A girl needs to keep her brushes clean. That is a feature, I believe many look for. I travel a lot, so my roll up bag (for my other set) is essential.
As it is, Cosmopolitan magazine's website has an article on how to use different makeup brushes. It was helpful for a few of the brushes, which I now use everyday.

What I love:
*The sponges are fabulous for applying foundation and blending after you contour/highlight.
*The large, angled brush is great for applying blush, so it looks more natural.
*The large, pointed brush does a nice job, when adding bronzer to contour.
*The large, round brush is what I rely on for swirling on powder.
*The small, pointed brush is phenomenal at applying color at applying contour eye shadow.
* I use the small, tall bristled, rounded brush to blend the areas of shadow on my eyes that need softening.

What I didn't like:
*Obviously, not knowing what each brush is for.
*The eyeshadow? brushes use too much product and application is sparse. I believe it's because the bristles are stiffer than what I usually use.
*No case to keep them clean, which leads me to look for alternative solutions. Leaving them out in the air, exposed, is a bad idea. Think of the germs in the air, especially if you keep them on the bathroom sink. Eww! Bacteria grows quickly and can cause infections, such as pink eye.
User Tip: I use baby shampoo to wash my brushes. It is gentle on your brushes and it gets the job done.
I received this product at a discount, in exchange for my honest feedback and unbiased review.

Furthermore, this package is a lot bigger than what you usually get in the hair salons. So I think you definitely get your money's worth from this. I was so glad to be able to buy this product while they had a promotion going on. I think this is a great cream for getting that particular look or definition you want. They give you plenty of it too. This is well worth your money. In addition, it does not leave any white flakes in your hair. I have experienced that from other products. Pros:
Unscented
Works just as good as J.Crew product I used to use.

Cons:
A little more crumbly and not as nice to apply (very minor complaint)

The one review I saw that was negative said that the product was difficult to apply, but I think hair wax just can't be applied like hair gel. I thought I might share how I apply hair wax.

How to apply:
1. Wet your hair
2. Wet your hands
3. Take a small finger tip sized amount and rub it between the palms of your hands (like its a cold winter morning)
4. Keep rubbing until the wax turns into a cream which is covering palms and fingers in a thin coating.
5. Work it into your hair moving your hand back and forth through your hair vigorously.

This always gives me good application of the wax while still using a small amount of the product. I used to go through this stuff much faster when I tried to apply it dry and without "melting" it first.

text:
Since COVID-19 I have been cutting my mother's hair. I had been hoping to find a cape that I could protect her clothing while doing the cutting. I was very happy to be offered the opportunity to review this one.

The cape, in general, is okay. This is definitely not a professional quality cape that you find at salons. It's very thin and not waterproof. For dry cutting, it's perfect. This should not be considered for anything involving hair coloring.

The cape is quite large. It definitely serves the purpose of covering the entire body. It also has a nice, silky feel to it.

The fastening clasp is ultra-cheap and I found this to be the most unlikable aspect of this product. The clasps take considerable time to fiddle around with and fasten. It would have been a much better idea to offer velcro or button straps.

But here's the thing: This doesn't cost a lot of money. You definitely get what you pay for. So, if you are looking for something inexpensive for home cutting during the pandemic then this will fit the bill perfectly.

title: Sweepa's better! ..Limp-Uppers & Limp-Lowers = DeCepTive
text:
The upper bristles are limp.
The lower (suction cups) are limp as well.
Limp bristles + Limp suction = junk!
...(compare Easyfeet's limp bristles to the rubber bristles on SWEEPA!
......now why couldn't they have used Sweepa bristles on Easyfeet?

While the concept seems cool when viewing the ads, the reality is otherwise. In chrono order:

(1) First I had read the many poor reviews of easyfeet.
(2) Then I phoned Easyfeet, whereupon the guy insisted that the suction is excellent and the reviews were not true.
(3) So I found a place to buy this cheap, since I wanted them for a senior citizen
(4) Upon receipt I confirmed that the poor reviews proved correct. The suction cups are the kind which are LIMP & SHALLOW instead of "firm/resilient rubber".

Having bought & tried many bath mats over the years, I have experience with both good & bad suction cups. You'd be surprised how many bath mats have flat/limp suction cups. I had bought once a PVC bath mat from a reputable company which had similar limp cups. Upon complaining to them, they immediately replaced it with an identical mat, BUT this time, the model number was different. Because they knew full well that the latter model had deeper/firmer/resilient suction-cups which actually work, instead of shifting around!

(5) Finally, as stated previously, the bristles of easyfeet are a bad joke. (the upper ones) More like the bristles of a baby brush than the type to give a massage, the way the lower ones are. But actually, all of them are sorta scratchy. Instead, they should have used SWEEPA type of bristles. (see online images)

Very deceptive world we live in...

Also, the motor drive coupling has a spring and rubber O-ring to dampen noise and vibration.

title: Favorite Palette Ever!!
text:
I purchased this product in a store, but I am such a fan I had to write a review. Ever since I purchased this palette, it has been my go-to for everyday makeup. I am fair-skinned with dark hair and hazel eyes, and the colors are perfect. I don't always use every color in a palette and I don't always place the colors as directed, but in this case, Stila knows what they are talking about!

The large color on the left is your all-over base, and I apply that first. Next, I go to the top right corner and apply this grayish color from crease to browbone. Third, I take the darkest color and place it quite heavily (but narrowly) in the crease and a little in the corner and lash line. Next, I put the highlight (lightest) color just under the brow and also outside the inner corner of the eye. Finally, I put the shimmery gold-like color in the middle across the lid and blend all the colors with a blending brush. I use the darker blush normally, but use the light one as a highlight if I want the added effect. I love that when I am doing my makeup on the run, I only have to grab this one container and my makeup brushes (I have the EcoTools Eye Enhancing Duo Brush set with four tips on two brushes, so even there you don't have to take as much with you).

The quality of the product is excellent and it blends well. Other than the darkest brown, the eyeshadow pigments are not super intense, so you can go light or apply more for a deeper intensity.

title: I am pleased to report that all of my wishes were granted ...
text:
I purchased this grooming product for my boyfriend, who boasts a luxurious and manly beard and mustache. My hope was that I could cajole him into curling the length of his mustache into a jaunty upturned handlebar style by promising a product that would be effective without being offensive. I am pleased to report that all of my wishes were granted in Wild Willie's Mustache Wax.

The aroma was pleasant and subtle, neither irritating he, who had to wear it beneath his nostrils, nor myself, who inhaled of it's gentle fragrance upon each occasion that I did place my lips to his in affectionate embrace. Indeed after a short period of time, he did declare he was barely able to detect it at all unless he expended some considerable amount of effort into the pursuit. I myself was unable to detect it unless I found myself pressed closely against his person - a position I repeatedly sought out strictly for the purposes of ensuring the quality and inoffensiveness of this product. (A sacrifice I made gladly and would willingly make again.)

In terms of performance, he found the wax to be a most excellent medium to control the curvature and shape of his whiskers. While the wax did warrant reapplying after some wear, and particularly the consumption of liquids, it did not impart flavor upon his beverages, nor did it spoil the taste of foods. It would be worth keeping the container on his person though, should any man wish to enjoy a full night out with his facial hair elegantly sculpted throughout. Indeed, it would be a shame to spend an evening with a sad and droopy mustache.

When I try out a new electric toothbrush, I test it by using disclosing tablets. Using them, you can see the plaque on your teeth, and measure how much your brush leaves behind. This brush removed absolutely nothing. It's exactly like a standard manual toothbrush that buzzes.

The bristles on sonic toothbrushes vibrate in an up and down motion at high speed. They don't move far, but the speed they're traveling at allows them to scrub the surfaces of your teeth very efficiently. My old Sonicare (purchased before Philips bought them out) left NO plaque film behind.

Curious about the Oral-B's non-effectiveness, I held the bristles lightly against my tongue, and could feel no motion whatever. It's as though the handle vibrates, but the bristles remain stationary.

Fortunately, the brush is inexpensive, so I won't feel too bad about throwing it in the trash.

Nice Case. And YES - IT HOLDS THE REMMINGTON BEARD BOSS: Trimmer, plastic height adjusting heads, Charger, Beard Trimming Scissors, Manual and even the Beard Brush that comes with the Beard Boss set. I would describe the Case itself as being semi-rigid - there's a very tiny bit of flex at the center of the bottom and top - but it's more than rigid enough to protect the trimmer inside a suitcase. The area for the trimmer itself is a little narrower at one end, giving it a more "custom" fit, but which also means that the trimmer only fits one way.

Single zipper pull unlike the double zipper you frequently find in other types of cases now, but that is a minor characteristic that really doesn't affect its functionality.

There's also a very small metal ring (about an inch or so) at the end of the zipper run and I'm really not sure what the purpose of that is except to maybe to attach a tag of some sort.

Overall, a nice functional case.

title: Works well IF...
text:
The first time I used this, I could barely get the polish to lift up. I used cuticle oil and a cuticle pusher and I wound up tearing up some of my natural nail. After doing some reading, I saw a suggestion to use a traditional basecoat under the gel peel off basecoat. I thought that it sounded silly, but I was willing to try it, as I wanted to have an easy way to take off my gel polish. I have been using Nailtiques Nail Protein Formula 2 as my basecoat because my nails are thin and then tend to peel. Then I put the gel peel off basecoat over the Nailtiques. After that I polish as usual with whatever color/brand of gel polish I have selected. I used an orange stick to assist with lifting and peeling off the polish when I want to remove it, Following this method has worked REALLY well for me and I have done it 4 or 5 times now. No natural nail lifting up! This also lasts a long longer than when I tried to use UNT. UNT lifted on my nails after one 1-2 days usually. This lasts *easily* 1 week+ for me. Capping the free edge properly is key. I rated it 4 stars because, IMO, I shouldn't have to use a traditional basecoat with the peel off basecoat.

UPDATE 12.6.16: I have found that using an orange stick to assist in lifting the gel polish is a KEY FACTOR in making sure that your natural nail does not lift. I figured this out last night. Additional tips for minimal damage: file down your nails prior to taking off the polish. Breaking the seal on the free edge and then washing your hands helps loosen things up, making it easier to lift. Happy peeling!

text:
Primer, liquid Foundation, BB cushion, and a flat kabuki brush. I have another Phoera kit, and I like it a lot.
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B093GFPFP9

I am not sure if Nude (#102) is the lightest shade they have or not, but if you are like me and have fair skin with cool undertones this may lean a little warm. It isn't bad, but if they had a better match available I would want to get that.
THEY DO!! this is for fair with pink undertones
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07RZ6QZLJ/

My skin is 40+ so this is something I look for in make up.

The primer is fantastic. A LITTLE GOES A LONG WAY. Use less than you think you need lest you want a more oily look to seep through. I find that primers like this are great for dry skin, and for more dry feeling foundations.. but their foundations arent drying. So less is more with their primer.

The formula for the liquid foundation really impresses me. Staying power is good. Skin feels comfortable. Skin looks healthy. I can touch my skin after and it doesn't feel like there is make up on. Provides really good coverage with a little bit yet doesn't look cakey and fake. Can be built up. I would recommend this over dermablend, personally. All my redness disappears (from Type 1 Rosacea). To provide a more sheer wash, just change up your application- use a damp sponge to put it on, or use a damp sponge as last step to blend it in and lighten it up.

I really think it is worth the try. I wasn't even going to try this, but since they provided so much information in their product description it really piqued my interest. If you need coverage with a natural look.. try this!

The bristles are rather short, leaving me to wonder how well the brush will hold up in the long run, but it should last a while..

title: Pretty Simple To Use, Stings A Little, No Issues So Far, Awaiting Potential Results
text:
So far, I have no real complaints about this NIRA Skincare Laser & Hyaluronic Acid Serum Bundle. I’m still at the point where I’m not sure if I can say it truly works because I need to use it for a longer period of time, but I’ll discuss various aspects about the product that will hopefully help with your decision-making.

-Came well-packaged in a small, but sturdy cardboard box. Everything arrived intact. I have continued to use this box for storage of the product.
-Comes with the handheld laser device, charger with base to plug into an outlet, and manual
-No complaints about the battery life so far
-Simple to use: there are two buttons: The power button that turns the device on. Then you can press it to cycle through the various levels of intensity 1-5 which are clearly shown using green light bars. You can then hold the power button down to turn the device off again. The top button can be pressed to activate the laser after you have chosen the level of intensity you want.
-The laser only works if positioned correctly over an area of skin. It will give a single negative sounding beep if not positioned correctly, and a positive sounding double beep if it is positioned correctly as the laser works. You wait to move the device to the next area after you hear that second beep indicating that it is finished with that laser sequence
-The device has a white, plastic outer shell. It is lightweight while still feeling sturdy and durable. I would still be very careful not to drop this as I’m not sure how it could handle a fall
-I would recommend experimenting on the lower intensity settings. The undereye area is pretty sensitive. I feel I have a pretty high pain tolerance, but my eyes often still tear up after using per instructions on the highest settings of 4 and 5. For whatever reason, my left eye is much more sensitive to this.
-I don’t want to say it is truly painful, but I suppose the best way to describe the sensation is almost similar to if you were being stung by a rubber band that you pulled back and let hit your skin if that makes sense. It isn’t comfortable, but you do get more used to this and can work your way up to a higher level of intensity. You will probably also feel some warmth on the skin after using.
-I know this is marketed for under the eyes, but I have also been using on my forehead and by my smile lines.

***The instruction manual is pretty clear and straightforward. You definitely need to read this before getting started. Here is some information that you can find within the manual:

-They say all skin tones and anyone over the age of 12 can use NIRA to reduce the appearance of wrinkles around the eyes
-You need to clean and dry your face just prior to using NIRA
-It can be using morning or night and up to twice daily. They recommend waiting 1 minute before retreating each area and not to treat more than twice within a 1-hour period.
-Do not treat the same spot twice in a row, even if the pulse is rejected and you get the low pitched, negative sounding beep
-The instructions clearly show you the recommended way to treat the undereye area and the treatment pattern to use
-They recommend using the highest power level where you feel warmth without pain
-You should use a facial moisturizer after each treatment and a daily sunscreen with at least SPF 30 is recommended. This bundle includes the hyaluronic acid serum which can also be used.
-Device should be kept clean and free of dust, especially the glass lens which can be cleaned with a cotton swab. Surfaces can be cleaned with 70% alcohol solution between each use.
-They say some potential side effects include: skin warmth, redness, and stinging. Less frequent side effects include dryness, roughness, tanned appearance to skin, swelling, flaking, itching, crusting, bruising, pimple-like rash, irritated skin, blistering, scarring, infection, and skin color changes where your skin may become darker or lighter. I have only experienced the temporary warmth and stinging during use- no redness or anything else.
-The company also cautions those who have skin conditions or are undergoing professional cosmetic treatments such as injectable toxins like Botox or fillers- saying to check with your doctor or clinician prior to using NIRA.
-Only use on intact skin
-Don’t use if pregnant or nursing or undergoing fertility treatments
-Do not use if you have a history of skin cancer, any other cancer, or pre-malignant moles
-Do not treat if you have tanned skin which is apparently at increased risk of adverse effects with light-based devices

Overall, I’m happy with how the product functions and the ease of use. I will continue using and will update if I have any further comments or concerns. I haven’t noticed any real results yet, but I also haven’t been using it that long. One question that comes to mind is this: What is the lifespan of this device? Months? Years? Or does it give out after firing the laser a certain number of times? I could have missed it in the manual, but that is something I’m still not sure of. For the current price of $329, that is something I think people may want to know. I haven’t had any issues with the serum that comes in this package, but it seems pretty simple and basic.

title: Not a bad set but also not fantastic
text:
In this set you get a keratin shampoo and keratin conditioner. Both of them are sulfate free which is great, however when I read the ingredients it turns out that the shampoo actually has silicone in it, not a fan of that. Thankfully the conditioner does not seem to have any in it.

So the shampoo is not bad. The scent is decent, nothing spectacular though just ok in my eyes. It produces a nice lather that rinses out easily. What I do not like is the fact that it has silicone in it.

The conditioner in my eyes is much nicer. The big problem is, the pump dispenser does not work. The conditioner is just too thick and can not be pumped up for some reason. So the suggestion of another reviewer to switch the lids is not a bad one. The conditioner smells much nicer than the shampoo and produces a very nice soft feel on your hair while still wet. It also rinses out nicely.

When your hair is dry it does look and feel very nice. So in combination your hair does look nice when you use this combination, just not sure I am a huge fan of the shampoo in this set. All in all this gets a 3 star for me since the conditioner is pretty good, the shampoo is just below average in my eyes. As a set it may be just a tad overpriced though.

title: Awkward Review Time
text:
So you may be interested in this product to be hairless below the belt. Fortunately the product actually works.
The creators actually put alot of thought into this.

The wooden sticks are used to spread the cream on the hairy area. I found it easier to use latex gloves, but you do not want to rub the cream in your skin. You want to coat the hair at the root. Never use your bare hands, it will smell like the products for hours.

Depending on where you put the cream and your sensitivity will determine on the time the cream stays on. Groin is mostly 8-10 minutes I would say. Any other less sensitive areas would be 4-5 minutes.

When the time is up you will use your glove to remove the hair. I think this is the most genius part of the system. The hand glove is the most versatile tool for hard to reach areas. It is always easiest to perform the task in the shower. When you are done, just rinse and wash with soap.

Overall:
Nair for men has the same results. However, Nair for men smells very foul. This product does have a lighter odor to it.I would recommend cleaning the glove with detergent after each use. Surprising hair does not cling on as baldly has I expected on the glove so washing should not be an issue. I think this is a must buy. If you are on a budget, then nair is the way to go.

title: Vegetal, messy flower balls; not sure why anyone would use this for anything but tea
text:
I thought these were bath bombs when I ordered them. However, that is not what this is at all. There are 10 tiny balls of compressed flowers wrapped in various colored foils. They can be used as a tea, which is what I use them for, or they can be put in a bath. I have no idea how anyone would use this for baking as per the Amazon title.

Nevertheless, all but the purple and red balls have a purely vegetal scent. The purple and red smell flowery. I have used tea balls before and never cared for them but did like how most stayed together. However, these balls expand into many little flower particles that float in the water. If one were to put this in a bath, it would clog the drain unless the flower debris was scooped out with a skimmer.  I used the blue ball to brew into a tea and it was tasteless. I also had to use a strainer and remove the lid on my pot to keep the spout from clogging.

Besides the mess and lackluster flavor, there are absolutely no brewing instructions, no information on what tea ball is what flower.  The Amazon site has a list of the flower and the balls but does not show the foil color. It is almost impossible to reconcile that list with what is in front of me.

Shame on the vendor for not creating an insert or package label that says what is inside and which tea ball is what flower. I personally do not care for this at all and will probably throw this in the garbage.

This is not worth it to me at any price. It is certainly not a bath bomb, I can't see how it can be used for baking, and as a tea it is tasteless and messy. There is no fragrance, so its use as a bath bomb would be for romantic or ambiance purposes only.

At the current price of $9.88 for 10 balls it comes to almost $1 per tea ball.

text: I had mixed results with these 3 products.  The eye patches are gel patches and not meant to be wet with serum - the serum is released by the gel when it's in contact with skin.  The patches easily stayed in place, but resulted in no visible improvements, and left my undereye area feeling a little dehydrated.  The lip patch is also a gel patch.  It was odd to wear, but it stayed on while I moved around and almost seemed to form a suction seal around my mouth after 10 minutes.  I liked this patch - it left my lips smooth and soft for a day and a half...nice!  The foot booties are for moisturizing only...these are NOT exfoliating booties that take days to work and lead to skin peeling.  They were easy to use and comfortable to wear.  I wore them for 30 minutes and was quite pleased with how soft my feet still felt after 2 days.  My only issue was that after removing the booties I had to spend a good amount of time massaging in the lotion left on my feet...seriously, even after trying to dry them with a towel my feet felt greasy.  Be sure to allow time for the product to absorb afterwards and don't plan to run out the door like I did.  For all of this, I would give the set 4 stars.  However, there's an EXCESSIVE amount of packaging.  The patches all have plastic protectors on both sides, are enclosed in plastic clam shells, and are sealed in the final package.  I felt guiltier than usual when I saw the pile of trash I generated by using this set...these items are definitely over packaged.

Overall I found this body scrub to be too oily but works great on dry areas. It also doesn't have a strong scent.

Incredibly durable, very soft, and good for everyday use. There are a variety of options for different products. That being said, there were some brushes that were a total miss in the collection whereas others are my all-time favorite. While I didn't like the flat foundation brush or the flat angle brush at all, I thoroughly enjoyed the round dome brush, the tapered concealer brush, and the angled blush brush!

However, you shouldn't let this dissuade you from buying the brushes. Keep in mind that this review is entirely subjective, therefore the brushes that I listed as horrible may not be so bad for the prospective buyer (and vice-versa)

title: Thick hair, but U-tips are huge for fine hair. Removal breaks natural hair. Please see update!
text:
My once beautiful long hair is finally growing back in from chemotherapy for breast cancer. I had had it bonded by my hair salon about 6 months ago with Cinderella bonds that shed like a cat almost immediately and had hair that was split and damaged before I ever even washed it.

I took a chance on ordering 2-18 inch packs of #613 and 2-16 inch packs of #613 of Sunny hair. The hair looked beautiful and was a perfect match for my own color, but there is no way of telling until it's been washed, conditioned and blown out over a few weeks to really know how it will hold up.

My stylist, who specializes in hot fusion bonds, put in 1 pack of the 18 inch Sunny hair (50 U tips) and one pack of Cinderella hair (25 U tips) 5 days ago. I have very fine hair and a tiny head, so more would not have been possible (this amount also equals a full head of hair for me). We are experimenting to see which hair holds up better.

After one wash, conditioning and blow dry yesterday, the high priced Cinderella hair was tangling in the middle, while the Sunny hair stayed tangle-fee, but did shed quite a bit. The Sunny hair has more weight to it than the much more expensive hair though and combed out better.

One star off for how huge the actual keratin U-tip are and the shedding. My stylist tried to cut some of the tip off with great difficulty. This is an FYI for those with fine hair or those who want to be able to pull it back without the bond showing (the more expensive type has much smaller Keratin u-tips).

I will update this review after 4 weeks in, but for now, I'd like to thank other reviewers for their input as it helped me choose Sunny hair. You were all correct in saying the hair is thicker than most online hair, even though each strand is a bit different in strand width, health and quality. As the industry is unregulated, it's hard to know what you're getting and with blonde hair, just how much processing went into coloring the hair (causing damage).

If my Sunny hair holds up well, my stylist, who does at least 10 hot fusion bondings per month on clients, will be ordering directly from Sunny hair instead of the company that charges $125-$150 per pack. We are both hoping this is the case.

I hope others will try this brand and leave reviews on their experiences. Also, if this is your first time with bonds, please remember on length that it's not going from the top of your head. The lower layers will fall much longer - I'm 5'7 with a long neck and the 18 inch lower tiers fall just a few inches above my waist.

UPDATE: please don't buy this hair if you value your natural hair.
It's impossible to remove the bonds without breaking your own hair.
It breaks, frizzes, knots up like crazy if in a warm climate.
I loved those first packs until summertime. Absolutely awful in heat and humidity. I couldn't get a brush through the hair. It would just snap off. The knots were horrific. I had my hairdresser try to remove and this is more like crazy glue on the bond than keratin.

title: First Acrylic Plate
text:
I was a little skeptical about purchasing an acrylic stamping plate, as all my many others are the usual metal, and I knew nothing at all about plates made from anything else. Moreover, it meant buying a non-acetone polish remover, as acetone (which is used to clean metal plates) is the kiss of death for acrylics. But it wasn’t expensive, so I went ahead and bought a bottle, in preparation for the arrival of this plate. This plate had so many simple designs that I wanted, but didn’t have, like a basic chevron, diagonal lines, vertical and horizontal lines, and gradient dots. I loved the diminutive leopard print, since many of those designs are too big for my tiny nails. And a complete upper case and lower case alphabet?? Count me in!

The plate arrived just a few days before Christmas, so when I got it, I stashed it away, intending to play with it later. Later came today, and I’m in love! I tried out several stamping polishes with it, and most all of the designs. Even the polishes that have given me trouble in the past on metal plates picked up perfectly! The designs are all sharp and distinct. I believe that is due to the depth at which the designs are etched. They are nice and generous, meaning that even the smallest and finest of lines and features come out bold and beautiful.

Clean up is truly a breeze using the non-acetone remover on a cotton ball. And there is no chilling effect from acetone, which tends to dry out your stamping polish on the plate faster.

title: Great company, comfortable patches and worth the $.
text:
I ordered this mainly because of the company, IKIMI. A few weeks ago I had ordered their Hibiscus & Honey firming cream and had absolutely loved it. When I saw this product suggested, I was very interested and hoped I would love it as much. Also I was running low on face smoothing patches so no better time than now to try them out. The price is great, especially for 192 patches (12 sheets). I do not always use a whole sheet as my biggest concern is the y shaped strip for between the brows, as well as the patches for crow's feet. If I run out of my favorites, the other lesser used patches are a good substitute as they still keep the skin taut.
The packaging is very cute and clean looking, instructions are simple and show clearly where each patch goes.
As for the patches they are honestly very comfortable and I forget they are on after I apply them. I usually leave them on overnight, like most people. I would use them in the day sometimes but my toddler is too fixated on trying to peel them off.
These really do work great and will last me a while. My skin is definitely less creased after using them.
You can reuse the patches a couple of times if you are careful which is a plus.
I am looking forward to try more IKIMI products as so far I am really impressed.

I had to keep sanding because I’d test it, feel the area that snags, and then file again. By the time I finished, the whole thing was sanded down and looking awful. Can’t return it now! I used it once it wasn’t snagging all my hair and breaking it off, and it did work. Heat was coming out of the “tips of the fingers” and my roots were dried, and the rest of my hair could air dry in all its undisturbed curl pattern glory. But it was still kind of snaggy and I was just so over sanding this thing as it took way longer than it should have, which honestly, it should have not had to be done at all! title: Good product, excellent customer service!
text:
I'm not new to hair extensions. I've worn them for a few years quite a while ago when growing out a short cut. Once again, I went a little balayage bleach crazy and fried my longer hair which caused a ton of my length to break off. I decided to go this route again while growing my length back out. I have fine hair, but a lot of it, so I got 2 packs. I could probably use a few more for fullness but 20 sets looks fine. My hair is currently color treated dark red at the roots and the color fades to magenta at the ends. I got the light brown to blonde extensions so I could custom dye them to match. The extensions took the dye very well and you can't tell a color difference between my hair and the extensions at all.

The claim that they are thick from root to tip isn't true. Most extensions claim this though and I expected it, so I got longer hair than I really wanted so I could trim it and get rid of the thinning in the ends. I've had minimal shedding so all in all, that is a plus.

They come super straight out of the pack but have some natural wave to them when you wash them. Not a problem as my natural hair does too so they blend well there too. They are soft and as long as you use a leave in oil they will stay frizz free. They hold curl really well too. I curled them and they stayed curled over two days, long after the curl fell out of my natural hair. I've had some tapes separate after install, and removed some due to my own misplacement, but replaced them with tape I had before. Most of the original tape has been replaced at this point so I can't speak to its quality or longevity.

I'm not totally blown away but am happy enough with my purchase to wear them until it's time to replace them.

Edit 6/7/21: I was contacted by Easyouth customer service because my review wasnt a 100% satisfied review. They offered to send me a free pack and provide a discount code for my next purchase to update my review. I will say that they have gone above and beyond what I would expect from a seller. Given I wasnt disappointed in the product, but had a similar experience to what I'm used to from other experiences with extensions. They were very responsive, very quickly. That's something I appreciate.

The new pack I was sent was packaged differently than the two packs I ordered. They came in a branded cardboard box. The extensions were packaged nicely in a plastic sleeve and inside the sleeve the wefts were attached to a thinner paper card and tucked into a little hair net to keep them from tangling. (My first order was just attached to a long, thick paper sleeve.) The hair is still beautiful. I also ordered a halo using the code I was provided. So I plan to dye all of my new extensions to match my natural hair once it arrives.

Thanks for the great product and excellent customer service!

title: The best.
text:
After having used this product for a month, I find myself hooked. As YMMV when taking someone's word on shave gear, I thought I might provide some background about me: I have gentle to oily skin and stiff, tough neck hairs. I used to think I had sensitive skin until I married someone with actual sensitive skin. But the combination of the tough hairs and the gentleness of my skin leads to irritation on the neck when I am not careful. I learned to shave with a gillette adjustable years ago(which I still use), but out of "convenience" (really, a lack of good shaving products and knowhow) I stopped using it for cartridge systems in my early twenties. Since I started shaving right, some time ago, I got an EJ-89 which I use when I'm feeling raw, and an old type open comb gillette (which, for the moment at least, I favor for its closeness- I use personna lab blue blades or sharper in it). I've tried a number of different soaps and a few creams, most of which are good. Mitchell's is excellent. It has a simple, clean smell like fresh linen and is the most thoroughly hydrating shaving product I have ever used. It lathers up easily- I've used my beat up old drugstore boar brush which is now probly 15 years old and a silvertip badger brush.. In either case, the lather whips up in a minute or less with no complications. I'm not one of these people that soaks the puck either, I just heat it up in its dish, in a basin of hot water as I soak my brush and it is good to go. I've heard that water hardness and temp can make a difference with this stuff, but as I have decidedly soft water here in the city, I can't really comment on that. But once you get the lather right, with enough water, it is eaaasy on the face. Amazing even.. I dreamt wetshaving was like this as a teenager..
One might be put off by the price which may seem hefty for a newcomer to the wetshaving game, eager to start saving money (previously lost on walking the cartridge treadmill) and reticent to buy apparently expensive luxury shaving soaps, but aside from being a quality product, It lasts for a quite a while. I was really going to wait until I had exhausted mine to write this review but it's been a month, and the puck looks basically the same size! Growing up on Williams soap and favoring Van der Hagen as a drugstore standby these days, I notice one soap generally lasts me a month (some less than that), but aside from the simply larger size of Mitchells (4.4 oz to 2.5 oz for standard mug size soaps), you just get more bang for your buck. I'm guessing this one will last me three months or more.. So at that rate, the price basically factors out altogether.
To sum up, if you have gentle or easily irritated skin and aren't looking for a heavily scented product, this is the grail of soaps for you. One word: I wouldn't spring for the dish because I am cheap. You might not be.. But the soap itself does perfectly fit a rice bowl or large ramekin, in case you were wondering.. Probably not a mug though, unless it were seriously oversized..

With gel polish, you have to let the polish set into the design for about 20 seconds, scrap, let set another 20 seconds, then pick up the design. You also have to really know exactly where you want to place your design and instead of rocking back and forth, you firmly place down the stamp for the best, most crisp stamp. title: TLDR: Great Gift!
text:
I recieved the green one of these as a belated "birthday gift." Although to be clear, I picked it out and asked for it by link, because parents can be clueless sometimes.

Despite that I was concerned about this item for a few reasons, first being that I've been taught brushes should dry with the bristles pointed down in order to prolong the brush life. The second, which is somewhat tied in to the first, is that I have a variety of brushes ranging from 20+ y/o Arbonne brushes from mom's old WFH days, to the dollar store mermaid tale brushes my own little girls gave me last mothers day after they had destroyed a few of the Arbonne ones. I also have some random singles from Ulta and a couple double ended ones Walmart. All in all there were 13 ends I had to clean, including a spoolie.

I used my Simple brand moisturizing face wash as soap this time (I usually switch between this and coconut or olive oil every other week), and just put a dab of it on each section of the scrub side. Then I got the brush wet, and took it to the scrub side using a swirling motion. I did each brush one at a time and adding soap or water as necessary.

As you can kind of see in the pictures a few hairs from one of my Arbonne brushes got tangled in the scrub side. But other than that it seems like there was far less hair lost over all.

IMO the bottom half of the scrub side worked better for smaller brushes, eyeshadow, concealer, spoolie, etc. Where as the bigger brushes did best on the top half of the scrub side.

When I was done with all the brushes I rinsed the scrub side, shook it off, flipped it over and it was ready to go. To finish up the brushes I gently squeezed out the excess water. Then I pressed them with a paper towel a bit more firmly. Finally I arranged them in the stand in front of a fan. They dried pretty quickly and I haven't had any hairs fall out yet, so I don't think the glue inside was effected. If this changes in the future I'll come back and adjust this review.

All in all, I was pleasantly surprised by this thing. At first the scrub side didn't seem to be large enough over all or section wise, and the brush stand circles all looked to be too large for my brushes. But after having put it to the test, my brushes are cleaner than ever. I even washed one brush that I swore was clean. I was, as the kids say, shook. This thing helps you get deep in the bristles. And while I wouldn't recommend using the scrub side on your sponges/beauty blenders, the stand does well for holding them to dry too and they seem to dry quicker this way which I think has something to do with the fact that air can circulate underneath them.

Finally the brush color change sponge, is fantastic. I tested it out with my most pigmented dark glittery purple eyeshadow, followed immediately by my most matte nude shade. Worked perfectly. It's a great addition to a great product.

My only complaint is that this thing is called bear shaped. Now it may be because mine is green, but I swear it's a frog. But either way, I love it. I think this set, with some brush cleaner and a nice set of makeup brushes would make a great present, especially for a young lady who might not even be aware brushes need washing!

I just wasn't sure how my hair was going to take to it and if it would strip my hair, although it said it wouldn't. The first time I used it, I thought it was ok, but i've continued to use it and I think I'm falling in love. My hair feels so thick and moisturized using this stuff. I don't comb through my hair as i'm afraid of breakage when it is wet, but I am able to put this stuff in my hair and finger comb through it. The win for me is that I can put my Shea Moisture Curl Enhancing Smoothie right on my hair (once the condish has been rinsed out) and it works!! My hair isn't hard or crunchy (well, maybe from the CES and not the Pantene, LOL). I really like the way it makes my hair feel fuller. The product has oil in it, so i'm sure that is what's helping. I want to also try their curl smoothie product which they say gets better results the more one uses it.

Would I buy it again....yea probably.

My only con: the ingredients..YIKES. Some good stuff, but most of the 'bad' stuff is up front in the ingredient list.

title: Barista is the best IMO.
text:
I don't usually write reviews unless I'm reminded by some incentive email, but I had a hard time picking the dude out cologne, so I figured maybe this would help someone. Plus, I love solid colognes.
These are cute in that they definitely follow a wintery theme. Their subtlety is on point. The price is reasonable, so if he doesn't like one or two of them, that's fine. I took one star away because they are a little weird--and I wanted more vanilla, (literally, I was hoping Snow Leopard would have more vanilla). Here is my take on these:
Snow Leopard: Clean, crisp. Smells like dude just took a shower, and is now eating a candy cane in the shower steam. So at first, it's like: why? And where's the vanilla?
Woodland Ranger: Crisp, clean. Smells like a really fresh Christmas tree...and also that shower steam.
Uncle Jack: WTF. Smells like you are hugging a very drunk man in brand new leather jacket...who also just took a shower. Don't wear too much if you're driving. It's interesting tho, and one of the stronger scents.
Barista: Sweet, nutty. My personal fave; I'm probably giving him this one early. Smells like forgetting all your problems as you walk into a coffee house, where they make drinks with whipped cream and coco dust. Remember Barney's Coffee?
All in all, these are subtle yet manly, interesting yet familiar...srsly...I wonder if Uncle Jack has a name's sake. I hope he was a happy drunk.

To preface, I bought this product for when my hands or feet randomly get dry, and it seems I'll have to keep searching for a better product. Ultimately, I discarded this product. I do not recommend this because it did not moisturize my hands or feet. TIP: The best way to know if a product is good for your skin is to use it on your hands, feet, and/or face, since those are the most sensitive and picky areas (skin-wise) of the body. It dried out my hands and feet quickly after use, so I knew it would have the same effect on the rest of my body even if the effect is not as noticeable in other areas.

I tried to use this product when my hands or feet got dry. I like being in cold environments, so I often have lotion or something on standby for when my hands or feet inevitably get dry. Whenever I used this, my hands became dry again after about 30 minutes, when I expect it to last at least an hour like other products I've tried. So I decided this moisturizer is not for me and I ended up throwing this away.

Environmental considerations aside, I did not mind the glitter in the product. I just wish they focused more on the product actually working vs it looking pretty upon application.

title: and they are versatile enough to be perfect all on their own
text:
i am a hair stylist. i work in a busy salon and i always have someone in my chair. i have guests from all walks of life, all ethnicities, and all hair types. quality tools and appliances are a must, something i don't compromise on.

i have used three different types of clips in the salon. i have used smooth metal clips, plastic butterfly clips, and croc clips. the smooth metal clips work well for holding foils in place, but they don't do well for sectioning off large sections of hair. butterfly clips work well for sectioning off hair but not for holding foils in place. butterfly clips are also limited by their size. they come in two sizes but even the larger size isn't always big enough for some sections of hair. croc clips will do everything. they are long enough to hold foils, strong enough to hold large sections of hair (they have the expansion bar that bends to allow them to grip and hold large, bulky sections of hair), and they are versatile enough to be perfect all on their own. with croc clips, i don't have to have some of all the others in my station drawers. croc clips are the other clips all rolled into one. i don't foresee that i will ever use a different clip.

the Rioa croc clips are pretty standard. they are stamped with the brand name of "toni & guy," a well-known name in the styling community. i have purchased several sets of "toni & guy" croc clips from other merchants (including professional beauty supply stores) and the Rioa clips are equivalent to those.

title: Good value, except some of the pins aren't worth it.
text:
These pins are a mixed bag. The double-tined pins are the best. Those pins are long and strong, with a touch of flexibility. One of these keeps my hair up and out of the way without snagging or pulling.

The single pins, are also strong and flexible...just not very long. If you've got lots of thick curly hair as I do, it will take several strategically placed pins to keep things together.

Finally some of the single pins have a raised design that runs the full length of the too-short pin. The problem is that the raised design catches at my hair and pulls. You might get the pin in, and enough of them to hold your hair up, but it may come loose, carrying part of your hair with it, making it harder to reinsert. Intentionally pulling these pins out is just as bad.

So if you are fine paying the total price for the double-tined pins in the collection, it's all good. If not, and your hair is fine with the shorter smooth pins, it's still good.

I do not recommend using the pins with the full length design. Ouch.

title: Great Foundation
text:
I'm 45 and my skin has changed dramatically over the past 5 years. I had to move from loose powder coverage to more of a "foundation" coverage to hid all the flaws. After trying several different products, I came across this product from Avon. So, it's a cream foundation that goes on very smooth. I only apply it in the morning and find that if I don't mess with my face too much, it stays all day. It covers very well. All the little sun damage spots, redness, etc are covered evenly and smoothly. It doesn't look like you have a foundation mask on, but I also apply it down along my jaw line and neck to make sure.

There are two cons to this product: 1) it tends to accentuate fine lines until it settles. I use a magnifying mirror and you can see the make-up in the creases. From farther away, it's not that bad. I also notice that as it settles into my skin, that seems to fade. 2) I have combination skin, and it feels oily on my skin after a few hours. It does not cause breakouts (actually, my skin is so much better since I started using this product), so I don't think it's doing anything, but just feels a little oily. It doesn't LOOK oily, it just feels oily and I can't wait to get home and wash my face. I'm not a foundation user, so this may be typical, I'm not sure.

Overall, I really like this product. The coverage is fantastic and far outweighs the minor "cons" I have listed above. Since I only apply it once a day, on work days usually, it lasts a long time. It comes with a round sponge and mirror compact. It is definitely Avon quality.

title: SO Many Uses For Both Oils! I LOVE Them!
text:
I am finding SO many uses for Shiny Leaf's coconut and sweet almond oil! I do have some experience with coconut oil but this is my first time using sweet almond oil. Thanks the labels on the bottles, reviews and internet searches, I'm finding SO many ways to use these oils...sometimes together, sometimes individually.

Because I have terribly dry, sensitive skin, my main goal was to see how one or both oils could help protect my skin, especially now that winter has arrived and my skin is REALLY taking a beating. Both oils work well to hydrate and moisturize, so I mixed a few ounces of each in a mist bottle. After I bathe, I mist a combo of the oils over my skin to help hydrate and moisturize. The oils absorb quickly and do not leave an oily/greasy look OR feel to my skin. I'm already seeing a decrease in my dry skin/itchy red patches of skin. I experience NO discomfort whatsoever when misting these oils onto my sensitive skin. Both oils also work wonders on hair by moisturizing, hydrating, improving hair texture/strength, stimulate hair growth /thicken hair, and nourish the scalp to prevent dry, itchy flakes. In addition to using my combo of oils after bathing, I also give my hair a spray or two with the mister and sure enough, I'm seeing less hair in the drain and on my hairbrush after brushing. My hair is soft, smooth and shiny WITHOUT looking or feeling oily/greasy from the oil combo.

I use the coconut oil (alone) to help remove makeup, under and around my eyes to soften and reduce fine lines, I rub a small amount into my scalp (as does my husband) to help stimulate hair growth, on the kid's faces after their baths to soften (especially in cold weather!), on my nail beds every couple of days and a light amount on any patches of eczema/red skin. (It relieves the itching/burning and redness from eczema quickly!)

I use the sweet almond oil (alone) on dark circles under my eyes, a SMALL amount on split ends in my hair, a drop on chapped lips, I'm just starting to tinker with it for aromatherapy purposes. I recently learned that it can help fade scars so I've begun to rub some sweet almond oil into a scar on my finger to see what happens. If it helps, I'll then move on to a small facial scar I have. I'm also trying something on my own; just started doing this a few days ago. I get nosebleeds every single day, at least once a day, throughout the winter when the heat is on in the house. This started when I was 2 years old, I'm now 49 so I've experienced this my entire life. I now rub a small amount of sweet almond oil under my nostrils before bed. Since starting this, I continue to have nosebleeds. Yesterday, I had only one and it involved just a few drops of blood. I didn't whip through numerous tissues like normal. ONE tissue took care of it. (that's huge for me!) I have NO clue if its just a coincidence or if the sweet almond oil is helping in any way but I'm going to continue using it.

These oils are phenomenal! Both bottles are 16oz. I love the fact that they have normal caps on them but pumps for each bottle are included as well. The liquid of each is thinner oil than I expected, which I prefer. Both absorb quickly. Neither has a scent. I've found SO many uses for these oils, I can't wait to discover more. ( I'm SO happy with these oils, I recently purchased Shiny Leaf's biotin hair conditioner and cannot wait to try it! ) I find the price to be incredibly reasonable, especially since you're getting TWO bottles of oils! HIGHLY recommended!

*FYI...the mist bottle on the end in my photo is NOT included! I used one of my own mist bottles to combine both oils. You will get both bottles AND pumps that you see in my photo, NOT the mist sprayer!
