title: Works, but you have to have realistic expectations
text:
I have abundant, thick, coarse, wavy hair. I have done it all to tame the volume and sponginess of it, but finally gave up as it was too time consuming. I have very little time to get ready in the morning before heading out to work, so I bought this brush to try it, since I am always looking for a solution. Now the verdict:

It works well as long as you are not looking for a fast miracle. It heats up quickly and and goes through your hair like a regular brush. It dies tame unruly hair and gave me a flatish look very quickly, I went through my entire hair in less than four minutes and my back of the head volume went down and the sponge "pyramid" went down. I ended my few minutes long styling with balm and there! I looked human again and it lasted all day. My hair feels silkier and definitely looks like I spent more time styling it, but not salon styled of course. It suits my needs so I am keeping it. I would say it gives 68 percent flat hair, which is a good result considering the time invested, If you want to look like Hollywood star or the girl in the advertisement of the product, this is not for you, and you will need to go to 30 minutes blow dry and 30'minutes flat ironing if you want flat straight perfect results.

Pros
-Attractive packaging
-It works if you have reasonable expectations
- Fast fair to good results

Cons
- Product looks cheap and chintzy
- The brush's bristles are made out of very hard plastic, ouch!
- No glove included, although the handle doesn't get hot

I am satisfied with the results. Now I can go to work without looking like a mop everyday. Whenever I want my tresses to look flat, I would use my flat iron, but for every day, go and run quick styling, this seem like a good compromise. Hope it lasts as it looks like a cheap price of Chinese rubbish.

title: Close, comfortable, and convenient
text:
Other reviewers have covered just about everything that I would have to say, so let me just add a "me, too" to what I consider to be the most important points.

1) Very, very comfortable shave, the most comfortable I've ever had. (I will qualify that by saying that this is the first electric shaver I've used in the shower, so as far as that type of shaving goes, my experience is limited.) It's not as close as a blade -- almost, but not quite.

2) It's very easy to clean, charges fast, and holds a charge for a pretty good length of time (probably about 45 minutes or so of shaving time).

3) The gel and lotion packs are a neat idea and are very convenient, but they are exceptionally pricey. They're about $1.25 each, and they last only about a week. I do use them when I travel for the convenience, but at home, I use regular shaving gel, and I encourage you to try the same. It saves a lot of money.

4) As with any new shaving technique, you will need to experiment a bit to find out what works at what doesn't as far as direction of motion, amount of pressure, and the like. They do say in the manual that you should give it three weeks, so if you don't like it at first, give it some time and try different shaving methods.

5) I've never actually dropped mine, so I can't confirm or deny whether it breaks as easily as others have said it does, but the shaver does look a little delicate, so being careful is probably prudent.

6) I don't use the trimmer, either, but I can see how having to change the attachment would be annoying, as others have reported.

All in all, I'm very pleased with the shaver. It makes shaving easy, convenient, and even fun -- so much so that, for the first time since I started shaving over twenty years ago, I'm actually shaving every day. For me, that says more about the shaver than anything else could.

text:
I purchased my starter kit directly from Revel, plus an extra color. Since I rely on reviews from Amazon, I'm including mine to help others.
My colors are the first photo-Shady and Starburst.
My first attempt was with Shady and I did a great job on my left hand, but didn't smooth out the right enough. It held up well, but I only got a week out of it because I couldn't deal with the bad job I'd done on my right hand.
The second photo is the second time I did my nails and first time I used Starburst. Glitter is more forgiving. I realized that with two coats of the color, you could still see the white of my nail through it. The second time I used this color, I used a white base (Fresh Cotton from Sally's). This second time is the grid photo with the purple/silver.

From start to finish (with bare nails) this takes about 45 minutes.

Advice:
1-Watch YouTube tutorials. All systems have different instructions, so they might not all apply to your kit. Keep that in mind as you watch them.
2-Let the dip dry before you brush off the excess. I didn't do that before, but employed that advice my third time (purple/silver photo) and it was a better experience.
3-Don't do this without a good buffer. A plain old nail file ain't gonna cut it!
4-I bought nail clips to hold the acetone-soaked cotton on my nails and it works way better than foil. I can do all my nails at once.
5-Before stating dip polish, after washing hands, wipe nails with alcohol pad. It gets all the oils off your nails. This is good advice for regular polish, too.

title: So far I am pleased with this set, having sensitive skin, it works for me
text: First, this Beard Growth Kit, 10 In 1 Beard Kit For Men with Beard Oil, Beard Balm, Beard Conditioner set offers a nice number of items if you are considering a gift this holiday season (or any time). It’s a nice box, again, offers a good number of items for a gift, and is done nicely enough in box set up and presentation it would be well received. Second, the items in it are a good range of “quality” so I think it’ll be appreciated. What I am saying: the brush, comb, bag, scissors, and guard are decent, but not great quality. You can get better quality, but for working needs and for a gift, this is pretty good. But, for example the scissors feel a bit cheaper. But they will get use as long as they cut well enough. I’m not big into using a guard, but this one is like others I’ve had. The included bag is decent, but I’d never use it; if traveling or moving my stuff I’d use a toiletry bag. The brush is not as nice as others I have, but it’s useable and gets the job done. Same with the comb. That brings us to the shampoo, Conditioner, and oil. NOTE: I have extremely sensitive skin, so this review is based on my experience from that standpoint. I like a range of scents or items to keep my beard in good shape, but I have a far more difficult time finding things that work and are okay on my skin. I have only used these items once, but that’s all it takes to know. I come away happy - they all worked and NO reaction. I used the shampoo and conditioner in the shower today and they not only had a nice, light scent, but I was bale to let it sit on the beard for a few minutes each, having no issues with skin and liking the smell. The beard felt soft following and I liked how they worked overall. Next, the oil. I believe it is claimed to be used for “beard growth,” and maybe it’ll help with that. My beard is decent, but I do have spots that could use thickening, so again, I keep an eye open for options. However, there is no way to know if it’ll work for that for a few weeks if not months. So until then, it again did fine on my skin - not a single ounce of negative reaction. The sect is light, so it’s nice to smell, but one (my wife) has to get up close to smell it. I do like it that way, so it doesn’t bug my sinuses or overwhelm. In the end I’m very happy so far with this Beard Growth Kit, 10 In 1 Beard Kit For Men with Beard Oil, Beard Balm, Beard Conditioner set and happy I grabbed it. I’ll use it and if all stays well, would consider getting it again.

title: OMG! I'm in LOVE!!!
text:
Ok...I'm going to try to not write a novel here, but I am sooo in love with these polishes!!! I read a ton on reviews on these peel off polishes and finally chose these not expecting a whole lot. I have 100% no complaints!!! But I will say that I guess it all depends on what you are wanting out of your nail polish. If you are wanting it to last like it lasts on artificial nails... this is not for you. If you are wanting options and to not have to deal with nail polish remover...THIS IS FOR YOU!!!

I have loved painting my nails and having polished nails since a kid. I've always hated nail polish remover. I have thin nails and can't change my polish often because nail polish remover dries my nails out and makes them even weaker and it stinks...even nail polish stinks for that matter.
To make the polish last I've always added a top coat about every day or two and I've learned how to do touch ups that hardly show when the polish on tip of the nail (natural nails) chipped or wore away, so that I didn't have to use acetone any more often than necessary. But it was really self defeating because the more polish I had on, the more acetone I had to use to remove it.
So anyway...I got these little gems in...they are small....but then again, when you compare the price to buying regular polish ( I buy OPI normally ) and the fact that you are getting several colors of these for the price you'd pay for 1 or 2 bottles of decent regular polish, it's not a bad deal at all.
I tried them right away and
#1...they are hardly smell at all! I don't smell them unless I actually hold my nails or the bottle to my nose to smell them.

title: Mother knows best!!
text:
My mother told me never to use a brush on wet hair, because wet hair is weaker and more vulnerable to damage than dry hair, and needs the most gentle touch. Well, for years I was faithful to her advice. But then I strayed…

For the past few years, my newest hair stylist has used a brush to comb out my wet tangles. So when I left my trusty Fuller Brush wide tooth comb at a motel, I had only my brush. I figured “Well, my stylist uses a brush and she must know about these things, so I guess mom was just old fashioned.” But as my hair has grown (now at the middle of my back), I’ve been seeing tangles in the brush, even with the best detangling brush around. I was losing too much hair, but not from the roots (which is normal); it appeared to be breaking at some of the tangles, EVEN THOUGH I did not feel any particular “pull” with the brush.

I ordered this comb specifically because of its claims about detangling WET hair, but wasn't expecting much, except for a replacement of my lost comb. But after the first use on my clean damp hair, I saw only a few long and UNTANGLED hairs clinging to it, and they appeared to have come from my head, as in normal. I didn't see any hair that appeared broken or tangled. The combing was QUICK, easy, and completely without frustration. What more could anyone want? Those funny squiggly teeth DO SOMETHING, but how it works is a mystery to me.

I’d recommend this for any adult with medium to long hair, and particularly for CHILDREN who dread the after-shampoo combout.

SORRY, MOM, you were right all along!!

I'd be remiss no to mention the two products that have done the most for the appearance of my hair over the years. Both are available on Amazon, with terrific pricing on hard-to-find larger sizes of Bain de Terre.

* Bain de Terre Recovery Complex smoothes and conditions hair with only a few drops, adding a healthy look to my hair.

title: Shaves as good as a blade - if you use it right
text:
This is the second 7775X I have owned. The first lasted two years, but this after extensive travel all over the world. It does shave as well as a blade (I use one of those too now and then) if you use it right (see below)

Positives

1) Quick charging - less than an hour to charge.
2) Long lasting - I have used it 10 days without recharging - great if you travel.
3) Seems to prevent ingrown hairs - which is something I run into when I use a blade consistently. My face definitely breaks out much less when I use this razor versus a blade (and I own some expensive blade razors as backup!).
4) So long as you follow instructions (don't press down hard, but when you need to go over an area again, do it firmly) you won't get nicked. Nice when you are in a strange hotel in a strange time zone and waking up jet lagged but needing to look presentable for a meeting.

Negatives

1) A little expensive
2) The shaving lotion cartridges are also expensive - I would just buy a can of regular shaving Gel (eg Edge).
3) Constantly pressing the dispenser for more gel can be a pain in the neck, and you go through those cartridges quickly (one every 10 days at most). If I wanted to redesign this shaver, I would junk the shaving dispensor entirely - I now find it just another moving part with the hinged lid.
4) I wish Norelco had come up with a way for this razor to use a standard charger jack of some kind, as having another electrical cord when I travel (especially one that does not work with multiple corded adaptors such as I-go) means I don't take the cord unless I am gone more than 8-10 days.

To use this right, just buy regular shaving gel, put it on your face, wait 30 seconds for the gel to soften your beard, and go for it. This is the best way I have found to get a clean, smooth shave. Gel in a can also has the advantage of going on thickly (versus the Coolskin dispensor) and not drying up quickly. Also, having a can of the shaving gel when you travel (checked baggage of course) can also come in handy if your Norelco runs out of charge, and you need to switch to that backup Gillette you should have in your shaving kit (I travel with enough cords as it is).

title: The cute isn't a cover up...
text:
A good number of times when you see something as cute as this little bee-esque slicker brush, the manufacturer is covering up a shoddy product and hoping the "awwww, it's SO CUUUUUUTE!!!!!" factor will overwhelm the buyer so much they don't notice and/or care when the product gives up the ghost after only a few uses. So yes, choosing this slicker based on looks probably wasn't the smartest of choices, but in the end it seems to be a good one. This slicker brush is rather nice (and should be for the $20 price tag). It's comfortable to hold. There is weight to it so this doesn't feel flimsy to where the grooming head will break off if you try to comb out a snarl in your pet's fur, or like the body is the thinnest molded plastic they could get away with so it didn't break just removing it from the packaging. Another plus is the end of the tines are tipped/dipped in protective little drops of plastic so the sharp metal ends don't harm your pet. I've always avoided those slickers as they seem like some kind of torture device - how can bare metal ends be comfortable when raked over skin?

For taking care of loose hair, this did a bang up job on our two Maine Coons, including the one who absolutely loathes - and I mean to the depths of H.E. double hockey sticks with a side of utter disgust - being brushed. She was adopted from the shelter as an abused kitty from the home of an older cat hoarder, and whatever happened during her first six years of life there were traumatic enough that she will do her best to eviscerate anyone who tries to groom her long fur beyond the area of her neck. She actually lets us very gently use this on the rest of her back and legs and tail for around 45-60 seconds before flipping out, and that's a big improvement! Who knows, maybe she's as amused by the itty bitty bee antenna as we are, but this is the first slicker brush (even with the safety tipped teeth) she's let us use on her back, sides, and legs. The other Maine Coon (a big chonker of a guy) lays on his back with his legs stretched out and purrs like a race car when he gets groomed, so it's not a surprise that he loves this slicker as well. Cleaning the hair out is easy. Just press the button, the plastic disk pushes up, and the hair is forced off of the tines for easy removal. A few of the finer hairs may stick to the plastic or around the tines, but nothing major. When the slicker gets dirty between the base and the underside of the plastic disk, one of those super skinny reusable straw scrubby brushes and a bit of dish soap does the trick. We clip a wooden clothespin on either side of the plastic disk to keep it raised so the tines can air dry and not rust from trapped moisture. Since the tines all seem to be securely anchored to the base of the slicker head, we aren't too concerned about one being pulled out while trying to work through a tangle. It's still a good idea to check the tines every so often to make sure they are all there, none are loose, and that none of the little safety tips at the end of the tines have come off.

The only thing that could improve this slicker is a price reduction. A pair of googly eyes wouldn't hurt, either.

title: Great e file with a dust collector and light, all in a compact package.
text:
I do my own nails at home, and this item is perfect. When I tried a different e file I learned really fast that a dust collector was essential — the dust got *everywhere*. I thought having everything in one machine would be a compromise, but all three functions work great. The light is nice and bright and I can put it exactly where I need it, for both application and filing. The fan is a little loud (too loud to hear the tv), but I don’t have anything to compare it to and I don’t mind anyway because it does such a great job with the dust.

The e file is way better than the cheap one that is the most popular on here (you know the one). I bought and tried both and kept this one, so I will compare the two. The hand piece on this one is smaller, lighter, with less vibration and it’s quieter too. The speed adjustment is incredibly smooth and accurate, and it will spin at a very low speed. The other one will spin slow but it’s tough to adjust the speed accurately, and the lighted display on that one doesn’t tell you anything. I also like that this one has an “off” position on the rotation switch in between “forward” and “reverse”, so it’s impossible to harm the motor by switching too fast between forward and reverse. The motor is plenty strong too.

If you want a less expensive e file then this is the one to get. If you get a cheap e file and a dust collector separately it would be the same price, and with this one you have higher quality and a lamp too.

title: Fan of Power Toothbrushes for 10 years!
text:
I've used different brands of power toothbrushes for the past 10 years. I started off with the Colgate battery powered ones, and they were good for dorm life but not a longterm investment. These Oral B brushes are great. They have different variations in the $20 price range, and they're great investments but keep in mind the rechargeable battery does eventually poop out (I've had to replace mine about every 2 years). This last part I don't mind because dirty mouths yield dirty toothbrushes! The instructions state that to properly clean after brushing, you need to remove the brushead and rinse under running water.

PROS:
This model has a rubberized grip, 2 minute timer (I didn't brush long enough before), rechargeable, never experienced overheating, since using these brushes my dentist says my gums look great, small enough to get precision cleaning

CONS:
Will most likely need to replace unit every 2 years or so, expensive brusheads (keep an eye on Amazon sales) - I might put too much pressure on my brush but I have to replace a brushead every 2 months although the savings in dental bills make up for that!

If you're new to power brushes, it takes some time to get used to the vibrations, but that's the cleaning mechanism.

title: A wonderful garden that you can plant in your nail art!
text:
I ordered these plates because I love stamping nails. I use the stamps for stamping my nails and also for testing out ideas for new nail art designs.

So finding a set of 5 plates that were well priced like this was amazing. I was thrilled to snap them up. The package was shipped extremely promptly and arrived very quickly after ordering. Everything was well packaged and safe. When I opened it up, everything was separated into their own little zip top bags. Each stamper and scraper were in their own bags and the plates were separated from them by another bag. I really appreciate this because the scrapers have metal blades and I always fret a bit that the plates will be scratched in transit.

First thing I noticed was the metal scrapers, and that was almost enough to drop the star rating. I despise metal scrapers. I have had them scratch up my plates before, so I won't use them. I used an old Starbucks card for scraping instead for this review.

The plates are all a little thin, but they don't bend all over the place, they don't warp or get misshapen through general handling. They do not have the backing of plastic coated cardstock like some plates do, so I absolutely recommend getting a plate storage device of some kind. I have a little binder style one and these plates fit easily into the sleeves.

I did test out all three stamping heads on the stampers that came with the plates. The stamping heads are very firm. VERY firm. They are not my favorite, however, they picked up well and transferred the images pretty easily most of the time. There is a learning curve with stamping and sometimes an image just doesn't pick up. I did experience that a few times, but I experience that with most plates at least once or twice. All of the images that I tried picked up very well with the stampers that came with the plates. I tried both unprimed and primed. I would recommend testing first and see how they pick up for you. I think mine would have been just fine with a quick wash in warm soapy water and not much else in the way of priming.

All the images that I tested out worked very well. I really love the goldfish and the frog images. There is a huge selection of plants and flowers, and it's not a preponderance of roses like with so many plates. I really love the ivy and there's an image of strawberry plants (no berries, just the leaves and a flower, I think.) There are quite a few butterflies, but not just one style. There are several styles of butterflies. So I really enjoyed the plates, they will definitely be regulars in my nail art.

The stampers won't be tossed, but they won't be my go to stampers. I like slightly softer stampers, and I admit a definite bias towards my clear jelly stamper. :)

Is this a good buy? Yes. The plates are beautifully engraved, and make for a lovely set either for a beginner or someone just looking to expand their collection of plates. There are a lot of images to choose from, and while the images are not full nail for someone with really long nails, they are full nail images for a more average length and a moderate length nail. Most images are about an inch tall, and I had no trouble filling a swatch nail with the frog image. If I have friends who are looking to start a stamping plate collection, they will be pointed here for sure because I really do like the plates and the images and the quality.

And THAT is why metal scrapers couldn't take away a star from the 5 star rating. Because I have a large collection of stamping plates and these are a fantastic addition. I can get rid of the metal scrapers and use my regular scrapers and no harm done.

I did receive these plates at a discount for consideration and review. However, this does not impact or affect my review in any way. This is my honest opinion on this item.

title: Perfect for beginners with small hands.
text:
I’ve tried a couple e-files in the past, all of them have been a bit too bulky for me to properly hold. I always wondered how everyone managed to use e-files with ease, and didn’t fumble because they didn’t have a good grip. It always felt like I didn’t have a good hold of the e-files and it just made them hard to use properly. I never really thought I had small hands until a friend of mine suggested I look into slimmer e-files. Honestly, it seemed the slimmer e-files were more expensive so I just gave up and stuck to handle filing everything. Until recently when I came across this e-file... It’s been game changing for me.

The first thing I will say is it is SLIM and small. THANK GOODNESS! It’s so easy to hold and properly use. Which leads me to the next great thing about this e-file, the fact that it is small and slim doesn’t effect its performance at all. This things is very strong and fast. As many of you know, you’re not supposed to use your e-file on it’s fastest speed unless you absolutely need to. So when this e-file gets the job done even on its slowest setting, it’s just amazing. I’ve tried e-files that had little power, so I’m thrilled that this one is so powerful. There’s a dial on the cord that controls the speed. There’s also a switch that goes from off to on, and reverse. It also comes with two sets of bits. Both come in their own containers. You also get a dusting brush and two extra bags of sanding bands. Considering some bands can be completely shot after one full set of nails, it’s nice to be supplied with extra! To change out the bits, you just put the metal post of the bit into the hole, and push it down until you feel it’s securely in it. You don’t have to twist or lock anything into place. The bits stay securely in place while filing despite not actually being locked in place. To remove the bit, just pull it out (it doesn’t come out easily so you will have to pull a little).

I’m still very much a beginner with e-files because I never had luck with any before this one, so I can honestly say that this e-file is perfect for beginners. I had no issues with learning how to use it and Controlling it. It’s made filing and shaping my nails so much easier. I use builder gels, gel polish and dip powders. This e-file has worked wonderfully with all of those, when it come to filing, shaping or taking product off. It’s been wonderful and game changing for me. I love it and would recommend it to everyone.

The only downfall is it is powered by a USB cord. The outlet plug is not supplied so you will need one of those, but everyone has them laying around somewhere (iPhone outlet plugs). The instructions give a wattage requirement for the plug. I use my iPhone one and have had luck with that. But that Means you need to be by an outlet or power cord. Switching from hand to hand can be annoying with a cord in the way. I do think I will be upgrading to a wireless e-file down the road. But for now, this is great.

I am not a beautician or barber, just someone with 2 dogs needing regular clipping. I remember seeing this product or a similar one in barbershops where my Dad would go to get a haircut. It was in a good-sized flatish round jar and the barber would dip the tip and bottom of his clippers in it while running and they would come out shiny and hair free. Now the jar looked like a pot of disease waiting to get passed on to the next customer as it had floating bits of hair and residue from who knows what.

I had been cleaning and oiling my clipper blades after each grooming and using a coolant on them during clipping to keep the blade's surface from getting too hot. Cleaning the blades afterwards never seemed to get all the hair from between the teeth even using a tooth brush and sliding the two blades back and forth. This stuff really CLEANS all the hair off and you can hear that the blades are better lubricated by the reduced noise. I do wipe them quickly so as not to drip any of the H42 onto the dog. They are shining and humming pleasantly after dipping them into this stuff. I will continue to buy this product as I feel it will extend the life of my clippers and make for a better cutting blade.

Now for the down side and why I took off one star. This stuff still comes in the good sized flatish round "tub-like" container and is seems intended that you dip the blades (not the motor, just the blade tips and bottom) into the whole container full and continue to reuse this stuff over multiple cuts. I don't care if it is Virucidal and Anti-bacterial, that seems like a really unclean way to use this. I solve this problem by pouring a small amount into another container (at least 1/4 inch deep) and dip my clippers in that. I discard the stuff after each groom. Unfortunately the container it comes in does not pour without dripping and yes, you use more of this stuff using my method. I continue to use oil and coolant, but this stuff truly cleans off the bits that get between the teeth and seems to get the blades running much smoother. I do recommend this product, but not for using the reservoir full repeatedly over several cuts or clippings. That method just doesn't sound like a healthy way to go. So if you use clippers on humans or dogs, I feel this product may be of use to you.

title: Great starter lamp for people getting into gel polish.
text:
Why all the hate and bad reviews? This lamp is the price of a Chipotle burrito (for context). This is basically the same lamp that comes with the Madam Glam Gel Kit (which costs $35 if you buy it separately on Madam Glam, this one just doesn't have the cute designs on it).

I wanted to make sure I liked the gel polish system but I didn't want to spend a ton of money on a lamp until I knew I liked the gel system. This is nothing fancy: turn it on, it lights up for 60 seconds then turns off (30 seconds will be nice but that's what your phone timer is for). USB powered so the short cord is a non-issue for me (always close to a computer and you can use your portable cell phone battery charger to power this). It's small, but I have small hands so no big deal. You can't get your whole hand in there, but it do both my thumbs last. The polish cures in 30-60 seconds (depends on what your polish says), works as advertised.

The short cord and the small sized are its weak points, but the price makes up for all that and I can live with the flaws. Since this is so portable, this is great for mani/pedi parties with your girl/guy friends, or use as a back-up lamp.

text:

at first i was confused thinking i ordered a 12 or 14 inch by mistake but then noticed that the manufacturer bag it’s in and the amazon sticker both say 24 inches, and checked my order and the description and the price matched the 24 inch as well. plus a 12 or 14 inch option isn’t even available right now! so i know i purchased the correct length.

i’m super disappointed because my birthday is this weekend (the day before halloween) and i had planned to use this wig for both days’ celebration (and again in the future). obviously that plan is out the window and i’m getting ready as i type this to go to the wig store and pray they have a similar one for my look! either way it’s gonna be way more expensive than this one which sucks. i already paid my hairdresser a deposit for the wig install tomorrow so i cannot wait for a new one to come in the mail.

this bad mistake aside, i will say everything else about the unit is as described, the hair is natural and soft, has a nice natural curl to it and no odor, it is a really natural looking piece that would probably look great once washed and styled. the hairline is pre-plucked with baby hairs as advertised so you could probably wear it without too much customization. the knots are small and more natural looking. the lace is not true transparent lace but very light like the other reviews have mentioned, and of good quality, it is 360 degree lace with combs inside so it probably fits well too ( i didn’t bother trying it on since im returning but it looks more secure than others i’ve bought in the past ). the wefts are sewn in well and gives the look of naturally thick hair without being too voluminous and wiggy. it does seem prone to shedding though so that’s a downside. if i didn’t need it by saturday and my install appointment tomorrow i would maybe have replaced instead of returned because it looks to be a good quality wig. but this is a huge mistake that i can’t overlook if i’m paying $300.

I started by putting the wrap at the top of my head, claw clipped it in place and moved strands of hair from the back of my head, underneath to the front and combined it with strands from the front, then continued to wrap the strands of hair around the wrap. I repeated this on each side until I was done. I used the hair ties at the ends to secure my hair in place. Getting strands of hair from the back to the front in sections can be a little complicated. I finally broke down and decided it was time to get a power toothbrush. I decided to go with the Oral-B over the Sonicare per dentist recommendation. I am very happy with the decision.

It does take a little time getting used to brushing with a power toothbrush over a regular one. You have to get used to letting the toothbrush do the work. You also have to get used to the pulsating action, it can feel a little weird the first couple of brushes.

I have been working on brushing for the full 2 mins, I don't find it that hard to do. It goes by pretty fast for me. I use the toothbrush's built-in timer.

I also don't have a problem with the toothbrush heads. I find I can reach the back teeth easier with this than a manual toothbrush. It is really not that uncomfortable for me either.

One thing I found that is an added bonus with this toothbrush are the "Made in" stampings on both the toothbrush and the charging base. I prefer to purchase as many things as I can that are made in America or Germany. It turns out both this toothbrush and charging base are made in Germany and not China.

title: which is very nice, and the scent is subtle
text:
I'm a hair dye junkie, and I've dyed my mohawk almost every color in the crayon box. I heard of Iroiro through an Instagram ad, touting its "all-natural" formula. Since I'm always game to try a new dye brand, I gave it a shot.
Pros:
1. Scent - It says "Yuzu-cranberry" on the packaging, but it smells closer to a fruit punch-bubblegum hybrid. Either way, no plasticy nor ammonia smell, which is very nice, and the scent is subtle.
2. Thinkness - This has a thick opaque cream consistency slightly thicker than Manic Panic or Jerome Russell Punky Colors. No drips nor runniness! This can be used in large-mouth dye bottles, but the bowl&brush method works best.
3. Longevity - My hair is thin and porous, thus dye fades to pastel usually within ten days (even with sulfate-free shampoo and every-other-day washing). Ten days after using this dye, my hair is still a nice royal purple with only slight fading. That surprised me.
4. Conditioning - This dye has coconut oil as a conditioner, so I was concerned it'd make my hair greasy. Nope! Hair came out soft and nicely conditioned with very little limpness.
5. Color Match - The sticker label on the front suggests Iro Violet is a royal purple with a hint of dark blue; I applied the dye to bleached (level 9) hair. The end result looked like the sticker color. So, no color shift here. It will appear slightly different on non-bleached hair, but that is expected.
Neutral:
1. Packaging - The pouch is quite light, plus it does not take up much shelf space when stored upright. So far, the tip does not clog. However, the cap is difficult to open at first, you can't put the dye back in the pouch once it is out (measure carefully!), and the instructions are in a very small print.
2. Heat Requirements - The instructions say that, for best results, heat should be used neat the end of the hair dying phase. I didn't use heat, but left the dye in slightly longer than the instructions. Have a blow dryer handy.
Cons:
1. Staining - This stuff is HIGHLY pigmented, so it will stain anything it touches. Wear gloves!!! Only Splat! stains worse than this dye. You need to cover work surfaces with plastic or else you'll have permanent purple spots everywhere. I even had issues removing staining from my skin, even with rubbing alcohol! It will also permanently stain pillowcases, clothes, towels, and bath mats. Also, I don't recommend rinsing in a tile or porcelain shower or sink because of high stainage; use a laundry sink, steel sink, bucket, or other slop sink area.
2. Rinsing - This stuff takes a bit of time and effort to rinse out, and you still will get dye-tinted water with every hair wash. This dye isn't as notorious to rinse out as Splat!, but it takes longer than Manic Panic or Punky Colors or Pravana.
3. Extra Equipment - This comes with just the dye pouch. You will need your own gloves, dye bowl, dye brush, clips, shower cap, and foils (if you are doing highlights).

Overall, this is an excellent dye for experienced hair dyers, but may be a bit tricky for dye rookies. For an all-natural hair dye, this was surprisingly great! I just bought Iro Pink and I hope it is as good as Iro Purple.

title: Norelco Quality Going Downhill
text:
The Good

9170XLCC gives an excellent shave in about 5 minutes. It'll take about 2 weeks of daily use for your beard to adjust to the razor heads, but after that it's as close and clean as any blade shave.

The Bad:

1. It's cheaply made. Norelco has outsourced manufacturing & it shows. The frame holding the razor heads is plastic; every other Norelco I've owned (over 30 years) has been metal. The frame is supported by these weird plastic-bubble "shock absorbers" that will probably go in a year or two. The shaver has a junky, cheap feel to it. I have always gotten 5-6 years of use out of my past Norelcos; this one feels like it'll last about two years.

2. Cleaning tank is a marketing gimmick to sell $[...]/bottle cleaning solution. Way overkill. It does work OK, but the shaver gets just as clean if you rinse it under hot tap water (which you will have to do anyway because the cleaning solution leaves the razor heads coated with a slimy residue). You can pretty much throw it out after the free bottle of solution is used up.

3. I'm already on my second unit. The chip that controls the battery level indicator, recharging, etc. is flakey. The first one I had never could accurately display battery level even after 3 complete charge-discharge-recharge cycles. It'd show 15-20 minutes remaining, then just die in the middle of the shave; battery tapped out. Also, it would sometimes illuminate for no reason at all; had to turn on-off to clear it. If it happened during the night, the battery would be fully discharged by morning. So I returned it to Amazon.com (thx Amazon for great customer service!!!).

The second one that they sent to me recharges continuously when you use it with the cleaning tank -- it's not supposed to charge during the 55-minute cleaning cycle, but mine does. That means that you have to catch it about 5 minutes into the cycle, after it's done it's dunking in the tank, or it'll recharge completely after every shave (which the instructions tell you not to do because it shortens battery life). More reason to toss the cleaning unit. Ridiculous on a shaver this expensive that they'd ship junk to their customers before fixing these problems.

4. The travel case is worthless for protecting the shaver on the road. It's nothing but a zippered nylon sack. You'll have to put the shaver into something else if you pack it in checked luggage or it'll be a pile of parts when you unpack.

5. They don't include a stand so when you're done shaving you lay it on the bathroom countertop. I'm using the one from my old Norelco, but if you don't have one, storage between shaves is just setting it down somewhere.

Sad to see a fine old company like Norelco cheapening it's flagship product like this. I've been a customer for 30+ years, but next time I'm in the market for a shaver I will definitely comparison-shop the competition.

Two stars because it does give a good shave; the rest is a mess.

title: Much better then the Sonic Spinbrush by Arm & Hammer
text:
Until a year ago, I never liked the idea of owning an electric toothbrush: I'd owned several cheap ones and never liked any of them. Then I figured that I'd try one again about a year ago and so I chose the Sonic Spinbrush by Arm & Hammer. I chose the Spinbrush because it had a large brush, which I thought meant less time/effort brushing my teeth.

The Spinbrush worked pretty well, but the large brush head gagged me horribly. Because of this, I decided to give the Oral-B Vitality a try and I like it much better. The first reason I prefer the Vitality is because it has a much smaller brush head (you don't need a large brush with an electric toothbrush, since the toothbrush is doing all the work.) The smaller brush head also allows me to reach places the larger Spinbrush cannot reach, because it's too big. The Vitality is easier to maneuver in your hand as well, thanks to the smaller handle base.

Another thing I didn't like about the Spinbrush is how it would click off automatically after 2 minutes (I don't think all models of the Spinbrush do this, though.) The Vitality purposely sputters after 2 minutes for it's timing function, but then continues it's normal operation after a second or two. I still find this annoying, but at least I don't have to remove it from my mouth, dripping with toothpaste, just to turn it back on. And if I finish early, the Spinbrush required me to punch the button twice to stop it (again, something not easy to do with a vibrating toothbrush in your mouth), whereas the Vitality only requires a single button push. These two things alone make the Vitality much more convenient.

I also think the Vitality is more powerful then the Spinbrush. The reason you had to push the button on the Spinbrush twice was so you could use it at a lower speed if necessary, but I never found that necessary at all. I prefer the more powerful Vitality, because it feels like it's cleaning better by not slowing down if I push too hard.

About the only thing I liked better about the Spinbrush was that it had an indicator light on the base to tell you it was receiving power (I think it gauged the charge, too, but that was never a problem for me.) I'm not sure if that's even important, but it is something I tend to prefer with rechargeable items. Other than that, I love the Vitality and I much prefer it over the Spinbrush. Now I can brush my teeth without gagging and I am thankful for that.

title: Same Results as Dunking in a Bowl of Water
text: If you're a dog owner, its practically guaranteed at some point, you will have to deal with your dog having dirty, muddy paws. Happens often with our bichon Mac. (Naturally, it recently happened right after I cleaned and mopped the house! lol)  I ordered the Mr. Ros automatic cleaner for small/medium dogs. Its very sturdy and durable, not at all flimsy.  Its roughly 8"tall  and has a removable mat with silicone bristles in the interior which is easily removable for cleaning purposes.  The bristles are very soft and not at all hard or sharp. It arrived already charged. A USB cord is included. To operate, simply add water to the washer-(2-3 cups per instructions) Liquid soap may be added as well. (I didn't use soap) Turn the washer on-it does make noise though its  not terribly loud at all-and place the dog's paw in the washer for 1-2 minutes. Dry each paw with a towel after cleaning. Mac wasn't thrilled throughout the cleaning process but he also wasn't really scared by it. My husband started to pour out the dirty water before I could stop him so you won't see much,  but you can see in my photo the water is discolored a bit following the cleaning.  If a wet towel isn't enough to clean Mac's muddy/dirty paws, my regular cleaning method is to put some lukewarm water in a small bowl , dunk each paw one at a time and use my hand to remove the dirt from his fur while submerged. Quite honestly, I really don't see much of a difference between that cleaning method and the Dr. Ros paw washer. Perhaps results vary depending on the breed of dog but for our bichon, I really don't see a  difference.

title: Relatively strong water flosser but reservoir is attached which makes drying it nearly impossible
text:
I have used various countertop water flossers in the past such as the countertop WaterPik and the [[ASIN:B07HRNGS3Q Truwell Handheld Water Flosser]]. I love the idea of a hand held irrigator and this does work to remove most stuck debris from between the teeth. What is nice about this one over the other handheld I tried, is that there is very little splash back. However, I personally do not like that the reservoir is not removable for drying.

IN THE PACKAGE
- One reservoir attached to handheld flosser unit
- One USB cable (wall adapter NOT included)
- One instruction manual
- One standard jet nozzle
- One orthodontic nozzle (larger brush)
- One pocket nozzle (smaller brush)
- One tong scraping nozzle (what looks like a spoon)

I charged the unit fully before use. The white light on the side blinks when charging and remains steady when it is fully charged. Note the charging port is hidden behind a silicone nub below the grip dots on the top of the unit. Be careful to cover the charging port with this nub when the flosser is in use.

There is an on/off switch and a mode switch. The three water pressure modes are soft, standard, and massage can be cycled through using the mode switch prior to turning the unit on. The jet tip (or any of the other three tips) gets inserted into the top. Be careful to make sure it is seated with the notch in the groove as the first time I put it in the hole, I did not have it seated all the way. To eject, press the release button to the left side.

The reservoir IS NOT removable. Instead water enters through the small opening on bottom through which one has to fill the unit. I do not like that the reservoir is attached as I have to drain the remaining water out of that hole and leave the door open for drying. Also, the little button through which the water enters can easily break after lots of use. I personally would prefer not to have to use that hole.

I held my mouth almost totally closed during use and tried all three modes. I did not have splash back, which was very nice. Splash back is usually typical of almost any type of water flosser so to some extent I was surprised. This flosser does work to dislodge most debris between teeth but not everything because it is not super powerful but is powerful enough. I am also impressed that the manual is relatively well written; kudos to the manufacturer on this. Normally, I feel as if I am reading Pig Latin when I receive products from China or other countries.

In summary, my biggest disappointment with this unit is the attached reservoir that prevents me from drying this out easily.

title: Isopropyl-based hand sanitizer that meets both CDC & WHO guidelines
text:
Much of the hand sanitizer we have been using is ETHYL alcohol (ethanol) based. THIS sanitizer is ISOPROPYL alcohol based. Note that historically most hand sanitizer has been based on isopropyl alcohol whereas ethanol has been used in things like alcohol that you drink of as a gasoline additive for oxygenated fuels (for environmental purposes) as well as other purposes. Isopropyl has been used in hand sanitizer and "rubbing alcohol" among other things. Both are now approved for use in hand sanitizer. Ethynol-based sanitzers are becoming much more common due to high demand and supply constraints on Isopropyl-based sanitizers.

The interesting thing is that the CDC and WHO have different guidelines for hand sanitizer effectiveness for these two types of alcohol:
CDC: Ethyl - at least 60%, Isopropyl - at least 70%
WHO: Ethyl - at least 80%, Isopropyl - at least 75%
You can see that it is interesting that the CDC recommends higher concentrations of Isopropyl whereas WHO recommends higher concentrations of Ethyl. Curious. Rather than dig into too many details on the difference, the easiest thing is to find a way to meet both...

The most common ethyl alcohol hand sanitizers that we have been getting (and the most common out there) are 70% -- which exceeds CDC 60% threshold, but is below the 80% WHO threshold.

THIS SANITIZER has an ISOPROPYL concentration of 75% which exceeds the CDC 70% threshold and meets the WHO 75% threshold.

Clearly these thresholds are not hard limits as indicated by the difference of opinion between CDC and WHO, but it is mildly comforting to meet both recommendations if you can do so with no downside or extra expense.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Easily squeezes out of bottle in controlled amount as a gel
* Rubs in easily and absorbs within less than a minute to leave no noticeable residue or tackiness on your hands
* Aloe helps to keep your hands moist, fighting the drying effects of the alcohol
* Small bottles are easy to take in car, backpack, purse, etc.
* Scent is minor and dissipates quickly (we're not using this for its smell after all)

SUMMARY:
A cost effective way to keep you hands sanitized when you can't use soap & water. Meets both CDC and WHO guidelines for effective hand sanitizer formulations.

title: An All-Natural Pain Neutralizer that gets 2 Thumbs Up in our experiences and home
text:
Let me first of all say that Pain is the body's way of telling you that something is wrong, and that you should respond with a treatment that behooves the problem. Don't expect this product to miraculously heal something that is broken or badly sprained. However, you may have good success temporarily "erasing" the pain from over-use of muscles or whatever, and may allow you to be able to sleep when that is not possible without having applied it. As you heal when you're sleeping, this can be a real advantage.
The body can quickly learn to expect a continuation of pain from a minor problem, and it will linger on and on, even becoming chronic as you change your posture or gait to accommodate the ache or pain. My experience has been that if you can reduce the pain even temporarily (especially) in acute situations, it may break the cycle and never return. People we have spoken with have also experienced relief with chronic aches and pains.
In addition, some users have reported that it is effective with masking the pain of fibromyalgia.
Some reviewers here have complained about the smell - duh - it's from the natural oils. I think it is a pleasant smell, but it is a bit oily, so if you put it on before going to bed, give it some time to soak in, and cover it to reduce the amount that transfers to your sheets. You may also want to use less than more and will find that a little goes a long way. And - oh yes- it won't cause you to fail a drug test as many OTC remedies do.
I have used this product personally for more than 10 years, have given it to older family members, and given dozens of the towelettes to strangers who were in dire need of quick relief - never with a complaint. I strongly recommend it with the above caveats.
One size doesn't fit all, but if you are one of the vast majority that are not allergic or bothered by any of the natural oils used in its manufacture, you may find comfort and relief in what it can do for you.

title: Works well
text:
My usual sun protection is avoidance. I have sensitive, allergic, rosacea skin. I'm allergic to most chemical sunscreens, so decided that I would make my own this Spring. Actually went to a presentation by one of the big mlm essential oil companies, because they were going to present recipe for using EOs in a natural sunscreen (later research told me that EOs don't have sun prevention qualities.) The bad news is that the presentation was appalling (safety and lack of ingredient knowledge), the good news was it made me do research and take two online courses from a reputable online aromatherapy institute. One of which was a Butters & Balms course. Make a lot of my own skin products now. I had previously ought all of the ingredients to make my own sunscreen, but then decided to buy some to see how it worked for me. It did. Got one on Etsy. It was fine. There were some times during the summer that my skin was so awful that nothing wouldn't have upset it. It's a firmer consistency, I used it MANY times and barely made a dent in the jar. Bought a natural sunscreen lotion on Amazon, it had an SPF of 32. Because it contained so much of the zinc oxide, it made my face chalk white. The Tropical Sands Sunscreen only has an SPF of 8, so no white face.

The Tropical Sands All Natural Sunscreen is a lotion consistency. I'm not ready to make my own products with a water base because they need a preservative system. Lotion is easier to apply and make sure you cover the body parts completely. Probably a better consistency for sunscreen. The bottle is 8oz. It recommends application every 40 minutes if swimming or sweating. Even with the frequent application, it should still last a while. It's also the most reasonable price of all the ones I've tried.

Many sunscreens that contain non nano zinc oxide or titanium dioxide call themselves "nearly natural." Did some research because I thought they were chemicals, they are minerals. They provide a physical block rather then a chemical block. The biggest problem with the products that contain mineral blocks is that they make your face white--the more minerals, the whiter your face gets. Before the rosacea, I was light skinned, but not that porcelain white. It's December and while the weather is warmer then normal, it's not suntan weather, so my face doesn't have any other color. The Tropical Sands was fine, didn't change my skin color.

As with any new product on my face, I did a sample application. Put a little on the side where my hair would cover a reaction. It didn't make my skin reactive negatively, so I tried it on my nose and cheeks (most reactive part of my face.) I didn't have a negative reaction there. I'll definitely have to experiment with it during the prime sun time because there are times I have to be out in the sun.

I received this product at a discount for an honest review.

This is my go-to palette every day! I specifically use the bronzer, blush, and highlight on a daily basis. The eyeshadows are only for when I have extra time and want to look more made up, but the 3 top colors are perfect for everyday wear.

If you're a beginner to contouring like I am, you'll appreciate the bronze powder in this compact that will easily start as baby steps for contouring. Just grab a small contouring brush and dab it in the bronzer, make a goldfish face and sweep along the sucked in cheeks line. It might also help to do a sideways 3 on the side of your face.

The blush is a very cute peachy pink color that works well with my skintone and lasts a long time. I used to use a cream blush but it was really messy. I love the staying power in this blush!

The highlighter is also amazing where you can dust along your cheekbones, under eyebrow, and the bridge of nose to bring out your features. I haven't tried strobing yet, and I think this highlighter would be too powdery for it. But still a gorgeous color for normal highlighting.

The eyeshadows themselves are pretty pigmented too. I use both this palette and the NAKED ones from UD and I like both.

The packaging is also gorgeous and is well-made. I have brought this on my vacations, and all I need extra is foundation, eyeliner, and my eyebrow pencil. LOVE this palette.

title: Fantastic quality matte black lipstick, with great depth that lasts
text:
Thick, velvet smooth and beautiful, this lipstick is some of the best I've ever tried. This stuff is very similar to Wet n Wild's "Mega Last" lipstick, which is also excellent -- the texture is almost identical and so is the lifespan, up to a couple hours if careful before reapplication is needed to keep the colour full and deep. The "Pagan Angel" black is stunning and rich, and it builds well onto the lips for full coverage. The taste and smell is completely neutral.

I really, really recommend this lipstick.

You might be hesitant to try this stuff if you've ever used the "Fantasy Makers" black lipstick, a Wet n Wild Halloween/Costuming sub-brand, which doesn't build at all and shows through your natural lip colour a lot, has an odd smell, and doesn't last -- but their main brand lipsticks are worlds better.

The "Fergie" black lipstick is the best black lipstick I've tried so far, I can't recommend it enough. If you find that you like the "Fergie" branded lipsticks, definitely try Wet n Wild's "Mega Last" as well, it's almost identical with a different line-up of colours.

title: Weightless, Skin Feels Silky, Makeup Lasts Longer, Blurs Lines-Odd Smell, Skin Gets Weird Sensation
text:
This Grown Alchemist Anti-Pollution Primer has a gel texture that feels weightless on my skin. This doesn’t have a lot of ingredients and lacks chemical fragrance, but I find the scent is moderately strong. I assume it’s mostly from natural lavender, rose and grapefruit oils. I really don’t love the scent as it smells odd to me, but it mellows out and doesn’t really bother me. The lavender and grapefruit oils are potential irritants, but my sensitive skin hasn’t had any visible reaction or real discomfort using this primer.

I have dry skin and when I apply the primer my skin feels a weird initial sensation that reminds me of alcohol, but so far it hasn’t caused any visible dryness. I do always apply a hydrating essence, serum and cream before the primer and I see the primer has glycerin, so that may be why I don’t see dryness or maybe something in this just feels mildly irritating to my skin. This does have benzyl alcohol pretty low on the list, so maybe I’m feeling that but the good part is that I haven’t had any real issue. I can’t say if daily use might dry my skin.

This primer is super lightweight, so sheer it’s invisible and I don’t feel any sticky residue. It makes my skin feel silky, and my cream and liquid foundations spread smoothly and evenly over it. I do notice a blurring effect, especially around my mouth area where I need all the help I can get. My makeup holds up well all day even though the weather has been so really hot lately. Other than that weird sensation I get that does eventually pass, my skin generally feels comfortable. Like it. 4 stars. Made in Australia.

Ingredients: Aqua/Water/Eau, Sodium Acrylates Crosspolymer-2, Acetyl Heptapeptide-4 (Prebiotic-Peptide/Peptides Prébiotiques), Caprylyl Glycol, Glycerin (*Plant/Plante), Fructose, Withania Somnifera Root Extract (*Plant/Plante), Ganoderma Lucidum ( Mushroom) Extract, Citrus Paradisi (Grapefruit) Peel Oil, Lavandula Angustifolia (Lavender) Oil, Rosa Damascena (Rose Absolute/Rose Absolue) Flower Oil, Benzyl Alcohol, Dehydroacetic Acid. (*Plant Derived/Dérivé des Plantes).

title: Ummm Quirky?
text:
I tend to bounce back and forth between Braun and Norelco and I've owned several models of each brand. As for this one, Norelco Arcitec 1090, I think it's a bit awkward to hold against the face. Norelco used to have a nice angled handle/body that made it very comfortable to use but not so with this one. It also seems very light weight and is a bit louder than my old Norelco. The shaving performance is very good but I'm not sure it's any better than the older models. I love the look of the charging stand but I found one fault with it. There is no power switch to turn it off which means that you have to unplug the power cord after the charge is complete. The owners manual says not to leave it plugged in 24/7 which kind of defeats the purpose of the charging stand IMO. The stand is functional as a place to store the razor when charging is complete. Replacing the $35 head (blades) is by far the easiest of any razor that I've ever owned. Cleaning the blades is also easy by rinsing under running HOT water. I've had self cleaning Braun and Norelco's and got tired of buying those cleaning cartridges every month which made the purchase decision on this razor easier to make. The pop out mustache trimmer is way too small and very hard to deploy. They could have left that out of the design and included a separate trimmer which would have been more useful. All in all I like this razor but I must admit that I'm not as excited about the purchase as I have been in the past with older models.

UPDATE: After spending a few days with this shaver I decided to return it. I don't think that it's performance justifies the price. It's awkward to use, noisy and it's performance is no better than the outgoing models. I have decided to save my money and buy replacements heads and cleaning solution for my old razor.

I normally wear color street. I wanted to find something similar with a different variety to chose from so I tried these out. This is a comparison of the two.
This nail sticker pack has 8 sheets in it for 8 uses and color street has 2 sheets meant for one use, but my nails are short so I can get two. The price point is the same but the stickers have 6 more sets for me.
Color street is pretty easy to put on but these seemed to be slightly easier.
Color street normally lasts about 7-10 days for be before they start coming off and chipping (no additional top coats or extra effort other than the nail strips themselves). These last a solid 3 days with no chipping but then they come off on the 4th day.
Color street instructions are easy to read and make sense. I am not a big beauty person and I don't know everything there is to know about nails, thus my willingness to put stickers on my nails instead of getting manicures but I don't know what nail artichoke is so I didn't do that part. title: Hint: Pour step 1 into a spray bottle
text:
This stuff is amazing. I have a tendency to get bored with my hair color, and every once in a while I will go against my better judgment for the sake of fashion and instead of waiting for my current color to fade, just strip it instead. You'd think I'd know by now that I stand gratification often comes with consequences and sacrifice. Well, after this last color swap, which I brilliantly felt compelled to do at about 3:15 in the morning two weeks ago, I immediately knew upon rinsing that I had just pushed my poor hair over the edge. I could see the damage when I fluffed my hands through and watched tiny little, broken pieces of hair fly off my head and sink to the floor like little blonde, fluffy tears.

I used the treatment last night. The first step is runny, like water. I poured a bit into my hand, and most of it went down the drain. Wasted product is wasted money, I want gonna play that game. I almost grabbed a color bowl and brush, but decided to try something else first, because I don’t have time for that. And by time I mean the patiennce. I carefully put the packet down and grabbed a funnel, an empty spray bottle and poured it in. I sprayed the product into my hair and combed it through. Much easier than wrestling a packet, a liquid product, and my hair all at once. In addition to just being easier, I felt this was the safer route to go considering the small bit of product I did get on my hands stung my cuticles and really stung a small scratch from my rude cat. Not sure which ingredient caused it, but I was surprised the packaging didn’t recommend wearing gloves.

I let my hair air dry last night and styled it with my flat iron this morning. The first difference I noticed was how much smoother and easier the plates glided over my hair. I can often feel the roughness of my most damaged areas because any amount of buildup product on my flat iron will "catch" the roughed up cuticle. No catching this morning. I am currently floofing my hair....No breakage. Like, zero. No sad blonde tears. I am not surrounded by a hair-nado. I am not adding to the graveyard of sad, sacrificed strands that I should probably sweep off my bathroom floor. HOW IS THAT EVEN POSSIBLE?!

I didn't expect the stuff to suck but I didn't expect it to be blessed by some ancient Goddess of damaged hair either.

Ordering the full size as soon as I submit this review.

title: A fairly aggressive razor
text:
Coming from my mild Rimei and Baili razors, I'd say this razor is pretty aggressive. Significantly higher blade exposure than what I'm used to. I have very coarse, tough facial hairs, but pretty sensitive skin on my throat and upper lip, so as you can imagine, shaving can be a nightmare for me if the razor and blade combo is wrong.

I like this razor, but it will take some getting used to. I would recommend using a less sharp, smoother blade at first, such as a Derby or a Big Ben, unless you already know you can handle the combination of an aggressive razor with a very sharp blade.

I first ordered the Rapira Swedish Supersteel razor, but it came with a bent guard (looked damaged in shipping), so I sent it back. Aside from that, that razor has a metal handle (zinc?) and the weight was more balanced towards the handle. This razor is overall lighter and the weight is more balanced towards the head, which I prefer. The head on both razors is the same Tech-type design.

The handle is good, probably not as tough as a metal handle though. I'd prefer a better grip on it, similar to a rougher checkered surface like on a plastic rifle stock or something, but it does the job.

title: A convert!
text:
I had a Norelco 6800 series shaver before this one, and it did great for me. However, my wife wanted to use it ... and I made her promise to let me buy a new "good shaver" if she took my 'old reliable'.

So I bought this shaver. I have always been intrigued by the idea of a wet shave, since shaving 'wet' always shaves better.

This shaver delivers on the promise and it does it extremely well. I use it with shave gel, and it gets closer and cleaner than any foil shaver or any other electric I have EVER used. That's saying a lot, since I've tried almost every kind out there that there is to try, starting WAY back when Norelco only made the two-head shaver.

A big Plus to this shaver is that you can rinse it out right away and hang it up with the little strap provided. It hangs head down, and it dries out just fine between shaves for me. The stand they provide with it doesn't make you fiddle about with the strap to disconnect it; rather it just drops into the charging stand to recharge.

To say I'm happy with this shaver is to understate it. I have MUCH less of a 5 o'clock shadow, and I am very happy with the way I look when I leave for work. To me, clean and neat is professional, and this shaver enhances the look.

title: An addition to my top of the line fragrances. A MUST BUY.
text:
This perfume screams Sophistication, Youth and Trendy. I am so in love with the fragrance that I cannot possibly appreciate enough. The notes are as below:
Starting with carambola, with a bubbly and nonconformist personality, which immediately makes a contrast with the tradition of white lemon and with the nobility of rose wood. Then the distinctive character of cedar leaves rises up, to highlight the vibrant notes of tarragon and the manliness of clary sage. Precious understandings finally leave their stamp on an irresistible trail: sycamore wood, comforting amber and sparkling musk offering mysterious and skin-deep sensations.

That was what the Versace website explains about notes. Here's what I felt.
Top Note: Woody (possibly rose wood)
Mid Note: Tarragon (It's a spice, green and looks like grass)
Base Note: This is my fave part. Once the top and mid note subsides, you will not stop smelling yourself. Amber, musk and berries - So attracting still not over-powering.

I have to agree it does not last too long. For me, it did 4 hours in fall. It could be less in summer. But it totally depends on the kind of skin you have. I am Asian and have brown skin. Caucasian will hold this for longer (somehow this seems to be the case). But also depends on what kind of environment you work on. But, that's not a deal breaker.

I would highly recommend this to college students, young people who work in office environments, perfect for a date or a dinner with someone special. Goodluck.

title: A Great Shave
text:
First off let me start off by saying that like most 17 year old males, I have very sensitive skin. Before buying the Norelco Advantage, I could not find a simple solution to getting a nice quick shave without all the hassle that comes along with it. I did not really have a problem at the time, with the length of time that shaving took, but rather, the razor-burn afterwards. I went through about 10-12 different types of creams, and 6-7 different razors, trying to find the right combination. It wasn't until a good friend of mine recommended this, that I decided to try an electric razor. The Norelco definately lived up to it's reputation, as one of the best electric razors out there. Two things that stuck out about it was that you could get a good clean shave in hardly any time at all, and in my case, the gel worked wonders on my previous razor burn.

Now, there are however a few things that could have been improved on. None of these however seriously demote the quality of this razor. The first thing that I noticed is that it is not good with multiple day stubble. If I go for a few days without shaving, I end up having to switch to the beard trimmer, and then back again to the regular blade, in order to get a good shave. This can get quite tedious and annoying in a hurry. Another thing that I noticed is that the blades tend to gunk up quite easily making cleaning almost a weekly thing. The last thing is that unless at full charge, the blades tend miss some of the longer hairs.

All around this is a great product for those of you out there who are looking for a nice quick close shave. Dollar for dollar this is one of the better products that I have bought, but I look foward to seeing an upgrade on this Electric.

title: you will see results if you commit to it
text:
I've been using this for 3 months now and I do think this works with longterm use. You obviously aren't going to see overnight results but if you keep at it you will notice a difference on your wrinkles. Luckily I don't have too many yet but I did use it on the little areas where I'm starting to see wrinkles. I noticed a tightening of the areas I used the laser on for the past 3 months. I really liked the hyaluronic acid serum that was included in the set - the serum felt gentle and has no smell (fragrance free). On some days where I didn't use the laser I would still use the serum to moisturize my face. I looked into purchasing just the serum, which they do have for sale, as I really like the product. The laser is easy to operate and charge (usb). I didn't use this daily as I wanted to give my skin a rest, but I think if you used this religiously then you would see results at a much faster rate. It isn't painful, but you feel a little zap. I would equate it to the same level of "pain" as a derma roller, that spikey/zappy feeling - not painful, not super uncomfortable. That of course, will depend on your skin sensitivity. I recommend using the lowest setting first then working your way up as your skin sensitivity will allow. Don't force your skin into what it cannot handle - listen to your body's reaction!

text:
The hair shaving kit comes in a nicely packaged box, with 8 pieces: the shaver itself, 3 different shaving guides that offer 3 mm, 6 mm, 9 mm and 12 mm hair length, a small brush to clean the blades, a power cord, a plastic hood to put around the child and to keep hair out and lastly a powder pad to dust off hair from the face. The plastic hood and the powder pad are nice touches and they come in very handy in keeping the hair off my kid’s body. I am sure little hair bits don’t feel too good directly in contact with the skin. However, my favorite parts of the products are the shaving guides: they can be snapped on to the shaver and protect the scalp from getting ever pinched by the blades. And based on the relatively length of the guide teeth, you can adjust the hair length you want to cut to. I find that very convenient to keep the hair length consistent throughout the head (which is really not easy if your kid happens to squirm around and try to get away from the hair cut). The blades are quite easy to clean with the help of the brush and the cover of the blades can even be snapped off by a light push so you can clean the inside of the blade chamber. My only issue with the product is the manual: it seems to me that the manual I get is for a different product, since many accessories discussed in the manual are not included in this particular package. However, it did not affect my use so I am not bothered by it.
Overall I think this is a great product for some simple hair cut at home for my kid. I would recommend it to anyone who’s looking for something simple to use without breaking a bank. I received this product at a discounted price for my honest and unbiased review.

I the bottle, the smell of the lotion is horrible - I found it to have a strong, artificial scent similar to alcoholic spirits. I decided to give it a try so that I could write an accurate review. The good news is that once on the skin, the distasteful fragrance does not last; I didn't really detect much scent at all after that, but there may have been a faint hint of rose in the dry-down. The moisturization was adequate, nothing more.

I do like the Nail & Cuticle Oil, which comes in a little roller bottle and actually DOES have a rose scent. But this set is absolutely NOT worth the cost, especially given that the lotion is likely to be completely gone after just a few weeks of daily use. Not recommended.

Since I don't like the scent of this product, I decided to try it on my feet. Despite the lotion being very thin, I actually found it to work quite well on my feet! title: Looks great and works well!
text:
I have a very eclectic look in my house and I like the style of this!
-The white part is not plastic. It’s heavy and solid. I’m not sure if it’s breakable as I don’t want to find out.
-There is a “max fill” sticker inside which is visible through the slits. It cannot be removed. I remedied this by spinning it to the back, but the button for the lights and power are now in the back. Not a big deal to me, but I try to give as much info as I can.
-Also, the fill tank is attached to the unit base and not removable like some other brands. It must be unplugged to be refilled, again, not a big deal.
-The lights can change colors, be set to one, or turned off by pressing the light button (on the left)
- it’s a smaller tank. I used 3 drops of eo and felt it worked well.
-along with vacuuming and carpet shampooing, I have found this to be the best way to keep dog smell from being too overpowering in my house.
-I keep hearing a little bubbling sound coming from it. It’s extremely soothing like listening to a river almost.
-Nice unit, works well. No complaints, but I will update if further use shows any problems.
